name: Bachelor of Agricultural Sciences
description:
A three-year, 144-unit degree (102 core + 18 work-integrated learning + 24 elective units) taught across Waite, Adelaide City, and Roseworthy campuses, with February and July intakes. Combines crop and livestock science, soil and water management, agricultural genetics and biochemistry, agribusiness, and precision-agriculture technology (GPS, sensors, drones) rather than focusing narrowly on farm operation.

Includes at least 240 hours of industry placement across three dedicated work-integrated-learning courses. Waite Campus (about 7km from the Adelaide CBD, ~184 hectares) is a major agricultural research precinct with laboratories, greenhouses, orchards, and vineyards; Roseworthy Campus (about 50km north of Adelaide) focuses on dryland agriculture and animal production.

Adelaide University lists graduate career paths including agronomist, agricultural scientist, soil scientist, livestock scientist, horticultural manager, biosecurity officer, sustainability officer, and agribusiness roles.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — AGRI1002 Agricultural Systems; BIOL1004 Biology 1B: Evolution and Diversity of Organisms; CHEM1000 Foundations in Chemistry (or CHEM1002 Chemistry 1A); STAT1000 Data Skills for Scientists (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — AGRI1000 Agricultural Production; AGRI1003 Soils and Landscapes; BIOL1003 Biology 1A: Molecules, Genes and Cells; AGRI1910 Introduction to Professional Skills in Agriculture (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — AGRI2004 Soil and Water Resources; AGRI2006 Agricultural Biochemistry; AGRI2013 Microbiology and Invertebrate Biology; AGRI2011 Foundations in Plant Science (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — AGRI2005 Crop and Pasture Production; AGRI2910 Agricultural Science Work Experience; ANIM2006 Livestock Production 2; AGRI2017 Agricultural Genetics (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — AGRI3003 Agricultural Economics and Policy; AGRI3007 Agricultural Experimental Design and Analysis; 2 electives (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — AGRI3004 Professional Skills in Agricultural Science 3; AGRI2010 Agribusiness; 2 electives (24 units).
admission_requirements: Secondary education equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE); no formal prerequisite, but assumed knowledge of SACE Stage 2 Chemistry and Mathematical Methods (or equivalent) is expected. Country-specific academic benchmarks apply for international applicants.

name: Bachelor of Architectural Design
description:
A three-year, 144-unit foundation degree (90 core + a 36-unit major/discipline stream + 18 elective units) at Adelaide City Campus, with February and July intakes. Covers design studio work, technical drawing and construction, digital modelling, sustainability, and architectural history/theory. No prerequisites or assumed knowledge required.

Adelaide University frames this as the first stage toward architectural registration rather than a standalone qualification: it feeds into the Master of Architecture, with a packaged Bachelor + Master of Architecture pathway offered at 5 years full-time; this bachelor's degree alone does not qualify a graduate as a registered architect. Students can also specialise via a major in Urban Planning, with a combined Bachelor of Architectural Design (Urban Planning) + Master of Urban and Regional Planning pathway at 4 years, or a Bachelor of Architectural Design + Master of Landscape Architecture pathway at 5 years.

Adelaide University lists graduate career paths including architect (with further study), landscape architect (with further study), architectural graduate, draftsperson, urban designer, environmental designer, architectural technician, and heritage consultant.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — ARCH1000 Design Studio (Principles); ARCH1002 Design Communication (Principles); ARCH1003 Design Construction (Principles); 1 common core course (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — ARCH1004 Architectural Design Studio (Home); ARCH1005 Architectural Design Cultures; ARCH1006 Environmental Design and the Sensory Body; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — ARCH2004 Architectural Design Studio (Urban Landscapes); ARCH2007 Digital Design Communications; 1 common core course (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — ARCH2011 Architectural Design Studio (Communication); ARCH2000 Contemporary Architectural Theory; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — ARCH3001 Architectural Design Studio (Tectonics); ARCH3003 Multi-storey Technologies; 1 common core course (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — ARCH3013 Architectural Design Studio (Context and Cultures); ARCH3014 Environmental Ecologies and Systems in Architecture; 1 elective (24 units).
admission_requirements: Secondary education equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE) or higher; no formal prerequisites and no assumed knowledge required.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
The Bachelor of Arts at Adelaide University runs on a two-major structure: every student picks two of the 26 available majors, from long-standing options like English, History, and Politics to newer additions such as Digital Humanities and Criminology. Each major is built from eight courses across three years (two in first year, three in second, three in third), so switching or adding a major stays a genuine option rather than paperwork.

Running alongside the majors is a University Common Core: three interdisciplinary courses spread across the degree rather than front-loaded, plus three Work Integrated Learning courses (Professional Pathways and Destinations 1 and 2, and a final-year Internship in Society and Culture) that push students into placements, portfolio work, or applied projects tied to their chosen field.

No two Arts degrees look quite the same in practice; a History/Politics combination reads very differently to a Creative Writing/Film Studies one, and the university markets that flexibility as the point rather than a limitation. Career paths span journalism, policy and government, publishing, and education, with a meaningful share of graduates going on to postgraduate study in law, teaching, or their chosen discipline.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — 1 course from Major 1; 1 course from Major 2; SOCI1007 Professional Pathways and Destinations 1; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — 1 course from Major 1; 1 course from Major 2; University Common Core course 1; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — 1-2 courses from each major; University Common Core course 2 (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — 1-2 courses from each major; SOCI2019 Professional Pathways and Destinations 2 (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — 1-2 courses from each major; University Common Core course 3 (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — 1-2 courses from each major; SOCI3903 Internship: Society and Culture (24 units).
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 70.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.0, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Bachelor of Aviation: Management
description:
A three-year degree (144 units) at the Mawson Lakes campus, on the business and operational side of aviation rather than flying: airline finance and operations, airport administration, aviation safety, supply chain and logistics, and strategic planning. Students get about five hours of flying and five hours of observational flying for context but do not train for a licence.

The third year includes two aviation project courses applying the material to real problems. Entry is an ATAR of about 70. It suits people who want a management career in airlines, airports or the wider aviation sector, in roles such as operations manager, fleet planner, safety manager or airport manager.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (or equivalent secondary qualification) (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Aviation: Pilot
description:
A three-year degree (144 units) that shares its first year with the aviation management major before specialising. It combines aviation coursework with flight training delivered in partnership with Flight Training Adelaide, including single and multi-engine aircraft and A320 and 737 simulators.

Students can take a concurrent Graduate Diploma in Aviation that carries the Commercial Pilot Licence, command instrument rating and multi-engine class rating; the flight training is an additional cost on top of tuition and follows CASA's integrated-course timeline. Entry is an ATAR of about 70, and an aviation medical is required to fly. It suits students set on an airline or commercial flying career who want a degree alongside the licences.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (Australian applicants); country-specific secondary-qualification equivalents for international applicants (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Biomedical and Health Sciences
description:
A three-year science degree (144 units) about how the human body works in health and disease, with a choice of eight majors: biochemistry, clinical trials, genetics, medical science, microbiology and immunology, neuroscience, public health, or reproductive and childhood health, and the option of two majors.

Students use dedicated anatomy laboratories with real human specimens and complete a final-year work placement or research project. Entry is an ATAR of about 80 with no specific prerequisites. It prepares graduates for research and health-industry work and is a common foundation for postgraduate study, including graduate-entry medicine.
admission_requirements: ATAR 90 (competitive health-science entry) (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
A three-year degree (144 units) at Adelaide University's city campus. The structure is a common core (ethics, data literacy, First Nations knowledges, responsible AI), a program core (accounting for decision makers, management and leadership, emerging technologies and business analytics, marketing principles), one 48-unit major, a work-integrated learning block, and electives.

Students choose one major from 13 options, including Digital Business, International Business, Management, Marketing, Project Management, Human Resource Management, Real Estate, Sport Management, Procurement and Supply Chain Management, and Tourism, Events and Hospitality Management. The work-integrated learning courses provide internships, practicums, or industry projects as part of the degree rather than as an add-on.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Business: Digital Business
description:
The digital business major of the Bachelor of Business (three years, 144 units). Alongside the shared business core it focuses on how organisations run and compete online: digital strategy, e-commerce, digital marketing, data-informed decision-making and the management of technology-driven change.

Work-integrated learning is built in, with February and July intakes at the city campus and an ATAR of about 70 for entry. It is less technical than an IT degree and suits students who want to lead digital projects and transformation from the business side, in roles such as digital coordinator, e-commerce officer or business analyst.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Business: Human Resource Management
description:
The human resource management major of Adelaide University's Bachelor of Business: a three-year degree (144 units) with a shared business core in accounting, economics, marketing and management, a 48-unit HR major, work-integrated learning, and electives.

The major covers recruitment and selection, employee development, performance and reward, workplace relations and employment law, and the growing use of people analytics. February and July intakes, city campus, entry an ATAR of about 70. It suits students aiming at generalist HR, recruitment, learning and development or workplace relations roles, with the broad business core keeping other paths open.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Business: Innovation, Entrepreneurship and Strategy
description:
The innovation, entrepreneurship and strategy major of the Bachelor of Business (three years, 144 units). On top of the shared business core it covers new venture creation, business model design, innovation management and competitive strategy, often through project work on real or student ventures.

The degree includes work-integrated learning, with February and July intakes at the city campus and an ATAR of about 70 for entry. It suits students who want to start a business or work in a strategy, product or innovation role inside an established organisation.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Business: International Business
description:
The Bachelor of Business with an International Business major, on the standard three-year Bachelor of Business structure (common core, business program core, 48-unit major, work-integrated learning, electives).

The major's 48 units cover managing across cultures, the international business environment and operations, international human resource management, international business in the Asia-Pacific, internationalisation of small and medium enterprises, and contemporary issues in international business. Professional internships run through the degree, and flexible electives leave room for a semester of international exchange. It suits students aiming at trade, export, global supply chain, or multinational management roles.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Business: Management
description:
The Bachelor of Business with a Management major, sharing the standard three-year Bachelor of Business structure (common core, business program core, 48-unit major, work-integrated learning, electives).

The Management major covers organisational behaviour, organisational leadership, managing decision making and communication, the international business environment, foundations of project management, applied creativity for business, triple bottom line and innovation, and managing ethics and values. Work-integrated learning is taken as a workplace placement or an alternative such as the eChallenge startup course. It is the general-purpose major for students heading into supervisory and operations roles across industries.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Business: Marketing
description:
This is the Bachelor of Business with a Marketing major. The degree structure is the same across all Bachelor of Business majors: a common core, a business program core (accounting, management, business analytics, marketing principles), a 48-unit major, a work-integrated learning block, and electives, over three years.

The Marketing major's 48 units cover consumer behaviour, marketing analytics, advertising, market research and customer insights, branding, distribution, marketing planning, and service design. Work-integrated learning is taken as an Integrated Marketing course or an internship. It suits students aiming at brand management, market research, digital marketing, or advertising roles.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Business: Marketing and Communication
description:
The marketing and communication major of the Bachelor of Business (three years, 144 units). Built on the shared business core, the 48-unit major pairs marketing fundamentals, consumer behaviour and marketing analytics with communication content: public relations, media, campaign messaging and stakeholder engagement.

Work-integrated learning is part of the degree, with February and July intakes at the city campus and an ATAR of about 70 for entry. It suits students who want to work where marketing and corporate or public relations meet, in roles such as communications coordinator, campaign manager or brand and PR assistant.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Business: Marketing and Design
description:
The marketing and design major of the Bachelor of Business (three years, 144 units). It combines the marketing sequence, consumer behaviour, branding and analytics, with design thinking and visual communication, so graduates can both plan a campaign and shape how it looks and feels.

The degree keeps the shared business core, includes work-integrated learning, and runs February and July intakes at the city campus with an ATAR of about 70 for entry. It suits students interested in brand design, content and creative direction within a marketing team, rather than a pure graphic design degree.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Business: Procurement and Supply Chain Management
description:
The procurement and supply chain management major of Adelaide University's Bachelor of Business: a three-year degree (144 units) with a shared business core and a 48-unit major covering sourcing and supplier management, logistics, inventory and distribution, contract management and the analytics used to run a supply chain.

Work-integrated learning is part of the degree, with February and July intakes at the city campus and an ATAR of about 70 for entry. It suits students aiming at procurement, logistics, operations or supply chain analyst roles, a function that has drawn much more attention since recent global supply disruptions.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Business: Project Management
description:
The Bachelor of Business with a Project Management major, on the standard three-year Bachelor of Business structure (common core, business program core, 48-unit major, work-integrated learning, electives).

The major's 48 units cover foundations of project management, scheduling and cost management, project management methodologies, systems thinking, project risk management, infrastructure and sustainability, and a project management research study. Work-integrated learning is a 12-unit Project Management Professional Practice course in third year. The major is accredited by the Project Management Institute's Global Accreditation Center, which is useful for students planning to pursue PMI certification.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Business: Real Estate
description:
The real estate major of the Bachelor of Business (three years, 144 units). Alongside the shared business core it covers property valuation, property investment and finance, development, agency practice and the law and regulation of real estate.

Work-integrated learning is built in, with February and July intakes at the city campus and an ATAR of about 70 for entry. It is aligned to the licensing and professional pathways in the property industry and suits students aiming at valuation, agency, property management, development or property investment roles.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Business: Sport Management
description:
The sport management major of the Bachelor of Business (three years, 144 units). The 48-unit major applies the shared business core, marketing, finance, management and law, to the sport industry: club and facility administration, sport marketing and sponsorship, event delivery and the governance of sporting bodies.

Work-integrated learning is part of the degree, with February and July intakes at the city campus and an ATAR of about 70 for entry. It suits students who want a business career specifically in professional or community sport, events or sporting administration.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Business: Tourism, Events and Hospitality Management
description:
The tourism, events and hospitality management major of the Bachelor of Business (three years, 144 units). The 48-unit major applies the shared business core to visitor industries: destination and tourism management, event planning and delivery, hospitality operations, and the marketing of experiences.

Work-integrated learning is part of the degree, with February and July intakes at the city campus and an ATAR of about 70 for entry. It suits students who want a management career in tourism bodies, event companies, hotels, venues or festivals rather than a general business role.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Clinical Exercise Physiology (Honours)
admission_requirements: ATAR 80 (allied-health honours entry) (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, no band below 7.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL), required for health/education placements

name: Bachelor of Commerce: Accounting
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Commerce (Accounting major) sits within the standard 144-unit, three-year commerce structure: a common core shared across all commerce degrees, an accounting major built from financial and management accounting, auditing, and taxation law courses, plus electives students can use to add a second major or take free-standing units in business, management, or a language. February and July intakes, delivered mainly at Adelaide City Campus with occasional online options.

The accounting major is built to satisfy the accreditation requirements of both CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, a distinction not every accounting degree in the state carries, and one that matters for graduates aiming at Big Four or mid-tier firm graduate programs. Coursework goes beyond bookkeeping mechanics into the professional judgement calls accountants actually make: revenue recognition disputes, audit independence questions, and the ethical grey areas around tax minimisation.

Career paths the university lists include auditor, tax accountant, management accountant, financial analyst, and forensic accountant. Many students pair the major with Finance or Business Analytics for a double major rather than taking accounting alone.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — ACCTING 1006 Financial Accounting; COMMERC 1004 Data Analysis for Business; ECON 1002 Introductory Microeconomics; COMMERC 1006 Business, Society and the Planet (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — ACCTING 1007 Management Accounting; COMMERC 1005 Marketing Principles; ECON 1004 Introductory Macroeconomics; COMMLAW 1004 Business Law (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — ACCTING 2005 Financial Accounting and Reporting; ACCTING 2008 Cost Management; COMMLAW 2101 Corporations Law; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — ACCTING 2006 Accounting Information Systems; ACCTING 3014 Auditing and Assurance Services; TAXATION 2000 Taxation Law; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — ACCTING 3007 Advanced Financial Accounting; ACCTING 3009 Contemporary Issues in Accounting; 2 electives (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — ACCTING 3010 Strategic Management Accounting; COMMERC 3005 Business Capstone; 2 electives (24 units).
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 80.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.0, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Bachelor of Commerce: Banking and Finance
description:
The banking and finance major of Adelaide University's Bachelor of Commerce: a three-year degree (144 units) with a 66-unit commerce core, then major courses in options, futures and risk management, portfolio theory, business valuation, and regulation and ethics in finance, with electives in fintech, international banking and treasury.

It is built around the pathway to the Chartered Financial Analyst credential, and includes more than 300 hours of work-integrated learning across years two and three through a business practicum and business clinic. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students aiming at investment, corporate finance, risk or banking roles.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Commerce: Business Analytics
description:
The business analytics major of the Bachelor of Commerce (three years, 144 units). On top of the commerce core in accounting, finance, economics and management, the major covers foundations of business analytics, predictive and visual analytics, business applications of artificial intelligence, and chatbot design and prompt engineering, using industry-standard tools.

Two work-integrated learning courses, a business practicum in year two and a business clinic in year three, are built into the degree. Entry is an ATAR of about 80. It suits students who want to work in analytics, business intelligence or data-informed consulting across finance, marketing, health, tech and government.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Commerce: Financial Planning
description:
Adelaide University offers financial planning within the Bachelor of Commerce as a combined Financial Planning and Property double major (three years, 144 units). The financial planning side covers superannuation, retirement planning, insurance, estate planning and the regulatory framework for advice; the property side adds valuation, property law, investment analysis and agency practice.

The degree includes more than 400 hours of work-integrated learning through case studies and industry collaboration, and points toward professional recognition in both fields. Entry is an ATAR of about 80. It suits students who want a client-facing wealth advisory career and value having property expertise alongside financial planning.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Commerce: Property
description:
The property major of Adelaide University's Bachelor of Commerce (three years, 144 units): a 66-unit commerce core plus property courses in property economics, property investment, property development, and statutory and advanced valuations.

Adelaide University is working with the Australian Property Institute on program accreditation, so the valuer registration pathway is not yet finalised. Two work-integrated learning courses, a business practicum and a business clinic, run in years two and three. Entry is an ATAR of about 80. It suits students aiming at commercial property development, investment analysis, asset management or valuation.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Computer Science
description:
At 72 units across three years, Adelaide University's Bachelor of Computer Science front-loads breadth: first year covers programming fundamentals, IT systems, structured data, and security foundations, before requiring a major from second year on: Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Distributed Systems and Networking, or Programming Languages, among others.

Unlike some computing degrees that treat security as a bolt-on elective, security foundations sit in first year here, reflecting a program design that assumes cybersecurity literacy is baseline rather than a later specialisation. The AI major benefits from Adelaide's strength in machine learning research, and feeds directly into the university's Master of Computer Science for students who want to continue rather than enter the workforce at three years.

Like its postgraduate counterpart, the degree carries provisional accreditation from the Australian Computer Society at the Professional level and is recognised under the Seoul Accord. Career paths listed include software engineer, systems analyst, data engineer, and cybersecurity analyst, with February and July intakes.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Programming; Introduction to Computer Systems; Discrete Mathematics; 1 common core course (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Object-Oriented Programming; Security Foundations; Structured Data and Databases; 1 common core course (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Algorithms and Data Structures; Software Engineering; 1 major course; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Operating Systems; Requirements and User Experience; 1 major course; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — 2 major courses; 2 electives (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Capstone Project; 1 major course; 1 elective (24 units).
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 80, including recommended study of Mathematical Methods.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.0, with a minimum of 6.0 in each band (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Computer Science (Honours)
description:
A four-year degree (the honours is built in, not a separate year) with a fourth-year thesis run across three courses, where students define a research topic and work with academic staff. First year covers programming, structured data, object-oriented programming, mathematics, and security; later years add theory of computation, operating systems, algorithms, distributed computing, and language models.

Students take one major from Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, Human-Centred Computing, or Programming Languages, and complete 12 to 24 units of work-integrated learning through an intensive computing project or ICT internships. The degree is provisionally accredited at professional level by the Australian Computer Society and recognised internationally through the Seoul Accord. Part-time study is not available to international students.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Computer Science: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
description:
The artificial intelligence and machine learning major of Adelaide University's Bachelor of Computer Science: a three-year degree (144 units) with a 66-unit computing core in programming, data structures, security and mathematics, then a 54-unit major concentrating on machine learning algorithms, data analytics and the systems that put models into production, finishing with a team capstone project for a real client.

The degree is accredited by the Australian Computer Society and recognised internationally through the Seoul Accord. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students who want to build AI systems rather than just use them, heading into machine learning engineering, data science or research roles across defence, health, finance and agriculture.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Computer Science: Human-Centred Computing
description:
The human-centred computing major of the Bachelor of Computer Science (three years, 144 units). It keeps the full computing core, programming, data structures, security and mathematics, and directs the 54-unit major toward how people actually use software: interaction design, user experience, usability testing and accessible interfaces, ending in a team capstone project for an external client.

The degree is accredited by the Australian Computer Society and recognised under the Seoul Accord. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students who want to stay technical but work at the boundary between engineering and design, moving into UX engineering, product roles or front-end and interaction development.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Computer Science: Programming Languages
description:
The programming languages major of the Bachelor of Computer Science (three years, 144 units). On top of the shared computing core it focuses the 54-unit major on the design, semantics and implementation of programming languages, compilers and translators, and the theory that underpins reliable software, finishing with a client capstone project.

The degree is accredited by the Australian Computer Society and recognised under the Seoul Accord. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It is the most theoretical of the three computer science majors and suits students drawn to compilers, language design, formal methods and systems programming, or planning postgraduate research.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Construction Management
description:
A three-year degree (144 units) covering the construction process end to end: low-rise and high-rise construction, structures, construction science and materials, economics and procurement, quantity surveying and cost estimating, contract administration, planning and safety, building codes, building services, and scheduling. Digital construction tools are taught from first year.

Work-integrated learning is one mandatory professional practice course. On accreditation: as of 2026 the Australian Institute of Building Surveyors has accredited years 1 and 2 at Level 2, with year 3 accreditation being pursued, and the page does not list quantity surveying accreditation, so applicants who need a specific professional pathway should confirm the current status with the university.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Civil) (Honours)
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Engineering (Civil) (Honours) is a four-year AQF Level 8 degree built around a common first two years of mathematics, mechanics, and design fundamentals shared with other engineering streams, before students specialise into civil-specific coursework in structures, geotechnics, water engineering, and transportation.

From third year, students choose a major (Construction Management, Environmental Engineering, Renewable Energy, or Structures and Infrastructure) or add a minor in Defence Systems, Entrepreneurship, or Humanitarian Engineering, so the same base degree can point toward quite different careers: site engineer on a construction crew, dam safety analyst, or renewables project developer.

Fourth year centres on an honours research project run more like a live consulting engagement than a purely theoretical thesis. A real client, either an industry partner or an academic researcher, sets the brief, and students work through feasibility, concept design, and detailed design stages. Adelaide University lists graduate destinations including structural engineer, geotechnical engineer, water resources engineer, transport engineer, and construction manager, and the degree is accredited by Engineers Australia to Washington Accord standard for professional registration.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — ENG 1001 Engineering Mechanics; MATHS 1011 Mathematics IA; CIVIL 1002 Introduction to Civil Engineering; 1 common core course (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — ENG 1003 Engineering Modelling and Problem Solving; MATHS 1012 Mathematics IB; CIVIL 1004 Statics and Dynamics; 1 common core course (24 units).
Year 2 — CIVIL 2001 Structural Analysis; CIVIL 2002 Fluid Mechanics; CIVIL 2003 Geomechanics; CIVIL 2004 Construction Materials; CIVIL 2005 Surveying; MATHS 2107 Engineering Mathematics IIA; 1 elective.
Year 3 — CIVIL 3001 Structural Design; CIVIL 3002 Water Engineering; CIVIL 3003 Geotechnical Engineering; CIVIL 3004 Transport Engineering; CIVIL 3005 Construction Management; CIVIL 3006 Environmental Engineering; ENG 3004 Engineering Practice; ENG 3005 Project Management, plus major/minor electives.
Year 4 — CIVIL 4050 Honours Research Project (year-long, industry- or academic-supervised); ENG 4002A/ENG 4002B Engineering Practice Capstone; remaining major specialisation courses.
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 85, including Mathematical Methods and a recommended study of Physics.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with 6.0 minimum in each band (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Electrical) (Honours)
admission_requirements: ATAR 80 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Environmental) (Honours)
admission_requirements: ATAR 80 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Mechanical) (Honours)
description:
A four-year degree (132 core units) with honours built in. Core courses cover solid mechanics, dynamics, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, acoustics and vibrations, control systems, manufacturing processes, and computer-aided design, and year four is a major industry research project.

Students complete up to 450 hours of supervised industry work experience through professional practice courses and internships of up to 12 weeks. The degree is provisionally accredited at Professional Engineer level by Engineers Australia, which on full accreditation gives Washington Accord international recognition. Entry requires IELTS 6.5 and a Stage 2 mathematical methods prerequisite. Indicative international fee is around A$57,100 per year.
admission_requirements: ATAR 80 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science
description:
A three-year degree accredited by Exercise and Sports Science Australia, so graduates are eligible to register as an Accredited Exercise Scientist. Students complete more than 140 hours of industry placement across sporting clubs, gyms, fitness centres and schools.

Facilities are a strength: exercise testing labs, a high-performance sport centre, exercise physiology clinics, an environmental chamber, and a sport science hub at the South Australian Sports Institute. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students heading into strength and conditioning, performance analysis or exercise science, and it is the standard first step toward postgraduate clinical exercise physiology.
admission_requirements: ATAR 75 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Film and Television
description:
A three-year degree (144 units) covering the full production cycle from script to post, across screenwriting, cinematography, directing, editing, sound design and visual effects, with technical strands in digital compositing, 3D design and motion capture, plus film theory courses on world cinema, genre and documentary.

Facilities include a virtual production and TV studio, cinema cameras and industry-standard software, and students complete two work-integrated learning courses, an industry placement and a professional experience component, with partners such as Channel 44. Entry is an ATAR of about 70. It suits people aiming at directing, cinematography, editing, screenwriting or content production.
admission_requirements: ATAR 65 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Fine Arts
description:
A three-year studio degree that starts broad, sampling painting, drawing, printmaking, photography, sculpture, ceramics, jewellery, glass, and time-based work in video, sound and performance, then narrows to chosen disciplines in years two and three.

Work-integrated learning runs through partnerships with the Samstag Museum, JamFactory and the Art Gallery of South Australia, and students build a portfolio and exhibit publicly. Entry is an ATAR of about 70. It suits students who want to build a practice as a working artist, or move into curatorial, gallery, education or arts administration roles.
admission_requirements: ATAR 65, or portfolio/interview for non-ATAR applicants (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Graphic Communication Design
description:
A three-year studio-based design degree (144 units) taught across the city and Magill campuses, covering identity and branding, typography, interactive and digital design, UX design and packaging, with diploma and associate-degree exit points.

Much of the assessment is real client work, competitions and a final-year industry placement, so students graduate with a professional portfolio. Entry is an ATAR of about 70. It suits students heading into graphic design, branding, web and UX design, or visual communication roles across advertising, tech and corporate settings.
admission_requirements: ATAR 65 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Human Movement
description:
A three-year degree (144 units) built on anatomy, exercise physiology, biomechanics and motor control, paired with practical coaching and teaching skills and a human movement practicum.

Students choose one major: sport coaching, secondary health and physical education, or human nutrition, so the degree ranges from athlete development through to a pathway toward teaching health and PE. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits people aiming at coaching, sport development, physical education or community health and fitness roles, and it differs from the Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science, which is the ESSA-accredited exercise science pathway rather than a coaching and education one.
admission_requirements: ATAR 75 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Human Nutrition
description:
A three-year science degree grounded in anatomy, physiology, chemistry and biochemistry, with applied courses in nutrition across the lifespan, sports nutrition, public health nutrition and food science, and up to 200 hours in an industry or research setting in the final year.

It is a nutrition science degree rather than a dietetics qualification: it does not by itself make graduates dietitians. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students interested in designing diet and lifestyle programs for individuals and communities, working as nutritionists, sports nutritionists, community health workers or food industry advisers, or continuing to a postgraduate dietetics degree.
admission_requirements: ATAR 75 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Illustration and Animation
description:
A three-year studio degree covering drawing, traditional and digital illustration, 2D and 3D animation, stop-motion, motion capture and visual effects, along with character design and visual storytelling.

Students work in industry-standard studios with visual effects software and AR and VR tools, and build a professional portfolio through real project work. Entry is an ATAR of about 70. It suits people aiming at careers as animators, illustrators, concept artists or visual effects artists in film, games, publishing and advertising.
admission_requirements: ATAR 65 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Industrial Design
description:
A three-year studio-based degree (144 units) in designing physical products, systems and services, with an explicit emphasis on ethical, social and environmental responsibility alongside CAD, digital visualisation and materials.

Students work in purpose-built studios with CNC machines, 3D printers, laser cutters and VR and AR systems, and the third year includes a capstone design project and an industrial design practice course run with industry partners. Entry is an ATAR of about 70. Graduates work as industrial and product designers across consumer goods, furniture, packaging, assistive technology and related fields.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Information Technology runs a 72-unit, three-year structure split cleanly into thirds: 27 core units, a 27-unit major, and 18 units of free electives. The major choice does most of the work differentiating graduates: Software Development, Networking and Cyber Security, and Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning are the most commonly taken.

Compared to the Bachelor of Computer Science, the IT degree leans more applied in its core, with less emphasis on algorithmic complexity and formal computation theory and more on systems integration, project delivery, and IT service management. It's aimed at graduates headed toward corporate IT departments and consultancies rather than pure software development houses.

Career paths the university lists include IT consultant, network administrator, cybersecurity analyst, systems analyst, and software developer. February and July intake, delivered mainly at Adelaide City Campus.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Introduction to Programming; IT Systems Fundamentals; Business Analysis (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Database Systems; Networking Fundamentals; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Systems Analysis and Design; 1 major course; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — IT Project Management; 1 major course; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — 2 major courses; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — IT Capstone Project; 1 major course; 1 elective (24 units).
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 75.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.0, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology: Data Analytics
description:
The data analytics specialisation of Adelaide University's Bachelor of Information Technology: a three-year degree (144 units) with a 66-unit IT core and a common first year that lets students change major, then a specialisation in turning data into decisions, covering data management, analysis, visualisation and the tools used across industry.

The degree is provisionally accredited at professional level by the Australian Computer Society, and it includes an industry capstone project with a real client. Study is split across the Adelaide city and Mawson Lakes campuses. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students aiming at data analyst, business intelligence or analytics-focused IT roles rather than software engineering.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Information Technology: Games Development
description:
The games development specialisation of the Bachelor of Information Technology (three years, 144 units). It keeps the IT core and common first year, then focuses on game engines, mobile game development and entertainment software built on object-oriented programming, with an industry capstone project for a real client.

The degree is provisionally accredited at professional level by the Australian Computer Society, taught across the city and Mawson Lakes campuses. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students who want to build games and interactive media and keep general IT employability, since the shared core still covers programming, systems and networking.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Information Technology: Networking and Cyber Security
description:
The networking and cyber security specialisation of the Bachelor of Information Technology (three years, 144 units). On top of the shared IT core it covers network infrastructure, security operations, and both defensive and offensive security practice, with an industry capstone project.

The degree is provisionally accredited at professional level by the Australian Computer Society and taught across the city and Mawson Lakes campuses. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students heading into network administration, security operations or cyber security analyst roles, in a sector with a well-documented shortage of graduates in Australia.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Information Technology: Software Development
description:
A three-year degree (February and July intakes) with a 66-unit IT core covering problem solving, programming, structured and unstructured data, IT systems, security, cloud platforms, agile development, and business for IT professionals. The 48-unit software development major adds object-oriented programming, web and mobile development, concurrent and cloud programming, system design, design patterns, and an introduction to DevOps.

Work-integrated learning is 12 to 24 units, taken as an ICT capstone project with a real client or an ICT internship of 6 to 24 units. The degree is provisionally accredited at professional level by the Australian Computer Society and recognised internationally through the Seoul Accord. Indicative international fee is around A$52,500 per year.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Interior Architecture (Honours)
admission_requirements: ATAR 75 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of International Relations
description:
A three-year degree (144 units) built around a 66-unit core plus one 48-unit major chosen from options that include international security, international development, politics, population and migration studies, environmental management, and seven language streams from Chinese to Spanish.

Students complete a 15-day internship or an international exchange, with study tours and semester exchange also available, and teaching leans on simulations, case studies and seminars with visiting scholars. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students aiming at diplomacy, foreign affairs, international organisations, policy analysis or development work.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
Adelaide University's single Bachelor of Laws is a 96-unit, four-year AQF Level 7 degree: half core, half elective, but with real constraints on when students can take the elective half. No more than 9 units can be taken at Level I, and a minimum of 12 units is reserved for Level III, so students can't front-load easy electives early and coast.

Of the 48 elective units, 36 must be law electives, leaving 12 units as genuinely broadening electives students can take from outside the law school, such as a language, a science course, or a business elective, depending on interest. That's a deliberate design choice distinguishing the single LLB from Adelaide's various double-degree law combinations (Arts, Business, International Relations), which restructure the unit split differently and run longer.

The degree meets the requirements set by the Legal Practitioners Education and Admission Council of South Australia for admission to legal practice, subject to completing Practical Legal Training after graduation. Career paths span solicitor, barrister, in-house counsel, and policy roles, and a meaningful share of graduates go on to further postgraduate study rather than practising law directly.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Legal Method and Reasoning; Criminal Law; Torts; 1 broadening elective (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Contracts; Constitutional Law; 1 law elective; 1 broadening elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Property Law; Equity and Trusts; 2 law electives (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Administrative Law; Evidence; 2 law electives (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Corporations Law; Civil Procedure; 2 law electives (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Professional Conduct and Ethics; 3 law electives (24 units).
Year 4, Semester 1 — Level III law electives; clinical legal education component (24 units).
Year 4, Semester 2 — Level III law electives; research elective (24 units).
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 90.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Bachelor of Music
admission_requirements: ATAR 65, plus audition for performance majors (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Nursing packs 880 hours of clinical placement into its 144-unit, three-year structure, delivered as five credit-bearing Professional Experience Placement courses worth 42 units in total, starting in first year rather than being held back until students have finished the theory-heavy component.

Placements run across metropolitan, regional, and rural South Australian health services, and the degree is offered not just at Adelaide City Campus but also at Mount Gambier and Whyalla, meaning some students train in genuinely regional clinical settings rather than only large metropolitan teaching hospitals, a point of difference for students planning to work rurally after graduation, where SA has persistent nursing workforce shortages.

The degree qualifies graduates to apply for registration as a nurse with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. Career paths include registered nurse across acute, aged, mental health, and community care settings, with many graduates staying within the SA Health system given the placement relationships built during the degree.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Foundations of Nursing Practice; Anatomy and Physiology 1; Health Assessment; Professional Experience Placement 1 (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Anatomy and Physiology 2; Pharmacology for Nursing; Mental Health Nursing Foundations; Professional Experience Placement 2 (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Acute Care Nursing; Pathophysiology; Nursing Research and Evidence; Professional Experience Placement 3 (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Chronic and Complex Care; Aged Care Nursing; 1 elective; Professional Experience Placement 4 (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Child and Family Health Nursing; Leadership in Nursing Practice; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Transition to Professional Practice; Complex Care Capstone; Professional Experience Placement 5 (24 units).
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 80; current National Police Certificate and immunisation compliance required prior to placement.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, with a minimum of 7.0 in each band (registration/AHPRA English requirement).

name: Bachelor of Property
description:
Adelaide University delivers property as a major within the Bachelor of Commerce rather than as a standalone Bachelor of Property. It is a three-year degree (144 units) combining a commerce core in accounting, finance, economics and management with property-specific courses in property economics, investment, development and statutory and advanced valuation.

The university is working with the Australian Property Institute on accreditation, so the formal valuer registration pathway is still being finalised. The degree includes work-integrated learning through a business practicum and business clinic. Entry is an ATAR of about 80. It suits students heading into valuation, property investment, development or asset management.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Psychology
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Psychology builds on twelve core psychology courses common to every specialisation in the suite (Cognitive Neuroscience, Counselling and Interpersonal Skills, and the general stream), meaning students can defer choosing a specialisation without falling behind, since the differentiation mostly happens in fourth-year honours options.

From 2026, progression to the fourth (honours) year requires a GPA of at least 6.0 across all psychology core courses completed in years one to three. That's a real bar, not a formality, and the university is explicit that not everyone clears it. Students who don't can still graduate with the three-year Bachelor of Psychology, or apply separately for the one-year stand-alone Bachelor of Psychology (Honours) or the Graduate Diploma in Psychology (Advanced) as alternate routes.

The degree is accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council, a prerequisite for eventually registering as a psychologist in Australia. Career paths before further study include research assistant, human resources, and community services roles; full registration as a psychologist requires completing honours plus supervised postgraduate training or a further accredited program.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Introduction to Psychology A; Biological Bases of Behaviour; Research Methods in Psychology 1 (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Introduction to Psychology B; Social Psychology; Research Methods in Psychology 2 (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Cognitive Psychology; Developmental Psychology; Statistics for Psychology (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Abnormal Psychology; Personality and Individual Differences; Research Methods in Psychology 3 (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Psychological Assessment; Health Psychology; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Applied Psychology Capstone; Ethics in Psychological Practice; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 4 (Honours, GPA-gated) — Advanced Research Methods; Honours Thesis; specialised electives (Cognitive Neuroscience or Counselling and Interpersonal Skills stream).
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 85.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
A three-year degree (144 units) with February and July intakes, built from a common core, a science program core, one major or a discipline-course block, a required work-integrated learning component, and electives. The work-integrated learning is mandatory and ranges from research projects to fieldwork to industry placements depending on the major.

There are more than 30 majors across animal and veterinary sciences, chemistry, molecular and biomedical sciences, earth sciences, physics, ecology and evolution, environmental and plant sciences, and food science. Students can extend to a four-year Bachelor of Science (Honours) for research training, or fast-track into a Master of Research with about one further year.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Teaching
admission_requirements: ATAR 75; personal-capacity interview typical for teaching entry (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, no band below 7.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL), required for health/education placements

name: Bachelor of Veterinary Bioscience
description:
A three-year science degree that is the first half of Adelaide University's six-year veterinary pathway: graduates move into the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine, and only the two together lead to registration as a vet.

Year one covers foundational biology and chemistry, with later years moving into veterinary anatomy and physiology, animal nutrition, genetics, microbiology, parasitology and epidemiology, and hands-on animal work from first semester. It includes a 12-week animal husbandry placement on farms with cattle, sheep and horses, taught at purpose-built facilities including a teaching hospital. Entry is competitive: an ATAR of about 90, SACE Stage 2 biology, chemistry or mathematical methods, plus a questionnaire and the Casper assessment. It suits students committed to the full veterinary pathway.
admission_requirements: ATAR-equivalent selection rank of 90.00 or higher (adjusted) (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, no band below 7.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL), required for health/education placements

name: Master of Accounting
description:
A two-year conversion master's accredited by both Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand and CPA Australia, so graduates are eligible for membership of both and can enter their professional programs.

No accounting background is required: the curriculum runs from financial and management accounting, business law, economics and business mathematics through auditing, taxation and financial statement analysis, ending with an accounting industry project in the final semester. Entry is a completed bachelor's degree or equivalent. It suits career changers and mid-career professionals heading into audit, tax, management accounting or forensic accounting roles.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline (cognate discipline preferred)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Accounting and Finance
description:
A two-year master's (96 units) that sits between the Master of Accounting and the Master of Finance, giving both a professional accounting qualification and genuine finance depth. It is accredited by Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand and CPA Australia, so graduates can join both professional programs.

The accounting side covers financial and management accounting, auditing and taxation; the finance side adds investment, derivatives and corporate finance, with access to simulated trading environments. A graduate certificate or diploma exit is available. Entry needs a bachelor's degree with a GPA equivalent to 4.5 on Adelaide's 7-point scale, no accounting background required. It suits people who want both the CA or CPA pathway and finance skills for a broader commercial or leadership role.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline (cognate discipline preferred)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Applied Finance
description:
A shorter, more applied companion to the Master of Finance: 1.5 years full-time (72 units, 54 core plus 18 electives), with a graduate certificate or diploma exit point. The core runs through accounting concepts, principles of finance, economics, equity valuation, fixed income, derivatives and advanced investment management, plus an ethics course, and electives include financial modelling, behavioural finance, fintech, blockchain and international finance.

The emphasis is on applied courses and real-world problem solving rather than finance theory, and the finance courses align with major professional bodies. Entry needs a bachelor's degree with a GPA equivalent to 4.5 on Adelaide's 7-point scale. It suits people who want a faster route into financial analyst, investment or corporate finance roles.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline (cognate discipline preferred)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Architecture
description:
A two-year graduate-entry master's for people who hold a Bachelor of Architectural Design or an equivalent three-year pre-professional architecture degree; international applicants may be considered on portfolio. It is accredited by the Architectural Practice Board of South Australia and meets the National Standard of Competency for Architects, so after supervised experience and the registration exams graduates can register as architects in Australia and New Zealand.

Learning is studio-based in dedicated design studios and workshops, with real projects and industry input across sustainable design, heritage conservation and construction technology. It suits architecture graduates who need the accredited master's to register and want to develop a specialisation.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.0/7.0; Bachelor of Architectural Design or 3-year pre-professional architecture degree (portfolio required otherwise)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
description:
A two-year master's (66 core units) covering AI ethics, privacy and security, programming for AI and ML, statistical foundations, machine learning algorithms, applied AI, advanced topics, deep learning applications, and generative AI, ending in a two-semester industry capstone project. Students also take 18 elective units in areas such as computer vision and multimodal ML, data-driven decision-making, and prediction.

Entry requires a bachelor's degree in computer science, computer systems engineering, or software engineering (or a graduate certificate in computing), a GPA around 4.5 on a 7-point scale, and IELTS 6.5. It is not a conversion degree for people without a computing background. Part-time study is not available to international students.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in a related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Biotechnology
description:
Adelaide University offers biotechnology at master's level as the Master of Science specialising in Biotechnology: a two-year degree (96 units) combining advanced research platforms and techniques with a strong commercialisation focus, including a science commercialisation and innovation course covering intellectual property and taking discoveries to market.

Electives include animal biotechnology, genomics applications, good manufacturing practice and risk assessment, and academically strong students can take a year-long independent research project. Entry needs a bachelor's or honours degree in a related field such as genetics, biochemistry or molecular biology with a GPA equivalent to 5.0 on Adelaide's 7-point scale. It suits science graduates heading into research, product development or commercialisation roles in pharmaceuticals, healthcare, agriculture or biotech startups.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in a related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Business Administration (MBA)
description:
Adelaide University's MBA is a compact 36-unit program designed to run 1.5 years full-time, aimed at people who already have several years of management experience rather than a direct pathway from undergraduate study.

The core is 27 units including a capstone course, with 3 units set aside for an applied research component and 6 units of electives students can draw from any postgraduate coursework the university offers, which in practice lets students informally lean the degree toward finance, marketing, or entrepreneurship without committing to a named specialisation. A dedicated specialisation track (Human Resource Management is one option) restructures this into seven core courses plus three specialisation courses and two electives.

Intake runs three times a year (March, June, and August), unusually frequent for an MBA and suited to working professionals who can't always start in February. Graduates typically move into senior management, consulting, or start their own ventures, and the degree leans on case-study teaching and industry guest input rather than a purely lecture-based format.
curriculum:
Term 1 — Managing People and Organisations; Financial Management for Decision Making; Strategic Marketing; 1 elective.
Term 2 — Business Analytics; Managerial Economics; Operations and Supply Chain Management.
Term 3 — Leadership and Change; Corporate Strategy; Applied Business Research Project (part 1).
Term 4 — MBA Capstone: Integrative Business Strategy; Applied Business Research Project (part 2); 1 elective.
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus a minimum of 3 years' relevant professional work experience (or approved equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Master of Business Analytics
description:
A two-year master's (96 units) with February and July intakes. The core covers accounting concepts, principles of finance, business statistics, economic principles, predictive and visual analytics, chatbots and text analytics, and managing with big data. Discipline courses add analytics fundamentals, customer analytics, and two Business Analytics Projects in the final semester that act as the capstone.

Electives range across financial modelling, blockchain and smart contracts, fintech, people analytics, and advanced marketing analytics. A maths background is recommended but not required; entry is a bachelor's degree with a GPA around 4.5 on a 7-point scale and IELTS 6.5. Indicative international fee is around A$57,100 per year.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline (cognate discipline preferred)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Computer Science
description:
A two-year, 96-unit degree (66 core + 30 elective units) at Adelaide City Campus with February and July intakes, weighted heavily toward artificial intelligence and machine learning alongside cybersecurity.

The 30 elective units (five 6-unit courses) can be drawn from options including generative AI, applied AI and machine learning, deep learning applications, data in IT systems, requirements and user experience, and an ICT internship.

Provisionally accredited at the Professional level by the Australian Computer Society (ACS) and recognised internationally through the Seoul Accord. Adelaide University lists graduate career paths including computer scientist, AI specialist, defence scientist, IT manager, and systems programmer.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — ARTI5006 Ethics, Privacy and Security in AI and ML; COMP5004 Programming for AI and ML; INFO6004 Cloud Security; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — ARTI6003 Machine Learning Algorithms; COMP5050 Event Driven Computing (PG); COMP5800 Industry Research Project; PROJ5001 Project Management for IT Professionals (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — ARTI6000 Advanced Topics in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning; INFO6003 Security Architecture and Engineering; 2 electives (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — COMP6024 ICT Master Capstone Project 1; COMP6000 ICT Master Capstone Project 2; 2 electives (24 units).
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (AQF7) or bachelor honours (AQF8) in computer science, computer systems engineering, or software engineering (or a graduate diploma AQF8+ in computer science), with a GPA equivalent to 4.5/7.0.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with 6.0 minimum in each of reading, listening, speaking, writing.

name: Master of Cyber Security
description:
A two-year master's (96 units) in Adelaide University's Master of Information Technology family, which share a common first four courses so students can switch specialisation early. It is open to graduates without an IT background, starting from foundational IT before moving into security principles, networking, governance risk and compliance, cloud security, security architecture, enterprise security, cyber law and critical infrastructure protection.

Three work-integrated learning courses, including an industry research project and two capstones, give applied experience. Entry needs a bachelor's degree with a GPA equivalent to 4.5 on Adelaide's 7-point scale. It suits people moving into roles such as cybersecurity analyst, security consultant, IT auditor or compliance specialist, in a market with a well-documented skills shortage.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in a related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Data Science
description:
Adelaide University's Master of Data Science combines computer science, mathematics, and statistics with a significant capstone project (either research-based or industry-based) sitting alongside a flexible mix of core and elective courses that lets students lean toward machine learning, AI, or data engineering depending on background.

Unlike the more AI/cybersecurity-heavy Master of Computer Science, the Data Science degree keeps a stronger statistics and mathematics backbone throughout, useful for students coming from an analytics or actuarial background rather than straight software engineering. Electives can be drawn from programming, systems programming, algorithms, and distributed systems courses shared with the Computer Science program, so the two degrees overlap more than their names suggest.

Adelaide runs three intakes a year for this degree, in January, May, and September, which is unusual outside the standard February/July starts, and well suited to international students whose home academic calendars don't line up with the Australian one. Career paths include data scientist, data engineer, machine learning engineer, and business intelligence analyst.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Statistical Learning; Programming for Data Science; Data Management and Databases; 1 elective.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Machine Learning; Big Data Analytics; 2 electives.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Data Science Capstone Project (Research or Industry-based); 1 elective.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Advanced Topics in Data Science; 1 elective.
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a quantitative discipline (mathematics, statistics, computer science, engineering, or similar) with a GPA equivalent to 4.5/7.0.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Master of Education
description:
A two-year master's for people already working in education, not a route to initial teacher registration. It can be shortened to one to 1.5 years for applicants with a teaching qualification and experience.

Students choose one of ten focus areas, including education leadership and innovation, digital learning, early childhood, the brain and learning, TESOL, wellbeing and inclusion, First Nations cultures and perspectives, and a research stream with a two-part dissertation. Research methods coursework and a major project run through the degree. It is offered on campus or online (international students study mainly on campus). It suits teachers, school leaders, trainers and consultants wanting a specialisation or a research pathway.
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (AQF Level 7) or higher in any discipline; advanced standing available for education-specific backgrounds
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Engineering
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in a related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Environmental Policy and Management
description:
