A two-year master's (96 units) taught at the city campus with February and July intakes, with a coursework or research route in the second year. The core covers research design and methods and environmental planning and governance, with electives in sustainable cities, environmental economics, impact assessment and resource management.

Students complete a dissertation or research project on a real environmental problem. Entry needs a bachelor's degree with a GPA equivalent to 5.0 on Adelaide's 7-point scale. It suits people moving into environmental consulting, policy advice, sustainability management or conservation roles.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in a related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Finance
description:
A two-year master's (96 units) open to graduates from any background, with mathematics knowledge recommended. Year one covers accounting, finance principles, business statistics, economics, fixed-income securities, equity valuation and ethics; year two moves into derivatives, advanced investment management and financial statement analysis, with two industry projects and electives in areas like blockchain, fintech, behavioural finance and real estate investment.

Students use a Financial Lab with the simulated trading platforms used by banks and investment firms, and the curriculum is developed with industry. A graduate certificate or diploma exit is available. It suits people targeting specialist roles in finance, investment banking or corporate finance.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline (cognate discipline preferred)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Finance and Business Analytics
description:
A two-year master's (96 units: 30 core, 66 specialisation) that pairs finance, equity valuation, fixed income, derivatives and investment management, with analytics, predictive modelling, customer and text analytics, big data and AI tools.

Year two includes two capstones, a finance industry project and a business analytics project, done with industry input. Entry needs a bachelor's degree with a GPA equivalent to 4.5 on Adelaide's 7-point scale. It suits people targeting quantitative and data-heavy roles in banking, investment, risk analysis or consulting, where both financial judgement and analytics skills are expected.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline (cognate discipline preferred)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Financial Planning
description:
A two-year master's approved under the Financial Adviser Standards, so graduates meet the qualification requirement to give personal financial advice in Australia (a Professional Year and the ASIC adviser exam still follow separately).

Foundation courses in business statistics, economics, accounting and finance lead into advanced investment management, risk and insurance, estate planning, taxation law, superannuation strategy and the practice of delivering financial advice. Entry is a completed bachelor's degree with no specific prerequisites. It suits career changers and finance professionals moving specifically into financial planning and wealth advice.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline (cognate discipline preferred)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Human Resource Management
description:
A two-year master's (96 units) with a stackable structure allowing a graduate certificate or diploma exit. The curriculum covers strategic HR, talent acquisition and development, performance and rewards, people analytics, industrial relations, employment law and managing global workforces, alongside business foundations in accounting, marketing and negotiation.

An industry-based project runs through two courses, Applied Challenge and Integrated Learning, turning coursework into practice. Entry is a completed bachelor's degree in any field. It suits people moving into or up within HR, toward roles such as HR business partner, talent specialist, chief people officer or organisational consultant.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline (cognate discipline preferred)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of International Business
description:
A two-year master's (96 units) taught at the Adelaide city campus with February and July intakes. Foundation courses in marketing, accounting, management and entrepreneurship lead into international business strategy, managing multinational corporations, cross-cultural management and negotiation, and global business analysis.

Students complete an internship with a global business, NGO or government organisation, plus a two-semester industry research project. Entry is a completed bachelor's degree or graduate certificate in any field. It suits people aiming at leadership roles in multinational firms, international consulting or development work, or planning to run a business across borders.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline (cognate discipline preferred)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Marketing
description:
A two-year master's (96 units) with a stackable structure: students can exit after six months with a graduate certificate or after a year with a graduate diploma. Year one covers advertising, digital marketing, consumer behaviour, marketing analytics, and leadership and entrepreneurship; year two moves into brand management, global marketing and services marketing, ending with a capstone marketing research project done as work-integrated learning.

Advanced digital marketing and advanced marketing analytics sit in the core, reflecting where the field is heading. Entry is a completed bachelor's degree in any field. It suits people deepening an existing marketing career or moving into marketing from another discipline, with graduate roles such as brand manager, campaign manager, digital marketing specialist and marketing analyst.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline (cognate discipline preferred)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Professional Engineering
description:
A two-year master's (96 units) that is the accredited professional qualification for people who already hold an engineering bachelor's degree and want the credential recognised for practice. It is offered in discipline streams such as electrical, mechanical, and civil. Core courses cover professional engineering management, discipline-specific technical subjects, engineering data analytics, a design project, and a two-part masters research project, plus about 450 hours of industry placement.

Entry requires a four-year bachelor's or honours degree in a relevant engineering field and IELTS 6.5. Early exit points exist (graduate certificate at six months, graduate diploma at one year). The program holds provisional Engineers Australia accreditation with Washington Accord recognition expected after the first cohort graduates. Some courses run across the city and Mawson Lakes campuses.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in a related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Psychology
description:
Adelaide University's Master of Psychology (Clinical) is a highly competitive two-year master's accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council. It combines coursework, three placement courses totalling 24 units, and two research projects in the second year.

Graduates are eligible for general registration as a psychologist and can then complete a supervised registrar program for clinical endorsement. Entry requires an APAC-accredited four-year psychology honours sequence with an upper second class result or better, plus the Casper situational test, referee reports and an interview; selection weights the interview at 50 percent and Casper at 40 percent. It suits psychology graduates set on clinical practice in mental health assessment and evidence-based therapy.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 5.0/7.0; APAC-accredited psychology honours degree or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, no band below 7.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL), required for health/education placements

name: Master of Public Health
description:
Adelaide University's Master of Public Health runs three distinct end points on the same 96-unit, two-year frame: a Professional Practice pathway built around a 24-unit placement for people wanting applied, workplace-ready public health skills; a Dissertation pathway (60 core units, a 24-unit dissertation, and 12 electives) for students weighing a PhD later; and a Research Thesis pathway that swaps in a 48-unit thesis for those committed to a research career from the outset.

Core content covers epidemiology, biostatistics, health promotion, and communicable disease control. A Translational Health Sciences specialisation is delivered entirely online for students who want to keep working while they study, a genuinely different format from the on-campus-and-online Public Health specialisation.

Adelaide has a long track record in this field through its School of Public Health, building on established South Australian public health research in areas like Indigenous health and chronic disease epidemiology. Graduates go into state and federal health departments, NGOs, and international agencies, with the Professional Practice placement often functioning as an unofficial foot in the door at SA Health or a similar employer.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Epidemiology 1; Biostatistics for Public Health; Health Promotion: Principles and Practice; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Communicable Disease Control; Health Systems and Policy; Research Methods in Public Health; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2 (Professional Practice pathway) — Public Health Placement (24 units); Global Public Health; 2 electives.
Year 2 (Dissertation pathway) — Public Health Dissertation (24 units); 2 electives.
Year 2 (Research Thesis pathway) — Public Health Thesis (48 units).
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in any discipline (health-related background preferred but not required).
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Master of Social Work
description:
A two-year qualifying master's (96 units) that leads to eligibility for practice as a social worker. It includes up to 1,000 hours of supervised field placement across two practicum courses, typically 3 to 5 days a week including outside teaching weeks, so it is difficult to combine with heavy outside work.

Entry needs a bachelor's degree with at least one year full-time equivalent study in social and behavioural sciences, a GPA around 5.0 on a 7-point scale, and IELTS 7 across all bands. A criminal history check and Working with Children clearance are required within the first six months. One caveat: as of 2026 Adelaide University is working with the Australian Association of Social Workers on reaccreditation of the program for 2027, which applicants should confirm before enrolling.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 5.0/7.0; minimum one year full-time study in social/behavioural sciences
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, no band below 7.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL), required for health/education placements

name: Master of Teaching
description:
A two-year initial teacher education master's (96 units) that leads to eligibility for teacher registration. Adelaide University offers it in primary (Reception to Year 6) and secondary streams. The primary program includes 520 hours of supervised placement (about 60 days) across two professional experience courses.

It is accredited by the Teachers Registration Board of South Australia; recognition in other states and countries varies. Entry requires a bachelor's degree with a GPA around 5.0 on a 7-point scale, IELTS 7 across all bands, and a Working With Children Check, and students must pass the national LANTITE literacy and numeracy test before their final placement. Primary is taught mainly at the Magill campus, with Mount Gambier and Whyalla options.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 5.0/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, no band below 7.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL), required for health/education placements

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
At 240 credit points, ACU's Bachelor of Arts gives students room to build a genuine major (80cp in one discipline) plus a minor (40cp) or a second major, drawing from disciplines that range from history and philosophy to global studies and theology. Because ACU runs Arts alongside so many double-degree combinations (Arts/Laws, Arts/Commerce, Psychological Science/Arts), the standalone BA tends to attract students who want breadth rather than a professional accreditation attached to the degree itself.

One quirk worth knowing: students aren't restricted to units badged under "Arts." They can draw from units across ACU's Schedule of Unit Offerings, campus and prerequisites permitting, which in practice means a philosophy major can pick up business or education units as electives without switching degrees.

It's a degree that rewards students who already have a direction in mind (further study, teaching, writing, policy work) since it doesn't come with the built-in professional pathway of, say, nursing or paramedicine. The value is in the major chosen and what's built around it.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introductory units in chosen major (e.g. History, Philosophy, English, Global Studies), breadth electives
Year 2: 200-level major units (minimum 40cp at this level across the degree), elective units from other Arts disciplines or ACU schools
Year 3: 300-level major units, minor sequence or second major, capstone or research-based unit in the major discipline
Structure: 80cp major, 40cp minor (or second major), remaining credit points as electives
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Science (Honours)
description:
This is an 80-credit-point add-on year for students who've already completed a relevant bachelor's degree and hold at least a 5.0 GPA on ACU's seven-point scale, not a standalone four-year degree. The structure splits into coursework (including HLSC406 Research Methods in Biomedical and Health Sciences Research) and a research component worth either 20 or 40 credit points depending on the pathway chosen, with prerequisite units like SCIE403 or SCIE405 gating entry into the higher-research-weighted option.

The point of the year is to pair students with an academic supervisor and have them contribute to an actual area of research rather than complete another year of taught units, a deliberate bridge toward higher degree research (Masters by Research, PhD) for students who discover during their undergraduate degree that they want a research career in biomedical or health science rather than a purely clinical one.

Because it's a single honours year rather than a full degree, applicants are typically ACU biomedical science graduates staying on, though the pathway is open to graduates of equivalent degrees from other universities.
curriculum:
Coursework component: HLSC406 Research Methods in Biomedical and Health Sciences Research, plus discipline-specific advanced units
Research component: independent research project (20cp or 40cp depending on pathway) under academic supervision, culminating in a thesis
Prerequisites for higher-research pathway: completion of SCIE403 or SCIE405
Total: 80 credit points, combining coursework and supervised research
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 75 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Education (Primary and Secondary)
description:
Most initial teacher education degrees pick a lane, primary or secondary, but this ACU course runs 320 credit points to give graduates both: a broad primary teaching qualification plus one specialist secondary teaching area. It's a longer, more demanding structure, but it produces a graduate who can move between a Year 4 classroom and a Year 10 specialist subject, which matters in regional and outer-suburban schools where staffing flexibility counts.

The unit structure separates education theory (the EDES-coded units, including a mandatory unit on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander knowledges, histories and cultures) from discipline-specific curriculum and pedagogy units, and from the EDET-coded "effective teaching" sequence that runs across all four years, tying theory back to classroom practice each semester rather than leaving it until the practicum blocks.

Professional experience is substantial: a minimum of 80 days of supervised placement, plus a required 25 hours of direct service delivered through a dedicated social justice and community engagement unit (EDES206). Graduates come out eligible for provisional teacher registration and, given the primary-and-secondary combination, tend to have an easier time picking up early-career roles in schools that need coverage across both bands.
curriculum:
Year 1: EDES100 Understanding Learning and Teaching, EDES103 Understanding Learners and Their Contexts, EDES104 Digital Cultures and Capabilities, EDEN100 Foundations of Literacy, EDET100
Year 2: EDES105 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Knowledges, Histories and Cultures, EDMA291 Mathematics Curriculum Pedagogy and Assessment 2, EDSI290 Science Curriculum Pedagogy and Assessment, EDET200, first professional experience placements
Year 3: Secondary discipline studies units (100- and 300-level in chosen specialist area), EDES206 Social Justice and Community Engagement for Educators (25 hours), EDET300
Year 4: Advanced primary curriculum units, final secondary discipline units, EDET400/EDET401, capstone professional experience block
Total professional experience: minimum 80 days across the four years
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent (teaching registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sports Science
description:
The course is aligned to Exercise and Sports Science Australia (ESSA) standards for Accredited Exercise Scientist registration, and ACU has built in a checkpoint most competitor programs don't: a strengthened Exercise Assessment and Conditioning unit that functions as a secure, skills-based gate students must pass before they're allowed into practicum. It's there to make sure students can actually design and justify a safe, evidence-based exercise program before they're let loose on real clients.

Placement is a two-stage structure: Professional Experience 1 runs internally with heavy support, Professional Experience 2 is external, across a minimum of two placement sites and 140 total hours, 90 of which must be exercise testing, prescription and delivery specifically. The degree finishes with an Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE), the same kind of practical, station-based assessment used in medical and allied health training, which is a more rigorous capstone than many exercise science degrees use.

Depending on which electives students choose, graduates can also become eligible for Level 1 accreditation with the Australian Strength and Conditioning Association, giving the degree a foothold in both clinical exercise science and performance/strength coaching pathways.
curriculum:
Year 1: Human Anatomy, Exercise Physiology, Biomechanics, Functional Anatomy
Year 2: Exercise Assessment and Conditioning (checkpoint unit — secure skills-based assessment), Nutrition for Exercise and Sport, Motor Learning and Control
Year 3: Professional Experience 1 (internal, supported placement), Clinical Exercise Prescription, Strength and Conditioning electives (ASCA Level 1 pathway)
Year 4: Professional Experience 2 (external placement, across minimum two sites, 140 hours including 90 hours exercise testing/prescription/delivery), capstone Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE)
Accreditation: aligned to ESSA Exercise Scientist standards; ASCA Level 1 eligible depending on electives
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
ACU's IT degree is built around a deliberately broad first year (ITEC100 Information Technology in Action, ITEC105 Cybersecurity For Everyone, ITEC201 Fundamentals of Information Technology) before students specialise, and it lets students borrow electives from any other ACU bachelor degree, so a student leaning toward health informatics could pick up health science units, or one leaning toward fintech could add business units, without a formal double degree.

A required community engagement unit, BIPX202, puts a strengths-based service component into what's otherwise a fairly technical degree, which is a bit unusual for an IT program of this size: most comparable degrees leave community or service learning out entirely.

Minimum duration is three years full-time. It suits students who want breadth across programming, data management and cybersecurity fundamentals rather than committing early to one narrow specialisation, and who are open to picking up complementary units from business or health disciplines along the way.
curriculum:
Year 1: ITEC100 Information Technology in Action, ITEC105 Cybersecurity For Everyone, ITEC201 Fundamentals of Information Technology, BUSN113 Managing People and Organisations
Year 2: ITEC200 Data and Information Management, ITEC217 Programming Concepts, elective units (IT-specified or cross-degree), BIPX202 Community Engagement: Building Strengths and Capabilities (10cp)
Year 3: Advanced programming and systems units, capstone IT project unit, further electives from ITEC or other ACU degrees
Structure: foundation units, IT-specified units, and a flexible elective pool drawn from ITEC offerings or any ACU bachelor course
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
The single Bachelor of Laws at ACU runs to 320 credit points, longer than a typical arts or science degree, and includes a distinctive requirement: 80 hours of pro bono legal work after first year, which counts toward a compulsory community engagement unit. It's a practical touch that puts students in front of real legal need (community legal centres, tenancy advice services) well before they graduate.

Accreditation covers admission to legal practice in New South Wales, Queensland and Victoria, with recognition extending to other states and territories, so graduates aren't locked into one jurisdiction. Students with a strong first two years of law units (GPA 5.75 or above on ACU's seven-point scale) can apply to upgrade into the honours stream, which adds a research component on top of the standard core.

Because ACU offers this as both a standalone LLB and in combination with Arts, Business, Psychological Science and other degrees, the standalone version tends to suit students who already know law is the destination rather than one option among several. It moves faster into legal reasoning and doctrine without the breadth units a double degree would carry.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Law and Legal Research, Criminal Law, Contract Law A and B, Legal Institutions
Year 2: Torts, Property Law, Equity and Trusts, Constitutional Law, community engagement pro bono placement (80 hours)
Year 3: Corporations Law, Administrative Law, Evidence, Civil Procedure, elective law units
Year 4: Ethics and the Legal Profession, Advanced electives (e.g. family law, international law, intellectual property), capstone unit integrating practical legal skills
Honours pathway (GPA 5.75+): additional research-based unit sequence replacing part of the standard elective load
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 80 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Clinical hours are the headline number here: at least 800 hours of professional experience across five placements, spanning aged care, community nursing, high dependency, medical/surgical, mental health, paediatrics, palliative care and perioperative settings, a genuinely broad spread compared to nursing degrees that concentrate placements in one or two specialty areas. The placements escalate in length as students progress: a two-week block in first year, three weeks in second year, and a six-week placement in the final year, which mirrors the way clinical confidence and responsibility should build over time.

Structurally, ACU embeds an Integrating Practice unit every semester rather than treating theory and placement as separate phases. The idea is that clinical reasoning gets reinforced consistently rather than crammed before each placement block.

Graduates register with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia via Ahpra and can go straight into hospital, community or aged-care roles; the breadth of the placement settings also means graduates aren't narrowly specialised on day one, which some new-grad hospital programs value when rotating nurses through different wards in their first year.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, first Integrating Practice unit, two-week clinical placement
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology for Nurses, Integrating Practice units each semester, three-week clinical placement
Year 3: Aged Care and Palliative Care Nursing, Paediatric Nursing, Perioperative Nursing, Community and Primary Health Care Nursing, Integrating Practice units, six-week final clinical placement
Total: minimum 800 hours of professional experience across five clinical placements in varied healthcare settings
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 65-70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.5) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Paramedicine
description:
ACU's paramedicine degree runs across three years and puts students into ambulance and simulated-emergency settings early rather than saving clinical work for the final year. Five clinical practice units are spread through the course, adding up to a minimum of 360 hours in acute care environments, and before anyone can start placement with an Australian ambulance service they have to pass a medical and physical capacity test, a reminder that this is a physically demanding job, not just an academic one.

The teaching leans on scenario-based learning: simulated emergencies, standardised patients, and debriefs that force students to justify their clinical decisions rather than just execute a checklist. That matters because paramedic assessment is judgment under time pressure, often with incomplete information, and ACU builds units specifically around ethical and culturally informed decision-making alongside the clinical assessment skills.

Graduates register with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (Ahpra) once the Paramedicine Board opens registration pathways for a given cohort, and most go on to work for state ambulance services, though some move into event health, remote-area health, or defence force roles. It suits people who want a hands-on clinical career without the multi-year hospital-based training of nursing or medicine, but who are comfortable with shift work and unpredictable, sometimes confronting, callouts.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Paramedicine, Human Anatomy and Physiology, Foundations of Clinical Practice, Introduction to Pharmacology, first clinical practice unit
Year 1-2: Pathophysiology, Emergency Care Principles, Trauma and Medical Emergencies, second and third clinical practice units in acute care settings
Year 2: Mental Health and Complex Presentations, Paediatric and Obstetric Emergencies, Clinical Reasoning and Decision Making
Year 3: Critical Care Paramedicine, Multi-Casualty and Disaster Management, Professional Practice and Ethics, fourth and fifth clinical practice units (minimum 360 hours total)
Throughout: medical and physical capacity testing prior to ambulance service placement; capstone integration of clinical assessment and decision-making skills
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 75 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.5) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
This is the accreditation degree: ACU's Bachelor of Psychological Science carries APAC (Australian Psychology Accreditation Council) Level 1 accreditation, meaning it's the first rung of the standard psychology registration pathway. An honours year and postgraduate study still stand between graduates and registration as a psychologist, but this degree is the one that has to come first.

Core units run through foundations of psychology, applications of psychology and research design early on (PSYC100, PSYC101, PSYC110), building toward a distinctive third-year unit, Psychological Services Experience, where students log 25 hours of community engagement rather than sitting purely in lectures and labs. That's a deliberate attempt to get students into applied settings, such as schools and community organisations, before they've committed to a specific postgraduate specialisation.

Students who decide partway through that they want the faster honours-integrated route can look at ACU's separate Bachelor of Psychology (Honours), but the standard Psychological Science degree remains the more common entry point, especially for students combining it with Arts, Laws or Exercise and Sports Science as a double degree.
curriculum:
Year 1: PSYC100 Foundations of Psychology, PSYC101 Applications of Psychology, PSYC110 Research Design and Data Analysis 1, breadth electives
Year 2: Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Biological Bases of Behaviour, Research Design and Data Analysis 2
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology, Cognitive Psychology, PSYC108 Psychological Practice: Theory and Techniques, PSYC310 Psychological Services Experience (25 hours community engagement)
Accreditation: sequence accredited by APAC at Level 1 — honours and postgraduate study required for registration as a psychologist
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
ACU's MBA sits inside the Peter Faber Business School, which carries AACSB accreditation (held by roughly six per cent of business schools worldwide), and that accreditation now covers all of ACU's business courses. At 120 credit points, the structure is fairly standard for an MBA: a run of core units covering the major business functions (BUSN609 Business Communication, BUSN612 Managing Market Environments, MGMT641 Organisational Dynamics and Behaviour, ACCT600 Accounting for Decision Making) followed by four open electives students can pull from any discipline.

What differentiates it on paper is that every unit is explicitly mapped to the UN Sustainable Development Goals, and Microsoft certification is embedded into the coursework, so students walk away with credentialing beyond the degree itself, which matters for graduates going into roles where a vendor certification is a genuine hiring signal (data, cloud, analytics-adjacent management roles).

The four open electives are the real point of difference between one student's MBA and another's: someone heading into healthcare management, IT leadership or entrepreneurship can shape the back half of the degree quite differently while sharing the same core.
curriculum:
Core units: BUSN609 Business Communication for the 21st Century, BUSN612 Managing Market Environments, MGMT641 Organisational Dynamics and Behaviour, ACCT600 Accounting for Decision Making, plus additional core units in strategy, finance and marketing
Electives: four open elective units, selectable from any discipline across the university
Embedded: Microsoft certification pathways integrated into coursework; units mapped to UN Sustainable Development Goals
Total: 120 credit points, accredited under AACSB (Peter Faber Business School)
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline) typically with some professional work experience preferred (typical MBA entry bar, approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
At 160 credit points, ACU's Master of IT is pitched at graduates moving into tech from another field as much as at computing graduates deepening their expertise. The foundation units (ITEC610 Introduction to Data Science with Python, ITEC612 Modern Information Technology Infrastructure, ITEC617 Modern Database Management, ITEC619 Programming Fundamentals) assume no prior programming background, then the skills units branch into cyber security, machine learning and advanced programming for students to specialise.

It's accredited by the Australian Computer Society (ACS), which matters for the 485 graduate work visa pathway and for employers who specifically look for ACS-recognised qualifications, and it layers in Microsoft certification pathways across Power Platform, Azure Cloud and Azure Data Fundamentals, giving graduates vendor credentials alongside the degree itself.

The course description leans hard on cyber security, data science and AI as its core pitch, which places it more in the "modern generalist tech degree" category than a narrowly specialised master's: a reasonable choice for someone unsure yet whether they want to end up in security, data or software roles.
curriculum:
Foundation units: ITEC610 Introduction to Data Science with Python, ITEC612 Modern Information Technology Infrastructure, ITEC617 Modern Database Management, ITEC619 Programming Fundamentals
Skills units: ITEC621 Advanced Programming Principles, ITEC614 Cyber Security Concepts, ITEC613 Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, and further electives across business analytics and mobile/web development
Capstone: applied IT project or research unit integrating a chosen specialisation
Embedded: ACS accreditation; Microsoft certification pathways (Power Platform, Azure Cloud, Azure Data Fundamentals)
Total: 160 credit points
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in any discipline; relevant work experience considered
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Teaching (Secondary)
description:
At 160 credit points, this is ACU's graduate-entry route into secondary teaching for people who already hold a relevant bachelor's degree in their intended teaching discipline. The course structure separates Curriculum, Pedagogy and Assessment (CPA) units, built around the student's first and second teaching areas, from Education Studies and Effective Teaching units that cover the theory and generalist teaching skills, plus a Professional Practice strand that includes teacher-led research and the mandatory LANTITE literacy and numeracy testing.

Professional experience is a minimum of 60 days of teaching rounds, split into three blocks rather than one long placement, which gives students a chance to apply feedback from an earlier round before the next one starts. That's backed by school-based tutorials and workshops that run alongside the formal placement blocks.

It's designed for career-changers or graduates from non-education degrees, such as someone with a science, humanities or maths background who's decided teaching is the destination, rather than students moving straight from an undergraduate education degree, who'd typically already hold a four-year initial teacher education qualification.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Foundations of Teaching, first Curriculum, Pedagogy and Assessment (CPA) unit in first teaching area, Education Studies unit
Semester 2: Second teaching area CPA unit, Effective Teaching unit, first professional experience block (teaching rounds)
Semester 3: Advanced CPA units in both teaching areas, Professional Practice unit incorporating teacher-led research, second professional experience block
Semester 4: Capstone Effective Teaching unit, LANTITE completion, third and final professional experience block
Total professional experience: minimum 60 days of teaching rounds across three blocks
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in a relevant discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent (teaching registration requirement)

name: Associate Degree in Management
description:
This sits below AIB's postgraduate management suite as an undergraduate-level entry qualification, aimed at people early in a management career, or moving into a first supervisory role, who want a formal credential without committing to a full three-year bachelor's degree. It's a shorter, more compact award (typically two years full-time equivalent) built around the fundamentals of business operations, people management and workplace communication rather than the deeper strategic and research content of AIB's MBA suite.

Because AIB's whole model is built around working adults studying online, the Associate Degree follows the same delivery pattern as the rest of its portfolio: case-based assignments tied to the student's own workplace, flexible pacing, and no requirement to attend campus. Graduates can generally use it as a credit-bearing pathway into AIB's Bachelor of Business Administration if they decide to keep going.

It suits someone who's stepped into a team-leader or coordinator role without formal training and wants the underlying management theory (planning, budgeting basics, communication, workplace law) to catch up with the responsibility they already carry.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Management, Business Communication, Accounting Fundamentals, Workplace Relations
Year 2: Marketing Principles, Operations and Supply Chain Basics, Business Ethics and Law, Leading Teams
Structure: two-year, AQF Level 6 award; credit-bearing pathway into AIB's Bachelor of Business Administration
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; relevant work experience considered
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Business Administration
description:
AIB's undergraduate business degree gives students the same practitioner-oriented, workplace-connected teaching style as its MBA suite, but built from the ground up rather than assuming existing management experience. It runs across the standard business disciplines (accounting, marketing, management, economics, business law) over three years, with electives allowing some specialisation in the later stages.

Because AIB is best known for its postgraduate MBA and doctoral programs, the BBA functions partly as a feeder into that pipeline: graduates who want to keep progressing academically can move directly into AIB's Graduate Certificate/Graduate Diploma/MBA sequence, carrying the same online, case-based teaching approach through from undergraduate to postgraduate level.

It suits school leavers or early-career workers who want a business degree delivered in the flexible, online-first format AIB has built its reputation on, rather than a traditional campus experience, and who may already be planning to continue into postgraduate management study down the track.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Fundamentals, Principles of Marketing, Business Communication, Microeconomics
Year 2: Organisational Behaviour, Business Law, Management Accounting, Macroeconomics and the Business Environment
Year 3: Strategic Management, elective specialisation units, Business Ethics, capstone business project
Pathway: direct progression into AIB's Graduate Certificate in Management / MBA sequence available to graduates
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; relevant work experience considered
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Doctor of Business Administration
description:
AIB was the first private provider in Australia approved to award doctoral degrees in business-related fields, and its DBA reflects that positioning: an AQF Level 10 professional doctorate combining coursework with a substantial research thesis (50,000 to 80,000 words) that has to make an original contribution to knowledge in management or professional practice, not just apply existing theory. It typically takes a minimum of three years and up to six, with each candidate assigned a supervisory panel (a principal supervisor plus associate supervisor(s)) rather than working through the degree alone.

Unlike a traditional PhD, which AIB also offers, the DBA is explicitly framed around professional and management practice: candidates are usually senior managers, consultants or executives investigating a real problem from their own field (their industry, their organisation, their functional area) rather than pursuing a purely academic research question. That distinction, professional practice versus pure academic research, is the main line AIB draws between its DBA and PhD programs.

Graduates typically move into, or further embed themselves in, senior leadership, consulting or executive roles, or into academic and higher-education positions where a doctorate in business is a baseline requirement for teaching or supervising at that level.
curriculum:
Stage 1: advanced research methods coursework, business and management theory review
Stage 2: thesis proposal and confirmation, supervised by a principal and associate supervisor panel
Stage 3: independent research and thesis writing (50,000-80,000 words), presenting an original contribution to management or professional practice knowledge
Stage 4: thesis submission, examination, and oral defence
Duration: minimum 3 years, maximum 6 years
admission_requirements: Masters degree plus substantial senior management experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Doctor of Philosophy (Business)
description:
AIB's PhD sits alongside its DBA as the university's other doctoral offering, but where the DBA is explicitly a professional practice doctorate for senior managers and consultants investigating a workplace problem, the PhD follows the traditional academic model: an independent, supervised research project intended to generate new theoretical knowledge in a business, commerce or management-related discipline, typically aimed at candidates who want to move into academia or high-level research roles rather than stay in corporate management.

Like the DBA, candidates work with a supervisory panel (a principal supervisor and associate supervisor(s)) over a multi-year candidature, and the thesis has to represent a genuine, original contribution to the field rather than an applied practice project.

It's the right choice for someone whose interest is in the theory itself, testing a management framework or building new empirical evidence in a business discipline, rather than someone trying to solve a specific problem inside their own organisation, which is the more common motivation behind AIB's DBA candidates.
curriculum:
Stage 1: research methods and discipline literature review, development of a research proposal
Stage 2: proposal confirmation with supervisory panel (principal and associate supervisors)
Stage 3: independent research, data collection and analysis
Stage 4: thesis writing, submission and oral examination
Focus: original theoretical or empirical contribution to a business, commerce or management discipline
admission_requirements: Masters degree with a substantial research component
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Graduate Certificate in Management
description:
This is the entry tier of AIB's nested management qualification: four subjects, completed in as little as eight months studying one subject per term, that stand alone as a formal AQF Level 8 credential or feed directly into the Graduate Diploma and then the MBA without repeating coursework. It's the option AIB positions for managers who want a fast, low-commitment way to test postgraduate study, or who need a credential quickly for a role or promotion rather than the full MBA timeline.

The four subjects cover core business fundamentals (accounting for managers, economics for business, organisational behaviour and marketing management), taught in AIB's standard eight-week online terms with case-based, workplace-relevant assignments rather than traditional lectures.

Because the same four subjects form the first stage of the Graduate Diploma and MBA, nothing is wasted if a student who starts here decides to continue: it functions as a genuine "try before you commit" entry point into AIB's broader postgraduate business suite.
curriculum:
Subject 1: Accounting for Managers
Subject 2: Economics for Business
Subject 3: Organisational Behaviour
Subject 4: Marketing Management
Structure: four subjects at AQF Level 8, completable in as little as two 8-week terms studying two subjects concurrently; credits directly into AIB's Graduate Diploma in Management and Master of Business Administration
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in any discipline, or significant management experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Graduate Diploma in Management
description:
The Graduate Diploma is the middle tier of AIB's nested management qualification, sitting one level above a bachelor's degree at AQF Level 8, and it's built for people who already have management experience and want to formalise it rather than start postgraduate study from zero. Completing its eight core subjects (which double as the first eight subjects of the MBA) gives direct entry into the full Master of Business Administration if a student wants to keep going, so nothing done at this level is wasted if ambitions grow.

Subjects run in the same eight-week terms as AIB's MBA, entirely online, and cover the functional core of business management: accounting, marketing, strategy, HR, operations, without yet layering in a specialisation or capstone research project, both of which are reserved for the final MBA stage.

It's a common choice for managers who want the credibility of a postgraduate qualification for a promotion case but aren't yet ready to commit to (or pay for) the full MBA, with the option to upgrade later without repeating coursework.
curriculum:
Subjects 1-4 (Graduate Certificate component): accounting for managers, economics for business, organisational behaviour, marketing management
Subjects 5-8: strategic management, human resource management, operations management, business law and ethics
Completion: eight subjects at AQF Level 8; direct credit into AIB's Master of Business Administration for students continuing to the MBA
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in any discipline, or significant management experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
AIB built its name as Australia's largest online MBA provider, and the structure reflects that scale: twelve subjects total, delivered in eight-week terms with a built-in reflection week, so students can either double up and finish in twelve months or take one subject per term over two years. There's no residential requirement and no fixed intake calendar in the way a campus MBA works: the whole thing runs through AIB's own Student Learning Portal, with 24/7 access to material.

The degree is staged rather than all-or-nothing: the first four subjects constitute a Graduate Certificate in Management, the first eight a Graduate Diploma in Management, and all twelve the MBA. That means a student who has to step out partway still leaves with a recognised qualification rather than nothing. Lectures in the traditional sense are largely replaced by case studies, structured discussion and workplace-relevant assignments, on the logic that most MBA students are already working managers who need the coursework to connect directly to decisions they're making at work, not abstract theory.

Students who don't want to commit to one of the five available specialisations (Finance, Entrepreneurial Management, Marketing Management, Human Resource Management, or Logistics and Supply Chain Management) can take the generalist MBA, which finishes with a capstone project addressing a real business problem, often drawn from the student's own workplace.
curriculum:
Stage 1 – Graduate Certificate in Management (4 subjects): core units in accounting, economics, marketing and organisational behaviour
Stage 2 – Graduate Diploma in Management (adds 4 subjects): strategy, human resource management, operations management, business law
Stage 3 – MBA completion (adds 4 subjects): three electives plus a final capstone project applying learning to a real business problem
Delivery: 100% online, 8-week terms with a reflection week; completion in 12 months (accelerated) or 24 months (standard pace)
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline) typically required; relevant work experience preferred (approximate, typical private-provider MBA bar, not program-page-verified)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall (typical bar for postgrad at private AU providers, approximate)

name: Master of Business Administration (Entrepreneurial Management)
description:
This specialisation swaps the later-stage electives and capstone of AIB's standard MBA toward founding, scaling and managing a business rather than working within an existing corporate structure. It's a track aimed at students who already run a business, plan to start one, or work inside a family enterprise and want the strategic tools of an MBA applied to that context specifically.

The shared core (accounting, economics, organisational behaviour, strategy, operations, business law, marketing, corporate finance) is identical to every other AIB MBA specialisation, so students can generally decide on the entrepreneurial track partway through if their circumstances change (moving from employee to founder, for instance) without restarting.

The specialisation content leans into venture planning, growth strategy and innovation management, and the capstone project is commonly built directly around the student's own venture or a proposed one, which is a genuinely practical outcome compared to a hypothetical business plan exercise.
curriculum:
Core subjects (1-8): accounting for managers, economics for business, organisational behaviour, marketing management, strategic management, operations management, business law and ethics, corporate finance
Specialisation subjects (Entrepreneurial Management): venture planning and new business development, innovation and growth strategy, entrepreneurial finance
Capstone: business plan or growth strategy project, often built around the student's own venture
Delivery: 100% online, 8-week terms
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in any discipline, or significant management experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Business Administration (Finance)
description:
Of AIB's five MBA specialisations, Finance is the one most directly aimed at students planning a move into corporate finance, financial management or investment-adjacent roles rather than general management. The first eight subjects are the same core every AIB MBA candidate completes (accounting, economics, organisational behaviour, strategy, operations, business law, marketing and corporate finance) before specialisation units narrow into financial analysis, valuation and corporate financial strategy.

As with the rest of AIB's MBA cohort, the degree runs entirely online in eight-week terms, with the final capstone project typically built around a genuine finance-related business problem drawn from the student's own employer or industry, rather than a hypothetical case study.

It's a reasonable option for accountants, financial analysts or finance-adjacent managers who want the broader strategic and leadership grounding of an MBA rather than a narrower Master of Finance, while still coming out with specialised financial coursework on the transcript.
curriculum:
Core subjects (1-8): accounting for managers, economics for business, organisational behaviour, marketing management, strategic management, operations management, business law and ethics, corporate finance
Specialisation subjects (Finance): financial analysis and valuation, corporate financial strategy, investment and risk management
Capstone: applied finance-focused business project
Delivery: 100% online, 8-week terms
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in any discipline, or significant management experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Business Administration (Human Resource Management)
description:
This is AIB's generalist twelve-subject MBA with the elective slots and capstone project directed into human resource management, one of five specialisations the institute offers alongside Finance, Marketing Management, Entrepreneurial Management, and Logistics and Supply Chain Management. The first eight subjects match every other AIB MBA student's coursework (the core business fundamentals that also make up the nested Graduate Certificate and Graduate Diploma awards) before the specialisation subjects and capstone narrow the focus toward workforce planning, industrial relations, and organisational design.

Because the whole program runs in eight-week online terms with no fixed campus requirement, it's aimed squarely at working HR practitioners or generalist managers looking to move into a dedicated people-leadership track, using their own workplace as the case study for assignments rather than hypothetical scenarios.

The capstone project, completed at the end of the degree, is typically framed around a genuine HR or organisational challenge from the student's own employer, giving the final piece of work practical value beyond the grade attached to it.
curriculum:
Core subjects (1-8): accounting for managers, economics for business, organisational behaviour, marketing management, strategic management, operations management, business law and ethics, corporate finance
Specialisation subjects (HR): recruitment and workforce planning, employee relations and industrial law, organisational design and change management
Capstone: applied HR-focused business project, typically drawn from the student's own workplace
Delivery: 100% online, 8-week terms
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in any discipline, or significant management experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Business Administration (Logistics and Supply Chain Management)
description:
Same twelve-subject AIB MBA backbone as the other specialisation streams, with the final subjects and capstone steered toward logistics and supply chain management, one of the less commonly offered MBA specialisations in Australia, and a natural fit for AIB's working-professional student base given how much of the logistics and freight sector operates around shift work that doesn't suit campus-based study.

The first eight subjects are identical to every AIB MBA candidate's coursework (the shared core that also forms the Graduate Certificate and Graduate Diploma stages), which means students who started in a general management track can pivot into this specialisation later without losing credit for work already completed.

Specialisation content covers procurement, inventory and distribution strategy, and supply chain risk, culminating in a capstone project that AIB structures around a real operational problem, useful for students working in freight, retail distribution, manufacturing or import/export businesses who want the degree to double as a work output.
curriculum:
Core subjects (1-8): accounting for managers, economics for business, organisational behaviour, marketing management, strategic management, operations management, business law and ethics, corporate finance
Specialisation subjects (Logistics and Supply Chain): procurement and sourcing strategy, supply chain risk and resilience, distribution and inventory management
Capstone: applied supply chain or logistics project addressing a real operational problem
Delivery: 100% online, 8-week terms
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in any discipline, or significant management experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Management
description:
Distinct from the MBA suite, AIB's Master of Management is pitched at students earlier in their career progression: people who want postgraduate management credentials but don't yet have the years of managerial experience that AIB's MBA cohort typically brings, or who want a shorter, more focused qualification than the full twelve-subject MBA.

The coursework covers the same functional foundations that run through AIB's other management qualifications (organisational behaviour, strategy, marketing, operations) but without the specialisation tracks or the capstone research project that distinguish the MBA, making it a faster route to a postgraduate management qualification.

It suits graduates moving into their first management or team-leader roles who want formal training in management theory and practice earlier in their career, with the option to progress into the MBA later if their ambitions or experience level changes.
curriculum:
Term 1-2: Organisational Behaviour, Marketing Management, Accounting for Managers
Term 3-4: Strategic Management, Operations Management, Business Law and Ethics
Term 5-6: Leadership and Change Management, elective units, final applied management project
Delivery: 100% online, 8-week terms; no specialisation stream or capstone research thesis
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in any discipline, or significant management experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Music (Composition)
description:
The Composition stream at AIM runs on trimesters (AIM calls them study periods, three a year) rather than a conventional semester calendar, so students move through composition theory, arranging, orchestration, and soundtrack work at a different pace than a typical conservatorium degree.

Composition Module 1 opens the degree by setting out the compositional and production fundamentals the rest of the course builds on. From there, industry-focused units have students designing and producing a full musical work in collaboration with peers from AIM's performance and creative technology streams rather than composing in isolation. A mid-term proposal presentation and a formal delivery are both assessed. A dedicated self-management unit, unusual for a composition degree, addresses the practical realities of a freelance creative career: resilience, collaboration, and the business side most conservatoire training skips.

The degree closes with a Final Major Project in the last trimester: a portfolio of compositions, a recording, or a multimedia work, built under one-to-one supervision alongside masterclasses and guest lectures from working composers. Electives can be pulled from AIM's performance, production, management, media, and technology streams, letting a composition student pick up mixing skills or music business units rather than staying confined to a single track.
curriculum:
Study Period 1 — Composition Module 1; Music Theory and Aural Skills 1; Music History and Contextual Studies 1; 1 elective.
Study Period 2 — Composition Module 2; Arranging and Orchestration 1; Self-Management for Creative Practice; 1 elective.
Study Periods 3-4 — Composition Modules 3-4; Soundtrack and Media Composition; Collaborative Industry Project; electives.
Study Periods 5-6 — Advanced Composition; Portfolio Development; electives across performance, production, or business streams.
Final trimester — Final Major Project (composition portfolio, recording, or multimedia work); one-to-one supervision, masterclasses, guest lectures.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; portfolio/audition required
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Music (Creative Technology)
description:
Creative Technology is AIM's production and audio engineering major, and it runs on a genuinely different clock to the rest of the institute's degrees: domestic students can complete it in 6 study periods (2 years full-time), while international students on visa-compliant course loads take 9 study periods (3 years): the same content, different pacing rules.

Foundational units get hands-on fast: DAW navigation and editing for both musical and non-musical audio, MIDI editing, signal processing (EQ, compression), virtual instruments, and fundamental mixing sit in the early units rather than being saved for later specialisation. From there the degree moves into recording theory, sound design, mixing, and mastering, treating studio technology as a creative instrument in its own right rather than purely a technical support skill for other musicians.

Entry requires an interview and a portfolio of two contrasting pieces, and because the degree sits alongside AIM's Performance, Composition, and Music Theatre majors on the same campus, Creative Technology students frequently end up mixing, recording, or scoring work for students in those other streams as part of their coursework rather than only working on their own material.
curriculum:
Study Period 1 — Audio Fundamentals and Acoustics; DAW Techniques 1; Music Theory for Producers.
Study Period 2 — Recording Theory 1; MIDI and Virtual Instruments; Signal Processing (EQ and Compression); 1 elective.
Study Periods 3-4 — Sound Design; Mixing Techniques; Collaborative Production Project (with Performance/Composition students); electives.
Study Periods 5-6 (domestic final study periods) — Mastering; Advanced Production Portfolio; Final Major Project.
Study Periods 7-9 (international students only) — extended major project and elective sequence over the additional year.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; audition/portfolio required
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Music (Musicology)
description:
Musicology is AIM's non-performance major, built for students more interested in writing, researching, and critically engaging with music than performing it themselves, though a foundational level of practical musicianship is still expected. Coursework moves through music history and contextual studies, critical writing, and the theoretical and analytical skills used in scholarship, program notes, liner notes, and music journalism.

Because it sits inside the same trimester-based, industry-facing institution as AIM's performance majors, Musicology students study alongside performers, composers, and creative technology students rather than in an isolated academic track. Collaborative units draw them into critiquing and contextualising work being produced elsewhere in the building, a genuinely different experience to a musicology degree at a conventional university conservatorium.

Graduates go into music journalism, arts administration, artist management, music education, and further postgraduate research, with AIM's industry-facing culture giving Musicology graduates practical exposure to the music business that a purely academic musicology degree elsewhere often lacks.
curriculum:
Study Period 1 — Music History and Contextual Studies 1; Music Theory and Analysis 1; Introduction to Musicology; 1 elective.
Study Period 2 — Music History and Contextual Studies 2; Critical and Analytical Writing; 1 elective.
Study Periods 3-4 — Popular Music Studies; Music and Media; Research Methods; electives.
Study Periods 5-6 — Music Industry and Arts Management; Advanced Musicology Seminar; electives.
Final trimester — Musicology Capstone Project; portfolio of critical and analytical writing.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Music (Performance)
description:
Performance at AIM is built around weekly private lessons rather than group tuition as the spine of the degree. Performance Major units run as one-on-one instruction supported by a Performance Practice class of masterclasses, workshops, and seminars, so the individual teacher relationship, not a lecture theatre, is where most of the actual musical development happens.

Repertoire and technical demands escalate through the Performance Major sequence, but the degree also pushes students into collaboration outside their own instrument or voice, working with composition and Creative Technology students on new material rather than only performing established repertoire. Electives in entertainment management let performance students pick up the business side (booking, touring, artist management) without switching majors.

Entry requires a live audition or interview plus a portfolio of two live or recorded performances, a real filter reflecting AIM's position as an audition-based conservatoire rather than an open-entry university degree. AIM also runs a separate Classical strand of the Performance degree for students focused on that repertoire, distinct from the contemporary/commercial-leaning general Performance stream.
curriculum:
Study Period 1 — Performance Major 1 (weekly 1:1 lessons); Performance Practice 1; Music Theory and Aural Skills 1; 1 elective.
Study Period 2 — Performance Major 2; Performance Practice 2; Music History and Contextual Studies 1; 1 elective.
Study Periods 3-4 — Performance Major 3-4; Ensemble and Collaborative Performance (with Composition/Creative Technology students); electives.
Study Periods 5-6 — Performance Major 5-6; Advanced Performance Practice; entertainment management electives (optional).
Final trimester — Final Recital/Performance Project; portfolio and public performance assessment.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; audition required (two contrasting performance pieces)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Music Theatre
description:
Music Theatre at AIM trains across four disciplines at once: singing, dancing, acting, and creating, with one-on-one tuition in singing, dancing, and acting rather than folding those into shared group classes, an unusually resource-heavy structure for a music theatre degree.

Performance Skills units build the singing-actor specifically: students apply contemporary acting technique to vocal performance while deepening technical vocal work, rather than treating singing and acting as separate skills bolted together. Masterclasses, ensemble work, and live performance aren't extracurricular add-ons here; they're written directly into the coursework and assessed as part of it.

Delivery is face-to-face with some online components, typical for AIM's performance-based majors generally but worth noting for a discipline this practice-heavy: most of the actual training still happens in a studio or rehearsal room rather than online. Graduates head into professional music theatre, cabaret, and commercial theatre work, and the degree's dual training in singing and acting technique is built specifically for the audition demands of that industry.
curriculum:
Study Period 1 — Singing Technique 1 (1:1); Acting Technique 1 (1:1); Dance Technique 1; Performance Skills 1.
Study Period 2 — Singing Technique 2; Acting Technique 2; Dance Technique 2; Performance Skills 2; 1 elective.
Study Periods 3-4 — Singing-Actor Technique 3-4; Ensemble Music Theatre Workshop; Masterclass Series; electives.
Study Periods 5-6 — Advanced Performance Skills; Repertoire and Audition Preparation; electives.
Final trimester — Final Music Theatre Showcase (public performance); portfolio assessment.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; audition required (singing, acting, dance)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Diploma of Music
description:
AIM's Diploma of Music is built as a genuine on-ramp rather than a watered-down bachelor's. Students cover Music History and Contextual Studies, Theoretical and Practical Application, and a Major Study in their chosen creative practice, and strong performers can transfer into the Bachelor of Music partway through based on progress and results rather than needing to reapply from scratch.

Entry asks for a resume of musical study or practical experience rather than the live audition and recorded portfolio required for AIM's bachelor's degrees, making the Diploma a lower-barrier entry point for students who haven't built an audition-ready portfolio yet but can demonstrate genuine musical background.

It functions as both a standalone qualification for students wanting a shorter, practice-focused credential and a pathway credential for those building toward a full Bachelor of Music, and the option to shift between the two based on results gives students a low-stakes way to test whether the full degree is the right fit.
curriculum:
Study Period 1 — Music History and Contextual Studies 1; Music Theory 1; Major Study 1 (practical).
Study Period 2 — Music History and Contextual Studies 2; Music Theory 2; Major Study 2 (practical); 1 elective.
Study Period 3 — Applied Musicianship; Major Study 3 (practical); 1 elective.
Study Period 4 — Performance and Portfolio Assessment; Major Study 4 (practical); pathway review for Bachelor of Music transfer.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; audition required
english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.0) or equivalent

name: Graduate Diploma of Music
description:
AIM's Graduate Diploma of Music sits between the Master of Music and the undergraduate degrees: a shorter, more contained credential for graduates (in music or another field) wanting focused postgraduate-level training without committing to the full research-and-major-creative-project structure of the Master's.

Like the Master of Music, it runs across AIM's trimester calendar and draws on the same faculty of working composers, performers, and producers, but compresses the creative and research components into a single-year format rather than spreading them across a longer program. That's useful for career-changers or international graduates wanting a faster postgraduate qualification with an Australian credential attached.

It also functions as a bridge for students who complete a Graduate Certificate of Music and want to continue without committing immediately to the full Master's, or as a standalone finishing qualification for a specific creative or technical specialisation within music.
curriculum:
Study Period 1 — Advanced Creative Practice; Research Methods for Creative Practice; 1 elective.
Study Period 2 — Creative Project Development; Industry and Context subject; 1 elective.
Study Period 3 — Creative Project: Major Work; Presentation and Critique.
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in a related discipline, or equivalent audition/portfolio
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Music
description:
AIM's Master of Music treats the degree less as coursework to complete and more as a vehicle for one significant, self-directed creative project: a festival, an album, a body of new compositions, a business plan for reaching new markets. Roughly half the program is built around delivering that project against milestones the student sets and refines with supervisors, with a further block of research subjects designed to sharpen and justify the creative direction rather than sit apart from it.

That project-first structure suits musicians already working professionally who want a credential and a structured runway to test an idea (a touring musician developing a new show, a producer building a label, a composer assembling a portfolio for film and screen work) more than someone coming straight from undergraduate study with no practice of their own yet.

AIM runs three intakes a year (trimesters, or "study periods" in AIM's own terminology) rather than the standard two-semester calendar, letting students start closer to when they're ready rather than waiting out a February or July cycle. Delivered from AIM's Surry Hills campus in Sydney, with faculty drawn from working composers, producers, and performers rather than purely academic staff.
curriculum:
Study Period 1 — Creative Project Proposal and Methodology; Research Methods for Creative Practice; 1 elective.
Study Period 2 — Creative Project Development 1; Research subject aligned to project; 1 elective.
Study Period 3 — Creative Project Development 2; Industry and Context subject.
Study Period 4 (final) — Creative Project: Major Work; Research subject aligned to project; presentation and critique.
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in music or related field, plus audition/portfolio (approximate, typical bar, not program-page-verified)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall (typical for creative/performance postgrad programs, approximate)

name: Bachelor of Accounting
description:
ANU's Bachelor of Accounting is a 144-unit, three-year degree run through the College of Business and Economics and built to satisfy the education requirements of CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants ANZ directly. A student who completes the required accounting course sequence graduates with the academic side of professional accreditation already handled, rather than needing bridging study afterward.

What differentiates it from a generic accounting degree is the amount of room left over: only 14 CBE courses (84 units) are mandatory, leaving up to 60 units for courses from other ANU colleges. A student can, and often does, pick up a genuine second interest (a data science sequence, a language, or international relations units) inside what still reads on the transcript as a single-focus accounting degree.

The compulsory sequence runs from foundational processes through to accounting theory in third year, covering both the technical mechanics (company accounting, management accounting) and the more conceptual side that shows up in CPA exam preparation later. ANU's Canberra location also means a disproportionate number of graduates land roles auditing or advising Commonwealth government entities, alongside the usual Big Four graduate program pipeline.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Processes and Systems, Foundations of Finance, Principles of Economics, introductory electives
Year 2: Management Accounting, Company Accounting, Business Law, Business Information Systems, electives from other colleges
Year 3: Accounting Theory, Auditing and Assurance, advanced electives (finance, business information systems, corporate sustainability), remaining free electives
Minimum 14 CBE courses (84 units) required; up to 60 units may come from other ANU colleges; satisfies CPA Australia and CAANZ academic requirements
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 80 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Actuarial Studies
description:
ANU's actuarial degree exists because ANU holds Centre of Actuarial Excellence status from the US Society of Actuaries (a fairly small list of universities globally carry that designation), and the course sequence is built to satisfy accredited requirements from the Actuaries Institute directly, meaning graduates head into the professional exam process with the academic component largely done rather than facing years of additional exemption-chasing.

The practical quirk worth knowing: first-year mathematics isn't one-size-fits-all. Students can take the standard MATH1113 or split it into MATH1013/1014 (recommended for those less confident mathematically) or the more advanced MATH1115/1116 pairing. That's a level of built-in flexibility that reflects how varied students' high school maths backgrounds actually are coming in, rather than assuming a uniform starting point.

Many students pair it as a double degree with Finance or Accounting, since the actuarial profession increasingly overlaps with quantitative finance and risk roles beyond traditional insurance. ANU's proximity to APRA and Treasury in Canberra gives actuarial students a slightly different graduate destination mix than the Sydney-heavy insurance industry pipeline most Australian actuarial grads follow.
curriculum:
Year 1: Mathematics (MATH1113, or split as MATH1013/1014 or advanced MATH1115/1116 depending on background), Foundations of Finance, Principles of Economics, Statistics
Year 2: Probability and Statistical Models, Life Contingencies, Financial Mathematics, electives
Year 3: Actuarial Statistics, Actuarial modelling electives satisfying Actuaries Institute accreditation, transdisciplinary problem-solving course, remaining electives
Total: 144 units, 24 courses; common double-degree pairing with Finance or Accounting
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 90 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Advanced Computing (Honours)
description:
This is ANU's flagship computing degree for students who already know they want to go deep rather than broad: a four-year, 192-unit honours program accredited by the Australian Computer Society, built around choosing a specialisation and finishing with an honours research year that most Australian CS degrees don't offer at undergraduate level at all. It sits alongside the standard Bachelor of Advanced Computing without honours, and the honours track specifically targets students aiming at research careers or R&D-heavy industry roles.

The first two years are common to all students regardless of eventual specialisation, which is a deliberate design choice. ANU wants everyone solid on systems, algorithms, and software engineering fundamentals before they branch. From third year, students commit to a specialisation area and the honours thesis component means a real supervised research project, typically attached to one of the School of Computing's active research groups, rather than a capstone assignment marked against a rubric.
