Students frequently combine this degree in a Flexible Double Degree, pairing with Science, Economics, or Politics/Philosophy/Economics as the most common combinations, which stretches the timetable but lets a student, say, pair machine learning coursework with an economics major aimed at quantitative finance.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Computer Systems, Introduction to Programming, Data Structures and Algorithms, Discrete Mathematics, university electives
Year 2: Software Engineering, Computer Organisation and Program Execution, Databases, specialisation-track foundational courses
Year 3: Specialisation core courses, Professional Practice in Computing, electives
Year 4 (Honours): Honours thesis (individually supervised research project), advanced specialisation seminars, research methods coursework
Accredited by the Australian Computer Society
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 95 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
The ANU Bachelor of Arts is deliberately open-ended: 144 units with no compulsory course sitting inside the degree itself, just a requirement to complete one arts major and one arts minor from a list running past fifty options. That's unusually wide even by Group of Eight standards; students end up building a genuinely idiosyncratic combination, say a Linguistics major with an Ancient Greek minor, or Political Science paired with a Creative Writing minor, rather than following a fixed pathway.

Because ANU sits next to the National Library, the National Archives, Parliament House, and a cluster of foreign embassies, the Arts cohort has access to internships and research placements that a BA at a metro university in Sydney or Melbourne doesn't offer in the same concentration. Students doing History or Political Science majors frequently end up doing a placement in a federal department or an embassy cultural section during their degree.

Most people take it as part of a Flexible Double Degree rather than standalone, pairing Arts with Science, Law, or PPE is common enough that it shapes how the timetable is built. Students who take it standalone often use the flexibility to front-load electives outside arts entirely before settling into their major in second year.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introductory major and minor courses (typically two per semester in each area), electives
Year 2: Intermediate major courses, minor courses, electives from across ANU colleges
Year 3: Advanced (3000-level) major courses — minimum 18 units required at this level — capstone or research-methods course within the major where offered, minor completion, remaining electives
Structure requirement: one Arts major (48 units) and one Arts minor (24 units) minimum, maximum 60 units at 1000-level, 12 units of transdisciplinary problem-solving coursework
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 80 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
ANU runs its engineering degree on what it calls a systems engineering framework, and the practical effect is that nobody picks a major until third year. Every student, whether they'll end up in mechatronics or renewable energy systems, does the same first two years of common engineering coursework. The rationale is that modern engineering projects rarely stay inside one discipline's boundary, so ANU wants graduates who understand how electronics, mechanical systems, and software interact before they specialise.

Specialisation options run through electronics and communications, mechatronics, aerospace, renewable energy, and environmental or nuclear systems, a broader spread of energy-related options than most Australian engineering schools offer, which tracks with ANU's research strength in energy systems and its physical proximity to national energy policy bodies.

Engineers Australia accreditation requires 12 weeks of full-time work experience outside the university, and ANU treats this as a genuine placement requirement rather than a box-ticking exercise. Students often use it to test out a specialisation area (a stint with an energy utility, for instance) before committing to it formally in third year.
curriculum:
Years 1-2 (common to all students): Engineering Mechanics, Introduction to Programming for Engineers, Mathematics for Engineers, Engineering Design, Electrical Systems fundamentals, Thermodynamics
Year 3: Specialisation core courses (electronics and communications, mechatronics, aerospace, renewable energy, or environmental/nuclear systems), engineering electives (24 units), university electives (24 units)
Year 4: Advanced specialisation courses, capstone design project, Professional Practice work placement (12 weeks full-time, required for Engineers Australia accreditation)
Total: 192 units over four years, one Engineering major of 48 units required
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 90 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of International Relations
description:
The undergraduate version of ANU's international relations degree covers global politics, international political economy, security studies, and development through a 144-unit structure that leaves a genuinely large elective block (between 48 and 72 units) open for students to fill with whatever else interests them, from computing to history to marketing units, rather than locking IR students into a narrow disciplinary silo.

The theory-and-region combination is the degree's real identity: students work through the major schools of IR theory but also take region-specific courses, and given ANU's location within the College of Asia and the Pacific, those regional options skew toward Asia-Pacific affairs more heavily than an equivalent degree at a Sydney or Melbourne university would.

Students who want the professional edge often combine it as a Flexible Double Degree with Law, Arts, Social Sciences, Business, or Science: an IR/Law combination in particular is a common pathway toward international law, DFAT, or NGO policy roles, leveraging ANU's location next to Parliament House and most of Canberra's diplomatic missions for internships along the way.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Politics and International Relations, International Relations Theory, foundational electives (up to 60 units at 1000-level across the degree)
Year 2: International Political Economy, International Security, region-specific courses (Asia-Pacific focus), electives
Year 3: Advanced (3000-level) IR courses — minimum 18 units required — Aid and Development, transdisciplinary problem-solving course (12 units), remaining electives (48-72 units total across the degree)
Common combination: Flexible Double Degree with Law, Arts, or Science
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 85 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Laws (Honours)
description:
ANU's law degree is a four-year, 192-unit program and one of the few Australian law schools where the compulsory first-year sequence is taught with an explicit foundations-first structure: Foundations of Australian Law and Torts in semester one, Lawyers, Justice and Ethics and Contracts in semester two, each paired with two non-law electives so students aren't buried in law content immediately. That structure is a deliberate response to the fact ANU takes students straight from high school into a professional degree rather than as a graduate-entry JD.

The location does real work here. Being five minutes from the High Court, Federal Court, and Parliament House means moot court exercises, clerkships, and guest lecturers from sitting judges or government solicitors aren't occasional; they're baked into how the degree runs, and a noticeable share of graduates end up in Commonwealth government legal roles, the Attorney-General's Department, or federal judicial associate positions straight out of the degree.

The 4000-level requirement (48 units minimum) pushes students into genuinely advanced seminar-style courses in their final year rather than coasting on core units, and electives can range from international humanitarian law to Indigenous legal issues, reflecting research strength areas within ANU's law school specifically.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1: Foundations of Australian Law, Torts, two non-law electives
Year 1, Semester 2: Lawyers, Justice and Ethics, Contracts, two non-law electives
Year 2: Criminal Law, Administrative Law, Constitutional Law, Property Law
Year 3: Equity, Federal Constitutional Law, electives including international or comparative law options
Year 4: 4000-level advanced seminars (minimum 48 units across the degree), Legal Theory or Jurisprudence-type capstone, remaining electives
Maximum 60 units may be taken at 1000-level across the whole degree
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 95 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
ANU's Bachelor of Science is a straightforward 144-unit degree structured around choosing a major from the College of Science and Medicine's list (anything from Chemistry to Genetics to Mathematics to Marine Science) with the flexibility to pair a science major with a minor from almost anywhere in the university. Unlike some Australian BSc degrees that lock students into a faculty from day one, ANU's version keeps first year broad enough that switching majors after a semester or two doesn't usually cost a student time.

The practical draw for a lot of applicants is proximity to national research infrastructure that sits literally on campus or a short walk away: CSIRO facilities, the Mount Stromlo Observatory (for astronomy-leaning students), and Geoscience Australia connections that feed into earth science majors. Students in laboratory-heavy majors get access to research groups earlier than at some larger universities, partly because ANU's science cohort per major is smaller.

Honours is the expected next step for anyone aiming at postgraduate research, and ANU treats the fourth year as a genuine research year rather than a formality: a thesis supervised one-on-one, often feeding into a group's ongoing project rather than being a standalone exercise.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundational courses in chosen major (two subjects generally required in first year), mathematics or statistics service course where relevant, electives
Year 2: Intermediate major courses, laboratory or fieldwork components, minor or elective courses
Year 3: Advanced (3000-level) major courses, research methods course, capstone or project course in some majors
Optional Year 4: Honours — original research thesis under individual supervision plus coursework, required for direct entry to a PhD
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 85 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Science (Psychology)
description:
This is ANU's psychology degree structured through the science faculty rather than as a Bachelor of Psychology, which matters mostly for how first year is built: students do a genuine science foundation alongside the psychology sequence before specialising. Across the three years, ANU's Research School of Psychology teaches six core areas: developmental, social, personality, quantitative methods, cognition, and biological psychology, with the compulsory course list running from an introductory two-course sequence through advanced research methods and psychopathology in third year.

What separates this from a generic psych major is how seriously the methods content is taken. Quantitative Methods in Psychology and Advanced Research Methods are both compulsory, and ANU treats statistical literacy as core to the discipline rather than an optional add-on, which shows in how competitive the honours entry is afterward.

Students aiming at registration as a psychologist need the fourth-year honours program, which is genuinely selective (a strong GPA through the first three years is expected, not just a formality), and from there the standard pathway into a Masters or Doctorate in clinical, organisational, or forensic psychology. Students not planning to become registered psychologists still find the degree useful groundwork for HR, UX research, or policy roles given the heavy methods training.
curriculum:
Year 1: Psychology 1 (Understanding Mind, Brain and Behaviour), Psychology 2 (Understanding People in Context), science foundation courses, electives
Year 2: Social Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Biological Basis of Behaviour, Cognition
Year 3: Quantitative Methods in Psychology, Advanced Research Methods, Psychopathology Across the Lifespan, Personality Psychology, applied elective (health, organisational, or forensic psychology)
Optional Year 4 (Honours): supervised research thesis, advanced seminars — competitive entry, required for registration pathway
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 85 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Computing
description:
ANU built this Master of Computing for people who didn't start in computing: a lawyer, a biologist, an economist who wants to pivot into software or data work without redoing an undergraduate degree. Two years full-time gets a career-changer to a level where they're competitive for graduate roles at the big consultancies, government agencies, or tech firms that hire out of Canberra, and the Australian Computer Society accreditation matters if the plan is eventual professional registration.

The defining feature is the specialisation requirement: everyone picks one of seven tracks tied to an actual research group at the School of Computing, not a marketing label. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning draw on ANU's decently well-known ML theory group; Computer Systems and Computational Foundations lean toward people who want to understand how the machine actually works rather than just call libraries. Human Centred and Creative Computing is the odd one out and tends to attract students with a design or humanities background.

What sets the finish line apart from a lot of conversion masters is the capstone choice between an internship and TechLauncher, ANU's client-project unit where teams of students solve a real problem for an external organisation (a startup, a government department, sometimes a research group) over two semesters. It's messier than a typical group assignment and that's the point; students who've done it talk about client meetings going sideways as much as the code.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1: Introduction to Computer Systems, Introduction to Programming, Data Structures, one specialisation-track course
Year 1, Semester 2: Algorithms, Databases, Software Engineering, specialisation elective
Year 2, Semester 1: Specialisation core courses (two), one computing elective, one general elective
Year 2, Semester 2: Capstone — TechLauncher client project (two-semester, spans into final term) or Professional Practice Internship, remaining specialisation electives
Exit points: 48 units completed at credit average or better allows exit with Graduate Diploma of Computing; GPA above 6 allows transfer into Master of Computing (Advanced) with credit
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (or international equivalent) with a minimum GPA of 5.0/7.0, or a GPA of 4.0/7.0 plus 3 years full-time professional experience at ANZSCO Skill Level 1 in a related field.

name: Master of International Relations
description:
The Coral Bell School's Master of International Relations bills itself, not unreasonably, as the only IR program in Australia that combines mainstream IR theory with sustained regional focus on the Asia-Pacific. That's a distinction that matters if a student's actual interest is China-Australia relations, Pacific Islands security, or Southeast Asian political economy rather than a generic transatlantic-flavoured IR degree imported wholesale from a US or UK textbook tradition.

Structurally it's a 96-unit, two-year program: two foundational courses, two compulsory courses, four core courses, then eight units' worth of electives drawn from a wide list across the Bell School and the broader College of Asia and the Pacific. That elective breadth means two students can graduate with quite different transcripts: one weighted toward security studies, another toward international political economy or diplomacy.

The internship pipeline is the standout practical feature: competitive, credit-bearing placements with NGOs, Australian government departments, embassies, and the private sector, on top of ANU's usual proximity advantage of having DFAT, Defence, and most foreign missions within a short drive of campus.
curriculum:
Foundational courses (2): core IR theory and methods
Compulsory courses (2): required departmental units
Core courses (4): selected from IR-specific offerings covering security, political economy, and regional studies
Electives (8): drawn from Coral Bell School and College of Asia and Pacific offerings, including credit-bearing internship option (subject to competitive application)
Total: 96 units over two years full-time, part-time available
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree, minimum GPA 5.0/7.0 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Public Policy
description:
Crawford School rebuilt its Master of Public Policy in 2015 from a one-year program into a two-year, 16-course structure, a deliberate lengthening that reflects Crawford's argument that a serious policy degree needs more than a single accelerated year, especially for the specialisation tracks it now offers. It sits inside the College of Asia and the Pacific, so the program carries a heavier Asia-Pacific and development-economics flavour than an MPP from, say, a Melbourne or Sydney school built around domestic Australian policy.

Students choose between a general MPP or one of several named specialisations: Contemporary Regulation, Economic Policy, Social Research Methods, and Regulation: National and International Regimes among them. The Contemporary Regulation specialisation is a genuine point of difference: compulsory foundation courses in regulatory theory followed by electives that range into disruptive technology regulation, global business regulation, restorative justice, and climate and health policy, an unusually wide net for what's often a narrower regulation label elsewhere.

Since 2024 all Crawford graduate courses run with both in-person and online options, though live attendance at scheduled sessions is still expected. That's useful for the significant share of MPP students who are current or former public servants studying while working, including a steady contingent of students sponsored by governments across the Asia-Pacific region.
curriculum:
Pre-sessional components: quantitative and policy-analysis foundations before formal coursework begins
Year 1: Public Policy foundations, Microeconomics for Policy, Policy Analysis and Program Evaluation, specialisation foundation courses (if pursuing a named specialisation)
Year 2: Specialisation electives (Contemporary Regulation, Economic Policy, Social Research Methods, or International Regimes), capstone policy project, general electives
Total: 16 courses over two years; general MPP or named specialisation pathway available; in-person or online delivery with scheduled live sessions
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree GPA 4.0/7.0 plus 3 years relevant work experience, or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
Avondale's Bachelor of Arts covers more scientific ground than the name implies. Biological Science, Chemistry and Mathematics all sit as available majors alongside the humanities staples (English, History, Music, Communication, Religious Studies), a structural quirk that comes from Avondale folding its science majors into the BA rather than running them exclusively through the Bachelor of Science. Students pick an 8-unit major and can add a 4-unit minor from the same list, or take strands borrowed from Business or Ministry and Theology to build a more interdisciplinary profile.

The Communication major is the one with a defined career on-ramp built into the structure: it requires a professional internship in the final year, placing students with media, marketing, or communications employers rather than leaving that experience to chance. Chaplaincy is the other major with embedded work-integrated learning, reflecting Avondale's role training pastoral and chaplaincy staff for Adventist schools and hospitals across the region.
curriculum:
24 units, 144 credit points, three years full-time
Major (8 units) chosen from: Biological Science, Chaplaincy, Chemistry, Communication, English, Food & Nutrition, History, Mathematics, Music, Religious Studies, Visual Arts
Optional minor (4 units) from the same list, or a strand from Business or Ministry & Theology
Christian Studies core units
Communication major: Professional Internship unit in final year
Chaplaincy major: work-integrated learning embedded across CHPL-coded units
General elective units to complete the 24-unit total
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Arts/Bachelor of Teaching (Secondary)
description:
This is Avondale's combined arts/teaching degree for people who know from day one they want to teach secondary school. It runs longer than the standalone BA (the paired BSc/BTeaching runs 32 units over four years, and this Arts equivalent follows a similar extended structure) because it has to satisfy both a full arts major and NSW Education Standards Authority accreditation requirements for secondary teaching in that subject area.

Graduates come out with two teaching methods areas typically drawn from English, History, Music, or Religious Studies, which matters practically: secondary schools, and especially the Adventist school system Avondale feeds heavily into, hire teachers who can cover two subjects on a timetable, not one. Professional experience placements are substantial and staged across the degree, from early observation placements in first year building up to a full practicum block in final year, rather than concentrated into a single end-of-course prac.
curriculum:
Combined BA content major (8 units) plus a second teaching method area, drawn from English, History, Music, or Religious Studies
Education core: Educational Psychology, Curriculum and Pedagogy, Classroom Management, Assessment and Reporting
Professional experience placements staged from Year 1 observation through to a capstone full-time practicum block in final year
NSW Education Standards Authority (NESA)-accredited secondary teaching methods units
Christian Studies core units
Final-year Professional Studies seminar preparing for graduate teacher accreditation
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent (teaching registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The Bachelor of Business at Avondale is a 24-unit degree structured around double majors rather than a single specialisation. Most students pair accounting with a second area (marketing, HR, or business administration) or take a major-and-minor combination, and the accounting major itself carries accreditation from both CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants ANZ, which matters if the end goal is a CA or CPA designation later.

The smaller cohort size compared to a metropolitan business school shows up in practice: internship placements are built into the course rather than bolted on as an optional extra, and Avondale's business faculty draws on its Sydney campus location (Wahroonga) for placements with businesses and Adventist-affiliated organisations across Sydney's north. Christian Studies core units run alongside the standard business core, including accounting, economics, management, marketing, and law, reflecting the university's integration of faith and vocation rather than treating them as separate tracks.
curriculum:
Business core (Years 1–2): Financial Accounting, Economics, Marketing Principles, Business Law, Management, Business Statistics, Business Communication
Major 1 and Major 2 (or major + minor), selected from Accounting, Marketing, Human Resource Management, Business Administration, with an Entrepreneurship minor available
Christian Studies core units (compulsory across all Avondale undergraduate degrees)
Professional internship unit, undertaken within a major or minor field of study
Capstone: Strategic Management or equivalent integrative unit in final semester
Elective units to complete 144 credit points across 24 units
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Nursing is arguably the program Avondale is best known for outside its own denomination, largely because of the pipeline into Sydney Adventist Hospital ('the San') and other major health networks across the Hunter and Central Coast region. The course runs 24 units over six full-time semesters and builds in more clinical hours than the accreditation minimum: students log at least 800 hours of professional experience placement, starting from semester two once first-year prerequisites and pre-clinical checks (police check, vaccination status, National Police Certificate) are cleared.

What distinguishes the Avondale version from a standard metropolitan nursing degree is the deliberate inclusion of a whole-person model of care, a legacy of the university's Seventh-day Adventist health philosophy, which has produced a genuine research output in lifestyle medicine and preventive health (the same tradition behind the Blue Zones research on Adventist longevity in Loma Linda, California, that Avondale's own academics have contributed to). Clinical rotations cover acute medical/surgical wards, emergency and ICU exposure, maternal and child health, mental health, aged care and community settings, so graduates aren't narrowly trained into one specialty before they've even sat the registration exam.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy & Physiology I & II, Introduction to Professional Nursing, Psychology for Health Professionals
Year 1 Semester 2: first clinical placement block begins (subject to pre-clinical clearance)
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pathophysiology & Pharmacology, Research in Nursing Practice, extended clinical placements in acute and high-dependency settings
Year 3: Maternal & Child Health Nursing, Aged Care and Chronic Disease Management, Community and Primary Health Care Nursing, Emergency and Critical Care Nursing, capstone Transition to Professional Practice placement
Minimum 800 hours supervised clinical placement across acute, community, mental health and aged care settings
Registration pathway: eligible for AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse on graduation
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.5) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
The standalone Bachelor of Science at Avondale is smaller than its BA counterpart in terms of enrolments, since several of the science disciplines (Biological Science, Chemistry, Food & Nutrition, Mathematics) are also offered as majors within the Bachelor of Arts. Students choosing the BS specifically want the science degree title, often because it reads better for graduate entry into health science postgraduate courses, dietetics, or laboratory-based careers.

Food & Nutrition is worth flagging as a genuine point of difference: it draws on Avondale's Adventist health heritage (the same institutional lineage that produced Sanitarium and its Weet-Bix brand a century ago) and is taught with a research base in lifestyle and preventive health rather than as a generic nutrition science unit bolted onto a chemistry-heavy degree. Students combining it with Biological Science are well placed for further study in dietetics or public health.
curriculum:
Major (8 units) chosen from Biological Science, Chemistry, Food & Nutrition, or Mathematics
Core mathematics and science foundation units in Year 1
Second major or 4-unit minor from the same disciplines
Laboratory-based practical units across chemistry and biological science majors
Christian Studies core units
Research or research-methods unit in final year for students proceeding to honours or postgraduate study
24 units, 144 credit points, three years full-time
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Theology
description:
Avondale runs one of the only standalone Bachelor of Theology degrees in Australia housed within a Seventh-day Adventist institution, and the course reflects that heritage directly: alongside standard biblical studies and biblical languages (Greek and Hebrew feature prominently), students work through Adventist doctrinal history and the denomination's distinctive eschatology, taught by faculty attached to the Seminary at the Cooranbong campus.

Most students aren't just doing this for personal interest. A large share go on to ministerial credentialing within the Adventist Church across Australia and the Pacific, or use the degree as the entry point into postgraduate theological study (Avondale's own Master of Arts in Theology, or seminaries overseas). The course is unapologetically confessional rather than comparative-religion in orientation, which is worth knowing going in: this isn't a general religious studies degree, it's training within a specific tradition.
curriculum:
24 units, 144 credit points, six full-time semesters
Biblical Studies core: Old Testament Introduction, New Testament Introduction, Biblical Hermeneutics
Biblical languages: Greek I & II, Hebrew I & II
Systematic and Adventist Theology units, including denominational history and eschatology
Christian History and Church History units
Practical/Pastoral units: homiletics (preaching), pastoral care, mission and evangelism
Elective units and a research or ministry-placement capstone in final year
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Arts
description:
Avondale's Master of Arts is a coursework postgraduate degree that mirrors the BA's breadth into postgraduate territory, with a Theology and Religious Studies concentration being the most established pathway given the Seminary's presence on the Cooranbong campus. Students who did their undergraduate degree elsewhere and want to formalise theological study without committing to a full Master of Divinity often land here.

Because cohorts are small, the degree runs with a good deal of supervisory attention per student, and a research project or minor thesis component in the final stage of the degree is standard rather than optional. This isn't a pure coursework-only credential; it expects candidates to produce a piece of independent research under supervision by the end.
curriculum:
Coursework units in the chosen discipline (e.g. Theology, Religious Studies, English, History)
Research Methods unit (compulsory)
Advanced seminar units in the specialisation area
Minor thesis or research project, undertaken in the final stage under individual supervision
Elective units to complete the total credit point requirement for the degree
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in any discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Education
description:
Avondale's Master of Education is built for working teachers rather than career-changers. Every unit runs by distance, with a single Winter School each July drawing students back to the Lake Macquarie campus for a week of face-to-face intensives. That residential week matters more than it sounds: it's where the small cohort (Avondale's education postgrad numbers stay modest compared to the Group of Eight providers) actually meets in person, and where the program's Christian education strand gets taught alongside the research methodology core.

The degree suits teachers chasing a leadership track, a curriculum specialisation, or simply the credential bump for promotion within Adventist and independent school systems, where an Avondale postgrad carries particular weight. Because it's capped at eight units (48 credit points) and deliberately excludes a full-time pathway (Avondale is upfront that some units simply aren't offered often enough to support one), most candidates are two to three years into full-time teaching before they enrol, doing the degree one or two units a semester around a teaching load.
curriculum:
EDUC50000 Introduction to Educational Research (compulsory)
One compulsory unit in Christian Education (theological/philosophical foundations)
Specialisation stream: 4 units drawn from a single list (e.g. leadership, curriculum, literacy, or special/inclusive education) for a named specialisation, or
General stream: 4 elective units drawn across multiple specialisation lists for an unspecialised MEd
2 remaining units to complete the 8-unit, 48 credit-point total
Winter School residential (July, Lake Macquarie campus) attached to select units
No capstone thesis in the standard coursework pattern; research-intensive exit available via an extended project unit in some strands
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in education or a related field, or relevant teaching experience (approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Leadership and Management
description:
A 12-unit postgraduate degree aimed at people already in, or heading into, management roles who want the credential without leaving their job. It's delivered by distance with a mid-year residential intensive, which is the only time the cohort is physically together. One compulsory unit, LAMC50600 Theology, Theory and Practice of Leadership, signals the degree's actual orientation: it treats leadership as something with an ethical and, specifically, a Christian dimension, not just a set of management techniques lifted from a generic MBA-style curriculum.

Compared to Avondale's separate Master of Business Administration, this degree sits closer to organisational leadership than finance or strategy: it's a reasonable fit for people running teams in healthcare, education, ministry, or not-for-profit settings where Avondale's networks (particularly Adventist Church institutions across the Pacific) provide a natural graduate destination, though it isn't restricted to those sectors.
curriculum:
LAMC50600 Theology, Theory & Practice of Leadership (compulsory)
Core units in Organisational Behaviour, Strategic Management, and Human Resource Leadership
Research methods unit
Elective units selected from leadership specialisations (change management, conflict resolution, or health/education-sector leadership streams)
Mid-year residential intensive (on-campus attendance required for designated units)
12 units total, offered in two study patterns over a maximum candidature of 5 years
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in any discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Nursing (Coursework)
description:
This is Avondale's postgraduate nursing pathway for registered nurses who already hold a first degree and want to specialise rather than start over. At 11 units (72 credit points) it's a lean coursework masters, and it's built with defined exit points: a Graduate Certificate at 4 units, a Graduate Diploma at 8, so a nurse who needs to pause partway through still walks away with a recognised credential rather than nothing.

The two specialisation tracks on offer, Clinical Nursing/Clinical Teaching and Leadership and Management, split off after five shared core units, and the choice matters for career direction: one leads toward advanced clinical practice or clinical education roles (increasingly in demand as hospital-based clinical facilitator positions expand), the other toward nurse unit manager and health service leadership positions. Given Avondale's ties to Sydney Adventist Hospital, a number of students are already working within that network while completing the degree part-time.
curriculum:
Core units (5): Advanced Nursing Practice, Research Methods in Health, Health Policy and Systems, Evidence-Based Practice, Professional and Ethical Issues in Nursing
Specialisation A — Clinical Nursing/Clinical Teaching: 6 specialty units in advanced clinical assessment, clinical education and supervision, and specialty clinical practice
Specialisation B — Leadership and Management: 6 specialty units in health service management, leadership theory and practice, and organisational change in health settings
Exit points: Graduate Certificate in Nursing (4 units/24 CP), Graduate Diploma in Nursing (8 units/48 CP)
Full Master of Nursing: 11 units/72 credit points
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in nursing or related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.5) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Actuarial Science
description:
Bond is one of only seven universities in Australia accredited by the Actuaries Institute, and the only one in Queensland, so the Bachelor of Actuarial Science is built to carry students through Part I (Foundation) exemptions rather than leaving that accreditation work for after graduation. The degree runs across three years, with subjects sequenced into connected themes each trimester so probability, financial mathematics and statistical modelling build on each other rather than sitting as isolated units.

International students complete the program across the January and September intakes, giving two full semesters a year rather than Bond's usual three, while domestic students can use all three trimesters to finish faster. Class sizes stay small enough that lecturers know students by name, which matters in a discipline where a misunderstood assumption in one trimester tends to resurface as a mistake two subjects later. Graduates leave with a credential recognised by employers hiring for insurance, superannuation and financial risk roles across Australia.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Introduction to Probability and Statistics, Financial Mathematics, Microeconomics, Communication and Thought
Trimester 2: Life Contingencies I, Regression Modelling, Macroeconomics, Corporate Finance
Trimester 3: Life Contingencies II, Survival Models, Stochastic Processes, Business Law
Trimester 4: Actuarial Statistics, Investment and Asset Modelling, Financial Reporting, elective
Trimester 5: Actuarial Modelling and Simulation, Risk Theory, Actuarial Control Cycle, elective
Trimester 6: Capstone actuarial project, Professionalism and Ethics for Actuaries, discipline electives
Program maps to Part I (Foundation Program) exemptions with the Actuaries Institute on completion.
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent) with strong results in Mathematical Methods/Specialist Mathematics; Bond uses its own entry score rather than a strict ATAR cut-off, and considers alternative pathways (Diploma, Foundation Program).
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Actuarial Science (Honours)
description:
This is a two-semester honours program (80 credit points), taken after the Bachelor of Actuarial Science, not a standalone degree. Semester one covers Actuarial Control Cycle 1 and the first part of a research thesis; semester two covers Actuarial Control Cycle 2, statistical learning and regression models, and the second part of the thesis, which ends with a research seminar. Thesis topics are drawn from current developments in actuarial practice and financial services.

Completing it gives all university components of Part II of the Actuaries Institute's Actuary Program. Full Part II accreditation also requires two further subjects delivered online by the Actuaries Institute. Students who want the professional pathway generally take this honours year rather than stopping at the pass degree.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
Bond's Bachelor of Arts is a two-year degree (six semesters) built around majors rather than a fixed curriculum: students take three university core subjects, then either two majors with nine electives or three majors with three electives. More than 20 majors are grouped into communication (journalism, public relations, advertising, social media, corporate storytelling), creative arts (film and television, digital media, media studies), global studies and philosophy (international relations, sustainability, philosophy), and social sciences (psychology, criminology, counselling interventions).

Relevant public relations majors are accredited by the Public Relations Institute of Australia, and teaching is project-based with small classes. Because the structure is modular, students commonly use it to combine two fields that do not usually sit in one degree, or as a faster route into postgraduate study.

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Science
description:
Bond's Bachelor of Biomedical Science is a two-year accelerated degree, made possible by studying across all three of Bond's trimesters rather than the usual two-semester academic year, a genuine time saving for students planning to go on to medicine, physiotherapy or another postgraduate health program where a biomedical degree is the entry pathway rather than the destination.

Students choose between two majors partway through the degree. The Pre-Health/Professional major is aimed at students heading toward clinical postgraduate study, pairing a Health Communication subject with electives chosen from nutrition, exercise and sports science, psychology or health innovation. The Laboratory/Research major instead trains students in advanced bioscience laboratory technique and molecular diagnostics, culminating in a two-semester individual research project, closer to what a student heading into medical research or a PhD would want on transcript. Both majors share a common science core in the first year, so the choice doesn't have to be locked in on day one.

Core (Year 1): Human Anatomy, Human Physiology, Biochemistry, Cell Biology, Medical Microbiology, Introduction to Biostatistics
Major choice (80CP) — Pre-Health/Professional: Health Communication plus electives from nutrition, exercise and sports science, psychology, or health innovation
Major choice (80CP) — Laboratory/Research: Advanced Bioscience Laboratory Techniques, Molecular Diagnostics, a two-trimester Individual Research Project
Shared upper-level subjects: Pathophysiology, Pharmacology, Immunology
Capstone subject in final trimester tied to the chosen major
Completed across 3 trimesters/year — typically 2 years full-time
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent) with strong results in Chemistry and Biology; Bond applies its own admission score.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The Bachelor of Business is Bond's general-entry business degree, built around a single major chosen from Entrepreneurship and Innovation, International Business, Management, Marketing, Marketing Communication or Tourism Management, with the option to add a second major or minor if a student wants breadth instead of depth. Every major sits on top of Bond's common business core, so accounting, economics, statistics and business law are covered before students specialise.

What distinguishes the degree isn't the subject list so much as the delivery: Beyond Bond, a compulsory professional development program, runs alongside the academic curriculum from first trimester, and most students layer in a for-credit internship, study tour or study-abroad trimester somewhere in the degree's three-trimester-a-year calendar. Because Bond runs January, May and September intakes, a student can complete the degree in around two years of continuous study rather than the standard three, without giving up any core content.

Core: Accounting for Business Decisions, Economic Principles, Business Statistics, Business Law, Marketing Fundamentals, Management and Organisational Behaviour
Major (choose one, 60CP / 6 subjects): Entrepreneurship and Innovation, International Business, Management, Marketing, Marketing Communication, or Tourism Management
Optional second major or minor to broaden the degree
Beyond Bond professional development program (compulsory, embedded across all trimesters)
General electives, with options for a for-credit internship, study tour or study abroad trimester
Capstone business subject in the final trimester

First year covers legal foundations and Bond's core subjects. It suits students heading into compliance, contract management, procurement, HR, or founding a company, where legal literacy matters but a practising qualification does not.

name: Bachelor of Climate Change and Sustainable Action
description:
This is deliberately not a climate science degree. It is a two-year non-science degree (six semesters, trimester intakes in January, May, and September) that approaches climate and sustainability through communication, media, psychology, health, law, and business. The structure is a core curriculum, a broad interdisciplinary foundation, a student-chosen major, and an electives and capstone block.

The final semester can be a capstone project or an internship applying the degree to a real sustainability problem, with some fieldwork such as environmental assessments. Graduates move into sustainability management, climate consulting, environmental policy, corporate governance and communications, and infrastructure planning. Students who want the science side (emissions modelling, ecology, engineering) should look at a science or engineering degree instead.

name: Bachelor of Clinical Exercise Physiology
description:
Bond added this degree to replace its Bachelor of Exercise and Sports Science, which stops taking students from January 2027. It runs over seven semesters (two years and four months) and moves from foundational exercise science into clinical practice, covering anatomy, pathophysiology, exercise prescription, behaviour change, biomechanics, and digital health.

Students complete at least 500 hours of supervised clinical placement across rehabilitation, sport, private practice, and community health, weighted toward the final year (roughly 70, 70, 180, and 180 hours across semesters three, four, six, and seven). One caveat for prospective students: as of 2026 the program is not yet accredited by Exercise and Sports Science Australia. Bond has applied and expects a decision in late 2026, aiming for provisional accreditation before the first cohort graduates. Accreditation is what allows graduates to register as Accredited Exercise Physiologists, so applicants should confirm its status before enrolling.
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent) with strong results in science subjects (Chemistry/Biology where relevant); Bond applies its own admission score, and some programs require an interview or additional selection criteria.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
Bond runs the Bachelor of Commerce over two years (six semesters) on its three-semesters-a-year calendar, so students finish a year sooner than a standard Australian three-year degree. First year is largely fixed: accounting principles, management accounting, principles of economics, fundamentals of finance, and a responsible-organisations subject, alongside one of Bond's cross-disciplinary core subjects. In second year students take one major from Accounting, Actuarial Science, Data Analytics, Economics, or Finance, with room for a second major or a minor.

The degree is accredited by CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, and the business school holds AACSB and EQUIS accreditation. Finance students work in the Bond FinTech Hub, which has 40 Bloomberg terminals and offers Bloomberg certification. A supervised business internship is available as an elective, and a semester on exchange can replace electives.

name: Bachelor of Communication
description:
Bond's Bachelor of Communication pairs a shared communication and media core with one of ten specialist areas: Advertising, Communication and Society, Corporate Storytelling, Creative Writing, Digital Media, Film and Television, Journalism, Media Studies, Public Relations, or Social Media. Students choose either a full major (six subjects in one area) or a minor (four subjects) topped up with two general electives, which makes it straightforward to pair, say, a Journalism major with a Digital Media minor, or to leave room for subjects outside the faculty entirely.

The degree leans hard on applied skills: strategic communication, persuasive writing, content creation for online platforms, podcasting, and intercultural communication all appear alongside the theory subjects. The Faculty of Society & Design's industry partnerships mean a for-credit internship is a realistic option for most students rather than a rare exception. Combined with Bond's three-trimester calendar, the degree is typically finished in around two years of continuous study.

On top of the marketing major, students can add a communication major or minor in advertising, public relations, journalism, film and television, digital media, social media, corporate storytelling, or creative writing. Relevant public relations majors are accredited by the Public Relations Institute of Australia. The degree suits students who want marketing as a career base with communication production skills alongside it.

name: Bachelor of Construction Management and Quantity Surveying
description:
A two-year accelerated degree (six semesters) covering construction technology, site management, contract administration, building measurement, tendering and finance, project delivery systems, and risk management. First year pairs introductory construction subjects with Bond's core subjects; second year works through the professional subjects and ends with an industry-based capstone project.

The degree carries a strong set of accreditations: the Australian Institute of Quantity Surveyors, the Chartered Institute of Building, and the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors, and it meets the education requirement for a Queensland Open Builders Licence. Teaching includes industry guest involvement and practical assessments modelled on workplace tasks, and students work in Bond's 6 Star Green Star Sustainable Development Building. It is a direct route into quantity surveying, contract administration, or site and project management.

name: Bachelor of Creative Arts
description:

Creative majors include advertising, corporate storytelling, digital media, film and television, journalism, media studies, public relations, and social media, all built on a creative writing foundation in first year alongside Bond's core subjects. Second year adds three open electives and a capstone, which is a sustained individual or small-team creative project made for the student's portfolio.

Students have access to one of the larger video production facilities in south-east Queensland, with editing stations and audio suites. The degree suits students who want to graduate with a body of produced work across two complementary fields rather than a single disciplinary track.

name: Bachelor of Criminal Justice and Criminology
description:
This two-year degree (24 subjects, six semesters) starts with criminology and legal foundations plus Bond's core subjects, then moves into applied areas: criminal investigation, cybercrime, youth justice, child protection, victimology, and crime prevention. Students choose one of three second-year pathways, adding a psychology specialisation, a law specialisation, or a broader set of electives.

Several subjects are taught by former practitioners, including an ex-Detective Inspector and researchers in police legitimacy. Internship placements are available for academic credit, and Bond's Transformer and Beyond Bond programs give students real projects with outside organisations. The degree suits students aiming at policing, corrections, intelligence, policy, or community justice roles, or planning to continue into postgraduate law or psychology.

name: Bachelor of Data Analytics
description:
This two-year degree (six semesters) is quantitative from the start. First year covers introductory data science, mathematical statistics, quantitative methods, statistical learning, regression, and applied econometrics; second year adds modern machine learning, deep learning with neural networks, and an applied data analytics project. R and Python are taught throughout, in the Bond FinTech Hub and Centre for Data Analytics, and Bloomberg certification is available.

description:

Like the Bachelor of Business Law, it is for students who want legal knowledge without the professional practice requirements, and it is not the pathway to admission as a lawyer, which is the Bachelor of Laws.

All students take legal foundations and Bond's four core subjects, then build the rest of the degree from law electives plus subjects in areas such as international relations, criminology, languages, communication, and humanities. The result is a customised law-plus-something degree aimed at careers in policy, journalism, government, advocacy, and business where legal reasoning is useful but a practising certificate is not needed.

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
Bond's Faculty of Law caps annual admission at around 180 students specifically to keep classes small, and the Bachelor of Laws uses that scale to run a genuinely accelerated model: eight semesters across Bond's three-trimester calendar, finishing in two years and eight months rather than the three or four years an LLB takes at a standard two-semester university. Students complete 170 credit points across 32 subjects: 17 compulsory law subjects, seven law electives, three university core subjects and five general electives.

The teaching emphasis sits on practice as much as doctrine: legal research and reasoning, legal writing and drafting, oral advocacy, negotiation and dispute resolution, and legal ethics are built into the compulsory sequence rather than left to a single skills subject. Because trimesters run back-to-back with short breaks, students moving straight through need to plan around a genuinely continuous academic year, which suits those wanting to qualify and move into practice or further study as quickly as possible.
curriculum:
Compulsory law subjects (17): Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Constitutional Law, Property Law, Equity and Trusts, Administrative Law, Corporations Law, Evidence, Civil Procedure, Legal Ethics and Professional Responsibility, and others across the sequence
Law electives (7 subjects): drawn from areas such as intellectual property, international law, family law, competition law and litigation practice
University core subjects (3): communication, thinking and analysis subjects taken by all Bond undergraduates
General electives (5): open to any faculty, used to add breadth or a minor
Integrated legal skills strand: legal research and writing, oral advocacy, negotiation and dispute resolution embedded across compulsory subjects
Total: 170 credit points / 32 subjects across 8 trimesters (2 years 8 months full-time)

The degree is aimed at students heading into the public service, government, policy institutes, think tanks, and not-for-profits, where the ability to reason across law, economics, and ethics matters more than depth in any one.

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
The Bachelor of Psychological Science is accredited with conditions by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council and approved by the Psychology Board of Australia, and it's built to count as the first three years of the standard six-year pathway to registration as a psychologist. Bond's three-trimester calendar means students can finish the bachelor's component in two years rather than the usual three, and the full run through to a fourth (honours) year and into a master's-level registration pathway can be completed in four years and eight months.

The subject list covers the breadth APAC requires: biological psychology, cognitive psychology, social psychology, personality and learning, developmental psychology, psychopathology, and cross-cultural psychology all appear across the degree rather than being compressed into one or two survey subjects. Graduates who complete the honours year become eligible to apply for provisional registration with AHPRA and move on to a master's program. The degree is explicitly built as a stepping stone rather than a terminal qualification for most students who take it.

Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Psychology, Research Methods and Statistics I, Developmental Psychology
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Social Psychology, Personality, Learning and Behaviour, Research Methods and Statistics II
Upper level: Psychopathology, Motivation and Emotion, Cross-Cultural Psychology, Health Psychology
Final trimester: Applied research project and electives
APAC-accredited (with conditions), PsyBA-approved; equivalent to years 1–3 of the 6-year registration pathway
Optional progression: Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours), then master's-level registration program

description:
Bond's Doctor of Physiotherapy is accredited as an entry-level program by the Australian Physiotherapy Council and approved by the Physiotherapy Board of Australia, and it's built around problem- and case-based learning rather than a lecture-heavy model: each teaching block centres on clinical cases students work through in small groups, mirroring how physiotherapists actually reason through a patient in front of them.

The degree includes up to 1,400 hours of clinical placement, spread across genuinely different settings: acute care such as cardiorespiratory and orthopaedic wards, inpatient and outpatient rehabilitation, musculoskeletal outpatient clinics, and, depending on availability and student interest, paediatrics, women's and men's health, elite sports, and rural, remote or international placements. Bond also runs an on-campus community physiotherapy clinic, so some placement hours happen without students leaving the Gold Coast campus. The final semester is built around a clinical internship placement specifically designed to push students beyond the caseload variety they've already encountered, ahead of entering the profession.

Foundational trimesters: Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy, Cardiorespiratory Physiotherapy, Neurological Physiotherapy, Clinical Reasoning and Case-Based Learning
Clinical placement blocks (up to 1,400 hours total) across acute care, inpatient/outpatient rehabilitation, and musculoskeletal outpatient settings
Elective clinical placements (availability-dependent): paediatrics, women's/men's health, elite sports, rural, remote or international placement
On-campus community physiotherapy clinic placement
Final semester: clinical internship placement extending beyond core clinical experiences
Program accredited by the Australian Physiotherapy Council; approved by the Physiotherapy Board of Australia

name: Juris Doctor
description:
The Juris Doctor is Bond's graduate-entry law degree for students who already hold an undergraduate qualification in any discipline and want to qualify for legal practice without repeating an LLB. The program is built on 240 credit points, and most students take four subjects a trimester, which at Bond's three-trimester pace typically brings the degree in at around two years rather than the three years a JD usually takes elsewhere.

Students complete a compulsory core of foundational law subjects, including constitutional law, contracts and criminal law, then select 70 credit points of electives, with the option to complete a formal Law Specialisation by taking at least four electives (40 credit points) within one subject area. Practical legal skills are woven through the degree rather than taught separately: legal writing, oral communication, negotiation, dispute resolution and professional ethics all sit inside the JD's integrated skills and professionalism strand. Graduates who also want to complete practical training requirements can continue directly into Bond's Graduate Diploma in Legal Practice, meaning the whole path to admission as a legal practitioner can be finished at the one university.
curriculum:
Core subjects: Constitutional Law, Contract Law, Criminal Law and Procedure, Torts, Property Law, Equity, Administrative Law, Corporations Law, Evidence, Civil Dispute Resolution
Electives (70CP): drawn broadly across commercial, criminal, international and public law subjects
Optional Law Specialisation: minimum 4 electives (40CP) concentrated in one recognised specialisation area
Integrated skills and professionalism program: legal writing and reasoning, oral advocacy, negotiation, dispute resolution, professional ethics, embedded across trimesters
Total: 240 credit points, typically 4 subjects per trimester
Optional progression: Graduate Diploma in Legal Practice (GDLP) for practical training requirements toward admission
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in any discipline (does not need to be in law) with a competitive GPA.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, with no band below 6.5.

name: Juris Doctor Online
description:
A fully online version of Bond's graduate law degree, 24 subjects completable in two years, for graduates of any discipline who want to qualify as a lawyer while working. Teaching is delivered through weekly live seminars plus recorded material and an AI tutor, with year one covering the foundational law subjects and electives and year two finishing the prescribed curriculum and a 15-day legal work experience placement.

That placement can count toward the workplace experience component of the Graduate Diploma in Legal Practice, which students typically take alongside or after the JD to complete the practical training required for admission. Applicants should confirm current entry requirements and, importantly, how the online JD is treated by the admitting authority in the state where they intend to practise, since admission rules are set by each jurisdiction.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in any discipline (does not need to be in law) with a competitive GPA.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, with no band below 6.5 (or equivalent).

name: Master of Accounting
description:
A 16-month conversion master's (four semesters, 13 subjects) for graduates without an accounting background who want a professional accounting qualification. The sequence runs from accounting principles, economics, and finance through management accounting, financial accounting and company reporting, business law, taxation, auditing, and data analytics for accountants.

It is accredited by both CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, so it satisfies the academic requirement for those professional programs. Students with a cognate undergraduate degree can receive up to 40 credit points of advanced standing, shortening the degree. Accredited by AACSB and EQUIS.

name: Master of Actuarial Practice
description:
The longer of Bond's two actuarial master's degrees, six semesters (two years) at three subjects a semester, built for students without a related undergraduate background. The first four semesters mirror the Master of Actuarial Science content, from financial mathematics and mathematical statistics through stochastic processes, corporate finance and asset-liability modelling; the final two semesters add the Actuarial Control Cycle, data analytics and an actuarial research essay.

It is accredited by the Actuaries Institute and covers all university components of both Part I (Foundation Program) and Part II (Actuary Program), which is the main reason to choose it over the shorter Actuarial Science degree. Teaching uses the Bond FinTech Hub and a Bloomberg certification pathway. It suits people who enjoy mathematics and want the fullest set of professional exemptions from a single coursework degree, heading toward insurance, superannuation, risk or actuarial consulting.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in a related discipline (or equivalent) with a competitive GPA; some programs consider relevant professional experience in place of a directly related degree.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Actuarial Science
description:
A four-semester master's (about 16 months) of twelve subjects, and the only actuarial program offered in Queensland. The sequence runs from financial mathematics, accounting principles and business economics through mathematical statistics, linear models and applied econometrics, then survival analysis, stochastic processes and corporate finance, finishing with stochastic asset-liability modelling and the valuation of financial derivatives.

It is accredited by the Actuaries Institute and covers all university components of the Part I Foundation Program, so graduates leave with exemptions toward professional qualification. Students with a cognate undergraduate degree can receive up to 30 credit points of advanced standing. Teaching draws on the Bond FinTech Hub and a Bloomberg certification pathway. The degree is aimed at numerate graduates from other fields who want to move into actuarial, risk or investment analysis work; anyone wanting Part II coverage as well should look at the longer Master of Actuarial Practice.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in a related discipline (or equivalent) with a competitive GPA; some programs consider relevant professional experience in place of a directly related degree.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

It covers the same accredited core, from financial mathematics, mathematical statistics and linear models through survival analysis, stochastic processes, corporate finance and asset-liability modelling, and adds further depth and elective specialisation on top.

Like the standard version it is accredited by the Actuaries Institute and covers the university components of the Part I Foundation Program, and it is the only actuarial program offered in Queensland. Teaching uses the Bond FinTech Hub and a Bloomberg certification pathway. It suits numerate graduates who want more coverage and a specialisation than the shorter Actuarial Science degree provides, without going all the way to the Master of Actuarial Practice.

The professional qualification in Bond's architecture pathway, about 16 months (four semesters) of project-based design studios ending in a master's thesis studio. Entry requires a prior degree in design or architecture, usually Bond's Bachelor of Design in Architecture or an equivalent.

name: Master of Arts (Coursework)
description:
A one-year master's (three semesters, January, May and September intakes) that lets students combine study across criminology, international relations, communication, public relations and advertising rather than staying in one discipline.

The first semester includes a research and data subject, and every student completes an independent research project, choosing either a major research project of 40 credit points with fewer electives or a shorter 10-credit project plus three electives. The research is set by the student around their own interests. It suits professionals and career changers who want a flexible postgraduate humanities qualification with a real research component, including as preparation for a PhD.

name: Master of Arts (TESOL)
description:
A three-semester master's (twelve subjects, intakes in January, May and September) in teaching English to speakers of other languages. It covers second language acquisition, applied linguistics, effective classroom and online teaching, language assessment design, curriculum development and research methods, and includes a roughly 30-hour teaching practicum with a minimum of six hours taught under the supervision of an experienced teacher.

Placement help is available on the Gold Coast; students elsewhere arrange their own, which can be in a school, a language centre or their own workplace. The degree does not qualify graduates to teach in Australian school systems, which requires an accredited teaching qualification. It suits current language teachers wanting an advanced credential, educators working with multilingual learners, and career changers moving into ESL teaching in Australia or overseas.

It is professionally accredited by the Australian Institute of Building Surveyors and the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors, which is what allows graduates to work toward accreditation as a building surveyor and certifier in any Australian state and be recognised internationally. Teaching is in small discussion-based classes led by practising surveyors, in Bond's award-winning sustainable Built Environment Precinct. It suits people already in construction, building control or a related technical role who want the qualification needed to certify buildings and move into senior surveying work.

name: Master of Business
description:
A 16-month master's (four semesters) aimed at graduates from non-business fields who want to move into management or a business function. Semester one covers accounting, marketing, and finance fundamentals; later semesters broaden into other business areas and a chosen specialisation, finishing with electives.

Students pick one specialisation from marketing, big data, health management, international business, finance, or tourism management. It differs from Bond's MBA in emphasis: the Master of Business is a conversion and upskilling degree with functional depth in one area, while the MBA is a general-management program built around leadership and strategy. No prior business study is required. Accredited by AACSB and EQUIS.

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Bond was Australia's first university to run a genuine three-semester-a-year academic calendar, and the MBA is where that timetable shows up most sharply: the full 12-subject generalist program can be completed in one year and four months of continuous study, roughly half the time a traditional two-semester MBA takes to deliver a comparable subject load. The first trimester front-loads eight core functional subjects delivered as intensive-mode bootcamps (compressed, immersive blocks rather than subjects spread thin across a normal semester) before students move into a business engineering component and then electives where they can build a specialisation.

Because Bond charges the same tuition to domestic and international students, cohorts are unusually mixed for an Australian MBA, and the accelerated calendar tends to attract candidates who want to return to the workforce, or start a venture, without a multi-year career gap. Students who want workplace exposure alongside the degree can take the MBA (Professional) variant, which follows the same subject structure with an additional 20-week professional placement component built in.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: 8 core functional bootcamps delivered in intensive mode (Accounting, Finance, Marketing, Economics, Organisational Behaviour, Operations, Strategy, Business Analytics)
Trimester 2: Business engineering component — integrated, project-based subjects connecting the core disciplines
Trimester 3: Electives, including the option to build a specialisation, plus a capstone strategy project
Optional MBA (Professional) pathway: same 12-subject structure plus an additional 20-week supervised professional placement
Total: 12 subjects, completed in as little as 1 year 4 months full-time
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree plus relevant professional work experience (typically 2+ years recommended, though not always mandatory).
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

The first semester is eight intensive core subjects covering leadership, organisational behaviour, decision-making, managerial economics, marketing, accounting, and financial decision-making. Later semesters cover creative thinking, data analytics, and strategic management, ending in a Business Transformation capstone project, followed by electives from the business school.

The program is built around three themes: innovation, data analytics, and business transformation. It is accredited by AACSB and EQUIS. Holders of CPA Australia, CA ANZ, or IPA membership can receive up to 50 percent credit. Entry requirements, including any work-experience expectation, should be confirmed with Bond directly.

name: Master of Enterprise Artificial Intelligence
description:
A four-semester master's (about 16 months on Bond's three-intake calendar) that builds AI capability from the ground up for people who will lead it inside an organisation rather than research it. Semester one covers programming foundations in Python, computational thinking, systems and cybersecurity; semester two moves to advanced programming and relational and non-relational data management; semester three adds software engineering practice, advanced data science and a responsible-business subject; the final semester is specialised AI electives and a capstone enterprise AI project.

Students shape the degree through electives in areas such as digital transformation, business intelligence, product innovation and data-driven strategy, and use the Bond FinTech Hub, Centre for Data Analytics and the Transformer entrepreneurship space. It is accredited by AACSB and EQUIS, and it replaced Bond's earlier Master of Business Data Analytics. It suits graduates and working professionals aiming for roles where AI and business strategy meet across business, government and the not-for-profit sector.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in a related discipline (or equivalent) with a competitive GPA; some programs consider relevant professional experience in place of a directly related degree.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Finance
description:
Bond's Master of Finance has been accepted into the CFA Institute University Affiliation Program, meaning the curriculum is deliberately mapped against the CFA Program Candidate Body of Knowledge rather than following a generic finance syllabus, useful for students planning to sit the CFA exams alongside or after the degree. It's designed for graduates from other disciplines who want a quantitatively rigorous route into financial markets, risk management and investment analysis, and runs across Bond's three trimesters to be completed in one year and four months.

Teaching is case-based and delivered with input from industry guest lecturers, and students get access to Bond's two financial trading rooms and 40 Bloomberg terminals, more Bloomberg terminals than any other Australian university offers, which matters for a degree built around live market data rather than textbook problem sets. Group projects and case presentations run throughout, so students graduate having actually built and defended investment analysis rather than only having studied the theory behind it.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Financial Accounting, Corporate Finance, Financial Markets and Institutions, Quantitative Methods for Finance
Trimester 2: Investment Analysis and Portfolio Management, Derivative Securities, Fixed Income Analysis, Financial Statement Analysis
Trimester 3: Risk Management, Applied Portfolio Management (trading room-based), Behavioural Finance, capstone finance project
Curriculum mapped to the CFA Program Candidate Body of Knowledge under the CFA Institute University Affiliation Program
Practical component: two financial trading rooms and 40 Bloomberg terminals used across coursework
Completed in 1 year 4 months full-time
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree (business/finance background preferred but not mandatory) with a competitive GPA.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Finance (Professional)
description:
A 16-month master's (four semesters), with this Professional version adding a supervised placement. The core runs through finance and investments, portfolio management, pricing of financial instruments, markets and institutions, and an International Finance capstone, with a large directed-elective component (financial accounting, quantitative methods, entrepreneurial finance, financial applications and analysis).

Teaching uses the Bond FinTech Hub and its Bloomberg terminals, with a Bloomberg certification pathway. Graduates of a cognate undergraduate degree can receive up to 40 credit points of advanced standing. The program leans quantitative; applicants from non-finance backgrounds should check the entry requirements.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in a related discipline (or equivalent) with a competitive GPA; some programs consider relevant professional experience in place of a directly related degree.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Healthcare Innovations
description:
A one-year master's (three semesters) for healthcare professionals moving into leadership, quality, or transformation roles, taught through intensive workshops. It covers four areas: evidence-based practice and research, health systems and policy, leading change and implementation science, and care quality and workforce development. Electives include innovation and entrepreneurship, data and project management, and advanced leadership through the business school.

The capstone is a portfolio of real workplace projects with measurable results, such as pilot projects and business cases. It is aimed at clinicians, administrators, and health entrepreneurs rather than new graduates, and it also sets up a PhD pathway through its research component.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in a related health/science discipline with a competitive GPA; interview and/or additional selection criteria apply.
