name: Master of International Hotel and Tourism Management
description:
A four-semester master's (about 16 months), eight core subjects plus four electives, that can be fast-tracked on Bond's three-intake calendar. The core moves from tourism and hospitality management issues, sustainable tourism and people management through revenue management and tourism analysis to marketing fundamentals and analytics in the final semester.

The program is built around industry contact: guest lecturers and live projects from Marriott, Accor, IHG, Wyndham, Village Roadshow Theme Parks and Star Entertainment, plus optional industry placements, employment activities and international internships arranged through tourism organisations. It is accredited by AACSB and EQUIS. It suits graduates aiming at senior operational or management roles in hotels, resorts, events and tourism, as well as people planning to run their own hospitality business.

name: Master of Laws
description:
An eight-month coursework LLM (two semesters, 80 credit points) for law graduates only. Students can take electives broadly or concentrate in one of six areas: corporate and commercial law, dispute resolution, international business and finance law, international commercial law and dispute resolution, family dispute resolution, or Canadian law and practice. There is no research thesis in the standard structure; it is a coursework degree.

Bond Juris Doctor graduates receive a 40 credit point exemption, halving the program. It suits practising or recently graduated lawyers who want a specialist credential quickly rather than a broad or research-based postgraduate qualification.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in any discipline (does not need to be in law) with a competitive GPA.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, with no band below 6.5 (or equivalent).

name: Master of Laws (by Research)
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree with first-class or upper-second-class honours (or equivalent research training) in a relevant discipline, plus an approved research proposal and supervisor agreement.

name: Master of Laws in Australian Law and Practice
description:
An eight-month coursework LLM (two semesters, 80 credit points) designed for overseas-trained lawyers who want to practise in Australia. After an admitting board assesses an applicant's overseas law degree and identifies which knowledge areas are missing, this program delivers those Priestley 11 gap subjects, with postgraduate electives making up the rest of the 80 credit points.

It covers the academic requirement for admission; graduates still complete practical legal training, typically Bond's Graduate Diploma in Legal Practice, before being admitted. It suits internationally qualified lawyers who want to close their admission gap and hold an Australian postgraduate law degree at the same time.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in any discipline (does not need to be in law) with a competitive GPA.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, with no band below 6.5 (or equivalent).

name: Master of Laws in Enterprise Governance
description:
An eight-subject LLM built for directors and senior managers, structured for part-time study over about 16 months through online modules and two-day intensive workshops at Bond's Brisbane campus. It is open to non-law graduates, who begin with Foundations of Enterprise Governance and Foundations of Enterprise Law before the specialist subjects covering ethics, commercial structures, strategy, risk, compliance, finance, tax and insolvency, privacy, consumer law, and IT law and cyber security.

Bond describes it as the only Australian LLM focused specifically on enterprise governance, oriented toward boardroom readiness rather than legal practice. Graduates receive an Advanced Credential in Enterprise Governance alongside the degree. It is aimed at experienced leaders, company officers and current or aspiring board members, and it is not a route to legal admission.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in any discipline (does not need to be in law) with a competitive GPA.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, with no band below 6.5 (or equivalent).

admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in any discipline (does not need to be in law) with a competitive GPA.

name: Master of Management
description:
A three-semester master's, just over a year full-time, starting in January. Semester one covers managing people and accounting principles alongside specialisation or elective subjects; later semesters add economics, international human resource management, leading innovation and change, and managing strategic change, with an optional internship or study tour in the final semester.

Students choose one specialisation from data analytics, finance, health management, international business, marketing, or hotel, resort and tourism management. It is shorter than Bond's four-semester MBA and Master of Business, and is pitched at recent graduates starting a management career rather than experienced managers: the MBA is built around leadership and strategy for people with work experience, while the Master of Management gives a faster grounding in how organisations run. Accredited by AACSB and EQUIS.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in any discipline with a competitive GPA; relevant work experience is regarded favourably but not always mandatory.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Marketing
description:
A four-semester master's that can be accelerated to about 12 months. The core runs through marketing fundamentals, market research, consumer behaviour, integrated marketing communications, marketing analytics, strategic marketing, and digital marketing, with roughly a third of the program open to electives or a Business Data Analytics specialisation.

Assessment is project-based rather than exam-based: students run social media campaigns, market research projects, and full marketing strategies. The Career Development Centre arranges internships. Accredited by AACSB and EQUIS. It suits students moving into marketing from another field as well as those deepening an existing marketing background.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in a related discipline (or equivalent) with a competitive GPA; some programs consider relevant professional experience in place of a directly related degree.

name: Master of Nutrition and Dietetic Practice
description:
A two-year degree (six semesters) that qualifies graduates for Dietitians Australia's Accredited Practising Dietitian program, the credential needed to work as a dietitian in Australia. It is placement-heavy: about 44 weeks of immersive experience, made up of four five-week clinical placements, two ten-week research internships, and a two-week international field trip.

Year one covers foundational nutrition, food science, clinical dietetics, public health nutrition, and food service management; year two is mostly placement plus a sports nutrition intensive, research coursework, a leadership subject, and an international nutrition practice intensive. The degree is also accredited in the United States by ACEND, though the US registered dietitian pathway needs extra supervised hours there. Applicants should check the specific prerequisite subjects with Bond.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in a related health/science discipline with a competitive GPA; interview and/or additional selection criteria apply.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, with no band below 7.0 (registration-board English requirement).

name: Master of Occupational Therapy
description:
Bond runs occupational therapy as an extended masters of about four years rather than a short graduate-entry program. It embeds around 1,040 hours of fieldwork, including 24 weeks of Level II supervised practice. Entry is with a bachelor's degree, with common pathways from exercise and sports science, biomedical science, health sciences, or psychological science.

The qualification is approved by the Occupational Therapy Board of Australia, recognised by the World Federation of Occupational Therapists, and separately accredited in the United States by ACOTE, which widens where graduates can register. Students choose a clinically focused or business-focused research pathway within the degree. Completing it leads to registration as an occupational therapist in Australia.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in a related health/science discipline with a competitive GPA; interview and/or additional selection criteria apply.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, with no band below 7.0 (registration-board English requirement).

name: Master of Professional Psychology
description:
An eight-month program that makes up the fifth year of the six-year psychology training pathway. Entry requires an accredited four-year psychology sequence (bachelor plus honours or a graduate diploma) and provisional registration with AHPRA before starting.

It includes 300 hours of supervised practice at Bond's on-campus psychology clinic, with mandatory in-person attendance. It is accredited to APAC standards. On its own it does not lead to registration: graduates then complete a further year of approved supervised practice (the 5+1 internship route) to reach the six years required for general registration. Students who want to finish the pathway entirely through university study take the two-year Master of Psychology (Clinical) instead.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in a related health/science discipline with a competitive GPA; interview and/or additional selection criteria apply.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Project Management
description:
Bond is the only Australian university whose project management programs carry recognition from all three major industry bodies at once: the Australian Institute of Project Management, the Project Management Institute's Global Accreditation Center, and the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors. That's a fairly unusual claim to be able to make and shapes how the Master of Project Management is built. Rather than teaching a single methodology, the curriculum aligns to the PMBOK Guide while explicitly training students in predictive, adaptive and hybrid ways of working, since that's closer to how project teams actually operate outside a textbook.

The degree is organised around four study themes (strategy; sustainability; managing complex problems and teams; and virtual teams and global working) that recur across subjects rather than being confined to one unit each. Content covers conflict resolution, integrated planning, portfolio management, and both public- and private-sector investment and risk, and the degree can be completed across Bond's three trimesters faster than an equivalent two-semester program elsewhere.
curriculum:
Core: Project Management Fundamentals, Project Planning and Control, Project Risk Management, Project Procurement and Contracts
Study theme — Strategy: Strategic Project Management, Portfolio Management
Study theme — Sustainability: Sustainable Project Practice, Public and Private Sector Investment
Study theme — Complex problems and teams: Managing Complex Projects, Conflict Resolution and Negotiation
Study theme — Virtual and global teams: Global and Virtual Project Teams, Cross-Cultural Project Leadership
Capstone: applied project management practicum aligned to the PMBOK Guide
Recognised by AIPM, PMI-GAC and RICS
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in any discipline; relevant work experience regarded favourably but not mandatory.

description:

Entry requires an accredited four-year psychology sequence (bachelor plus honours or a graduate diploma) and provisional registration with AHPRA before starting.

Placements are central: a first internship in Bond's on-campus psychology clinic under staff supervision in year one, then a second internship plus two community externships under external supervision in year two. The program is accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council. On completion graduates can apply for general registration with AHPRA and for the Australian Psychological Society's clinical college. Entry is competitive and based on prior grades.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in a related health/science discipline with a competitive GPA; interview and/or additional selection criteria apply.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Sport Management
description:
A four-semester master's that can be accelerated. Semester one covers event planning, organisational behaviour and financial decision-making; later semesters add marketing, sport as a product and service, data analytics, and a final semester on sport law, governance, elite athlete management and stakeholder relations, with an optional international study tour or internship.

Teaching draws on people from professional and Olympic sport organisations, and Bond's connections support placements with Australian rules football, the rugby codes and the World Surf League. The Bond Business School holds both AACSB and EQUIS accreditation. It suits people building or advancing a career in sport administration, whether coming from sport or from another field.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in a related discipline (or equivalent) with a competitive GPA; some programs consider relevant professional experience in place of a directly related degree.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Valuation and Property Development
description:
A four-semester master's (about 16 months), also available part-time, covering property finance and taxation, corporate portfolio management, risk, feasibility analysis, property law, and valuation and market analysis, with electives that lean toward either property valuation or city planning.

It is accredited by the Australian Property Institute, the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors and the Valuers Registration Board of Queensland, so it supports the pathway toward registration as a valuer. Classes are taught in Bond's Built Environment Precinct, which includes Australia's first 6-Star Green Star education building. The degree is designed both for people already working in property who want to formalise and extend their skills and for graduates moving in from finance, law or another field, with graduates working in valuation, investment, asset management and property research.

name: Medical Program* Bachelor of Medical Studies, Doctor of Medicine
description:
Bond's Medical Program is the shortest path to a medical doctorate in Australasia: students complete two consecutive degrees, the Bachelor of Medical Studies and the Doctor of Medicine, in four years and eight months total rather than the five to six years most Australian medical degrees take. The Bachelor of Medical Studies runs for two years and eight months (eight trimesters) and builds foundational clinical knowledge and skills, after which the Doctor of Medicine runs for a further two years (six trimesters); both degrees are conferred together on completion of the MD.

Teaching in the first two years is problem-based: each week opens with a clinical case that the week's learning is built around, worked through in small interactive groups rather than large lectures. From the third year, students relocate to the Bond University Clinical Education and Research Centre at Robina Hospital for a full year immersed in a genuine hospital environment before moving into the MD's more advanced clinical phases. The MD is accredited at AQF level 9 as an Extended Masters Degree, and graduates meet the requirements for provisional medical registration, allowing them to begin accredited intern training toward full registration.
curriculum:
Bachelor of Medical Studies (8 trimesters, 2 years 8 months):
Years 1-2 (5 trimesters): case-based small-group learning covering foundational biomedical science, clinical skills, and population health, structured around a weekly clinical case
Year 3: full-year clinical immersion at the Bond University Clinical Education and Research Centre, Robina Hospital
Doctor of Medicine (6 trimesters, 2 years):
Advanced clinical rotations across medicine, surgery, psychiatry, obstetrics and gynaecology, and general practice
Elective clinical placement, including options for rural or international rotations
Final trimesters: capstone clinical practicum and preparation for provisional registration
MD accredited at AQF level 9 (Extended Masters Degree); meets requirements for provisional medical registration
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent) with strong results in Chemistry and Biology, plus a competitive score on an approved medical admissions test (e.g. UCAT) and interview.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, with no band below 7.0 (registration-board English requirement).

name: Bachelor of Commerce (Applied)
description:
Box Hill Institute's Bachelor of Commerce (Applied) splits its three years into 12 core subjects (72 points), 8 major subjects (48 points), and 4 electives (24 points): accounting, finance, management, marketing, business ethics, and law all sit in the core before students specialise.

As a dual-sector provider, Box Hill teaches this degree the way it teaches its TAFE diplomas: smaller cohorts than a large university commerce school, and a direct line into the institute's own vocational accounting and business programs for students who want to start at certificate or diploma level and build up rather than enrolling in a bachelor's straight away.

The degree carries accreditation from both CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, which matters more than it might for a similarly-titled degree elsewhere. Box Hill isn't a research university trading on reputation, so professional body accreditation is the credential that does the work of assuring employers the accounting training meets the same bar as a larger institution's.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Foundations of Accounting; Economics for Business; Business Law; Marketing Principles; 2 further core subjects.
Year 2 — Financial Accounting; Management Accounting; Taxation Law; Corporations Law; 2 further core subjects; major subjects begin.
Year 3 — Auditing and Assurance; Strategic Management; Contemporary Issues in Accounting; remaining major subjects; 4 electives across the degree.
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall (Box Hill's own published bachelor-entry bar)

name: Bachelor of Computer Systems (Networking)
description:
This degree runs 19 core units plus 5 electives drawn from a choice of majors (cyber security, networking, or cloud and virtualisation), with the Networking major itself sitting inside a broader Computer Systems degree rather than being sold as a standalone qualification.

First year is deliberately generalist: basic networking, cloud computing, and introductory programming, so students don't have to commit hard to networking specifically before they've seen the alternatives. Second year gets specific fast: operating systems, cyber security, network security, systems security, virtualisation, and programming for web applications, alongside business and communication units that a purely technical program often skips. Third year moves into emerging ICT technologies, advanced security or virtualisation techniques, and entrepreneurship and innovation.

Box Hill delivers this in partnership with Cisco, VMware, and Microsoft, which shows up in the practical, vendor-relevant skills the networking major targets. Those skills sit closer to what a network administrator or systems engineer does day to day than a purely theoretical computer science curriculum, and they're useful for students aiming at Cisco or Microsoft certifications alongside the degree itself.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Introduction to Networking; Cloud Computing Fundamentals; Introductory Programming; IT Systems Fundamentals; foundational core units.
Year 2 — Operating Systems; Cyber Security Fundamentals; Network Security; Systems Security; Virtualisation; Programming for Web Applications; Business and Communication Skills.
Year 3 — Emerging ICT Technologies; Advanced Networking/Virtualisation Techniques; Entrepreneurship and Innovation; 5 electives (networking, cyber security, or cloud/virtualisation stream).
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood Education
description:
Box Hill's Bachelor of Early Childhood Education is built for people already working while they study, the program runs as blended delivery with classes on evenings and occasional Saturdays, and each core subject pairs 30 hours of face-to-face lecture, tutorial, and workshop time with around 5 hours of online activity rather than a standard daytime timetable.

The degree comprises 28 core subjects and 4 practicum subjects, totalling 80 days of supervised placement across a range of early childhood settings, deliberately including services other than the student's own workplace, so students already working in childcare still have to demonstrate their skills somewhere unfamiliar rather than only in a setting where staff already know them.

The program is recognised by the Australian Children's Education and Care Quality Authority and meets Victorian Institute of Teaching standards for Early Childhood Teacher registration, meaning graduates come out eligible to register as qualified early childhood teachers, not just educators, in Victoria.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Child Development; Foundations of Early Childhood Pedagogy; Health, Safety and Wellbeing in Early Childhood Settings; Practicum 1.
Year 2 — Curriculum Design for Early Learning; Language and Literacy Development; Working with Families and Communities; Practicum 2.
Year 3 — Leadership in Early Childhood Settings; Inclusive Practice and Additional Needs; Professional Practice and Ethics; Practicum 3.
Year 4 — Research and Reflective Practice in Early Childhood Education; Transition to Teaching; Practicum 4 (final placement block).
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent (teaching registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Fashion
description:
Box Hill Institute has run fashion design and merchandising training out of its Box Hill campus for decades, well before it offered bachelor's degrees at all, and the Bachelor of Fashion sits on top of that vocational base rather than starting from scratch as a purely academic program. The broader fashion degree family here splits 12 core units, 10 major units, and 6 electives across three years: pattern-making, garment construction, and textiles knowledge sit alongside business, marketing, and enterprise units rather than treating design as a purely creative pursuit separate from the commercial reality of running a label.

Students work with industry-standard equipment and, depending on the trimester, contribute to Box Hill's own fashion parades and graduate showcases, a public, portfolio-building event that functions as an informal industry pitch rather than a purely internal assessment.

Career paths lean toward fashion design, garment technology, buying and merchandising, and small-label entrepreneurship, reflecting Box Hill's applied, business-aware take on fashion education rather than a purely runway-focused design school model.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Fashion Design Fundamentals; Pattern-Making and Garment Construction 1; Textiles and Materials; Introduction to the Fashion Industry; core business unit.
Year 2 — Pattern-Making and Garment Construction 2; Fashion Illustration and Communication; Fashion Marketing; Sustainable Fashion Practice; major units begin.
Year 3 — Fashion Enterprise and Business Planning; Collection Development (culminating in graduate showcase); remaining major and elective units.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; portfolio may be required
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Hospitality Management
description:
The Bachelor of Hospitality Management at Box Hill covers accounting, marketing, business and hospitality law, workplace communications, strategic project management, and human resources management: a management-focused degree built for people planning to run hospitality operations rather than work the front line of them, though Box Hill's parallel commercial cookery and hospitality certificate programs mean many students arrive with genuine kitchen or floor experience already.

Small class sizes and direct lecturer contact are emphasised more than at a typical large university business school, consistent with Box Hill's TAFE-scale delivery model even at bachelor's level. A work-based hospitality management project gives students a real venue or business problem to solve rather than a hypothetical case study, drawing on Box Hill's existing industry relationships across Melbourne's hospitality sector.

Career paths include hotel and venue management, event management, hospitality operations, and food and beverage management, with the strategic project management and contemporary issues coursework aimed at people expected to run a shift, a venue, or eventually a business rather than simply staff one.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Introduction to Hospitality Management; Accounting for Hospitality; Workplace Communications; Marketing Principles.
Year 2 — Business and Hospitality Law; Human Resource Management; Contemporary Issues in Hospitality; Financial Management.
Year 3 — Strategic Project Management; Work-Based Hospitality Management Project; electives.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
Box Hill's Bachelor of Information Technology follows the same 12 core / 8 major / 4 elective structure as several of its other applied degrees, with specialisation streams in cyber security, data analytics and AI, cloud computing and IoT, and software engineering. It's TEQSA-accredited and pitched at AQF Level 7, the standard bachelor's level, despite Box Hill's identity as a TAFE first and university-level provider second.

That dual-sector status is arguably the more interesting fact about the degree: students can move between Box Hill's certificate and diploma-level IT courses and this bachelor's with credit transfer arrangements that a stand-alone university IT school doesn't usually offer as smoothly, useful for students who started in vocational IT training and want to step up without repeating content.

Career paths include software developer, cyber security analyst, data analyst, cloud engineer, and IT support/systems roles, with the elective structure letting students weight the final year toward whichever of the four specialisation areas matches where they want to work.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Introduction to Programming; IT Systems Fundamentals; Networking Basics; Database Fundamentals; core units.
Year 2 — Software Development; Cyber Security Principles; Cloud Computing Fundamentals; Data Analytics Foundations; major units begin.
Year 3 — Advanced specialisation units (cyber security, data analytics and AI, cloud and IoT, or software engineering); capstone IT project; 4 electives.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Music Industry (Major in Performance)
description:
Box Hill structures its Bachelor of Music Industry around six possible majors (Performance is one, alongside options like Audio Production and Composition), with a combined common core running through the first two years covering the music industry from multiple angles: innovation, creativity, entrepreneurship, and preparing for where the industry is heading rather than where it's been.

Once the major is chosen, it accounts for roughly half the remaining coursework, and students fill the rest by picking from a pool of more than sixty subjects, adding either two minors, a minor plus electives, or straight electives, a genuinely open structure compared to a fixed-major conservatoire degree. Full-time study runs at 16 contact hours a week plus an expected 16 hours of personal practice and study time, delivered face to face on weekdays.

Box Hill also builds in formal exit points most bachelor's degrees don't offer: a Diploma in Music Industry after one year and an Associate Degree in Music Industry after two, useful for students who want a credential if their circumstances change partway through, or who are testing whether a full three-year commitment is right for them.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Music Industry Foundations (common core); Performance Major 1; Innovation and Creativity in Music; electives.
Year 2 — Music Industry Perspectives (common core); Performance Major 2; entrepreneurship unit; electives or minor units. (Diploma exit available after Year 1; Associate Degree exit available after Year 2.)
Year 3 — Performance Major 3 (advanced); electives from the 60+ subject pool; capstone performance project.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; audition required
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Accounting
description:
The value proposition of CDU's Bachelor of Accounting is almost entirely about the accreditation stack: graduates meet the educational requirements for CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CAANZ), and the broader accounting suite at CDU also carries CIMA (UK) and ACCA recognition. For a degree at a regional Australian university, that's a fairly comprehensive set of professional pathways, and it means graduates aren't limited to local NT employers if they want to sit CPA or CA exams interstate or move to accounting roles in the UK or elsewhere in the Commonwealth.

Content-wise it's a fairly standard accounting core (financial accounting, management accounting, auditing, taxation, commercial law), but CDU frames electives around the resources and government sectors that dominate the Territory economy: mining royalties, public sector financial management, and small-business advisory work show up more than in accounting degrees oriented toward corporate finance in a capital-city CBD. A combined Bachelor of Accounting/Diploma of Laws option exists for students who want commercial law grounding without committing to a full LLB.

Delivery is flexible (on campus, online, or blended) and the degree can be taken part-time, which suits the number of students working in bookkeeping or para-accounting roles while they complete the qualification.
curriculum:
Core units: Financial Accounting, Management Accounting, Company Accounting, Auditing and Assurance, Taxation Law, Commercial Law, Corporations Law, Accounting Information Systems, Business Finance, Economics for Business
Electives: choose from public sector accounting, small business advisory, resources sector accounting, or a business minor
Capstone: integrated case study or professional practice unit in final year
Professional accreditation built into course design: meets CPA Australia and CAANZ requirements
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
CDU pitches its Bachelor of Arts around a genuinely distinctive regional angle: rather than being a generic humanities degree, it's built around issues facing Northern Australia, Indigenous communities, and South-East Asia, which makes sense given Darwin sits closer to Dili and Denpasar than to Sydney. Students choose from nine majors, including options rarely paired together at one institution: Digital Communication and Indigenous Studies sit alongside more familiar choices, and an Architecture major (unusual for a BA) covers representation, spatial design, and industry-standard drafting tools with a tropical-north focus.

The Indigenous Studies major is arguably the strongest reason to choose CDU specifically over an east-coast university for this degree; it's taught by staff embedded in Northern Territory Aboriginal communities and covers philosophy, sociology, and Indigenous perspectives in a way that's hard to replicate somewhere without that geographic and cultural proximity. The Digital Communication major, meanwhile, tracks social media, media ethics, and multi-screen communication, practical skills for content and comms roles rather than a literary-criticism-heavy media studies track.

As with most CDU undergraduate degrees, the BA is available fully online, on campus, or mixed, and can be taken part-time, which matters given a meaningful chunk of the student body balances study with work or family responsibilities in regional NT towns.
curriculum:
Foundation year: core arts units in critical thinking, research methods, and an introductory unit in the chosen major
Majors offered (choose one, minor optional): Digital Communication, Indigenous Studies, Architecture, Creative Writing, History, Politics and International Relations, Society and Culture, Asian Studies, Screen and Media
Years 2-3: major-specific sequence plus free electives, culminating in a capstone or independent research project
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time, on campus, online, or blended
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
CDU trains a disproportionate share of the Northern Territory's primary teachers, and the Bachelor of Education (Primary) is shaped by that reality: a strong First Nations education thread runs through the coursework because so many graduates end up teaching in schools with significant Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander student populations, including remote community schools where CDU-trained teachers are often the most viable local supply pipeline.

The course covers Transition through Year 6/7 and is structured around 30 core units plus two specialist elective areas chosen from English, humanities, science, technology and mathematics, health and PE, or the Arts, letting students build some depth in a curriculum area they want to specialise in, without turning the degree into a secondary-style single-subject major. Professional experience placements run throughout the degree rather than being backloaded into final year, and online students complete placements at schools near where they live rather than having to relocate to Darwin, which is a meaningful accessibility factor given how spread out the NT population is.

Graduates meet the Australian Professional Standards for Graduating Teachers and are eligible for provisional registration with the Teacher Registration Board of the Northern Territory, with mutual recognition arrangements applying interstate.
curriculum:
Core sequence (30 units) across child development, curriculum and pedagogy, inclusive education, classroom management, and First Nations education
Specialist elective areas (choose 2): English, Humanities and Social Sciences, Science, Technology and Mathematics, Health and Physical Education, The Arts
Professional experience: staged placements from first year through to a final-year extended practicum block
Capstone: final professional experience placement with formal competency assessment against the Australian Professional Standards for Graduating Teachers
Total: 4 years full-time, on campus or online with local placements
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent (teaching registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Engineering at CDU is explicitly oriented toward the infrastructure and resources challenges of northern Australia: remote power and water systems, tropical building performance, and the mining and gas projects that dominate NT industry. Students pick one of three specialisations (civil and structural, electrical and electronic, or mechanical engineering), and the course was developed with industry input specifically so graduates come out with skills that map onto what Territory employers (and the broader northern Australia resources sector) are actually hiring for, rather than a generic engineering curriculum transplanted from a southern capital city.

It's a four-year Honours-embedded degree (not a separate add-on year like some Group of Eight universities do it), accredited to meet Engineers Australia's requirements for professional engineer registration, and available fully online for students who can't relocate to Darwin. That's a genuinely unusual offering, since most accredited engineering degrees in Australia require substantial on-campus lab and workshop time. CDU manages this partly through intensive on-campus blocks for lab-heavy units combined with remote delivery for the more theory-based content.

Because Darwin's engineering employment market is smaller and more resources-and-government-heavy than Sydney's or Melbourne's, a good chunk of the practical/work-integrated learning component connects students directly with NT infrastructure and utilities employers rather than a broad national graduate market.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Engineering Mathematics, Mechanics, Materials Science, Engineering Design, Thermodynamics, Electrical Fundamentals, Professional Practice in Engineering
Specialisation streams (choose one): Civil and Structural, Electrical and Electronic, Mechanical
Year 3: specialisation core units plus Project Management, Fluid Mechanics or Power Systems (depending on stream), industry-linked design project
Year 4 (Honours): capstone engineering project, advanced specialisation electives, professional experience placement
Total: 4 years full-time, accredited by Engineers Australia; on campus or online with intensive lab blocks
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science
description:
CDU's Exercise and Sport Science degree gets students into practical, sport-specific coursework earlier than many equivalent programs, which tend to spend most of first year on generic science prerequisites before students see anything resembling their actual field. Anatomy, physiology, psychology, coaching, and nutrition units appear from early in the course, and the program builds toward supervised placements rather than treating practical experience as an afterthought bolted onto the final semester.

A five-day compulsory residential intensive at the Casuarina campus plus 80 hours of practicum placement are built in specifically to satisfy Exercise and Sport Science Australia (ESSA) accreditation requirements: this matters for online and remote students, who make up a meaningful share of enrolments given the Territory's dispersed population, because it means even fully online students have to travel to Darwin at some point for the intensive component. Graduates come out eligible for ESSA accreditation as an Exercise Scientist (via the non-accredited pathway track) and can also seek membership with the Australian Strength and Conditioning Association, Sports Medicine Australia, and Fitness Australia.

Given the NT's demographics and remoteness, several placement partners work in community sport and remote/Indigenous health and physical activity settings, which is a different practicum flavour than the elite-sport or metro gym placements more common in programs at east-coast universities.
curriculum:
Core units: Human Anatomy, Exercise Physiology, Biomechanics, Sport and Exercise Psychology, Nutrition for Performance, Motor Learning and Control, Strength and Conditioning, Exercise Prescription for Health and Disease
Practical components: compulsory 5-day residential intensive (Casuarina campus) and 80 hours of supervised practicum
Capstone: applied placement project in a community, clinical, or sport-performance setting
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time, on campus or online with mandatory on-campus components
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
Studying law at CDU means studying it in a jurisdiction most Australian law schools barely touch: the Northern Territory has its own quirks in areas like Indigenous land rights, mining and resources law, and criminal sentencing that don't come up the same way in a Sydney or Melbourne law degree. Students get exposure to that Territory-specific context alongside the standard Priestley 11 subjects the profession requires everywhere in Australia.

The LLB runs 240 credit points across three years full-time, with a maximum of 100 credit points able to come from first-year (100-level) units and at least 60 credit points required at 300-level or above, a structure meant to stop students front-loading easy units and coasting. Most of the core sequence (contracts, torts, criminal law, property, equity, evidence, civil procedure) is prescribed by the legal profession's admission requirements, so there's not much room to swap those out; the flexibility shows up in the specialist electives, where students can lean toward family law, international law, or competition and consumer law depending on where they want to end up.

CDU offers full online delivery for the whole degree, which is unusual for a law program and reflects the practical reality that a lot of NT residents live hours from Darwin. Graduates wanting Honours can roll straight into the one-year Bachelor of Laws Honours add-on rather than restarting a separate degree.
curriculum:
Year 1: Legal Process, Contracts A & B, Criminal Law, Legal Research and Writing, foundational electives
Year 2: Torts, Property Law, Equity and Trusts, Administrative Law, Constitutional Law
Year 3: Evidence, Civil Procedure, Company Law, Professional Conduct, capstone/clinical elective
Specialist electives across the degree: family law, international law, competition and consumer law, Indigenous legal issues
Structure: 240 credit points total, max 100 credit points at 100-level, minimum 60 credit points at 300-level or above
Optional: Bachelor of Laws Honours (1 additional year) for eligible graduates
Delivery: on campus, fully online, or blended; 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Remote and Indigenous health placements are the defining feature of nursing at CDU in a way they simply aren't at most Australian nursing schools, because the Northern Territory has some of the most acute rural and remote health workforce shortages in the country. Students complete 800 hours of clinical placement across metropolitan and rural/remote settings, and those who've finished second-year scope-of-practice units plus the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health unit can apply for a four-week remote placement, run in partnership with NT Top End Health Service, that puts them into genuinely remote clinical settings most nursing graduates elsewhere never experience before registration.

That partnership-driven remote placement track is a real point of difference for students who know they want a career in remote area nursing, a distinct, higher-paid, higher-autonomy specialisation within Australian nursing that's hard to break into without exactly this kind of exposure during training. Indigenous students undertaking placements also have access to 'away from base' funding support, recognising that a lot of NT students are commuting from communities well outside Darwin.

The degree meets registration requirements set by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, so graduates can register as Registered Nurses nationally; the remote and Indigenous health specialisation is additive, not a trade-off against the standard national scope of practice.
curriculum:
Core sequence: Anatomy and Physiology, Pathophysiology, Pharmacology, Nursing Practice (foundational through advanced), Mental Health Nursing, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health, Community and Primary Health Care
Clinical placement: 800 hours total across metropolitan and rural/remote settings
Elective pathway: 4-week remote placement (Northern Territory) available to eligible 3rd-year students, delivered with NT Top End Health Service
Capstone: transition-to-practice placement in final semester
Total: 3 years full-time, registration-ready under Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia standards
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.5) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
This is CDU's APAC-accredited entry point into psychology: the degree that has to exist before an Honours year, before provisional registration, before any of the postgraduate paths toward clinical or organisational psychology. Because that accreditation constrains the curriculum tightly (APAC dictates a lot of the sequencing and content to meet national competency standards), CDU's version looks broadly similar to psych degrees at other Australian universities, but it opens with a Year 1 that explicitly folds in Indigenous protocols and intercultural sensitivity content alongside the usual introduction to psychology and research methods, a reflection of the practicum and research contexts students are likely to work in around Darwin and remote NT communities.

Across the degree, students work through roughly 24 standard subjects covering biological, cognitive, developmental, and social psychology, plus a heavy research methods and statistics load that culminates in an independent research project in third year. Graduates who want to continue toward registration as a psychologist need the Honours year (also APAC-accredited at CDU) or an equivalent postgraduate qualifying program; this bachelor's alone doesn't get you registration, which surprises some students who assume otherwise.

Students can also join the Australian Psychological Society as student members while still completing this degree, which gives earlier access to networking and CPD content than waiting until after graduation.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Research Methods and Design, Psychology Ethics, Indigenous protocols and intercultural sensitivity, Biological Bases of Behaviour
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Statistics for Psychology, Personality and Individual Differences
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology, Psychological Assessment, Advanced Research Methods, independent research project, specialist electives
Pathway: Bachelor of Psychological Science Honours (1 additional year, APAC-accredited) required before provisional psychologist registration
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
CDU's plain Bachelor of Science is the flexible, build-your-own-major sibling to its more structured Environmental Science degree, and its real drawcard is what's on the university's doorstep: Kakadu, Litchfield, the Timor Sea, and some of the most intact tropical savanna and monsoon ecosystems left in the world. Research project options in the final year regularly draw on this: aquaculture, marine and freshwater ecology, botany, and zoology projects here look genuinely different from equivalent projects at a temperate-climate university, because the field sites and species are different.

Unlike a lot of generalist BSc degrees that are essentially a menu of first-year science subjects with no strong identity, CDU leans into its geography: field intensives take students into Northern and Central Australia and parts of the Asia-Pacific for hands-on data collection, which becomes a differentiator on a CV compared to lab-only science degrees. Students without a settled major can still keep options open through first year before choosing a direction.

It's worth being clear-eyed that CDU is not a large research-intensive science faculty compared to a Go8 university, so students chasing a narrow specialisation in, say, particle physics or advanced biochemistry will find the depth of elective offerings thinner than at a bigger institution. The strength here is specifically in field-based, tropical and environmental science.
curriculum:
Year 1: foundational units across two or more of Biology, Chemistry, Earth Science, Mathematics, Physics
Year 2: discipline deepening in chosen area(s), plus statistics and research design
Year 3: advanced electives and an independent or supervised research project (options include aquaculture, marine ecology, freshwater and terrestrial ecology, botany, zoology)
Field components: optional field intensives in Northern and Central Australia and the Asia-Pacific region
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time, on campus or online (lab units require on-campus attendance)
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
CDU's standard MBA sits alongside two other variants the university offers (a Sustainable Leadership MBA and an Executive MBA), so prospective students should be clear on which one they're looking at, since course codes and unit lists differ meaningfully between them. This general MBA builds a fairly conventional core around strategic management, accounting, economics, marketing, and leadership, but distinguishes itself through an applied social enterprise and consulting project where students work on real client problems rather than a purely theoretical capstone.

In final semester, students choose between a professional placement or a set of specialist elective units aligned to their career direction, useful for career-changers who want workplace exposure baked into the degree, versus people already established in a role who'd rather deepen technical knowledge in, say, data analytics or entrepreneurship. Business analytics and data-driven decision-making show up as a running thread across the core units rather than being siloed into a single elective, reflecting a broader shift in Australian MBA design over the past several years.

Given CDU's northern Australia positioning, the program draws a notable number of students working in the resources, government, and not-for-profit sectors that dominate Territory employment, and case material sometimes reflects that regional economic mix more than a program based in a purely metropolitan CBD would.
curriculum:
Core units: Strategic Management, Managerial Accounting, Economics for Managers, Leadership and Organisational Behaviour, Marketing Management, Business Analytics, Corporate Finance, Business Research Methods
Applied component: social enterprise and consulting project (client-based team consulting engagement)
Final semester: choice of professional placement or specialist electives (entrepreneurship, data analytics, human resource management)
Total: 2 years full-time / up to 4 years part-time, on campus or online
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in any discipline; relevant work experience considered
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Information Technology (Software Engineering)
description:
CDU's Master of Information Technology (Software Engineering) is built for people who already have an unrelated bachelor's degree and want a fast, structured route into software careers, rather than people who studied CS undergrad. Because Darwin isn't a tech hub the size of Sydney or Melbourne, the course leans hard on remote delivery and flexible timetabling, and a large share of the cohort is international students studying 100% online from overseas while working toward Australian permanent residency pathways in the ICT occupation list.

The degree is accredited by the Australian Computer Society at the Professional level and recognised under the Seoul Accord, which matters if graduates want their qualification to carry weight in Singapore, South Korea, or other accord countries later on. Coursework moves from foundational units in discrete structures and algorithms through to process-heavy software engineering units, the kind of project management, risk, and requirements-gathering content that shows up in day-to-day work at mid-sized dev shops more than in FAANG-style interviews.

Two research units close out the degree, which is a distinguishing feature next to some other Australian software engineering masters that are pure coursework. It gives graduates something to point to if they're considering a PhD later, though most treat it as an extended capstone project instead.
curriculum:
Core units: HIT137 Software Now, PRT580 Discrete Structures, HIT220 Algorithms and Complexity, HIT234 Database Concepts, PRT581 Principles of Software Systems, PRT582 Software Engineering: Process and Tools, PRT583 Process Development Methodologies, PRT574 Security Assessment in Software Development, HIT363 Enterprise IT Management, PRT551 Risk and Reliability Management, PRT585 Software Engineering Practice
Research component: two research units (40 credit points total), typically a supervised applied project or minor thesis
Total load: 160 credit points, full-time over 2 years (accelerated trimester options can shorten this)
Delivery: on campus at Casuarina or fully online, trimester intake
admission_requirements: Completion of a recognised bachelor's degree or equivalent international qualification. No specific field or GPA/WAM prerequisite is published; CDU's International Masters Qualifying Program offers an alternative pathway for applicants who don't directly meet entry criteria.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, minimum 6.0 in each band. Equivalent: TOEFL iBT 79 (writing ≥21); PTE Academic 58 (minimum 50 per skill); Cambridge C1 Advanced 176 (minimum 169 per skill).

name: Bachelor of Agricultural Business Management
description:
This degree pairs a genuine agricultural science base with a business major, taught out of CSU's Orange campus where students have direct access to the university's own farms and the EH Graham Centre for Agricultural Innovation, a joint venture with the NSW Department of Primary Industries that gives the course a research-farm feel rather than a lecture-hall-only one.

The first year is common ground in agronomy, animal production and farm business fundamentals before students move into accounting, marketing and agribusiness management units layered over continuing agricultural science. It's aimed at people who expect to run or manage a farm enterprise, work in agribusiness supply chains, or advise producers. It isn't aimed at general business graduates who happen to like the countryside. A supervised industry placement in the final year is a standard feature, usually with an agribusiness, bank rural lending team, or farm management company.
curriculum:
Year 1: Principles of Agriculture; Farm Business Management; Accounting Fundamentals; Introduction to Soil and Plant Science
Year 2: Agricultural Marketing; Livestock Production Systems; Agribusiness Finance; Elective
Year 3: Farm Management Economics; Supply Chain and Agribusiness Strategy; Rural Property Management; Elective
Year 4: Industry placement/work-integrated learning subject; Agribusiness Capstone Project; Advanced electives in cropping or livestock systems
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Agricultural Science
description:
Based at CSU's Orange campus, the Bachelor of Agricultural Science is a straight science degree rather than the business-agriculture hybrid CSU also offers. Students spend real time on the university's working farm and through the EH Graham Centre for Agricultural Innovation, a partnership with the NSW Department of Primary Industries that runs actual field trials students can be involved in. That gives the course a research-adjacent feel that's harder to replicate at a metropolitan university without its own farmland.

Core science subjects (soil science, plant physiology, animal production, genetics) build toward specialisations in cropping systems, livestock production or natural resource management, and the degree is designed as a genuine pathway into agronomy, farm advisory, or postgraduate research roles rather than just farm management. Students wanting the management/business side would typically look at the Agricultural Business Management degree instead. A supervised research project or industry placement in the final year is standard.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Plant and Soil Science; Animal Production Systems; Chemistry for Agriculture; Farm Systems
Year 2: Plant Physiology; Animal Nutrition and Genetics; Soil Fertility Management; Elective
Year 3: Cropping Systems; Livestock Production; Natural Resource Management; Elective
Year 4: Research Project or Industry Placement; Advanced Agricultural Science electives; Capstone Seminar
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Business Studies
description:
The Bachelor of Business Studies is CSU's broad, flexible business degree: a general foundation in accounting, marketing, management and economics with room to build a major, delivered heavily online to suit the working students and regional cohorts CSU has traditionally served. It's a less specialised alternative to CSU's dedicated agribusiness or wine business degrees, aimed at students who want conventional business career options (accounting, marketing, HR, management) rather than an industry-specific angle.

Students choose a major from areas such as Accounting, Marketing, Human Resource Management or Management partway through the degree, and the course is commonly taken part-time by people already working, using CSU's long-standing distance and online study infrastructure. A work-integrated learning or capstone subject in the final year ties the major together with a practical project, often completed in the student's existing workplace for part-time students.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Principles; Marketing Fundamentals; Introduction to Management; Business Economics
Year 2: Business Law; Organisational Behaviour; Quantitative Methods for Business; major subject 1
Year 3: Major subjects 2–4 (Accounting / Marketing / HR Management / Management); Elective
Year 4 (or part-time equivalent): Major subjects 5–6; Business Capstone Project or Work-Integrated Learning subject
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
CSU's standard Bachelor of Information Technology runs to 192 points across fourteen core subjects plus an eight-subject specialisation, and the specialisation choice (Cyber Security, Network Engineering, Software and Application Development, or Web Development) is really what defines the degree for each student, since the core is shared. Most students take it through CSU's online delivery model, which the university has run at scale for decades rather than as a pandemic-era add-on.

The Software specialisation starts from basic programming principles and builds to professional application and mobile development; Web Development covers page design, usability and e-commerce build-out; the others go deeper into infrastructure and security. A joint study option lets a student borrow five subjects from an unrelated discipline (business, criminology, and similar are common pairings) and have that show up alongside their specialisation title, which is a genuinely distinctive feature compared with a standard single-strand IT degree elsewhere.
curriculum:
Year 1: Fundamentals of Programming; Computer Systems and Networks; Database Fundamentals; IT Problem Solving; two more core subjects
Year 2: Systems Analysis and Design; Web Technologies; core subjects continue; begin specialisation strand (Cyber Security / Network Engineering / Software and Application Development / Web Development)
Year 3: Specialisation subjects continue (4 of 8); restricted elective; unrestricted electives or joint study sequence begins
Year 4: Remaining specialisation subjects; IT capstone/industry project; remaining unrestricted electives or joint study subjects
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
CSU's Bachelor of Laws is unusual for a regional university in that it's delivered as much through city-based study centres in Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane as from the Bathurst campus itself, which makes it a common choice for people who want a law degree without relocating. The course leans hard into practice readiness: CSU runs its own on-campus legal clinic where students under supervision advise real clients, and the later years fold in professional legal training subjects that in many other degrees are left entirely to the post-degree Practical Legal Training stage.

Core law subjects (contracts, torts, criminal law, property, equity, constitutional and administrative law) cover the Priestley 11 required for admission in every Australian state, and electives let students lean into areas like family law, elder law or Indigenous legal issues, reflecting the regional and rural client base many CSU law graduates end up serving. It suits students aiming at general or regional legal practice more than a big-city corporate law track, though the degree is fully accredited for admission anywhere in Australia.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Law and Legal Reasoning; Contracts A and B; Torts A and B; Legal Research and Writing
Year 2: Criminal Law; Property Law A and B; Administrative Law; Constitutional Law; Elective
Year 3: Equity; Evidence; Company Law; Elective; Legal Clinic (supervised client work)
Year 4: Civil and Criminal Procedure; Professional Conduct and Practice; Dispute Resolution; Capstone elective sequence (e.g. Family Law, Elder Law)
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Nursing at CSU is spread across several regional campuses, including Bathurst, Orange, Wagga Wagga, Albury-Wodonga and Port Macquarie, reflecting the university's original mandate to train health workers for country NSW and Victoria, and clinical placements tend to happen in regional hospitals and community health settings rather than only in large metropolitan teaching hospitals. That regional placement mix is a genuine point of difference: graduates come out with direct experience in settings with less specialist backup, which rural health services value.

The course meets national registration standards (accredited by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia through ANMAC) and combines science-heavy first-year subjects (anatomy, physiology, pharmacology) with progressively more clinical subjects and supervised placement blocks each year, totalling well over 800 hours of clinical placement by graduation, in line with national requirements. Students graduate eligible to register as a Registered Nurse.
curriculum:
Year 1: Anatomy and Physiology; Foundations of Nursing Practice; Health Assessment; Introduction to Pharmacology; clinical placement block
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing; Mental Health Nursing; Pharmacology and Therapeutics; Aged Care Nursing; clinical placement blocks
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing; Paediatric and Maternal Health Nursing; Community and Primary Health Care; Transition to Professional Practice; extended clinical placement
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.5) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Pharmacy
description:
CSU's pharmacy school sits at the Orange campus and was built with a deliberate rural focus: placements are weighted toward regional and rural community pharmacies rather than assuming a metropolitan hospital-pharmacy career path, which matters given how much of Australia's pharmacist shortage sits outside capital cities. It's accredited by the Pharmacy Board of Australia and follows the national competency standards required for provisional registration on graduation.

The first two years are pharmaceutical science heavy (pharmacology, pharmaceutics, medicinal chemistry) before the degree moves into clinical pharmacy practice, therapeutics and extended placement blocks in community and hospital settings. Students complete supervised practical placements each year rather than one block at the end, which means graduates arrive at their provisional registration year having already worked in real pharmacy settings repeatedly, not just once.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Pharmaceutical Science; Human Physiology; Pharmaceutical Chemistry; Professional Practice 1 (placement)
Year 2: Pharmacology; Pharmaceutics; Dose Form Design; Professional Practice 2 (placement)
Year 3: Therapeutics 1; Clinical Pharmacy Practice; Pharmacy Law and Ethics; Professional Practice 3 (placement)
Year 4: Therapeutics 2; Advanced Clinical Practice; Research Project; Extended Professional Placement
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 80 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.5) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Veterinary Biology/Bachelor of Veterinary Science
description:
When CSU opened this course in 2005 it was the first new veterinary school established in Australia in several decades, built specifically around training vets for rural and mixed-animal practice rather than the small-animal urban model that dominates elsewhere. The six-year double degree (Veterinary Biology feeding into Veterinary Science) is taught entirely at the Wagga Wagga campus, and students work with the university's own farm animals as well as companion animals from first year onward rather than being confined to lecture theatres until clinical years.

The course covers diagnosis and management of disease across cattle, sheep, pigs, poultry and fish alongside horses, dogs and cats, a genuinely broad species range that mirrors what a rural mixed-practice vet actually deals with. It's accredited for registration not just in Australia but in New Zealand, the UK, Hong Kong, Singapore and South Africa. Entry is highly competitive and typically requires a strong ATAR plus additional selection criteria (interview, personal statement, sometimes a CASPer-style test), and most students who get in are drawn specifically by the rural/production-animal focus rather than choosing CSU as a fallback from city vet schools.
curriculum:
Years 1–2 (Veterinary Biology component): Animal Anatomy and Physiology; Animal Genetics; Chemistry for Veterinary Science; Animal Nutrition; Animal Behaviour
Years 3–4: Veterinary Pathology; Pharmacology; Ruminant and Equine Medicine; Veterinary Reproduction; clinical skills training
Years 5–6 (Veterinary Science component): Clinical rotations across farm animal, equine and small animal medicine and surgery; Veterinary Public Health; supervised placements at teaching and partner clinics; final clinical practicum
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 90 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Wine Business
description:
Wagga Wagga sits inside one of Australia's wine regions, and CSU built the Bachelor of Wine Business around that geography: the course is run out of the National Wine and Grape Industry Centre, a joint centre with the NSW DPI and the Australian Wine Research Institute, so students are studying wine commerce next to people doing actual viticulture and oenology research, not in a business school treating wine as a case study.

The course covers the full grape-to-glass chain: viticulture and winemaking basics so graduates understand the product technically, then sales, marketing, export and wine tourism units aimed at running or working in a cellar door, distributor, or export operation. It's completed over 192 points, available full-time on campus or via CSU's online/blended options over a longer part-time timeframe, which suits people already working in the industry. Career outcomes lean toward wine marketing, brand management, export sales and cellar door/hospitality management rather than winemaking itself. The sister Bachelor of Wine Science covers the production side for students who want that instead.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Viticulture and Oenology; Marketing Principles; Accounting Fundamentals; Wine Business Environment
Year 2: Wine Marketing; Export and International Wine Trade; Wine Tourism; Elective
Year 3: Cellar Door and Direct-to-Consumer Sales; Wine Business Strategy; Supply Chain Management; Elective
Year 4 (or part-time equivalent): Industry placement; Wine Business Capstone Project; advanced electives
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Education (with specialisations)
description:
CSU is one of the largest producers of teaching graduates in Australia, and its Master of Education is built for people already in the classroom rather than as an entry qualification. Most students are practising teachers upgrading their credentials or repositioning into leadership, special education, TESOL or curriculum roles while still working. It's delivered predominantly online with intensive residential schools for some specialisations, a model CSU has run for teacher education longer than most competitors.

Students pick a specialisation stream (options typically include Educational Leadership, TESOL, Inclusive and Special Education, and Literacy) after a shared core of research and pedagogy subjects, and the course culminates in either a research project or an extended professional inquiry tied to the student's own school context, which makes the degree noticeably more workplace-embedded than a purely theoretical education master's.
curriculum:
Core (all students): Educational Research Methods; Contemporary Issues in Education; Leading Learning and Change
Specialisation stream (choose one): Educational Leadership; TESOL; Inclusive and Special Education; Literacy and Numeracy — four subjects per stream
Final subjects: Professional Inquiry Project or Research Dissertation; Elective from a second specialisation area
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in education or a related discipline, or teaching qualification
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.5) or equivalent

name: Master of Professional Information Technology
description:
Charles Sturt built its IT postgraduate offering around distance and online delivery long before it was standard practice, and the Master of Professional Information Technology still carries that DNA: most students study while working, often changing careers into IT from a completely unrelated first degree. The course doesn't assume a computing background: early subjects cover programming fundamentals, systems analysis and database design before moving into higher-level electives, so a former teacher or accountant can genuinely finish job-ready rather than half-converted.

What sets it apart from a generic IT master's is the flexibility to specialise late rather than early. Students pick up strands in areas like cyber security, data analytics or enterprise systems once they've got the grounding, and CSU's long history running IT via its regional study centres means the online cohort experience is mature rather than an afterthought. Discussion forums, recorded lectures and academic support are built for people juggling full-time work, not bolted onto an on-campus model.

Graduates tend to land in business analyst, systems administrator or junior developer roles, with a meaningful share moving into government IT given CSU's strong ties to NSW public sector employers through its Wagga Wagga and Bathurst campuses.
curriculum:
Year 1, Session 1: Fundamentals of Programming; Database Design; IT Project Management; Systems Analysis and Design
Year 1, Session 2: Network Design and Administration; Enterprise Architecture; IT Governance and Risk; Elective
Year 2, Session 1: Specialisation subject 1 (choose one strand: Cyber Security, Data Analytics, Enterprise Systems); Specialisation subject 2; Research Methods in IT; Elective
Year 2, Session 2: Specialisation subject 3; Specialisation subject 4; IT Capstone Project; Elective
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant or any discipline (typical Australian postgrad IT/CS entry bar used as approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
CQU's Bachelor of Arts covers Creative Writing, Literary Studies, Journalism and a Psychology major with a broader, less statistics-heavy approach than the dedicated Bachelor of Psychological Science, a genuine option for students who want psychological literacy without the accreditation-driven statistics load. Each major runs 8 units, generally weighted toward advanced-level content in the second half (Creative Writing runs its own six-unit structure with two double-weighted units, a slightly different shape from the rest).

Work-integrated learning is built in as a placement loosely tied to a student's major discipline rather than a rigid single-track internship, giving CQU's largely regional and online cohort some flexibility about where that placement actually happens, a meaningful accommodation for students who aren't based near a major media or publishing hub but still want the Journalism or Creative Writing major.
curriculum:
Major (8 units, typically 2 Level 1 + 6 advanced) chosen from Creative Writing, Literary Studies, Journalism, or Psychology (broad, non-accredited stream)
Second major or minor from the same or a related humanities discipline
Work-integrated learning placement, matched to the student's major discipline
Research and academic writing foundation units in Year 1
Elective units to complete the degree
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR/selection rank as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
CQUniversity's Bachelor of Business is unusually broad on majors for a regional university: Accounting, Digital Business, Financial Planning, Hospitality Management, HR Management, Management, Marketing and Property are all on the list, though not every major runs at every campus, so the actual mix a student gets depends heavily on whether they're at Rockhampton, Bundaberg, Cairns, Mackay, Townsville, Brisbane or Sydney, or studying online.

Property and Financial Planning majors stand out as less commonly offered at other Australian business schools; the Financial Planning major in particular is designed against the education standards required for financial adviser registration, giving graduates a direct professional pathway that a generic business degree wouldn't provide. Most students take a double major (two 8-unit blocks) rather than a single major with electives, reflecting CQU's emphasis on giving regional and online students broad employability across multiple functions rather than narrow specialisation.
curriculum:
Business core units: Accounting Principles, Economics, Marketing Fundamentals, Business Law, Management Principles, Business Statistics
Major 1 (8 units) chosen from Accounting, Digital Business, Financial Planning, Hospitality Management, HR Management, Management, Marketing, Property
Major 2 (8 units) or two 4-unit minors from the same list
Work-integrated learning or internship unit (major-dependent)
Capstone: Strategic Management or Business Consultancy Project
Electives to complete the total credit point load
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR/selection rank as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
CQU's engineering degree leans hard into dual-major combinations that most Australian engineering schools don't offer as standard: Electrical with Data Analytics, Electrical with Information Processing, and Civil with Humanitarian Engineering sit alongside the conventional Civil, Electrical and Mechanical majors, plus standalone Mechatronic and Resource Systems Engineering majors that run to 23 units rather than the standard load.

First year is structured around problem-solving, teamwork and professional practice before the major-specific technical content ramps up, and sustainability runs as an explicit overarching theme rather than a single elective, a reflection of CQU's regional footprint across mining, agriculture and resources-heavy parts of Queensland, where its engineering graduates most often end up working. The Humanitarian Engineering strand within Civil is a genuine point of difference, aimed at students interested in disaster response and development-sector infrastructure work rather than conventional civil contracting.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Foundations, Engineering Mathematics, Engineering Mechanics, Professional Practice and Teamwork
Major (choose one): Civil, Civil with Humanitarian Engineering, Electrical, Electrical with Data Analytics, Electrical with Information Processing, Mechanical, or 23-unit Mechatronic/Resource Systems Engineering
Sustainable development principles integrated across major units
Industry-based capstone design project in final year
Work-integrated learning/industry placement component
Accredited pathway to Engineers Australia professional recognition
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion with strong mathematics; ATAR/selection rank as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
The Bachelor of IT at CQUniversity runs core IT units through the first term before splitting students into Application Development, Business Analysis, or Cyber Security majors from term two onward.
