Cyber security in particular has become the major CQU pushes hardest in its marketing given the national skills shortage, and it's ACS-accredited at the professional level like the rest of the degree.

What sets the final-year structure apart is the explicit choice between an internship stream and a project stream for the capstone. Students on the internship track spend roughly 32 hours a week for ten consecutive weeks embedded with a host organisation, which is a substantial placement compared to a single-unit industry project elsewhere. For students who can't commit to that block (a real constraint for CQU's large regional and mature-age cohort juggling existing jobs), the project stream delivers an equivalent capstone experience without leaving paid work.
curriculum:
Term 1 core: Introduction to Programming, Computer Systems and Networks, Database Fundamentals, ICT Professional Practice
Major (from Term 2): Application Development, Business Analysis, or Cyber Security
Minor or elective units in a second ICT area, digital media, entrepreneurship, or marketing
Capstone (final term, choice of stream): Internship (32 hrs/week for 10 weeks with a host organisation) or Project
ACS-accredited at professional level on completion
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR/selection rank as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
CQU's Bachelor of Nursing is designed around the reality that most of its students are studying regionally or fully online, with campus-based support available in Brisbane, Bundaberg, Cairns, Mackay, Rockhampton and Townsville. Before any of the 800 required placement hours happen, students complete simulated clinical training at a nominated Clinical Learning Centre, a practical necessity given how spread out CQU's delivery footprint is across Queensland.

The placement structure is genuinely demanding for regional and online students in a way a metropolitan-campus student might not experience: CQU is upfront that placements are sourced as locally as possible but aren't guaranteed to be, and students may need to relocate temporarily and cover the associated costs themselves. That trade-off, flexibility to study from almost anywhere in regional Queensland against the possibility of having to travel for clinical blocks, is a defining feature of the course rather than an edge case.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing, Anatomy and Physiology, Introduction to Primary Health Care, first of six professional practice placements (following simulated Clinical Learning Centre training)
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology, Pathophysiology, Research and Evidence-Based Practice, continued placement blocks
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Maternal and Child Health, Aged and Chronic Care, Emergency Nursing, final capstone placement and Transition to Professional Practice
800 hours of professional practice placement across 6 blocks, commencing in first year
Eligible for AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse on completion
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR/selection rank as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
The Bachelor of Psychological Science is CQU's APAC-accredited foundation degree: 16 core psychology units plus a minor (either one 8-unit minor or two 4-unit minors) meet the Level 1 competencies needed to progress into the university's own one-year Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours) and, from there, into provisional registration pathways toward becoming a psychologist.

The capstone is a supervised applied project tackling a genuine real-world problem rather than a purely theoretical thesis, and the course is offered both online and on-campus, a meaningful distinction for CQU given how much of its psychology cohort studies from regional Queensland towns without ready access to a psychology department. Compared to CQU's separate Bachelor of Science (Psychology), this is the more direct route into the accredited registration pipeline.
curriculum:
16 core psychology units covering: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Psychology, Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Research Methods and Statistics I & II, Personality and Individual Differences, Abnormal Psychology, Psychological Assessment
Minor: one 8-unit minor or two 4-unit minors from outside psychology
Capstone: supervised applied research project on a real-world issue
APAC-accredited, satisfying Level 1 competencies for 3-year undergraduate psychology
Pathway: Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours), 1 year full-time
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR/selection rank as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Arts
description:
This is CQUniversity's coursework Master of Arts, built specifically as the next step for graduates of its own Bachelor of Arts, Digital Media, Music or Theatre degrees: it accelerates from the nominal 18 months down to a single full-time year if the incoming student already holds relevant CQU undergraduate credit, which is a fairly generous articulation compared to most postgraduate arts programs elsewhere.

The degree is explicitly research-oriented rather than a coursework grab-bag: candidates work with an academic advisor to scope a specific topic within the humanities or arts, produce a literature review, and build toward an independent dissertation-style project, which makes it a genuine bridge into PhD study for students who didn't do an honours year at undergraduate level.
curriculum:
Advanced coursework units in the chosen specialisation (drawn from Arts, Digital Media, Music, or Theatre disciplines)
Research Methods and Literature Review unit
Dissertation planning and academic advisor consultation
Independent research project/dissertation in final stage
Audition or interview required at entry for creative-practice specialisations
Accelerated 1-year pathway available for CQU Bachelor of Arts graduates with relevant credit; 18 months standard
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Business Management
description:
Master of Business Management sits as CQU's discipline-based alternative to a full MBA. Core units in applied business research, accounting, finance, HR, marketing and business communication feed into a specific major (Marketing, International Business, HR Management, Leading Organisational Change, or the less common Emergency and Health Services Management), rather than the generalist case-study approach an MBA takes.

The Emergency and Health Services Management major is a genuine point of difference nationally: CQU has strong regional ties to emergency services and health administration in Queensland, and this major reflects that connection directly. Every major offers an optional internship, and a professional practice and career development unit runs through the degree asking students to self-assess their own leadership and management competencies rather than treating that reflection as incidental to the coursework.
curriculum:
Core units: Applied Business Research, Accounting for Managers, Finance, Human Resource Management, Marketing Management, Business Communication, Professional Practice and Career Development
Major (choose one): Marketing, International Business, Human Resource Management, Leading Organisational Change, or Emergency and Health Services Management
Optional internship within the chosen major
Elective units, including options for an overseas study tour
Capstone: applied management project or professional practicum
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
CQUniversity's Master of IT opens with a shared first term (project management, introductory programming, ICT services management, and information systems analysis and design) before splitting students into a major-plus-minor structure across networks and information security, mobile application development, or software design and development. That structure is deliberate: CQU expects a chunk of its IT postgrad intake to be career-changers rather than CS graduates, so the common term functions as a leveller before the specialised units start.

Because the degree is delivered across three terms a year rather than two semesters, students who front-load their study can complete faster than the nominal 24 months, and there are built-in exit points at 4 units (Graduate Certificate) and 8 units (Graduate Diploma) if circumstances change. ACS accreditation means graduates can pursue Australian Computer Society membership on the way to a Skills Assessment for skilled migration, which is a genuine driver of enrolment for CQU's substantial international IT cohort.
curriculum:
Term 1 (common core): Project Management, Introduction to Programming, ICT Services Management, Information Systems Analysis and Design
Major (choose one): Networks and Information Security, Mobile Application Development, or Software Design and Development
Minor: second major area selected from the remaining two options
Elective units to complete the 24-month, three-term-a-year structure
Exit points: Graduate Certificate in IT (4 units), Graduate Diploma in IT (8 units)
Capstone project or industry-based unit in final term
ACS-accredited at completion of the full Masters
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant or any discipline (typical Australian postgrad IT/CS entry bar used as approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Management for Engineers
description:
The Master of Management for Engineers is built for practising engineers who want the management credential without doing a generalist MBA. Nine core units cover organisational behaviour, project management, operations, accounting for management and organisational governance, framed throughout with engineering contexts rather than generic case studies, and up to seven elective units let students pull from business analytics, HR, marketing or digital communications depending on where their career is heading.

Sustainable business development and globalisation run as a connecting theme across the core units rather than a single bolt-on subject, which lines up with CQU's broader engineering faculty emphasis on sustainability. An internship stream is available for students who want direct industry exposure rather than filling the elective load purely with coursework, useful for engineers moving from a technical role into their first management position.
curriculum:
Core units (9): People and Organisations, Organisational Governance and Leadership, Operations Management, Innovation and Sustainable Business Development, Project Management Concepts, Accounting for Management, Human Resource Management, Marketing and Digital Communications, Business Analytics
Elective units (up to 7), selectable from across the university's business and management offerings
Optional internship stream in place of some electives
Capstone unit applying management theory to an engineering-sector case or workplace project
24-month nominal duration
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in engineering or related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
Curtin's Bachelor of Commerce runs on a build-it-yourself model: a major is a fixed set of eight units, and students choose the first one in their opening semester with guidance from an advisor rather than being locked in at application. A second major can come from the rest of the Commerce list or, less obviously, from the Arts or Creative Arts major lists, which is how a Curtin commerce student ends up graduating with, say, Marketing paired with Screen Arts rather than a strictly business-only transcript.

The final-year capstone is framed around international business exposure specifically, applying entrepreneurial and critical-thinking skills to something closer to a live workplace problem than a standard assessed group project, which reflects Curtin's broader push to make its business degrees read as job-ready to Perth's resources, logistics, and professional services employers rather than purely theoretical.

Given Curtin's business school accreditation (AACSB) and its physical size, one of the largest commerce cohorts in Western Australia, the major combinations available (Accounting, Banking and Finance, Economics, Human Resource Management, International Business, Management, Marketing, among others) are broader than most WA competitors offer inside a single degree.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introductory business units across accounting, economics, and management, first major selection, foundational quantitative unit
Year 2: Core major units (four of eight), second major or minor units, electives
Year 3: Remaining major units, capstone experience (international business focus, applied workplace-style project), electives
Structure: one major minimum (8 units), optional second major from Commerce, Arts, or Creative Arts lists
admission_requirements: WACE/Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Creative Arts
description:
Curtin's Bachelor of Creative Arts narrows the choice to three majors (Fine Art, Screen Arts, or Theatre Arts) rather than the sprawling major list attached to the Bachelor of Arts, which makes it a more deliberately practice-focused degree from day one. Students build a thorough grounding in both the theory and the practice of their chosen discipline, then layer on a specialisation drawn from a different Creative Arts area or effectively any other field they meet the prerequisites for, so a Theatre Arts major might specialise in Screen Arts, or step entirely outside Creative Arts for something like marketing or writing.

The capstone unit is where the degree's practical bent shows most clearly: Fine Art students mount an exhibition, Theatre Arts students stage a performance, Screen Arts students complete a screen project, all functioning as a public-facing portfolio piece rather than a written exam or essay.

Curtin's location gives Screen Arts students in particular a practical edge. Perth's screen production sector has grown considerably with state government screen incentives drawing international productions to WA, and Curtin has leaned into that with industry-facing production units.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introductory major units (theory and practice foundations), specialisation exploration units, electives
Year 2: Core major units, specialisation units (Fine Art, Screen Arts, or Theatre Arts, or another discipline), electives
Year 3: Advanced major units, capstone project (exhibition, performance, or screen project depending on major), remaining electives
Majors offered: Fine Art, Screen Arts, Theatre Arts
admission_requirements: WACE/Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Curtin runs its engineering degree through a common Engineering Foundation Year before anyone commits to a discipline. First-year students cover fundamentals shared across all engineering areas and only choose their major (from Chemical, Petroleum, Electrical and Electronic, Mechanical, Mechatronic, Civil and Construction, Metallurgical, Mining, Industrial and Systems, or Environmental Engineering) heading into second year, which gives students who arrive unsure between, say, mechanical and mechatronic engineering a genuine trial period rather than forcing a decision at enrolment.

The major list itself is a tell for what Curtin is known for regionally: Metallurgical, Mining, and Petroleum Engineering majors sit alongside the more universally-offered options, a direct reflection of Perth's position as headquarters city for most of Australia's mining and resources companies, and Curtin's engineering graduates in those majors tend to move directly into WA's resources sector rather than needing to relocate.

Final year is a genuine honours research project done independently within the chosen major, and students can add a four-unit specialisation or minor on top of their major to sharpen the degree toward a specific career direction, pairing Mechanical Engineering with a renewable energy specialisation, for instance.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Foundation Year — common units across all disciplines (engineering mathematics, mechanics, computer-aided design, introductory programming)
Year 2: Major-specific core units (Chemical, Petroleum, Electrical and Electronic, Mechanical, Mechatronic, Civil and Construction, Metallurgical, Mining, Industrial and Systems, or Environmental Engineering)
Year 3: Advanced major units, specialisation or minor units (four units), professional practice exposure
Year 4: Honours-level independent research project, remaining advanced major units
Structure: pre-major foundation year, one Engineering major, optional four-unit specialisation or minor
admission_requirements: WACE/Year 12 completion with strong mathematics/physics; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Psychology (Honours)
description:
Curtin's Bachelor of Psychology (Honours) is APAC-accredited and runs as a combined four-year sequence rather than a standard three-year degree with honours bolted on afterward. The honours stream is embedded as an expected continuation for students who hit the mark, not a separate application most students won't get into. That said, entry to the honours stream itself is competitive: a minimum 70% average across the 14 core second- and third-year psychology units is required, and offers go out by invitation rather than automatic progression.

The APAC accreditation is the whole point structurally: it's what makes graduates eligible for associate membership of the Australian Psychological Society and sets up the standard Australian pathway toward provisional registration and eventual practice, which distinguishes this from a psychological-science degree that stops short of the accredited sequence.

Because the honours year functions as a genuine research year within the four-year structure rather than an optional fifth year, students plan their thesis topic and supervisor arrangements earlier than they would in a bolt-on honours model, and Curtin's psychology school covers a fairly broad research spread from clinical and health psychology through to forensic and organisational applications.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introductory Psychology (Level One sequence), foundational science or statistics unit, electives
Year 2: Core psychology units (part of the 14-unit core sequence) — social, developmental, biological psychology
Year 3: Remaining core units — cognition, research methods, psychopathology, personality; honours stream invitation based on 70% average across core units
Year 4 (Honours): independent research thesis, advanced seminars
APAC accredited; graduates eligible for APS associate membership
admission_requirements: WACE/Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Science (Nursing)
description:
Curtin's undergraduate nursing degree runs 840 hours of clinical placement across the course (hospitals, private practices, aged care, rural health settings, and mental health services), which starts as early as second semester of first year, meaning students are shadowing real clinical environments well before most other health degrees would send them out. Placements can involve shift work including night duty and weekends by design, since the point is exposure to how hospitals actually run rather than a sanitised nine-to-five version of nursing.

The course structure leans heavily on simulation before fieldwork: Curtin's simulated practice labs are used to build competency in a controlled setting first, so that clinical placement time is spent applying skills rather than learning them cold in front of a patient. Given Curtin's status as WA's largest nursing school by intake, the simulation infrastructure (mock wards, standardised patients) is a genuine scale advantage over smaller providers.

Students are pushed toward interprofessional learning throughout, working alongside pharmacy, physiotherapy, and medical students in shared units rather than training in a nursing-only bubble, which mirrors how WA Health actually staffs its wards and is meant to make the transition into a graduate nurse year less of a culture shock.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Introduction to Professional Nursing, simulated practice units; clinical placement begins second semester
Year 2: Adult Health Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology for Nursing, interprofessional learning units, clinical placements (hospital and community settings)
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Rural and Remote Health placement option, Aged Care Nursing, capstone clinical placement block, Transition to Professional Practice
Total: 840 hours clinical placement, 216 hours simulated practice across the course; registration pathway with Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia
admission_requirements: WACE/Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Science (Science)
description:
Curtin's Bachelor of Science (Science) covers an unusually wide net of majors for one degree title: Agricultural Science, Earth Sciences, Environmental Biology and Ecology, Environmental Science, Food Science and Technology, ICT, Marine Science, Mineral Processing, Software Development, and Space and Planetary Science all sit under it, which reflects Curtin's identity as a resources-and-industry-adjacent university rather than a pure research-science school. Mineral Processing and Space and Planetary Science in particular are majors you won't find at most Australian universities, tied respectively to WA's mining sector and Curtin's own astronomy research group (home to some of the country's radio astronomy and remote sensing work).

Students pick at least one science major and can double up, with extension specialisations layered on for those wanting to go deeper into a sub-area without adding a whole second major, plus minors that don't carry first-year prerequisites for students who want breadth without planning it out from day one.

Honours is a genuine one-year add-on rather than an embedded final-year component, which means students finishing the standard three years and wanting a research-track future need to apply separately and typically need a strong average across their major units.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundational science units (two areas typically), mathematics or statistics service unit, introductory major unit(s)
Year 2: Core major units, laboratory or fieldwork components, extension specialisation or minor units
Year 3: Advanced major units, capstone or research-methods unit within major, remaining minor or elective units
Optional Year 4 (Honours): independent research thesis, separate application required, competitive entry
admission_requirements: WACE/Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Technology (Computer Systems and Networking)
description:
This Bachelor of Technology sits in the more hands-on end of Curtin's ICT offerings: hardware, networking (LANs and WANs specifically), network management, and Internet of Things content, with Python and Linux taught progressively from basics through to advanced application rather than assumed as prior knowledge. It's a more infrastructure-and-systems-focused degree than a standard software-development-flavoured IT degree, aimed at students who want to end up managing networks and infrastructure rather than writing application code full-time.

The course is explicit about industry certification alignment: Cisco and Amazon Web Services certifications are named targets the curriculum is built to prepare graduates for, which matters in a job market where certifications often carry as much weight as the degree title itself for network engineering and cloud infrastructure roles.

The professional practice requirement (minimum 8 weeks, logged formally) pushes students into real workplace exposure before graduation, and Curtin frequently pairs this degree with a Bachelor of Information Technology as a double degree for students who want both the networking depth and the broader IT/software coverage on one transcript.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Programming (Python), Computer Systems Fundamentals, Networking Fundamentals, Linux Systems Administration (introductory)
Year 2: Network Programming and Distributed Computing, Security Fundamentals, LAN/WAN Design and Management, Linux Systems Administration (advanced)
Year 3: Internet of Things Systems, Network Management and Cloud Infrastructure, professional practice placement (minimum 8 weeks, logged), capstone networking project
Certification alignment: prepares students for industry certifications including Cisco and AWS
admission_requirements: WACE/Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Computing
description:
Curtin's Master of Computing is built for career-changers rather than CS undergrads looking to specialise further. The entry requirements assume a bachelor's degree plus some demonstrated programming, operating systems, and computing maths background, and the first stretch of the course deliberately re-teaches fundamentals before splitting into the three available majors: Computer Science, Cyber Security, or Artificial Intelligence.

What distinguishes it from a lot of one-size-fits-all computing conversion masters is the credit arrangement for Curtin's own graduates. Someone who already did a Bachelor of Technology or Bachelor of Computing at Curtin can be granted up to a full semester of credit, effectively turning this into an 18-month top-up for internal students while still running as a full two-year program for outsiders.

The major project in the final stage is where the specialisation actually gets tested. Students in the Cyber Security stream, for instance, end up doing something closer to an applied security research piece than a generic capstone, which matters given Perth's growing resources-sector demand for industrial cyber security skills specifically, an angle Curtin leans into given its mining and energy industry connections.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Programming Fundamentals, Computer Systems Fundamentals, Computing Mathematics, Database Systems
Semester 2: Data Structures and Algorithms, Networks and Security Fundamentals, major-track foundation unit, elective
Semester 3: Major units (Computer Science, Cyber Security, or Artificial Intelligence stream) x3, elective
Semester 4: Advanced major units, Major Project (capstone, specialisation-specific)
Credit: up to one semester's credit available for Curtin Bachelor of Technology or Bachelor of Computing graduates
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree with demonstrated knowledge/skills in programming, operating systems, and computing mathematics (or equivalent); Master Qualifying Program pathway available for those who don't meet direct entry.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall.

name: Master of Engineering Management
description:
Curtin's Master of Engineering Management is a genuinely fast program: 12 months full-time across three trimesters rather than the standard two years, jointly delivered by the Faculty of Science and Engineering and the Faculty of Business and Law, which shows up directly in the unit split: 125 credits of engineering units (choose five from six options) plus 125 credits of business units (four core plus one elective) plus a 50-credit engineering project capstone.

The business content isn't generic MBA filler bolted onto an engineering degree: strategic management, finance, projects and operations management, and human factors units are chosen specifically because they map onto what an engineer moving into a management or project-lead role actually needs, rather than a broad business-generalist curriculum. That combination is aimed at engineers already in the workforce who want to move from individual-contributor technical roles into managing engineering teams or projects, not new graduates.

Evening class availability is a deliberate accommodation for that same audience: working engineers studying part-time over a minimum 24 months rather than pausing a career for full-time study, which is a genuinely different student profile than most of Curtin's other engineering postgraduate offerings attract.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Engineering units (two of five chosen options), Strategic Management
Trimester 2: Engineering units (remaining chosen options), Finance for Engineers, Projects and Operations Management
Trimester 3: Human Factors in Engineering Management, business elective, Engineering Project (capstone, 50 credits)
Full-time: 12 months across three trimesters; part-time minimum 24 months, two units per trimester; evening classes available
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Nursing Practice
description:
Curtin's Master of Nursing Practice is the graduate-entry pathway into nursing registration for people who already hold a degree in something else. It runs four semesters plus a summer coursework term, condensed but not shortcut, since it still carries 840 hours of professional practice experience and 216 hours of simulated practice, the same clinical hour benchmarks the undergraduate degree runs on, just compressed into two years instead of three.

Because the cohort is graduate-entry, the theory content moves faster than an undergraduate nursing unit would: physical, biological, psychological and social science content is treated as something students can absorb quickly given prior degree-level study skills, with more weight placed on advanced clinical development and interprofessional learning than on foundational science literacy.

Professional practice placements run full-time and include shift and night duty work, mirroring the undergraduate program's approach of exposing students to how wards actually operate rather than easing them in. It's a deliberate design choice given these students will be entering the workforce as registered nurses within two years rather than three, so the placement intensity compensates for the shorter timeline.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice (accelerated), Anatomy and Physiology, Pharmacology, simulated practice units
Semester 2: Adult Health Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, clinical placement block (professional practice hours begin)
Summer term: intensive coursework unit, additional simulated practice
Semester 3: Complex Care Nursing, interprofessional learning unit, clinical placement
Semester 4: Transition to Professional Practice, capstone clinical placement block
Total: 840 hours professional practice, 216 hours simulated practice; leads to eligibility for registration with Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a health-related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Professional Engineering
description:
Curtin's Master of Professional Engineering is aimed squarely at Engineers Australia Stage 1 competency accreditation: students graduate meeting the academic benchmark for professional engineer status, with a formal logbook requirement tracking at least 12 weeks of professional practice exposure alongside the coursework, which is a heavier practical documentation burden than a typical taught masters carries.

Major choice spans Chemical, Civil, Electrical and Electronic, Mechanical, Mining, Petroleum, and Software Engineering. The Mining and Petroleum options in particular reflect Curtin's position as the go-to engineering school for Western Australia's resources sector, with a research and industry-partnership base (WA School of Mines heritage feeds into some of this) that eastern-states universities generally can't match for those two majors specifically.

The final-year major research or design project is meant to genuinely integrate everything from the coursework rather than function as an add-on. Students draw on both the technical major content and a research methodology grounding, working alongside academic researchers rather than purely on an industry-sponsored brief, though industry-linked projects are common given Curtin's mining and energy sector ties.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Mathematics and Modelling, major-specific core units (Chemical, Civil, Electrical and Electronic, Mechanical, Mining, Petroleum, or Software), Research Methods, professional practice logbook commencement
Year 2: Advanced major units, engineering management or industry-context unit, Major Research or Design Project (capstone), completion of 12 weeks professional practice exposure
Accreditation: meets Engineers Australia Stage 1 competency requirements, subject to accreditation
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a related engineering discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Psychology (Professional)
description:
Curtin's Master of Psychology (Professional) is a genuinely compressed program: one year full-time, integrating coursework, a research project, and supervised practical placements all within twelve months, which is unusually fast for a professional psychology masters and reflects Curtin's design choice to front-load the experiential placement work rather than spread it across a longer program. Part-time enrolment exists but is limited and offered mainly on equity grounds rather than as a standard option.

The placement component is where the degree earns its "professional" label specifically: students are taught and then supervised administering psychological assessments, conducting mental status examinations, and applying counselling skills in real placement settings, not just discussing these skills in seminar. That hands-on structure is what leads toward the practical competencies assessed in the National Psychology Examination.

Graduates who pass the National Psychology Examination become eligible for registration with the Psychology Board of Australia, making this one of the more direct routes from an accredited undergraduate psychology sequence into registered practice, compressed into a single intensive year rather than the two-year professional masters some other universities require.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Advanced Psychological Assessment, Psychopathology and Diagnosis, Counselling Skills, placement orientation and commencement
Semester 2: Research Project (professional application focus), supervised clinical placement (assessment and counselling practice), Ethics and Professional Practice in Psychology
Throughout: integrated placement hours across both semesters combining assessment, mental status examination, and counselling skill application
Outcome: eligibility to sit the National Psychology Examination and apply for registration with the Psychology Board of Australia
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in psychology or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
Deakin's Bachelor of Arts is a genuinely flexible humanities degree: students pick two majors from a list spanning literature, history, politics, sociology, creative writing, and languages, rather than being funnelled into one fixed track, and the same degree structure runs across Burwood, Geelong and Cloud Campus online delivery. It's less a single defined program than a framework, which suits students who aren't sure yet which humanities discipline they want to specialise in.

A recurring theme in Deakin's arts teaching is linking coursework to employability early: most majors include at least one unit built around a real-world writing, research or communication project rather than purely essay-based assessment, and Deakin's careers-focused STP-coded employability units are compulsory across its degrees, arts included. Students can also add a diploma of languages or a study-abroad trimester without extending the degree, which is a genuine structural option rather than an add-on marketing line.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introductory units in two chosen majors (e.g. History, Literature, Politics, Sociology, Creative Writing); Academic and Career skills unit
Year 2: Major subjects continue (2 per major); Elective from a third discipline
Year 3: Advanced major subjects; capstone or research project unit in at least one major; remaining electives
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
Deakin Business School holds triple accreditation (AACSB, EQUIS and AMBA), a status only a small number of business schools worldwide carry, and the Bachelor of Commerce is the school's broad flagship undergraduate degree: students choose from majors including accounting, finance, marketing, management, human resource management and business analytics, or combine more than one. It's offered at Burwood, Geelong Waurn Ponds, and online through Deakin's Cloud Campus, with the same majors generally available across delivery modes.

A distinguishing feature is Deakin's Work Integrated Learning unit requirement, which most commerce majors satisfy through an internship, consulting project with an external organisation, or a simulated business challenge rather than pure coursework. The university markets this heavily as differentiating its commerce graduates from those of pure-theory programs. Students with the accounting major who complete the right unit combination are also eligible for accreditation pathways with CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants ANZ.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Principles; Economic Principles; Marketing Principles; Quantitative Methods for Business
Year 2: Business Law; Organisational Behaviour; core major subjects begin (1–2 units per major)
Year 3: Major subjects continue (3–4 units); Work Integrated Learning unit (internship, consulting project or business challenge)
Final trimester: Capstone major subject; remaining electives or second major units
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Criminology
description:
Deakin's criminology program, taught mainly out of the Geelong Waurn Ponds and online cohorts within the School of Humanities and Social Sciences, has built a reputation partly around Australian-context research into policing, youth justice and cybercrime rather than importing a US-textbook criminology curriculum wholesale. Students move from foundational theories of crime and justice into applied units on policing, corrections, and increasingly cybercrime and digital forensics, an area Deakin has invested in given its parallel strength in cyber security.

The degree is commonly combined with a second degree: Deakin offers formal double-degree pairings with Criminology plus Laws, Psychological Science, or Cyber Security, which is a genuine structural feature rather than marketing, since students in those combined degrees take a blended unit set rather than simply two separate degrees end to end. A work placement or research project unit toward the end of the single degree lets students test interests in policing, youth services, or policy work before graduating.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Criminology; Crime, Justice and Society; Understanding Deviance; Introduction to Law
Year 2: Policing and Society; Youth and Crime; Research Methods for Criminology; Elective
Year 3: Corrections and Community Justice; Cybercrime and Digital Investigation; Criminal Justice Policy; Work placement or research project unit
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Cyber Security
description:
Deakin's cyber security degree runs out of its Centre for Cyber Security Research and Innovation, and the course structure reflects that research base: units on computer crime and digital forensics sit alongside more conventional network security content, and the degree can be paired as a double degree with Criminology or Laws for students aiming at policy, investigative or legal cyber roles rather than purely technical ones. That double-degree option is a genuinely distinctive structural feature compared with a standalone technical cyber security degree.

The standard single degree runs 24 credit points over three years full-time, split across foundational computing units, core security subjects, and later electives that let students lean toward penetration testing/technical security or governance and forensics. Deakin has also run national cyber security competitions and industry partnerships that regularly feed into student projects, giving students exposure to real incident-response style scenarios rather than only textbook case studies.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming Fundamentals; Networking Fundamentals; Introduction to Cyber Security; Systems Analysis
Year 2: Network Security; Digital Forensics; Cryptography; Elective
Year 3: Penetration Testing and Ethical Hacking; Security Governance and Risk; Cybercrime Investigation; Capstone Security Project
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Deakin's engineering degree is taught almost entirely out of Waurn Ponds in Geelong, a campus purpose-built around applied engineering and manufacturing research. The adjacent Carbon Nexus facility, one of the few pilot-scale carbon fibre production lines in the world outside Japan and Germany, gives the mechanical and materials-leaning specialisations a genuine industry-research flavour that's hard to find elsewhere in Australia. Students choose a specialisation (civil, environmental, electrical, renewable energy, mechanical, or mechatronics) partway through the course.

The degree is accredited by Engineers Australia and includes compulsory professional practice units around safety and project-based learning from first year, plus a substantial industry-based capstone project in the final year. Deakin also runs a parallel Bachelor of Engineering (Industry) (Honours) with built-in paid industry placements for students who want workplace experience baked into the structure rather than left to a single work-integrated-learning unit.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Mathematics; Introduction to Engineering Practice; Mechanics; Materials Science; Safety and Project-Oriented Learning
Year 2: Thermodynamics; Circuits and Systems; specialisation-track subjects begin (Civil / Electrical / Mechanical / Mechatronics / Renewable Energy / Environmental)
Year 3: Advanced specialisation subjects; Engineering Management; Elective
Year 4: Capstone Engineering Project (industry-based); remaining specialisation subjects; professional practice unit
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion with strong mathematics; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of International Studies
description:
International Studies at Deakin is built around a compulsory in-country component: students typically undertake a study period abroad or an international internship as part of the degree, not as an optional add-on, which reflects the university's positioning of the course as preparation for careers in diplomacy, international development, trade, or global business rather than as a generalist arts degree with an international flavour. Deakin has long-standing exchange partnerships across Asia, Europe and the Americas that this degree draws on directly.

Coursework blends international relations and global politics with a language stream (options have included Indonesian, Chinese, French, Spanish and others) and area-studies electives, and a research or professional placement unit toward the end lets students apply the language and policy background to something practical, typically a placement with an NGO, government department, or company with international operations.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to International Relations; Global Politics; Language stream unit 1; Global Issues
Year 2: International Political Economy; Comparative Politics; Language stream unit 2; Area Studies elective
Year 3: Study abroad trimester or international internship; Language stream unit 3; International Studies research project
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Deakin runs nursing across multiple Victorian campuses (Burwood, Geelong Waurn Ponds, and previously Warrnambool) and puts real weight behind simulation-based learning before students ever hit a ward. Its clinical simulation labs are built to mirror real hospital environments, which the university uses to front-load confidence before the roughly 800+ hours of clinical placement required for national accreditation. The course is accredited by ANMAC and the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, with graduates eligible for RN registration.

The curriculum runs from bioscience and health assessment fundamentals into progressively more complex clinical subjects (medical-surgical nursing, mental health, aged care, and community nursing), with a placement block attached to nearly every trimester rather than one concentrated block, so students are in real clinical settings from relatively early in the course rather than only in their final year.
curriculum:
Year 1: Anatomy and Physiology; Foundations of Nursing Practice; Health Assessment; Pharmacology 1; clinical placement
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing 1 and 2; Mental Health Nursing; Pharmacology 2; clinical placement blocks
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing; Aged Care and Chronic Illness; Community and Primary Health Nursing; Transition to Professional Practice; extended clinical placement
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
Deakin's Bachelor of Psychological Science is APAC-accredited, which matters because it's the first step of the standard Australian pathway into registration as a psychologist: students who want to go further typically follow it with Deakin's own fourth-year honours and then a master's or provisional registration pathway, and Deakin markets the degree explicitly around that multi-year trajectory rather than as a terminal qualification.

The course covers the core content APAC requires (biological bases of behaviour, cognition, social psychology, developmental psychology, research methods and statistics) with a heavier-than-average statistics and research methods load in the final year, reflecting the discipline's accreditation requirements. Deakin also runs the degree online through its Cloud Campus alongside on-campus delivery at Burwood and Geelong, which is less common for a laboratory/research-methods-heavy science degree and requires the university to run virtual practical and statistics tutorials at scale.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology; Biological Psychology; Research Methods 1; Lifespan Development
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology; Social Psychology; Research Methods and Statistics 2; Personality and Individual Differences
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology; Research Methods and Statistics 3; Psychological Assessment; Advanced elective and research project unit
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Deakin's MBA runs through a business school with AACSB, EQUIS and AMBA triple accreditation, and the course leans on that positioning. It's aimed at students with existing work experience rather than fresh graduates, and admission typically expects a few years in the workforce alongside the academic prerequisites. Delivery is flexible: trimester-based, available on campus at Burwood or through Deakin's Cloud Campus online model, which suits the working-professional cohort the MBA is actually built for.

Core units cover strategy, finance, leadership and business analytics, and students choose a specialisation stream (options have included areas like international business, marketing, or project management) before a capstone business strategy project that typically asks students to solve a real problem for their own organisation or an external partner, rather than a purely theoretical case study exercise.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Managing People and Organisations; Financial Management; Marketing Management
Trimester 2: Strategic Management; Business Analytics for Decision Making; Specialisation unit 1
Trimester 3: Specialisation units 2–3; Leadership in Practice
Final trimester: Capstone Business Strategy Project
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus relevant work experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Engineering
description:
Deakin's Master of Engineering is aimed at engineering graduates looking to deepen technical specialisation or pivot into a growth area. Offerings have included streams in areas like advanced manufacturing, renewable energy, and civil/structural engineering, reflecting the university's Waurn Ponds research strengths (including the Carbon Nexus carbon-fibre facility and Deakin's broader materials and manufacturing research groups). It's a coursework master's rather than a research degree, though most streams include a substantial engineering project unit.

Entry generally expects a relevant engineering bachelor's degree; students without one may be directed toward a longer pathway with additional foundation units. The degree suits engineers wanting formal postgraduate specialisation for career progression, plus a share of international students using it as a bridge toward Engineers Australia's Chartered status requirements.
curriculum:
Part A – Foundation (if required): bridging units in core engineering mathematics and systems
Part B – Core postgraduate engineering studies: Advanced Engineering Analysis, Engineering Project Management, Research Methods for Engineering
Part C – Specialisation stream (e.g. Advanced Manufacturing, Renewable Energy, Structural Engineering): 3–4 units
Part D – Capstone Engineering Project
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a related engineering discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
Deakin's Master of IT is organised into four deliberate stages rather than a loose bundle of electives: a foundation block for students without a strong computing background, a fundamentals block, a mastery block, and a final specialisation or elective block: two people can graduate with quite different course transcripts depending on how much catching-up they needed early on. That staged structure is one reason the course accepts graduates from non-IT bachelor's degrees, not just computer science.

Specialisation options run through Deakin's SIT/MIS-coded units and typically cover areas like data science, cyber security, and enterprise systems, taught out of Deakin's Cloud Campus infrastructure. Deakin was an early mover into fully online postgraduate IT delivery in Australia and still runs a large online cohort alongside on-campus students at Burwood. Work-integrated learning options (industry-based capstone projects with real client organisations) are a recurring feature of the specialisation stage, giving graduates a portfolio project rather than just coursework to point to.
curriculum:
Part A – Foundation IT Studies (for students needing a computing bridge): Programming, Systems Fundamentals, Database Fundamentals, Networking Fundamentals
Part B – Fundamental IT Studies: Software Engineering, IT Architecture, Data Modelling, Professional and Research Practice in IT
Part C – Mastery IT Studies: Advanced units in software development and systems, capstone-adjacent project subject
Part D – Specialisation or electives: four Level 7 SIT/MIS units (e.g. Cyber Security, Data Science, Enterprise Systems) or an industry-based capstone project
admission_requirements: Full (16cp) entry: bachelor's degree in any discipline. Reduced-credit pathways for a bachelor's/honours in a related IT discipline, or a bachelor's (any discipline) plus 2+ years relevant work experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
ECU's Bachelor of Arts covers a fairly focused set of four disciplines (Visual Arts, Creative and Professional Writing, English, and Historical and Political Studies) rather than the sprawling nine-or-more-major menu some other Australian BAs offer, which keeps the degree tighter but means students wanting, say, a straight sociology or anthropology major would need to look elsewhere. The Creative and Professional Writing major sits alongside ECU's newer standalone Bachelor of Creative Writing (launched 2025), so students who want writing as one part of a broader arts education rather than the sole focus of their degree take this route instead.

Historical and Political Studies pairs history with political science content rather than treating them as fully separate majors, giving students a combined lens on how historical events shape contemporary policy and politics, useful preparation for students eyeing government, policy, or journalism careers as much as academic history. Visual Arts, meanwhile, benefits from ECU's studio facilities and connections into WA's contemporary art scene, including opportunities tied to Perth galleries and public art commissions.

Combined degree options exist too, most notably Bachelor of Arts/Bachelor of Media and Communication, for students who want to pair a humanities major with a more vocationally-oriented communications qualification rather than choosing one over the other.
curriculum:
Foundation units: critical thinking and academic writing, introduction to research in the humanities
Majors (choose one): Visual Arts, Creative and Professional Writing, English, Historical and Political Studies
Years 2-3: major-specific unit sequence plus free electives across the university
Capstone: major project, exhibition, portfolio, or extended essay depending on major
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time, on campus or online
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The distinguishing feature of ECU's Bachelor of Business is the sports business major, which draws on the university's genuinely strong sport science research reputation (ECU runs one of Australia's better-known exercise and sport science schools) and pairs it with the standard business core, a combination that's harder to find with equal depth elsewhere. Other majors on offer include accounting, human resource management, management, marketing, and tourism, so the degree functions as a fairly conventional broad business qualification with one specific area of genuine differentiation.

Students who want to go deeper into the sport side specifically can also look at ECU's dedicated Bachelor of Global Sport Business Management or a Sport Business/Exercise Science double degree, which suggests the university has deliberately built out a cluster of related offerings rather than treating sport business as a single elective bolt-on. For students choosing the plain Bachelor of Business, the sports major functions as a genuine specialisation with its own unit sequence, not just a marketing label on generic management content.

Perth's business environment leans on mining services, government, and increasingly sport and tourism given WA's growing events calendar, and case studies and guest lecturer content in the degree tend to reflect that regional mix rather than a generic east-coast corporate framing.
curriculum:
Core units: Principles of Management, Marketing Fundamentals, Financial Accounting, Business Economics, Business Law, Business Analytics, Organisational Behaviour
Majors (choose one): Accounting, Human Resource Management, Management, Marketing, Sports Business, Tourism
Capstone: industry project or internship in final year
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time, on campus (Joondalup) or online
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Criminology and Justice
description:
This degree treats the criminal justice system as a single connected pipeline rather than teaching law, policing, courts, and corrections as separate silos. Students trace how a case moves from lawmaking through policing, prosecution, courts, and corrections, and examine how "justice" gets defined differently by different groups along the way. It draws explicitly on political science, psychology, sociology, and law as contributing disciplines rather than being housed purely within a law school framework, which shapes it toward a more social-science-flavoured criminology than a pre-law degree.

Two named majors, policing and youth work, let students specialise fairly early, and the degree's signature applied component is the Criminal Justice Review Project, a work-integrated learning unit where students conduct real review work connected to a justice agency rather than a simulated case study. Placements and industry-based projects with WA criminal justice agencies (police, courts, corrections, youth services) run alongside the 11 core units that anchor the degree regardless of major.

Graduates commonly move into policing, youth justice, corrections, community corrections, court administration, or policy roles within WA's justice and human services sector, and the degree can also combine with a Bachelor of Laws for students who want law and criminology credentials together.
curriculum:
Core units (11 total): Introduction to Criminology, Criminal Law and Justice, Policing and Society, Courts and Sentencing, Corrections and Community Justice, Youth Justice, Research Methods in Criminology, Justice Ethics
Majors (choose one): Policing, Youth Work
Applied learning: Criminal Justice Review Project (work-integrated learning), optional practicum or industry-based placement
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time, on campus or online
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
ECU's Bachelor of Education (Primary) leans on the university's placement network of more than 1,000 partner schools and early learning centres across Western Australia, spanning metro, regional, rural, and remote settings. It's a scale that gives students genuine choice in where they complete professional practice rather than being funnelled into a handful of nearby Perth schools by default.

Where the degree differentiates itself from a purely generalist primary teaching qualification is the option to add a formal specialisation in mathematics, music, science, or languages, layered on top of the generalist primary knowledge base. That's useful for graduates who want to be the designated specialist teacher in one of those areas at their eventual school, rather than a generalist competing for those roles without formal backing. The degree is nationally accredited and specifically meets Teacher Registration Board of Western Australia requirements, including the literacy and numeracy proficiency standards graduates must clear before registration.

Because WA has significant regional and remote school staffing need, a meaningful share of practicum placements and eventual graduate employment happens outside the Perth metro area, and the placement network is explicitly built to expose students to that range of school contexts before they're deciding where to apply for their first teaching job.
curriculum:
Core sequence: Child and Adolescent Development, Curriculum Studies (English, Mathematics, Science, HASS, Health and PE), Inclusive Education, Classroom Management, Aboriginal Education and Perspectives
Optional specialisation (choose one): Mathematics, Music, Science, Languages
Professional practice: staged placements across metro, regional, rural, and remote WA schools through all four years
Capstone: extended final-year professional practice placement with formal teaching standards assessment
Total: 4 years full-time, TRBWA-accredited
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Engineering Honours
description:
ECU offers an unusually wide spread of engineering specialisations for a mid-sized Australian university: civil, civil and environmental, chemical, mechanical, mechatronics, computer systems, electrical power, electrical and renewable energy, electronics and communications, and instrumentation control and automation are all separate accredited streams rather than a generic engineering degree with late-stage electives. The renewable energy and electrical power streams in particular line up with Western Australia's expanding renewables and grid infrastructure sector, which has grown substantially as WA moves away from its historical reliance on gas peaking plants.

The degree is delivered from the purpose-built Joondalup campus, which houses dedicated engineering labs and equipment for each specialisation rather than shared generalist facilities, meaningful for hands-on disciplines like mechatronics or instrumentation control where lab access shapes how much practical skill students actually build before graduating. It's a four-year Honours-embedded structure (Engineers Australia accredited), so students don't need to apply separately or add an extra year to graduate with Honours standing, unlike some universities that treat Honours as a bolt-on fifth year.

Given WA's resources sector dominance, civil, electrical power, and instrumentation control graduates in particular find a strong local employment pipeline into mining, oil and gas, and utilities work, while the computer systems and mechatronics streams connect more to Perth's smaller but growing tech and automation employers.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Engineering Mathematics, Engineering Mechanics, Materials Science, Circuit Theory, Thermodynamics, Engineering Design and Professional Practice
Specialisation streams (choose one): Chemical, Civil, Civil and Environmental, Computer Systems, Electrical Power, Electrical and Renewable Energy, Electronics and Communications, Instrumentation Control and Automation, Mechanical, Mechatronics
Year 3: stream-specific core units, industry-linked design project
Year 4 (Honours): capstone engineering project, advanced electives, professional experience placement
Total: 4 years full-time, Engineers Australia accredited, delivered at Joondalup
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 70-85 for competitive entry (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science
description:
Exercise and sport science is one of ECU's strongest-regarded programs nationally, and the degree sits inside a cluster of closely related offerings (a separate Exercise Science and Rehabilitation degree, a Sports Science and Football degree, and combined degrees pairing exercise science with sport business), which lets students self-select toward performance, rehabilitation, or management-adjacent career paths from the outset rather than treating "sport science" as one undifferentiated qualification.

Delivery mixes on-campus weekly labs and lectures with a blended format for some units (online content through the semester punctuated by two intensive on-campus lab/seminar blocks), which suits students balancing study with elite sport commitments, coaching work, or jobs in the fitness industry while completing the degree. ESSA (Exercise and Sports Science Australia) accreditation is built into the course design, so graduates come out eligible for ESSA credentialing without needing to complete bridging requirements afterward.

Career outcomes cited by the university span further than gym-floor exercise science roles: sports administration, teaching, coaching, strength and conditioning, corporate and workplace health, sports development, and performance analysis all show up as genuine graduate destinations, reflecting how broad the "sport science" label has become as an industry.
curriculum:
Core units: Functional Anatomy, Exercise Physiology, Biomechanics, Motor Control and Learning, Sport and Exercise Psychology, Nutrition and Performance, Strength and Conditioning, Research Methods in Sport Science
Practical components: on-campus laboratory sessions weekly (or intensive blocks for blended-format units)
Capstone: supervised placement or applied research project in an exercise, sport, or corporate health setting
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time, ESSA-accredited, on campus with some blended-delivery units
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Psychology (Honours)
description:
ECU folds Honours directly into its Bachelor of Psychology as a four-year combined structure rather than making students apply separately for a bolt-on fifth year, which is a genuine timeline advantage for students who already know they want the full APAC-accredited pathway toward provisional psychologist registration. Twelve core psychology units run through the degree, and one unit worth flagging specifically is Cross Cultural and Indigenous Psychology: not a universal fixture of Australian psych degrees, and it reflects a broader push across WA psychology programs to build cultural competency content directly into core curriculum rather than treating it as optional.

Students aren't locked into a single-track psychology-only degree either; ECU allows combining a psychology major with a second major or minor from elsewhere in the university, or choosing electives freely, which suits students who want breadth (say, criminology, business, or a language) alongside their psychology core. Entry into the Honours component specifically requires a Weighted Average Mark of 70+ with a credit average across second and third year units and the majority of psychology units, so it's a genuine academic gate rather than an automatic progression.

The degree is offered both online and on campus, and graduates with the completed Honours year are positioned for provisional registration with the Psychology Board of Australia or entry into further postgraduate training (clinical, counselling, organisational, forensic) depending on which specialisation they pursue after this degree.
curriculum:
Years 1-3: 12 core psychology units including Introduction to Psychology, Research Methods and Statistics, Cross Cultural and Indigenous Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Cognition and Learning, Social Psychology, Abnormal Psychology, Biological Psychology
Elective structure: combine with a second major/minor or free electives across the university
Year 4 (Honours): supervised empirical research thesis, advanced seminars in psychological research and practice
Entry to Honours year: minimum 70 WAM with credit average in 2nd/3rd year and majority of psychology units
Total: 4 years full-time, APAC-accredited, on campus or online
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 70-85 for competitive entry (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Science (Nursing)
description:
ECU's nursing degree runs on partnership-model placements rather than scattering students across many disparate providers for short rotations. Students can complete the bulk of their practical hours within one health service partner, among them Sir Charles Gairdner Osborne Park Health Care Group, North Metropolitan Health Service Mental Health, Ramsay Health Care, and Western Australian Country Health Service. That continuity model means students build depth with one clinical environment and its staff over multiple placement blocks rather than restarting orientation at a new site every rotation, which several graduates report as easing the transition into graduate-year employment at the same health service.

The WA Country Health Service partnership specifically opens placement pathways into regional and rural WA, which matters given the acute nursing workforce shortages outside Perth metro. Students interested in rural or remote nursing practice have a structured route into that experience during training rather than having to seek it out independently after registration.

As a Bachelor of Science rather than a Bachelor of Nursing by name, the degree still meets all Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia registration requirements for Registered Nurse practice; the science framing reflects ECU's faculty structure rather than a different scope of practice or accreditation pathway.
curriculum:
Core sequence: Anatomy and Physiology, Pathophysiology, Pharmacology and Therapeutics, Nursing Practice (progressive units through all years), Mental Health Nursing, Aboriginal Health, Primary Health Care and Community Nursing
Clinical placement: staged practical placements through partner health services (Sir Charles Gairdner Osborne Park Health Care Group, North Metropolitan Health Service Mental Health, Ramsay Health Care, WA Country Health Service)
Capstone: final-year transition-to-practice clinical placement
Total: 3 years full-time, registration-ready under Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia standards
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, plus health/immunisation checks and (for clinical placements) police check (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0 (typical registration-body bar for nursing/health programs, approximate)

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
ECU's School of Business and Law is ranked WA's top business school for quality and sits in the top two nationally on the AFR BOSS Best Business Schools list, and the MBA is AACSB-accredited, putting it in a global tier most Australian business schools outside the Group of Eight don't reach. Within the program, students choose from a genuinely large bank of 14 specialisation areas rather than a handful of generic tracks, which lets working professionals steer the degree toward whatever function or industry they're actually trying to move into.

Curriculum design has been updated to fold in ethical AI use directly into core content rather than treating it as an add-on module, which reflects how quickly generative AI has changed expectations for MBA graduates in strategy, marketing, and operations roles over the past couple of years. Cohorts skew toward working professionals studying part-time or online, so the teaching model relies heavily on case discussion and applied assignments tied to students' own workplaces rather than an on-campus-immersion residential model.

WA's economy is still heavily resources-and-services weighted, and a fair share of the cohort comes from mining services, government, and healthcare administration, which shapes case study content and networking opportunities differently than an MBA cohort concentrated in Sydney financial services.
curriculum:
Core units: Strategic Management, Managerial Economics, Financial Management, Marketing Management, Leadership and Organisational Behaviour, Business Analytics and Ethical AI, Operations Management, Business Research Project
Specialisations: choose from 14 areas including international business, human resource management, marketing, project management, finance, and entrepreneurship
Capstone: applied strategy project or business research report
Total: 2 years full-time / up to 4 years part-time, on campus or online, AACSB-accredited
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of Computer Science
description:
ECU's Master of Computer Science is a conversion-friendly degree: it's designed to take graduates from unrelated bachelor's disciplines and get them industry-ready in computing, which is why the first-year units look like a compressed CS undergrad (data structures, algorithms, systems, databases) before the program moves into more advanced electives in the second year. It's accredited by the Australian Computer Society, and ECU folds in its considerable cyber security research strength as an elective pathway rather than keeping the two programs walled off from each other.

That cyber security connection is worth noting specifically because ECU is one of only two Australian universities recognised by the federal government as an Academic Centre of Cyber Security Excellence, and the only one in Western Australia. Students in the computer science degree who want a security-adjacent skill set can pull electives from that research base without needing to enrol in the separate Master of Cyber Security. Beyond security, elective streams commonly run toward data science, machine learning, and software engineering practice.

Perth's tech employment market is smaller and more resources-and-mining-services-oriented than Sydney or Melbourne's, so ECU's industry placements and capstone project partners often skew toward that sector along with WA government IT roles, rather than the startup-heavy scene more associated with the east coast.
curriculum:
Foundational units: Programming Fundamentals, Data Structures and Algorithms, Database Systems, Computer Systems and Networks, Software Engineering Principles
Advanced units: choose electives across cyber security, data science and analytics, artificial intelligence, or advanced software engineering
Capstone: industry-linked project or research-based minor thesis
Total: 2 years full-time (shorter with credit for a relevant undergraduate background), accredited by the Australian Computer Society

name: Master of Cyber Security
description:
ECU is one of only two universities the Australian federal government has recognised as an Academic Centre of Cyber Security Excellence, and the sole one in Western Australia, a designation that reflects the size of ECU's cyber security research and teaching group, described by the university as the largest in Australia and ranked among the top ten globally. The Master of Cyber Security draws directly on that research base rather than being a generically branded security add-on to a computing degree, and it's built specifically to serve government, law enforcement, and industry demand for security specialists rather than general IT professionals.

Entry pathways are unusually flexible: applicants can come in with a related bachelor's degree, or with a bachelor's in any discipline paired with five years of relevant work experience, which opens the program to career-changers already working in IT operations, law enforcement, or defence-adjacent roles without a computing degree on paper. Course length can also compress for students with relevant prior qualifications or experience, rather than everyone doing a fixed two years regardless of background.

Perth hosts a meaningful concentration of defence, mining-sector, and government security roles, and ECU's placement and industry connections in cyber security lean into that local demand alongside the more geographically distributed remote/online cohort the program attracts nationally and internationally.
curriculum:
Core units: Cyber Security Fundamentals, Network Security, Digital Forensics, Security Risk Management, Cryptography, Incident Response and Threat Intelligence, Governance Risk and Compliance
Electives: penetration testing, cloud security, industrial control systems security, security research methods
Capstone: applied security project or research minor thesis, often linked to industry or government partners
Total: 2 years full-time / 4 years part-time (reduced duration available with relevant background), on campus or online
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of Education
description:
Rather than one generic Master of Education, ECU structures the degree around named specialisations: Behaviour and Wellbeing, Early Childhood Education, Learning Difficulties, Literacy Education, Special Education, and Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL). Each is built from the same four core units plus four specialisation-specific units, so the degree can serve very different practitioners (an early childhood educator and a TESOL specialist, for instance) without pretending one curriculum fits both.
