Where the degree diverges from a straight ecology or conservation biology program is its explicit policy and management strand: units on environmental impact assessment and natural resource management sit alongside the science, aimed at producing graduates who can work inside government departments or consultancies doing EIS work, not just researchers. Griffith's location gives students a front-row seat to a genuinely contested environmental policy landscape (Reef water quality, koala habitat protection, coastal development pressure) that shows up constantly in case-based assessment.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Environmental Science, Ecology, Earth Systems, Environmental Chemistry
Year 2: Freshwater Ecology, Environmental Impact Assessment, GIS and Remote Sensing, Soil and Land Management
Year 3: Conservation Biology, Natural Resource Management, Climate Science, capstone Environmental Field Research Project
Field components embedded across all three years (Moreton Bay, Lamington National Park, regional catchments)
Elective options in marine science or environmental policy depending on career direction
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
Griffith Law School runs its LLB out of Nathan, and the thing that distinguishes it from the more traditional Queensland law schools is how early students get put in front of actual clients. The clinical legal education component, placements through Caxton Legal Centre and similar community outfits, starts well before the final year capstone that most competitor programs treat as the only "practical" component.

The degree is Priestley 11 compliant (the national list of core subjects a law degree has to cover for admission purposes), so the compulsory spine looks similar to any Australian LLB, but Griffith's elective bench leans into areas the school has built genuine research strength in: environmental and climate law, given Queensland's Reef and mining exposure, and Indigenous legal issues, an area where Griffith's law academics have had real influence on Queensland's Path to Treaty process.

Most students combine the LLB with a second degree (Business, Arts, or Criminology and Criminal Justice are common pairings at Griffith), which stretches the combined program to five years but tends to sharpen job prospects: commercial law firms recruiting out of Griffith often specifically ask about the second degree during interviews.
curriculum:
Compulsory Priestley 11 sequence: Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Property Law, Equity and Trusts, Constitutional Law, Administrative Law, Evidence, Civil Procedure, Company Law, Professional Responsibility
Foundation units: Legal Research and Writing, Introduction to Law and Legal Reasoning
Clinical unit: supervised placement in a community legal centre
Electives (choose from): Environmental Law, Native Title and Indigenous Legal Issues, International Law, Intellectual Property
Capstone: Legal Practice unit combining advocacy and negotiation skills assessment
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 70-85 for competitive entry (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Music
description:
Griffith's Bachelor of Music is taught out of the Queensland Conservatorium at South Bank, right on the river next to QPAC, and the location isn't incidental: students get placement and performance opportunities with the Queensland Symphony Orchestra and Opera Queensland that a conservatorium without that kind of civic neighbour couldn't offer as routinely.

The Con's jazz program has a genuinely strong national reputation, built up over decades and associated with figures like James Morrison who've had long-running connections to the school, and it draws students specifically for that stream rather than classical performance, which is unusual for an Australian conservatorium where classical training still tends to dominate enrolment numbers.

Students choose a principal study early, classical performance, jazz, popular music, or composition and music technology, and the degree structure from second year onward is built almost entirely around one-on-one instrumental or vocal tuition plus ensemble work, which means the timetable looks very different to a standard university degree: far fewer large lectures, far more small-group and individual contact hours, and assessment that's mostly recital and portfolio based rather than written exams.
curriculum:
Year 1: Principal Study lessons begin (Classical, Jazz, Popular Music, or Composition/Music Technology stream), Aural and Theory Skills, Ensemble Performance, Music History Survey
Year 2: continued Principal Study, stream-specific units (e.g. Jazz Improvisation, Composition Techniques, Recording and Production for the tech stream)
Year 3: Principal Study intensifies, Performance Practice, capstone Recital or portfolio-based final project
Ensemble and small-group performance requirements run throughout all three years
Elective units available in arts management or music education for students considering non-performance careers
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, plus audition (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Griffith's nursing program has historically posted some of the strongest graduate satisfaction results in the national QILT surveys among Queensland providers, and the reason cited most often by students isn't the classroom teaching. It's the volume and variety of clinical placement hours across Gold Coast University Hospital, Logan Hospital, and a spread of smaller regional and private facilities.

The degree is delivered across three campuses (Nathan, Logan, Gold Coast) and each has slightly different placement partnerships baked in, so where you enrol has some bearing on what kind of clinical exposure you get in your first placement block. Griffith also runs one of the larger simulated clinical environments in the state: a mock hospital ward setup used heavily in first and second year before students are let loose on real wards.

Because Queensland's health workforce shortage has been acute in regional and mental health nursing specifically, Griffith has built electives and placement partnerships that specifically funnel students toward those areas, and a meaningful share of each graduating cohort ends up working in exactly those under-served specialties rather than general metropolitan ward nursing.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Health Assessment, first clinical placement block
Year 2: Nursing Care of Adults, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology, Pathophysiology, extended clinical placement
Year 3: Nursing Care of Children and Families, Complex Care Nursing, Aged Care Nursing, Professional Transition to Practice
Placement hours accumulate across all three years to meet AHPRA's registration requirements (minimum mandated clinical hours)
Final trimester: capstone clinical placement and Transition to Professional Practice unit
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, plus health/immunisation checks and (for clinical placements) police check (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0 (typical registration-body bar for nursing/health programs, approximate)

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
Griffith's psychological science degree is APAC accredited, meaning it satisfies the first stage of the pathway to provisional registration as a psychologist in Australia, and the school has a particular research reputation in forensic and clinical neuroscience that colours the elective offering more than at a generalist psychology department. Units in forensic psychology and offender assessment draw directly on the same Griffith Criminology Institute connections that shape the criminology degree.

The program runs at Mt Gravatt and the Gold Coast, and both campuses run a research methods sequence that's noticeably heavier on statistics than students sometimes expect walking in. Griffith treats quantitative competency as a selling point for graduates heading into either honours-track clinical psychology or non-clinical fields like market research and organisational consulting.

Because the registration pathway in Australia now requires an accredited fourth (honours) year before provisional registration, most students treat the three-year bachelor as a stepping stone rather than a terminal qualification, and Griffith's honours intake is competitive. GPA cutoffs mean a meaningful share of each cohort ends up pursuing psychology-adjacent careers (HR, research assistant roles, allied health support work) rather than continuing straight through to registration.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Psychology, Social Psychology, Research Methods and Statistics I
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Abnormal Psychology, Research Methods and Statistics II
Year 3: Personality Psychology, Psychological Assessment, capstone Research Project, electives in Forensic Psychology or Health Psychology
Honours (competitive entry, separate fourth year): independent empirical thesis plus advanced coursework, required for provisional psychologist registration
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Griffith's MBA is delivered through the AACSB-accredited Griffith Business School and is built primarily for working professionals. The timetabling (evening and intensive block formats, plus a fully online option) assumes you're doing this alongside a job rather than instead of one, which shapes the case-study-heavy assessment style more than a typical lecture-exam model would.

The degree doesn't force a single specialisation track on everyone; instead it lets students layer electives toward an area of interest (leadership, international business, project management) on top of a shared core, so two Griffith MBA graduates can come out with meaningfully different skill profiles depending on what they chose. The capstone strategy project is normally built around a real organisation, sometimes the student's own employer, sometimes a partner business Griffith has an existing consulting relationship with, which is a deliberate move away from hypothetical Harvard-style cases toward something with actual stakes attached.

Queensland's MBA market is smaller and less saturated than Sydney or Melbourne's, and Griffith's program tends to draw a heavily South-East Queensland cohort working in government, healthcare management, or mid-sized private enterprise rather than the finance-and-consulting skew you'd see in a Group of Eight MBA cohort further south.
curriculum:
Core: Managerial Economics, Financial Management, Strategic Marketing, Organisational Behaviour and Leadership, Managerial Accounting
Core continued: Operations and Supply Chain Management, Business Analytics for Decision Making
Electives (choose to build a specialisation): International Business, Project Management, Human Resource Leadership, Entrepreneurship
Capstone: Strategic Management project, typically built around a real host organisation
Delivered across trimesters in evening, intensive, or fully online formats
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
Griffith's Master of IT sits inside the university's Nathan campus tech precinct, a short walk from the Cyber Range that the School of ICT built with defence-industry funding. Students in the security specialisation actually run attack-and-defend exercises against simulated networks there rather than just reading about them. The degree is built for career-changers: roughly half of any given cohort arrives with an undergraduate degree in something unrelated (commerce, biology, the occasional music grad) and the first trimester is deliberately weighted toward programming fundamentals and systems thinking before the specialisations open up.

From second trimester students pick a track (software development, data science, network and cyber security, or enterprise systems), and the coursework gets noticeably more project-based, with several units assessed entirely on a working deliverable rather than exams. Griffith's industry ties in South-East Queensland (Telstra, Suncorp, various defence primes based near Amberley) mean the capstone project frequently comes with a real client brief attached, not a simulated one.

Graduates skew toward Brisbane's growing cyber security and fintech employers, though a decent slice go on to further study: Griffith runs a fairly well-used PhD pipeline out of this cohort for students who get hooked on a research problem during the capstone.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Programming Foundations, Systems Analysis and Design, Database Systems, Networking Principles
Trimester 2: Software Engineering, choice of specialisation stream begins (Software Development / Data Science / Cyber Security / Enterprise Systems)
Specialisation core units (varies by stream): Secure Systems Programming, Applied Machine Learning, Enterprise Architecture, or Advanced Web Development
Electives: two or three units drawn from the broader ICT school offering, including Cloud Computing and IT Project Management
Final trimester: industry-linked Capstone Project (client-brief based), plus one advanced elective
Non-IT-background entrants complete an additional foundation trimester before the above sequence
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant or any discipline (typical Australian postgrad IT/CS entry bar used as approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Public Health
description:
Griffith's MPH sits within the Menzies Health Institute Queensland research grouping, which gives the degree a noticeably strong lean toward chronic disease epidemiology and health services research relative to a public health program housed inside a standalone medical school. Griffith's public health researchers do a lot of work on obesity, diabetes, and Indigenous health outcomes specifically, and that shows up in elective choice and guest lecture content.

The cohort is genuinely international and mixed-career: working clinicians (nurses, allied health professionals, occasional doctors) doing the degree to move into policy or management roles sit alongside students coming straight from an undergraduate science or health degree with no clinical background at all, and Griffith structures the core sequence to be accessible to both without dumbing down the epidemiology and biostatistics content.

Students choose a specialisation stream (health promotion, epidemiology, or health management), and the practicum placement component, done with a health department, hospital, or NGO, is where the degree earns its practical reputation; Griffith's Queensland Health connections mean placements are relatively easy to secure compared to some interstate programs.
curriculum:
Core: Foundations of Public Health, Biostatistics, Epidemiology, Health Promotion Theory and Practice, Health Systems and Policy
Specialisation stream (choose): Epidemiology, Health Promotion, or Health Management
Research methods unit and choice of either a research minor-thesis or coursework-only pathway
Practicum placement with a health department, hospital, or community health organisation
Capstone: Public Health Project applying core skills to a real health issue
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
Holmes's Bachelor of Business is a 24-unit, three-year degree with four specialisation options (Management, Marketing, International Business and Hospitality Management), the last of which is a slightly unusual inclusion for a business-only private provider and reflects Holmes's history of teaching hospitality alongside its commerce offerings. Students complete a shared core of accounting, economics, law and management units in years one and two before specialising in year three.

As with most of Holmes's degrees, the cohort is heavily international, and the degree functions for a lot of students as the standard three-year pathway toward permanent residency via the skilled migration points test, rather than purely as an academic credential chosen on its own merits. That's not a criticism of the teaching: the core units are solid and cover the same ground as equivalent degrees at larger universities. But it's worth naming plainly rather than pretending every enrolment is driven by intellectual interest in business theory.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting for Business Decisions; Economics for Business; Business Communication; Introduction to Management; Business Law; Quantitative Methods
Year 2: Marketing Principles; Organisational Behaviour; Finance for Business; Business Ethics and Sustainability; Human Resource Management; Business Statistics
Year 3: specialisation strand (four units in Management, Marketing, International Business or Hospitality Management) plus Strategic Management and a capstone business project
Capstone: industry-linked business project or case competition in the final trimester
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Fashion Business
description:
Bachelor of Fashion Business is Holmes's attempt to sit between a straight business degree and a design school program. It teaches merchandising, buying, retail management and fashion marketing rather than pattern-making or garment construction, so students who actually want to design clothes should look elsewhere (RMIT or Whitehouse Institute are the more obvious choices in that space). What this degree is for is the commercial side of the fashion industry: supply chain, brand management, retail analytics and marketing applied specifically to apparel and accessories categories.

It shares a business core with Holmes's other undergraduate business degrees in years one and two, then narrows into fashion-specific units (trend forecasting, fashion retail management, visual merchandising) in year three. Melbourne's retail and wholesale fashion sector gives students some access to local industry placements and guest lecturers, though the program is smaller and less established than Holmes's mainstream business and accounting degrees, and prospective students should treat it as a niche offering rather than a flagship one.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting for Business Decisions; Introduction to Fashion Industry; Business Communication; Economics for Business; Marketing Principles; Business Law
Year 2: Fashion Retail Management; Consumer Behaviour; Finance for Business; Brand Management; Supply Chain Fundamentals; Organisational Behaviour
Year 3: Fashion Buying and Merchandising; Trend Forecasting and Product Development; Visual Merchandising; Digital Marketing for Fashion; Strategic Management; capstone fashion business project
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Information Systems
description:
This is a three-year degree for students who want an IT qualification with a business faculty attached rather than an engineering one: the difference matters, because the emphasis throughout is on systems that support organisations (databases, ERP-adjacent platforms, business analytics) rather than low-level programming or hardware. Holmes teaches it out of its Melbourne CBD and Sydney campuses to a mostly international cohort, many of whom are using the degree as a stepping stone toward the 189/190 skilled migration occupation lists that include ICT business analyst and systems analyst roles.

The 24-unit structure moves from foundational programming and database units in year one through systems analysis and network fundamentals in year two, before a final year that includes an IT project unit where students build and document a working system end to end. It suits someone who wants employable IT skills without committing to a heavier computer science or software engineering load, though students aiming specifically at software development roles at larger tech employers may find a more technically dense degree from a research university better positioned for that path.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Programming; Database Systems; Business Information Systems; Foundations of Business Communication; Accounting for Business Decisions; Quantitative Methods
Year 2: Systems Analysis and Design; Network Fundamentals; Web Application Development; Operating Systems; Business Law; Project Management Principles
Year 3: IT Project Management; Enterprise Systems; Cybersecurity Fundamentals; Data Analytics for Business; two electives
Capstone: IT systems project — students design, build and document a working information system for a simulated or partner organisation
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Professional Accounting
description:
This is the undergraduate counterpart to Holmes's Master of Professional Accounting: a three-year, CPA Australia and CA ANZ accredited degree built around the mandated accounting core (financial accounting, management accounting, auditing, tax, corporate law) plus general business units in the earlier years. It's the more common entry point for school leavers or first-degree students who know from the outset that they want to sit for CPA or CA membership after graduating, rather than coming to accounting via a conversion master's later.

The degree's reputation rests less on Holmes's institutional prestige and more on the fact that accreditation requirements are set externally by the professional bodies, so the technical content lines up closely with what's taught at any accredited Australian accounting degree. Where Holmes differentiates is smaller cohort sizes in tutorials and, for many international students, direct progression pathways from Holmes's own diploma and foundation programs into this degree with credit.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Systems and Processes; Economics for Business; Business Law; Quantitative Methods; Business Communication; Introduction to Management
Year 2: Financial Accounting; Management Accounting; Corporations Law; Financial Management; Business Information Systems; Organisational Behaviour
Year 3: Auditing and Assurance Services; Taxation Law; Advanced Financial Accounting; Ethics and Governance in Accounting; Strategic Management Accounting; capstone accounting project
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Graduate Diploma of Business
description:
The Graduate Diploma of Business is Holmes's shorter, standalone postgraduate business qualification: eight units over roughly eight months full-time, sitting below the MBA in the institute's course ladder and often used either as a terminal qualification for someone wanting a fast credential upgrade, or as a stepping stone that later articulates into the MBA with advanced standing.

The unit mix covers the standard generalist ground (accounting, marketing, management, economics) without the specialisation and elective units that round out the full MBA, so it's a leaner degree by design. Students who complete it and want to continue can usually move into Holmes's MBA with credit for overlapping units, which is the more common path than treating the Graduate Diploma as a final destination.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Accounting for Business Decisions; Economics for Business; Marketing Management; Management and Organisations in a Global Environment
Trimester 2: Finance for Business; Statistics and Research Methods for Business Decisions; Human Resource Management; Business Law and Ethics
Assessment: case-based assignments and a group consulting-style report in place of a thesis or major capstone
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Holmes Institute's MBA runs across its Melbourne and Sydney campuses to a full-time cohort that's overwhelmingly international, and the teaching reflects that: small seminar-style classes rather than lecture halls, with a lot of case discussion drawn from Asia-Pacific trade and services examples rather than the US case studies that dominate most MBA texts. The core is twelve units, everything from Accounting for Business Decisions through to Competitive Strategy, completed in about eighteen months, after which students pick one specialisation and one elective to round out the degree.

Because Holmes is a smaller private provider rather than a sandstone university, the MBA doesn't carry the brand weight of a Group of Eight degree, and it's honest to say most graduates use it as a credential to move into management roles in mid-sized firms or to support a permanent migration pathway, not to break into top-tier consulting or investment banking. Where it does its job well is for someone who already has a business degree or several years of work experience and wants the generalist management toolkit (finance, strategy, people management, research methods) without relocating overseas or taking two years out of the workforce.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Accounting for Business Decisions; Economics for Business; Management and Organisations in a Global Environment; Marketing Management
Trimester 2: Finance for Business; Statistics and Research Methods for Business Decisions; Leveraging Information Technology for Business Advantage; Human Resource Management
Trimester 3: Competitive Strategy; Corporate Governance and Ethics; International Business; Project Management
Final trimester: one specialisation unit (Marketing, International Business, Management or Hospitality Management) plus one elective
Capstone: applied strategy project addressing a real organisational problem, presented to faculty and industry panel
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline) typically required; relevant work experience preferred (approximate, typical bar, not program-page-verified)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall (typical bar for postgrad at private AU providers, approximate)

name: Master of Business Administration (Professional)
description:
The Professional variant of Holmes's MBA swaps the standard version's single specialisation-plus-elective tail for a much broader elective bank: eight core units and eight electives, which can be taken all from one specialisation to produce a focused MBA (Professional) in, say, marketing or international business, or spread across areas for a generalist qualification. It's aimed at students who want more say over the back half of their degree than the standard MBA structure allows.

In practice the two MBA products at Holmes overlap heavily in their core content (accounting, finance, economics, management, strategy), and the choice between them usually comes down to how much a student already knows they want to specialise versus keep options open. Neither carries the recruiting pull of an MBA from a AACSB-accredited research university, so it suits people building a management career step by step rather than those chasing a brand-name credential for a lateral move into strategy consulting.
curriculum:
Core (8 units): Accounting for Business Decisions; Finance for Business; Economics for Business; Marketing Management; Management and Organisations in a Global Environment; Statistics and Research Methods for Business Decisions; Competitive Strategy; Corporate Governance and Ethics
Electives (8 units): chosen from Marketing, International Business, Management or Hospitality Management strands, or mixed across strands for a generalist profile
Capstone: applied business project drawing on the student's chosen elective focus
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description:
The Master of Professional Accounting at Holmes is built to satisfy the CPA Australia and CA ANZ accreditation requirements for entry into those professional bodies, which is really the whole point of the degree for most people enrolled in it: it's a conversion course for graduates whose undergraduate degree wasn't in accounting and who need the full suite of core accounting units to sit the CPA Program or CA exams. It runs over roughly two years full-time across twelve to sixteen units depending on how much credit a student's prior degree earns them.

Because it's an accreditation-driven degree, the unit list is fairly fixed by the professional bodies rather than by Holmes itself: financial accounting, management accounting, auditing, taxation law, corporate law and finance all have to appear. What Holmes adds on top is smaller class sizes and, for many students, English-language academic support built into the first trimester, which matters given a large share of the cohort has come from non-English-medium undergraduate study.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Accounting Systems and Processes; Financial Accounting; Economics for Business; Quantitative Methods for Business
Trimester 2: Management Accounting; Corporations Law; Taxation Law; Financial Management
Trimester 3: Auditing and Assurance Services; Advanced Financial Accounting; Business Law; Research Methods in Accounting
Final trimester: Ethics and Governance in Accounting; Strategic Management Accounting; two accounting electives aligned to CPA Program entry requirements
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Business (Accounting)
description:
The Accounting specialisation at ICMS sits on the same core 12-subject business spine as the college's other Bachelor of Business streams, then adds the technical accounting sequence (financial accounting, management accounting, auditing, taxation and corporate finance) needed to satisfy the professional accreditation requirements of CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants ANZ. Getting that accreditation lined up matters more for accounting than for most other business majors, since it directly gates the pathway into the CA or CPA program after graduation, and ICMS structures the specialisation units specifically against those bodies' unit requirements.

Like every ICMS undergraduate degree, the course folds in two Work Integrated Learning placements totalling up to 600 hours, which for accounting students commonly means time inside a mid-tier or boutique Sydney accounting firm rather than a classroom-only capstone. That's a meaningful differentiator against accounting majors at universities where the professional placement is optional or informally arranged, since ICMS builds relationships with firms directly and treats the placement as a graded, credit-bearing part of the degree.

Graduates typically head toward roles in public practice, corporate accounting or financial analysis, with the accreditation pathway keeping CA/CPA progression open without needing a separate postgraduate conversion course.
curriculum:
Level 100: Pathway to Success; Accounting Fundamentals; Economics for Managers; Business Law; Management Solutions for a Changing World; Business Statistics
Level 200: Financial Accounting; Management Accounting; Corporate Finance; Company Law; Work Integrated Learning 1
Level 300: Auditing and Assurance; Taxation Law and Practice; Advanced Financial Reporting; electives; Work Integrated Learning 2 (professional placement)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Business (Marketing)
description:
ICMS runs its business degrees on a shared structural template: 12 core business subjects everyone takes regardless of specialisation, then a run of specialisation subjects, electives and two Work Integrated Learning placements bolted on. The Marketing stream slots into that frame with brand strategy, digital marketing and consumer behaviour content layered over the core management, economics and accounting units. The core subjects include named units like Pathway to Success and Unlocking Your Leadership Potential, which signals ICMS's employability-first pitch: these aren't abstract theory units but built around workplace-readiness skills from day one.

What differentiates ICMS's Marketing degree from a marketing major buried inside a big university's commerce degree is the WIL component: up to two trimesters, roughly nine months, of supervised professional placement built directly into the award. For marketing specifically, that tends to mean students working inside agency, retail or hospitality marketing teams around Sydney, given ICMS's strong existing placement relationships in the tourism and hospitality sector it was originally built around.

The Manly campus itself, a heritage sandstone building overlooking Manly Beach that students and staff refer to as 'the castle on the hill', gives the degree an unusually pleasant physical setting relative to most CBD-based business schools, something that comes up repeatedly in student reviews and open day materials.
curriculum:
Level 100: Pathway to Success; Management Solutions for a Changing World; Marketing Principles; Economics for Managers; Accounting Fundamentals; Creativity and Innovation for Business
Level 200: Consumer Behaviour; Digital Marketing; Brand Management; Marketing Research; two further core/specialisation units; Work Integrated Learning 1
Level 300: Strategic Marketing; Integrated Marketing Communications; electives; Work Integrated Learning 2 (professional placement)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Business (Property)
description:
ICMS's Property specialisation is a newer addition to its business degree suite, built to feed Sydney's persistently active property and construction sector, a market where demand for graduates with both business fundamentals and property-specific knowledge (valuation, property law, development finance, asset management) has stayed strong even through broader graduate market softness elsewhere. It sits on the standard ICMS core-subjects spine before specialising into property valuation, real estate law, property development and funds/asset management units.

The Work Integrated Learning placements (up to 600 hours across two subjects) commonly place students with real estate agencies, property funds, valuation firms or development companies around Sydney, giving graduates direct exposure to a sector where a large share of hiring still runs through personal networks and internship-to-hire pathways rather than open graduate programs.

Because the specialisation is smaller and newer than ICMS's hospitality-heritage degrees, cohort sizes tend to be modest, which in practice means closer staff-student contact and more individualised placement matching than a large-university property degree with hundreds of students competing for the same handful of industry placements.
curriculum:
Level 100: Pathway to Success; Management Solutions for a Changing World; Marketing; Economics for Managers; Accounting Fundamentals; Business Law
Level 200: Property Valuation; Real Estate Law; Property Development; Asset and Funds Management; Work Integrated Learning 1
Level 300: Strategic Property Management; Urban Planning and Development Economics; electives; Work Integrated Learning 2 (property industry placement)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Business (Sports Management)
description:
ICMS built its Sports Management degree around Sydney's genuine concentration of professional sport, and the college's placement network reflects that: students on this stream commonly end up placed with NRL and A-League clubs, stadium operators, or sports marketing agencies for their Work Integrated Learning component, rather than generic corporate placements. Content covers sports marketing, event operations and sponsorship alongside the standard ICMS core business subjects (economics, accounting, management, leadership), so graduates come out with a genuine business qualification rather than a narrower sport science credential.

The degree follows ICMS's usual 12 core, several specialisation, elective and two-WIL-subject structure, with sports-specific units layered into the specialisation slots. Sponsorship and commercial partnerships, facility and stadium management, and sports event logistics feature prominently given how much of Sydney's major-event calendar (State of Origin, international cricket, A-League finals) runs through venues the college has existing relationships with.

Students interested in athlete management, club administration or major event delivery tend to gravitate here rather than to ICMS's separate Event Management degree, though there's meaningful elective overlap between the two given how closely sports and events management skillsets sit together in the Australian industry.
curriculum:
Level 100: Pathway to Success; Management Solutions for a Changing World; Marketing Principles; Economics for Managers; Introduction to Sport Management
Level 200: Sports Marketing and Sponsorship; Sport Event Management; Facility and Stadium Management; Consumer Behaviour; Work Integrated Learning 1
Level 300: Strategic Sport Business; Sport Governance and Policy; electives; Work Integrated Learning 2 (placement with a sporting organisation)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Event Management
description:
ICMS markets this degree hard on rankings, and the underlying substance backs some of that up: the college has deep placement relationships across Sydney's events calendar, from Vivid Sydney to major conference and exhibition venues, which feeds directly into the course's Work Integrated Learning placements. The core business subjects (Pathway to Success, Management Solutions for a Changing World, Marketing, Economics for Managers, Creativity and Innovation for Business, Unlocking Your Leadership Potential) are identical to every other ICMS Bachelor of Business stream, with event-specific specialisation subjects layered on top.

Electives are unusually broad for a specialist events degree: students can pull units from fashion, tourism, entrepreneurship, hospitality and sports, letting someone interested in, say, fashion week production build a genuinely tailored transcript rather than a fixed events-only pathway. That flexibility matters in an industry where career paths fork wildly: corporate conference production looks nothing like festival logistics or luxury wedding planning, and ICMS's elective spread acknowledges that rather than forcing one generic events curriculum on everyone.

The course runs 12 core subjects, 8 specialisation subjects, 4 electives and 2 WIL subjects across three year levels, with a typical full load of 6 to 8 subjects a year.
curriculum:
Level 100: Pathway to Success; Management Solutions for a Changing World; Marketing; Economics for Managers; Creativity and Innovation for Business; Unlocking Your Leadership Potential
Level 200: Event Design and Production; Event Marketing and Sponsorship; Risk Management for Events; electives (fashion, tourism, entrepreneurship, hospitality or sports); Work Integrated Learning 1
Level 300: Strategic Event Management; Festival and Major Event Operations; electives; Work Integrated Learning 2 (event industry placement)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Fashion and Global Brand Management
description:
This degree runs a slightly leaner elective load than most ICMS undergraduate degrees (26 subjects total, split across 12 core business units, 6 fashion specialisation subjects, 6 electives and 2 Work Integrated Learning subjects worth up to 600 placement hours), built specifically to prepare students for brand, retail and visual merchandising roles across the global fashion and luxury sector rather than design or garment construction, which ICMS explicitly doesn't teach here. It's a business degree with a fashion industry lens, not a fashion design degree with business units bolted on, and that distinction matters for anyone comparing it against TAFE or fashion-college design programs.

Specialisation content covers how fashion and luxury brands are built and managed, visual merchandising strategy, and the retailing and marketing techniques used across both physical stores and the now-dominant online fashion retail channel. Entry requires a Band 2 in English and one other subject at HSC level (Mathematics Standard 2, Business Studies, Economics among the accepted options), a relatively accessible bar reflecting the degree's practical, industry-facing positioning rather than an academically selective one.

Graduates go on to brand management, visual merchandising, retail buying and marketing roles; the degree's own careers material name-checks boutique brand management and online fashion retail marketing specifically as target outcomes.
curriculum:
Level 100: Pathway to Success; Management Solutions for a Changing World; Marketing; Economics for Managers; Business Law; Accounting Fundamentals
Level 200: Fashion and Luxury Brand Management; Visual Merchandising; Retail Management; electives; Work Integrated Learning 1
Level 300: Global Fashion Marketing; Digital Fashion Retailing; electives; Work Integrated Learning 2 (fashion/retail industry placement, up to 600 hours combined with WIL 1)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of International Hotel and Resort Management
description:
This is one of ICMS's founding disciplines. The college began as a hotel and hospitality training institution before broadening into general business degrees, and the hotel and resort management program still carries that institutional memory in the depth of its industry relationships. The course structure runs 12 core subjects, 8 specialisation subjects, 4 electives and 2 Work Integrated Learning subjects, with the WIL component covering up to two trimesters (about nine months combined) of paid or supervised internship placement, commonly inside branded international hotel groups with a Sydney or regional NSW presence.

Specialisation content covers rooms division and front office operations, food and beverage management, revenue management and resort operations specifically (as distinct from urban hotel management), reflecting the realities of Australia's resort sector along the coast and in regional tourism hubs. Electives pull from marketing, tourism, entrepreneurship, event management and sport, so students can shape the degree toward luxury resort management, conference and events, or broader hospitality group leadership depending on where they want to end up.

Graduates commonly move into hotel management trainee programs with international chains, a pathway ICMS has cultivated for decades given its origins, though the degree equally supports resort-specific and boutique property careers less common among city-based hospitality programs.
curriculum:
Level 100: Pathway to Success; Management Solutions for a Changing World; Marketing; Economics for Managers; Introduction to Hospitality Operations; Accounting Fundamentals
Level 200: Rooms Division Management; Food and Beverage Management; Resort Operations; Revenue Management; Work Integrated Learning 1
Level 300: Strategic Hospitality Management; International Hotel Brand Management; electives; Work Integrated Learning 2 (hotel/resort industry placement)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of International Tourism and Hospitality Management
description:
Where ICMS's Hotel and Resort Management degree leans into property-level operations, this program takes a wider destination and industry-management view: tourism policy, destination marketing, and cross-sector hospitality management alongside the hotel operations content shared across the college's tourism-adjacent degrees. It follows the same 12 core, 8 specialisation, 4 elective, 2 WIL subject structure as ICMS's other undergraduate business degrees, with the WIL placements often arranged with tourism boards, travel operators, or hospitality groups rather than exclusively hotel front desks.

Sydney and the broader NSW coast give this degree a genuinely useful backyard for its subject matter. International arrivals through Sydney Airport, cruise ship tourism through Sydney Harbour, and the Northern Beaches tourism economy that ICMS's own Manly campus sits inside all provide accessible, real-world case material that a program based somewhere without a comparable tourism economy would have to teach more abstractly.

Graduates typically head into destination marketing organisations, travel and tour operators, tourism policy roles with state or local government, or hospitality group management, a broader spread of outcomes than the hotel-specific degree, reflecting its wider industry-management framing.
curriculum:
Level 100: Pathway to Success; Management Solutions for a Changing World; Marketing; Economics for Managers; Introduction to Tourism Systems; Creativity and Innovation for Business
Level 200: Destination Marketing; Tourism Policy and Planning; Hospitality Operations Management; Sustainable Tourism; Work Integrated Learning 1
Level 300: Strategic Tourism Management; International Tourism Trends; electives; Work Integrated Learning 2 (tourism/hospitality industry placement)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
ICMS's MBA is structured as 12 subjects of coursework plus two Work Integrated Learning subjects, an Action Learning Project and a Professional Placement, rather than the thesis-heavy research pathway some MBAs default to. The college pitches it explicitly around leadership development ('mastery of leadership' is the phrase ICMS itself uses), with a people-first management focus running through the core subjects rather than treating leadership as a single bolted-on unit near the end.

Delivery mixes small lectures, tutorials and workshops with an emphasis on industry research, and units are also available online for students who can't attend the Manly campus full-time, a flexibility that matters given a chunk of the MBA cohort is working while studying. Full-time completion runs two years, and international graduates become eligible for post-study work visas of up to five years, a detail that matters enormously to the significant international contingent in ICMS's postgraduate programs generally.

The Action Learning Project asks students to work through a real strategic problem, typically sourced from their own employer or an industry partner, while the Professional Placement adds direct workplace experience for students who haven't already accumulated substantial industry tenure.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Leadership and Personal Development; Managerial Economics; Accounting for Decision Making
Trimester 2: Marketing Management; Organisational Behaviour; Corporate Finance
Trimester 3: Strategic Management; Business Research Methods; elective
Trimester 4: Global Business Environment; Operations and Supply Chain Management; elective
Trimester 5: Action Learning Project (Work Integrated Learning); Innovation and Entrepreneurship
Trimester 6: Professional Placement (Work Integrated Learning); MBA capstone
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of Event Management
description:
This postgraduate degree builds on ICMS's undergraduate strength in event management, aimed at career-changers or industry professionals wanting a formal management qualification behind existing events experience rather than school leavers starting from scratch. Like ICMS's other masters, it combines dense coursework with two Work Integrated Learning subjects totalling 600 hours, and students already working in relevant event roles can apply for recognition of prior learning against that placement requirement rather than repeating hours they've effectively already logged professionally.

Content goes deeper into strategic event portfolio management, major event bidding and delivery, and event risk and crisis management than the undergraduate degree's more operational focus, appropriate for a cohort that in many cases already knows how to run an event and is here to learn how to manage an events business or a major event program at a strategic level. ICMS's Sydney location again does real work here, with access to major event case studies (Vivid Sydney, New Year's Eve on the Harbour, international sporting fixtures) that a program elsewhere would have to teach at a further remove.

Graduates typically move into senior event management roles, festival and major event directorships, or corporate event portfolio management within larger organisations.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Strategic Event Management; Event Marketing and Sponsorship; Managerial Economics
Trimester 2: Major Event Bidding and Delivery; Event Risk and Crisis Management; Research Methods
Trimester 3: Financial Management for Events; elective; Work Integrated Learning 1
Trimester 4: Event Portfolio Management; Global Event Trends; Work Integrated Learning 2 (or RPL pathway); capstone project
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of International Business
description:
ICMS's Master of International Business is built the same way most of its postgraduate degrees are: dense coursework paired with a genuine industry placement rather than a token internship. Students complete two Work Integrated Learning subjects worth 600 hours combined, working inside an actual organisation on real business problems, and anyone already employed in a relevant industry role can apply for recognition of prior learning against that requirement instead of duplicating hours they've already put in at work.

The degree covers trade and finance, international economics, accounting, marketing and people management, aimed at giving graduates from non-business undergraduate backgrounds (and there are plenty in ICMS's international cohort) a genuinely broad management skillset rather than a narrow specialisation. ICMS leans on its Manly campus location and small class sizes to run the program with more direct staff contact than a large city university's equivalent masters, which shows up in seminar-style teaching rather than large lecture theatres.

Most students take two years full-time, and the international business framing suits ICMS's own student demographic well: a large share of the cohort comes from overseas and returns home, or moves into export/import and multinational management roles in Sydney, after graduating.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Global Business Environment; Managerial Economics; International Trade and Finance
Trimester 2: International Marketing; Cross-Cultural Management; Accounting for Managers
Trimester 3: Human Resource Management in a Global Context; Strategic Management; elective
Trimester 4: Work Integrated Learning 1 (600-hour placement, part 1); Research Methods
Trimester 5: Work Integrated Learning 2 (placement continued); International Business Strategy capstone
Trimester 6: Global Supply Chain Management; final elective
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline) typically required (approximate, typical bar, not program-page-verified)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall (typical bar for postgrad at private AU providers, approximate)

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
JCU's Bachelor of Business runs a broad first-year core across accounting, economics, management, marketing and business law before students choose a major, and the degree's location gives it a genuinely useful backyard for several of those majors. Tourism and hospitality management draws directly on Cairns and the Great Barrier Reef tourism economy, while agribusiness and international business majors connect to North Queensland's sugar, cattle and mining export industries. That's a different flavour of business degree from one built around a generic capital-city commercial economy.

Majors typically span accounting, management, marketing, human resource management, tourism, and international business, with students able to combine a major with a minor from a different discipline entirely, including the sciences given JCU's research strength there. Work-integrated learning and industry placement opportunities lean toward regional Queensland employers, tourism operators, agribusiness exporters, mining services companies, and local government, rather than the large-city corporate employers a Brisbane or Sydney business degree would typically funnel students toward.

Graduates commonly move into regional Queensland business roles across tourism, agribusiness and government, though the degree equally supports relocation to southern capital cities for students wanting broader corporate career markets.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Fundamentals; Economics for Business; Introduction to Management; Marketing Principles; Business Law; Business Statistics
Year 2: Major units begin (Accounting, Management, Marketing, HRM, Tourism, or International Business); Business Analytics; interdisciplinary elective
Year 3: Advanced major units; Strategic Management; Work-Integrated Learning or Industry Placement; capstone project in chosen major
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Business - Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
This is one of JCU's double degrees, letting students complete a business qualification and an accredited psychology sequence concurrently rather than doing them back to back, shaving time off what would otherwise be two separate degrees. It suits students eyeing organisational psychology, human resources or consumer behaviour research, fields that sit squarely between the two disciplines, more than students who know from the outset they want a single clear specialisation.

The psychology component follows the standard Australian Psychology Accreditation Council-accredited structure (research methods, statistics, developmental and social psychology, cognitive psychology) needed to keep the postgraduate psychology pathway open, while the business side draws on core management, marketing, accounting and economics units. Because it's a combined degree, credit points are shared efficiently across genuinely overlapping content like statistics and research methods, rather than students repeating equivalent material twice.

Graduates typically move into HR, market research, organisational development or consulting roles that value the cross-disciplinary combination, or continue into an accredited fourth-year psychology program (Honours or Graduate Diploma) if aiming for registration as a psychologist.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology; Introduction to Management; Business Statistics; Biological Psychology; Marketing Principles
Year 2: Developmental Psychology; Social Psychology; Accounting Fundamentals; Economics for Business; Research Methods 1
Year 3: Cognitive Psychology; Organisational Behaviour; Research Methods 2; Business electives
Year 4: Abnormal Psychology; Psychological Assessment; Strategic Management; Research Project; business capstone unit
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
JCU's engineering degree runs across its Townsville and Cairns campuses with specialisations spanning civil, mechanical, electrical and renewable energy engineering, and the renewable energy stream in particular draws on North Queensland's genuine solar and wind resource base and the region's active renewable energy project pipeline. Like most Australian engineering degrees it's accredited by Engineers Australia and structured around a common early-years core: engineering mathematics, mechanics, materials, before students specialise.

What distinguishes it locally is the industry base students place into: North Queensland's mining services, tropical infrastructure (engineering built to cyclone-resistant standards is a genuinely different design problem than temperate-climate engineering), and renewable energy generation give JCU engineering graduates exposure to problems that don't come up in the same way at southern universities. Placement and industry-based project components are built into the later years, typically arranged with regional employers in mining services, utilities, or infrastructure contractors.

The honours year culminates in an independent capstone design or research project, commonly tackling a real regional engineering problem sourced from an industry partner, and graduates are well placed for roles across Queensland's resources, utilities, and infrastructure sectors specifically.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Mathematics 1 and 2; Engineering Mechanics; Materials Science; Introduction to Engineering Design
Year 2: Thermodynamics; Fluid Mechanics; Circuit Theory; Engineering Statistics; stream selection (Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, or Renewable Energy)
Year 3: Discipline-specific design and analysis units; Industry-Based Project or Placement
Year 4 (Honours): Capstone Engineering Project; Engineering Management and Professional Practice; advanced electives in chosen stream
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion with strong mathematics; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Marine Science
description:
JCU's marine science degree has a genuinely unusual advantage over almost every competitor: it's taught from a campus sitting on the doorstep of the Great Barrier Reef, with direct access to the university's own Orpheus Island Research Station for field-based coursework rather than occasional excursions. The degree runs an interdisciplinary structure spanning marine biology, oceanography, marine geoscience and marine resource management, so students don't specialise early: first year covers biodiversity, chemistry, earth science and mathematical foundations before marine-specific content ramps up.

By second and third year, students are working with functional biology of marine organisms, coral reef geomorphology, biological oceanography and marine chemistry, taught partly in JCU's research aquarium facilities and partly on-site at reef, island, seagrass and mangrove field locations around Townsville. That fieldwork access is the degree's real differentiator against marine science programs run out of universities with only occasional access to reef systems. JCU students are doing hands-on reef and coastal fieldwork as a routine part of coursework, not as an optional add-on.

Graduates go into marine research, environmental consulting, government marine park management (JCU's proximity to the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority in Townsville is a genuine local pipeline), and further postgraduate study in marine biology or oceanography.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Biodiversity; Chemistry: A Central Science; Evolution of the Earth; Mathematical Foundations; Introductory Marine Science
Year 2: Marine Physics; Marine Chemistry and Chemical Ecology; Functional Biology of Marine Organisms; Quantitative Methods in Science; Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
Year 3: Biological Oceanography; Coral Reef Geomorphology; Sedimentology and Stratigraphy; Advanced Environmental and Marine Geoscience Technologies and Applications; field research project (Orpheus Island Research Station)
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Medical Science (Honours)
description:
JCU's Medical Science Honours degree is a research-intensive four-year program that sits apart from the university's MBBS track: students here are working toward a biomedical science research qualification, not a clinical medical degree, though the two share early foundational science content and some students use this degree as a pathway into graduate-entry medicine. The honours year is built entirely around an independent, supervised research project, giving students a full year of genuine laboratory or field research experience with a personal academic advisor rather than the shorter research components typical of a standard science honours year elsewhere.

Core science content across the first three years covers human anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, pathology and biomedical research methods, with JCU's own research strengths in tropical medicine and infectious disease giving students exposure to research questions such as melioidosis, dengue, and tropical parasitology that most southern universities can't offer the same depth on. That tropical health research base is a genuine institutional advantage tied directly to JCU's location and long-running Australian Institute of Tropical Health and Medicine.

Graduates typically move into biomedical research careers, PhD study, or apply the honours research experience as part of a portfolio for graduate-entry medicine or other health professional programs.
curriculum:
Year 1: Human Anatomy 1 and 2; Biochemistry; Introduction to Pharmacology; Foundations of Medical Science
Year 2: Physiology; Pathology; Microbiology and Immunology; Biomedical Statistics
Year 3: Advanced Pharmacology; Molecular and Cellular Biology; Research Methods in Medical Science; electives (tropical medicine, infectious disease)
Year 4 (Honours): Independent Research Project (full year, supervised); Research Seminar Series; Thesis
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion with strong science background; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Nursing Science
description:
JCU's nursing degree is shaped heavily by where it's taught: Townsville and Cairns sit at the centre of North Queensland's regional and remote health system, and clinical placements routinely put students into settings that nursing students at metro universities rarely see: remote Indigenous community health services, Royal Flying Doctor Service-adjacent rural hospitals, and tropical disease presentations that simply don't show up in southern capital city caseloads. That regional and rural health exposure is arguably the degree's single biggest point of difference.

Core content follows the standard national nursing curriculum (anatomy and physiology, pharmacology, medical-surgical nursing, mental health nursing), building toward the clinical placement hours required for registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, but JCU folds in explicit content on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health and tropical and remote area health that reflects its own regional health workforce mission. The university has long positioned itself as training health professionals specifically to stay and work in northern Australia rather than training generalists who happen to study there.

Graduates commonly go straight into Queensland Health positions across the north, with a meaningful proportion moving into remote area nursing or Aboriginal community-controlled health organisations, career paths that JCU's clinical placement network is specifically built to support.
curriculum:
Year 1: Anatomy and Physiology; Foundations of Nursing Practice; Health Assessment; Introduction to Pharmacology; Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing 1 and 2; Mental Health Nursing; Pathophysiology; Clinical Placement 1 and 2 (regional/rural health settings)
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing; Rural and Remote Area Health; Community and Primary Health Nursing; Leadership and Transition to Practice; Clinical Placement 3 and 4 (culminating in a transition-to-practice placement)
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Engineering (Professional)
description:
JCU's professional engineering masters is aimed at engineering graduates looking to move into a specialised stream or convert international qualifications into Engineers Australia-recognised credentials, rather than a first engineering qualification. It typically includes a substantial industry-based project or work-integrated learning component, giving students without existing Australian industry experience a pathway into local employer networks.

Specialisation streams commonly mirror JCU's undergraduate strengths, including civil, mechanical, electrical and renewable energy, with advanced units in project management, sustainability and systems engineering layered over discipline-specific technical content. Given North Queensland's active mining services and renewable energy sectors, the program leans into practical industry-relevant content over pure research, positioning graduates for engineering management and senior technical roles rather than academic research careers.

Many students in the program are international graduates using it as both a technical upskilling qualification and a pathway toward permanent residency through the skilled migration program, given engineering's consistent presence on Australia's skilled occupation lists.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Advanced Engineering Mathematics; Engineering Project Management; Sustainability in Engineering Practice
Semester 2: Specialisation units (Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, or Renewable Energy stream)
Semester 3: Systems Engineering; Industry-Based Project (part 1); elective
Semester 4: Industry-Based Project (part 2) or Research Project; capstone seminar
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a related engineering discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
JCU's IT masters is built for career-changers as much as computing graduates, running a foundational first half that gets students with an unrelated undergraduate degree up to speed on programming, databases and systems analysis before the specialist content kicks in. That structure matters in practice: a large share of JCU's postgraduate IT cohort comes from Townsville and Cairns' international student population, many arriving from business, science or engineering backgrounds rather than computer science.

Specialisation options typically run through areas like cyber security, data science and networking, reflecting Queensland's own growing demand for security-cleared IT graduates given the state government and defence-adjacent employers based in the north. JCU doesn't try to compete with capital-city universities on sheer scale of tech industry placements, but it leans into a smaller cohort and closer staff access as its actual selling point, along with a research project or capstone in the final trimester that gives students a portfolio piece.

Graduates tend to move into regional Queensland IT roles, state government digital services, or relocate to Brisbane and interstate tech employers, with the degree also serving as a recognised pathway toward Australian Computer Society membership.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Programming Fundamentals; Database Systems; IT Systems Analysis and Design
Trimester 2: Data Structures and Algorithms; Networking Fundamentals; Professional Issues in IT
Trimester 3: Specialisation units (Cyber Security, Data Science, or Networking stream)
Trimester 4: Advanced specialisation units; Research Methods
Trimester 5: IT Project Management; elective
Trimester 6: Capstone Project or Research Dissertation

name: Master of Marine Biology
description:
This is one of JCU's flagship postgraduate degrees, built around the university's standing as a global hub for coral reef research. Students work directly with researchers connected to the ARC Centre of Excellence for Coral Reef Studies and use the Orpheus Island Research Station on the Great Barrier Reef as a routine part of coursework, not an occasional field trip. Core units include Advances in Marine Biology and Evidence and Controversy in Marine Science, both built to push students past undergraduate-level acceptance of textbook knowledge into critically engaging with live scientific debates in the field.

Students choose a major and then draw from an elective list that reads like a checklist of Great Barrier Reef research priorities: coral reef geomorphology, tropical marine ecology and coastal impacts, marine conservation biology, evolution and ecology of reef fishes, coral reef ecology, marine reserves as fisheries management tools, and the life history and evolution of reef corals. JCU frames the degree around five employer-demanded skill areas: marine biology, mathematics and statistical modelling, environmental science and management, marine and microbial ecology, and cross-disciplinary work, rather than a single narrow specialisation.

Graduates go into marine research institutions, conservation NGOs, government marine management agencies, and PhD study, with JCU's own research track record in reef science giving the degree real currency among employers in that space specifically.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Advances in Marine Biology; Evidence and Controversy in Marine Science; Career Planning
Semester 2: Major stream units begin; Biological Oceanography or Tropical Marine Ecology and Coastal Impacts
Semester 3: Elective units (Coral Reef Geomorphology, Marine Conservation Biology, Evolution and Ecology of Reef Fishes, Coral Reef Ecology, Marine Reserves as Fisheries Management Tools, Life History and Evolution of Reef Corals)
Semester 4: Research Project (Orpheus Island Research Station or affiliated field site)
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in science or related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Nursing
description:
JCU's Master of Nursing is aimed at registered nurses looking to move into advanced practice or leadership roles, with content shaped by the same regional and tropical health focus that runs through the university's undergraduate nursing program. Advanced health assessment, pharmacology and clinical reasoning units sit alongside content specific to rural, remote and Indigenous health service delivery, a genuine point of difference from masters programs built around a purely urban tertiary hospital model.

Many students in the program are already working across North Queensland's public health system while studying part-time, so JCU builds flexibility into delivery, with blended and online options supplementing on-campus intensives at Townsville or Cairns. The degree suits nurses aiming for clinical nurse consultant, nurse educator or nurse management roles more than the nurse practitioner prescribing pathway, though JCU offers separate specialist qualifications for that track.

Graduates typically move into senior clinical or leadership roles within Queensland Health or private health providers across northern Australia, and the degree is commonly used as a stepping stone toward further postgraduate study or PhD research in tropical and rural health nursing.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Advanced Health Assessment; Evidence-Based Practice; Pathophysiology for Advanced Practice
Semester 2: Leadership and Management in Health Services; Rural, Remote and Indigenous Health Systems; Research Methods in Nursing
Semester 3: Advanced Clinical Reasoning; elective; Practicum (part-time clinical cohort)
Semester 4: Capstone Project or Minor Thesis; Contemporary Issues in Nursing Practice
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a health-related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Public Health
description:
JCU's Master of Public Health draws heavily on the university's institutional focus on tropical health, and the degree's content reflects that: epidemiology and biostatistics units sit alongside genuine specialist content on tropical disease control, Indigenous and remote community health, and health system delivery across geographically dispersed, low-resource settings, problems that are core business for North Queensland's public health workforce rather than an academic afterthought.

Students typically move through core public health foundations (epidemiology, biostatistics, health promotion, health policy) before specialising, with JCU's own research centres in tropical medicine giving students access to genuine current research on diseases like dengue and melioidosis that remain far more relevant in the tropics than in temperate Australia. The degree also serves overseas students from the Pacific and Southeast Asia in meaningful numbers, given JCU's regional reputation in tropical and global health, which shapes cohort discussion and case studies toward a genuinely international public health lens rather than a purely domestic one.

Graduates move into state health department roles, Aboriginal community-controlled health organisations, international NGOs, and further doctoral research, with the degree also serving as professional development for practising clinicians moving into public health policy and management.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Epidemiology; Biostatistics for Public Health; Health Promotion and Policy
Semester 2: Tropical and Communicable Disease Control; Health Systems and Management; Research Methods
Semester 3: Indigenous and Remote Community Health; elective (Global Health, Environmental Health, or Health Economics)
Semester 4: Capstone Research Project or Practicum
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The generalist Bachelor of Business at Kaplan is the base version of a degree the school also sells with five bolt-on majors, so it's worth understanding what's actually compulsory before deciding whether the plain version or one of the named variants makes more sense. Only six subjects across the whole three-year degree are core: five foundational units at Level 100 covering business communication, accounting, economics, commercial law and numerical skills, plus a single Level 200 subject on governance, ethics and sustainability. Everything else, all the way through Level 300, is elective, which means this version of the degree is genuinely a choose-your-own-adventure business qualification rather than a management or marketing degree with a different label stapled on.

That structure suits two kinds of students: those who want breadth across accounting, marketing, management and IT without committing to a named major, and those transferring in in with credit from a Diploma of Business or another provider who want to fill out electives around whatever they've already completed. Nine trimesters and 24 subjects gets a full-time student through in three years, with intakes running five times a year (March, May, July, September, November) rather than the usual two-semester cycle, which is a real practical advantage for students who don't want to wait out a gap year to start.

Level 300 also carries the degree's two internship subjects, which give students who haven't locked in a specific career direction the chance to test an industry placement without it being tied to one major. It's an AQF Level 7 qualification, CRICOS-registered, and available at all five KBS campuses (Adelaide, Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth, Sydney), though the named-major versions of the degree aren't offered everywhere.
curriculum:
