name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Murdoch's nursing degree puts 20 weeks of supervised work experience into the course, spread across hospitals, aged care and community health settings rather than concentrated in a single block. Students typically encounter several different care contexts before they graduate rather than specialising in one setting by default. The School of Nursing's placement partners span both metropolitan Perth hospitals and rural WA services, so students can end up doing a rotation somewhere quite different from where they studied.

Before students reach a real ward, the course leans on simulated clinical environments and case-based learning to build competence and confidence, a fairly standard approach in Australian nursing education now, but one Murdoch runs with dedicated simulation labs on its Perth campus. Specialty placement areas mentioned by the school include gerontology, mental health, paediatrics and critical care, giving students exposure to sub-specialties they might not otherwise encounter until postgraduate study.

On graduation, students are eligible to register with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia through AHPRA, and the degree is commonly used as a springboard into postgraduate specialisation: critical care, mental health nursing or midwifery graduate-entry programs are the usual next step for those who want to sub-specialise.
curriculum:
Year 1: foundations of nursing practice, anatomy and physiology, health assessment, introduction to professional communication and ethics
Year 2: pathophysiology and pharmacology, mental health nursing, chronic disease and complex care, clinical placement blocks in hospital and community settings
Year 3: acute and critical care nursing, aged care and rehabilitation, leadership and transition to practice, specialty placement rotations (e.g. paediatrics, mental health, critical care)
Total placement across the course: approximately 20 weeks of work experience in hospitals, aged care and community settings
Total: 3 years full-time; graduates eligible for AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate and immunisation compliance required prior to clinical placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements for nursing.

name: Bachelor of Psychology
description:
This is Murdoch's APAC-accredited undergraduate psychology sequence: three years that lead, for eligible students, into a fourth Honours year rather than being accredited as a stand-alone terminal qualification. Students who complete both years exit eligible for provisional registration with the Psychology Board of Australia, which is the credential that actually matters for anyone planning to practise.

The Honours year is where the degree's research emphasis becomes explicit: students negotiate an original empirical research topic with a supervisor, and the year culminates in both a written thesis and a poster presented at a research conference, a dual output that mirrors how psychology researchers actually communicate findings, rather than a thesis alone. Advanced coursework alongside the research project balances theoretical grounding with the practical and professional issues graduates will face applying psychology in clinical, organisational or community settings.

Because Honours places are typically limited relative to the number of students completing the pass degree, students planning to progress need to maintain competitive grades through years one to three, a standard feature of Australian psychology accreditation nationwide, not unique to Murdoch, but one that shapes how seriously students need to take GPA management from first year.
curriculum:
Year 1: introduction to psychology, biological psychology, cognitive psychology, introductory statistics and research methods
Year 2: developmental psychology, social psychology, personality and individual differences, intermediate research methods
Year 3: abnormal psychology, psychological assessment, advanced statistics, discipline electives
Year 4 (Honours, separate accredited course): advanced seminars in applied psychology, supervised original empirical research project, thesis and conference-style poster presentation
Total: 3 years full-time (pass degree); Honours (4th year) APAC-accredited and required for provisional psychologist registration eligibility

name: Bachelor of Science / Doctor of Veterinary Medicine
description:
Murdoch runs the only veterinary school in Western Australia, and this is its flagship pathway: a three-year Bachelor of Science (Veterinary Biology) that transitions directly into a two-year Doctor of Veterinary Medicine, with the DVM itself run across trimesters rather than standard semesters to compress five years of content into the combined structure. Students don't apply separately into the DVM. The two qualifications are integrated by design, though academic progression standards still apply at the transition point.

The degree gives access to genuinely rare undergraduate infrastructure for an Australian veterinary program: a working teaching hospital treating companion animals, exotics, farm animals and horses, plus an operational farm, all on the same Perth campus rather than split across satellite sites. Species-group electives ("streaming") let students start weighting their final years toward large animal, equine or small animal practice depending on where they see their career heading, and the final year is largely spent immersed in the teaching hospital rather than in lecture theatres.

Because the DVM sits at AQF level 9, a master's-equivalent qualification, this is one of the longer and more structured pathways in the Murdoch catalogue, and the tuition reflects the cost of running live-animal clinical training rather than being comparable to a standard science degree.
curriculum:
Years 1–3 (Bachelor of Science, Veterinary Biology): animal biology and physiology, biochemistry, animal husbandry, foundational veterinary science units, six semesters total
Years 4–5 (Doctor of Veterinary Medicine, trimester-based): clinical veterinary training, species-group elective streaming (large animal, equine, small animal), professional and business skills for veterinary practice, six trimesters total
Final year: primarily hands-on clinical rotations through the on-campus veterinary teaching hospital and farm
Total: 5 years full-time, integrated BSc + DVM (AQF level 9 for the DVM component)

description:
A three-year degree accredited by Exercise and Sports Science Australia at exercise science level, so graduates are eligible to register as an Accredited Exercise Scientist. It covers exercise physiology, biomechanics, sport psychology and motor control, teaching students to assess performance, analyse movement and design exercise programs, with work-based learning across sport, fitness and health settings.

Facilities include a dedicated exercise physiology lab, strength and conditioning and rehabilitation labs, and a performance lab with 3D motion capture and a 50-metre running track. Entry is an ATAR of about 70 with several alternative pathways. It suits students who want an applied sport science career, and it is the standard entry point to Murdoch's Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology for those going on to clinical practice.

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Murdoch's MBA is a comparatively compact program by design, aimed at working professionals rather than career-switchers straight out of undergrad, and the course leans on Perth's business environment (mining and resources, agribusiness and government) for its case material and guest-lecturer network more than trying to compete with the east-coast MBAs on global brand recognition alone.

Coursework covers the standard MBA core (strategy, finance, leadership, marketing) but Murdoch places a specific emphasis on practical applied projects tied to real organisations, consistent with the university's broader Work Integrated Learning approach that shows up across its business degrees. Students without an undergraduate business background typically complete foundation units before the core MBA content, which widens entry beyond commerce graduates to professionals moving into management from technical or clinical careers.

The program is positioned as a flexible, often part-time-friendly qualification for working Western Australians rather than a full-time residential cohort experience, which shapes its delivery mode and scheduling more than curriculum content.
curriculum:
Foundation units (if required): accounting and finance fundamentals, economics for managers, quantitative methods
Core: strategic management, organisational leadership, corporate finance, marketing management, operations and supply chain management
Applied learning: business consulting project or work-based capstone tied to a real organisation
Electives: choice from areas such as international business, human resource management, or project management
Total: typically 1.5–2 years part-time (accelerated full-time options available)
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree plus at least 2-3 years of relevant professional work experience (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Business Administration (Global)
description:
A two-year MBA (48 credit points) that, unlike most Australian MBAs, requires no prior work experience, so it is built for early-career graduates and international students as much as for established managers. The core covers management, marketing, accounting, finance, strategy, and professional ethics, and students then choose a focus area such as business finance, people management, sustainability, health management, or international marketing.

A work-integrated learning component places students with local businesses and government departments for a professional placement or applied research project. It runs face-to-face and online with three intakes a year (trimesters). Entry is a bachelor's degree, or a portfolio route with a CV, a GMAT or GRE score, and an 800-word statement. It suits people using the MBA to change career direction or to build a general management base early rather than to convert existing seniority into a formal qualification.

name: Master of Clinical Chiropractic
description:
A two-year graduate-entry master's that, combined with an approved bachelor's degree, completes the qualification needed to practise as a chiropractor. Entry requires a cognate bachelor's degree with a GPA of at least 2.0 and completed tertiary units in human anatomy and human physiology within the last ten years; at Murdoch the usual feeder is the Bachelor of Health Science.

The program is accredited by the Council on Chiropractic Education Australasia, so graduates are eligible for registration with the Chiropractic Board of Australia and in New Zealand, with pathways to recognition in several other countries. Clinical training runs in Murdoch's teaching clinic. It suits health science graduates committed to a manual, primary-contact allied health career.

name: Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology
description:
A one-year master's (three trimesters) that builds on an exercise science background to qualify graduates as clinical exercise physiologists. It covers exercise prescription, clinical assessment and behaviour change for chronic disease management, and includes a year-long industry placement working alongside Accredited Exercise Physiologists and other health professionals.

The program is accredited by Exercise and Sports Science Australia at exercise physiology level, so graduates are eligible to apply to register with ESSA as an Accredited Exercise Physiologist. Entry requires a weighted average of at least 60 in prior study plus current ESSA Exercise Scientist registration, a recent ESSA-accredited exercise science degree, or completion of a graduate entry assessment. Facilities include physiology laboratories and a performance centre with 3D motion capture. It suits exercise science graduates moving into clinical practice with chronic and complex conditions.

english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

Students work with real clients through MESH, an on-campus communication consultancy, and a work-integrated learning placement is part of the program. Entry is a communication or related bachelor's degree, or substantial industry experience (about ten years in media and communication, or five in a management role), which opens it to career changers. It suits people moving toward senior roles in communication, PR, digital strategy or media.

Two supervised placements are required: an internal one at Murdoch's on-campus Caladenia Clinic and an external one in a community agency, covering assessment and individual and group treatment with diverse clients. The course is accredited by the Psychotherapy and Counselling Federation of Australia and the Australian Counselling Association, and graduates are eligible for provisional PACFA registration and Level 2 ACA membership. Selection includes a personal statement, CV and interview. It is taught face-to-face in Perth and suits people committed to clinical counselling practice in government or non-government mental health settings.

A two-year master's (48 credit points) open to graduates from any discipline, with three majors: Crime Science, Criminal Behaviour, and Legal Studies. The coursework covers criminological theory, criminal behaviour analysis, cybercrime, terrorism investigation, and the criminal law response to emerging offences, with an optional thesis pathway for students heading toward a PhD.

Teaching staff include people with policing and forensic backgrounds, and the degree includes work-integrated learning. Advanced standing is generous: up to 12 credit points for a criminology honours degree or relevant experience, up to 24 for a graduate diploma in criminology. It runs face-to-face and online from the Perth campus with two intakes a year. It suits graduates and working professionals targeting law enforcement, intelligence, corrections, cybersecurity or criminal justice policy.

A two-year master's (48 credit points) covering public policy and international affairs, critical approaches to development, sustainability, state and governance dynamics, food security, gender, health and security studies.

Students finish with a capstone that can be a case study project, a supervised internship or a research thesis. It runs full-time, part-time or blended, and is open to graduates of any discipline. It suits people heading into international development work with NGOs, government aid programs, regional organisations or consultancies.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Education
description:
A two-year master's (48 credit points) for people already working in education, not a route into teaching. Murdoch states plainly that it is not a teaching qualification and is not accredited by the Teacher Registration Board of WA.

Students choose one major from inclusive and special needs education, instructional leadership, international education (which can lead toward International Baccalaureate educator certification), sustainable pedagogies, or e-learning, and complete research methods units and a supervised research project. Classes run after work or in intensive blocks during school holidays. Entry is a bachelor's degree in any field. It suits practising teachers, school leaders and education administrators wanting a specialisation or a research pathway toward a PhD.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; teaching or workplace-training experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Education (Research)
admission_requirements: An honours degree or equivalent research qualification in education, plus a research proposal.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Engineering Practice
description:
A two-year master's that takes graduates of a three-year engineering technology degree up to professional engineer level, and also accepts holders of a four-year engineering degree wanting to upskill. Three majors hold full Engineers Australia accreditation at professional engineer level and are recognised under the Washington Accord: environmental and sustainable systems, smart and renewable electrical power systems, and intelligent industrial control and autonomous systems.

The degree builds in more than 300 hours of practical experience through an integrated professional practice unit and a professional portfolio, and offers design or research minors for those heading toward a doctorate. It suits engineering technologists seeking chartered-track recognition and engineers moving into renewable energy, automation or environmental systems work.
admission_requirements: A bachelor of engineering technology or equivalent, plus relevant industry experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Environmental Science
description:
A one-year master's built for people who already hold a graduate certificate or diploma in environmental assessment, management or science, taking that foundation into advanced research methods, 21st-century environmental policy, climate change adaptation for ecosystems and societies, and systems-dynamics modelling.

Field learning uses Murdoch's on-campus conservation wetlands and banksia woodland along with national and international field trips, and every student completes a supervised advanced research project with a written report and oral defence. It runs face-to-face or mixed-mode, with some external units still requiring short on-campus attendance. It suits environmental professionals moving into consulting, impact assessment or senior project roles who want a research-capable qualification while continuing to work.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in science, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Exercise Science (Research)
admission_requirements: An honours degree in exercise/sport science (or equivalent) and an approved research proposal.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Food Security
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Forensic Science
description:
An 18-month master's (36 credit points) that is unusually hands-on for a forensic science degree. Students work across bloodstain pattern analysis, forensic chemistry and toxicology, fingerprint and impression evidence, forensic anthropology and clandestine grave work, digital forensics, and expert-witness and courtroom skills.

The practical side is the draw: multiple crime scene simulation rooms on and off campus, and Whitby Falls Farm, where students process a simulated large-scale homicide and a clandestine grave. Guest lecturers come from law enforcement, forensic laboratories and medicine, and students contribute to a Cold Case Review initiative. Entry requires a bachelor's degree in biological or chemical science or a related health field; criminology graduates without science units complete a graduate certificate or diploma first. It suits science graduates moving into forensic analysis, investigation or research roles in policing, national security or pathology.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in science, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Health Administration, Policy and Leadership
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; healthcare-sector experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Health Care Management
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; healthcare-sector experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of High Performance Sport
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in sport/exercise science, or equivalent; coaching or high-performance sport experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Human Resources Management
description:
A two-year master's (48 credit points) with three trimester intakes a year, covering strategic HR planning and organisational change, talent acquisition and workforce planning, industrial relations and employment law, organisational culture, human capital development, reward strategy, and people analytics and evidence-based decision-making.

Murdoch builds in virtual-reality simulations, with avatars used to practise interviews and conflict resolution, alongside digital HR platforms and real industry projects with guest lecturers from healthcare, IT, aged care, banking and education. The course is professionally accredited. Entry is a bachelor's degree plus about two years of work experience, or a demonstrated equivalent through professional experience subject to approval. It suits career changers moving into HR and practitioners wanting to move from operational to strategic people-management roles.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; some professional experience preferred.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Infectious Disease Surveillance and Control
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in health/biomedical science, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
Murdoch structures this masters with real flexibility around exit points: complete 48 credit points of coursework alone, or 36 credit points of coursework plus a 12-point dissertation for students wanting a research component on their transcript. Students can also stop earlier and walk away with a Graduate Certificate after one semester or a Graduate Diploma after a year, which suits people testing whether a full masters is worth the time commitment before fully committing.

Three specialisation options are on offer (IT Management, Data Science, and Internetworking and Security), reflecting genuinely different career tracks rather than cosmetic variations on the same content. The course was designed with industry input specifically aimed at producing graduates who can solve applied IT problems rather than purely theoretical ones, and the school points to demand across sectors as varied as mining, health and government IT in Western Australia, which is a more resource-and-government-heavy economy than the east coast tech markets most IT masters programs are pitched at.

For international students in particular, the staged qualification structure (cert, diploma, masters) offers a practical safety net if visa timelines or personal circumstances change mid-course.
curriculum:
Coursework core: advanced database systems, IT project management, systems analysis and design, research methods for IT
Specialisation (choose one): IT Management, Data Science, or Internetworking and Security — each with four to six specialisation units
Coursework pathway: 48 credit points of coursework
Coursework plus dissertation pathway: 36 credit points coursework plus 12-credit-point dissertation
Exit points: Graduate Certificate (1 semester), Graduate Diploma (1 year), Master of IT (typically 1.5–2 years full-time)
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; no prior IT background required for the standard entry stream.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Laws by Research
admission_requirements: An honours degree in law (or equivalent) and an approved research proposal.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Philosophy
admission_requirements: An honours degree (or equivalent) and an approved research proposal; supervisor agreement required.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description:
This is Murdoch's conversion masters for non-accounting graduates wanting to move into the profession: a two-year program (or as fast as 16 months for students who can accelerate) that covers the accounting body of knowledge from a standing start rather than assuming a commerce background. It carries direct accreditation weight: graduates meet the academic requirements for CPA Australia associate membership and can enter the Chartered Accountants ANZ program directly, which are the two professional bodies that actually gate accounting careers in Australia.

There's also a less commonly advertised international angle: ACCA accreditation with exemptions covering up to nine exams across the Applied Knowledge and Applied Skills levels, which matters disproportionately for the international student cohort this kind of conversion masters typically attracts, since it shortens the path to a globally recognised qualification alongside the Australian one.

Because it's explicitly a professional-accreditation degree rather than a research or general business masters, the unit list is fairly prescribed by what CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants ANZ require for recognition, leaving less room for elective wandering than, say, an MBA.
curriculum:
Foundation/conversion units: accounting principles, financial accounting, management accounting, business law, economics for accountants
Core professional units: corporate accounting, auditing and assurance, taxation law, accounting information systems, corporate finance
Capstone: accounting theory and contemporary issues, professional ethics in accounting
Total: 2 years full-time standard (accelerated completion in as little as 16 months for eligible students); CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants ANZ recognised, ACCA exemptions available for up to 9 exams
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (no prior accounting background required for the standard entry stream).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Professional Accounting (Advanced)
description:
A two-year conversion master's (48 credit points) accredited by both CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, so graduates meet the academic entry requirement for the CPA Program and the CA ANZ Chartered Accountants Program.

It is explicitly for people without an accounting background: applicants who already hold an accounting major from an Australian university are not admitted. Students work in project teams with industry partners including government agencies, mining companies, accounting firms and real estate organisations, applying accounting and business finance theory to live problems. It runs face-to-face and online with three trimester intakes a year. It suits graduates from other fields moving into accounting, audit, tax, financial forensics, restructuring or enterprise risk work.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (no prior accounting background required for the standard entry stream).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Professional Communication
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Professional Psychology
description:
A postgraduate psychology degree that provides the coursework and supervised practice for the fifth year of the psychology training sequence, after an accredited three-year degree and honours. It is accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council as a packaged Level 2 and 3 program, and it includes two placements in the final stage.

Graduates are then eligible to apply for general registration as a psychologist after one further year of supervised practice, the 5+1 internship pathway. Admission is competitive: an accredited psychology sequence with a distinction average in psychology units is the guideline, plus referee reports, a statement and often an interview. It suits people whose goal is general registration as a psychologist by the most direct route.
admission_requirements: An honours degree (or equivalent GPA) in psychology accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Public Policy
description:
A two-year master's (48 credit points) covering the foundations of public policy, comparative governance, public sector administration and management, political communication, and public sector corruption and its prevention, with electives in areas such as environmental policy and international development.

Students complete a research project with a Murdoch industry partner for academic credit, and there is an optional in-country study option in Indonesia through the ACICIS consortium. It is open to graduates of any discipline and runs face-to-face or blended from the Perth campus with two intakes a year. Recognition of prior learning can shorten it. It suits recent graduates and working professionals aiming for roles as policy analysts, ministerial advisers, evaluation officers or policy consultants in government, the not-for-profit sector or consulting.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Renewable and Sustainable Energy
description:
A two-year master's covering renewable energy systems design, energy efficiency and building energy assessment, micro-grid technology, carbon management, and energy policy in developing economies, ending in a substantial research project.

Murdoch has taught and researched energy since 1975 and describes this as the most comprehensive renewable energy program in Australia, run through the Murdoch University Energy Research and Innovation Group with outdoor solar, wind and hybrid test facilities. Entry is a bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience, with some units assuming high school physics. It suits graduates moving into power generation, renewable manufacturing, energy consultancy, government policy or international development, and it deliberately spans both the technical and policy sides.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree in science/engineering, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Science in Information Technology
description:
An 18-month master's (36 credit points) with three specialisations: Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, Cyber Security and Networking, and Information Technology Management. The coursework covers IT systems management, data science, networking and network security, decision-making in IT environments, and the legal and ethical side of ICT, with an optional dissertation pathway and a one-year exit point to a graduate diploma.

Entry accepts non-IT graduates: an ACS-accredited IT bachelor's degree, or a bachelor's degree plus an approved AQF Level 8 IT qualification, or an honours degree with five or more years of relevant experience. It runs face-to-face and online. It suits people moving toward senior technical and management roles such as IT manager, CIO or director of technology.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent; no prior IT background required for the standard entry stream.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Sustainable Development
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Teaching (Primary)
description:
A two-year graduate-entry primary teaching degree (with a one-year graduate diploma exit point). Entry requires a bachelor's degree with at least one year of study across primary curriculum areas such as English, mathematics, science, the arts, humanities and social sciences, or health and physical education, plus evidence of consistently solid grades.

School placements run throughout the course, and Murdoch was the first Australian university to use SimLab simulated-classroom technology with virtual students for practising classroom management. It is accredited by AITSL in articulation with the Teacher Registration Board of WA, so graduates can apply for registration, and students must pass LANTITE. Commonwealth Prac Payment support is available during placements. It suits graduates and career changers moving into primary teaching.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree; satisfactory National Police Certificate and Working with Children Check required prior to professional placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Teaching (Secondary)
description:
A 1.75-year graduate-entry teaching degree. Entry requires a bachelor's degree with a main teaching area of at least six units (with depth at third-year level) and a second teaching area of at least four units, in fields aligned to the WA secondary curriculum: English, mathematics, science, humanities and social sciences, or health and physical education, with vocational education and training available as a second area for people with industry experience.

School placements run throughout the program, and Murdoch uses SimLab simulated-classroom technology to practise classroom management first. It is accredited by AITSL and the Teacher Registration Board of WA, so graduates can apply for registration. Students must attempt LANTITE in year one and pass it before graduating. It suits graduates with a strong subject background moving into secondary teaching.
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree; satisfactory National Police Certificate and Working with Children Check required prior to professional placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Veterinary Clinical Studies
description:
This postgraduate degree is aimed at practising veterinarians rather than new graduates: it's a clinical-studies masters, not an entry qualification, and it exists to let working vets deepen expertise in a chosen clinical area while using Murdoch's teaching hospital and specialist faculty as a resource base. That puts it in a fairly small category of Australian veterinary postgraduate offerings, since most CPD for vets in this country comes through shorter certificate-level courses rather than a full masters.

Because Murdoch's veterinary school runs an active teaching hospital treating companion animals, farm animals, horses and exotics, students in this masters typically get case exposure across species groups rather than being restricted to whatever caseload a private practice happens to see, and can work alongside specialist clinicians in the areas they're aiming to build depth in.

The degree functions as both a career step for vets aiming toward specialist recognition pathways and a way to formalise clinical knowledge gained through years of general practice into a credentialed postgraduate qualification.
curriculum:
Core units: advanced clinical diagnostics, evidence-based veterinary practice, research methods in clinical veterinary science
Clinical specialisation stream: selected from areas such as small animal medicine, large animal/equine medicine, or veterinary surgery, based on hospital caseload and supervisor availability
Applied component: supervised clinical case studies and clinical research project within Murdoch's veterinary teaching hospital
Total: typically 1.5–2 years, structured for practising veterinarians (part-time options available)
admission_requirements: A veterinary science degree (BVMS or equivalent) and current veterinary registration.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: OnTrack Flex
admission_requirements: No ATAR or Year 12 completion required; open to domestic students seeking an alternative entry pathway into a Murdoch degree.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent, typical bar for enabling/pathway programs.

name: OnTrack Sprint
admission_requirements: Must have completed Year 12 within the past 18 months; no ATAR required.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent, typical bar for enabling/pathway programs.

name: Research Masters with Training
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree with a strong academic record and an approved research proposal.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: TLC Learning for Tomorrow
admission_requirements: An enabling pathway for domestic students seeking an alternative entry route; no ATAR or Year 12 completion required.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent, typical bar for enabling/pathway programs.

name: Waardong First Nations Veterinary Medicine and Science Path
admission_requirements: An Indigenous-specific enabling pathway for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students aspiring to veterinary medicine and science; no ATAR required.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent, typical bar for enabling/pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Fine Arts (Acting)
description:
NIDA's Bachelor of Fine Arts (Acting) is the course most people mean when they say "I want to go to NIDA." It takes roughly 24 students a year, chosen from several thousand applicants who audition through a multi-round process rather than submit an ATAR or ranked application, and it runs them through three years of full-time studio training in acting, voice, movement and music. There's no lecture-hall version of this degree. Classes are built around scenework, rehearsal and full-scale production, with students mounting public seasons in NIDA's own theatres from second year onward.

What separates it from a drama major at a general university is density: cohorts stay small on purpose so that every student is cast, coached and critiqued individually across four disciplines simultaneously rather than picking one. Alumni include Cate Blanchett, Judy Davis, Mel Gibson, Baz Luhrmann and Hugh Jackman's Broadway-adjacent contemporaries, and the acting course's graduating showcases are attended by casting directors and agents as a matter of course, not aspiration. Third-year students perform for industry audiences as one of their final assessed units.

Graduates leave with an agent meeting more often than a job offer, and the degree makes no claim otherwise. NIDA is explicit that acting is a vocational, audition-driven career, and the course is built to get people work-ready rather than employed on day one. What it does guarantee is stagecraft: camera technique, microphone work and full-length production experience that most drama graduates elsewhere only get in a final-year showcase, condensed into three years of near-daily practice.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations in Acting, Voice Production, Movement for the Actor, Music and Singing for Actors, Introduction to Text and Script Analysis, first-year ensemble scene study
Year 2: Acting for Camera, Advanced Voice and Speech, Physical Theatre and Stage Combat, Period Style and Verse, Improvisation, rehearsal and performance in a NIDA mainstage production
Year 3: Contemporary and Classical Repertoire, Screen Acting Intensive, Audition Technique and Self-Tape, Industry Showcase preparation, capstone public season performed in front of casting agents and industry guests
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion (or equivalent) plus mandatory audition and interview; highly competitive, small annual intake
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Fine Arts (Costume)
description:
NIDA's BFA (Costume) trains makers, not just designers: the course sits deliberately closer to the workroom than the drawing board. Over three years students build hands-on competency in pattern cutting, fitting, construction, dyeing, millinery, leatherwork and tailoring, working on real costumes for NIDA's public season rather than folio pieces alone. It has been ranked among the world's top ten costume courses, a fact the school leans on in recruitment, and the comparison is fair: few undergraduate costume programs anywhere put this many construction hours into a three-year degree.

The career track this points at is costume making and costume supervision (theatre, film and increasingly streaming production in Sydney's growing screen sector) rather than costume design as a standalone creative role (that lives more in the Design for Performance course). Graduates tend to move into workrooms, wardrobe departments and supervisory roles on professional productions, sometimes returning to NIDA itself as workshop staff.

Because every cohort works across NIDA's actual production calendar, the degree doubles as an apprenticeship: students fit real actors, meet real deadlines, and answer to a costume supervisor the way they will on a professional job, well before graduation.
curriculum:
Year 1: Pattern Cutting and Construction Fundamentals, Fabric and Dye Techniques, Costume History I, hand and machine sewing intensives
Year 2: Millinery and Headwear, Leatherwork and Armour, Costume History II, fitting and alteration on a NIDA mainstage production
Year 3: Costume Supervision and Budgeting, Advanced Tailoring, Digital and Print Techniques for Costume, capstone placement supervising costume for a full production season
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion (or equivalent) plus portfolio submission and interview
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Fine Arts (Design for Performance)
description:
Where the Costume degree trains makers, BFA (Design for Performance) trains the designers who conceive the whole visual world of a production: set, costume, lighting and increasingly video, learned in combination rather than as separate tracks. Students take on key design roles across NIDA's public season over three years, working directly with directing, acting and technical production students under real staging conditions: a design has to survive a get-in, a budget meeting and a director's notes, not just look good in a folio.

The course structure reflects a specific argument NIDA makes about design training: that a set designer who has never had to think about how lighting or costume will interact with their set is only half-trained, so students are pushed toward frameworks that treat spatial design, costume, lighting, sound and staging as one integrated problem rather than four separate electives.

Graduates tend to move into design and associate design roles across Australian theatre and opera companies, with several going on to the MFA (Design for Performance) or directly into industry design assistant positions, carrying a body of produced work rather than a purely academic portfolio.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Spatial Design, Costume Design Fundamentals, Drawing and Model-Making for the Stage, Design History
Year 2: Lighting Design Principles, Collaborative Design Process, design role on a NIDA studio production
Year 3: Advanced Set and Costume Design, Video and Projection for Performance, capstone design role on a full mainstage production season
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion (or equivalent) plus portfolio submission and interview
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Fine Arts (Properties and Objects)
description:
NIDA's BFA (Properties and Objects), marketed by the school under the name Props and Effects, is one of only a small handful of dedicated undergraduate degrees anywhere in the world for prop-making and practical effects, and the course leans hard into that rarity. Students spend three years building genuinely wide-ranging maker skills: metalwork, woodwork, mould-making and casting, scenic art, puppetry, electronics, 3D modelling and digital fabrication, alongside costume jewellery and architectural model-making, entered by interview and a project portfolio rather than academic ranking alone.

The pitch is less about theatre alone than about the broader entertainment and events industries that need designer-makers who can build physical and digital objects to a brief, on a deadline, at production quality. Theme parks, film and TV art departments, opera and large-scale events all draw on this skill set, and the course is structured to make graduates employable across that whole range rather than only in a theatre workshop.

An industry placement is built into the degree, so students leave with a maker's CV that includes work outside NIDA's own walls as well as within them, a meaningful difference from props training folded into a general design degree.
curriculum:
Year 1: Prop-Making Fundamentals (wood, metal, mould-making), Technical Drawing for Props, Materials and Sustainable Making
Year 2: Puppetry and Animatronics, Scenic Art, Digital Fabrication and 3D Modelling, prop-building for a NIDA production
Year 3: Practical Effects and Electronics, Advanced Casting and Finishing, industry placement, capstone prop and effects design for a mainstage season
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion (or equivalent) plus portfolio submission and interview
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Fine Arts (Technical Production)
description:
Technical Production at NIDA is the degree behind the show rather than in front of it: stage management, lighting and sound operation, rigging, production management and the logistics that keep a season running on schedule and on budget. It is a three-year BFA assessed almost entirely through practical production work: students crew, call and manage real NIDA seasons from first year, moving from assistant roles to running shows solo by third year.

The course exists because Australian theatre, film and event industries have a persistent shortage of trained stage managers and production technicians relative to designers and performers, and NIDA markets the degree accordingly. Graduates report high placement rates into stage management and production roles across theatre companies, touring productions and corporate/event technical work, which pays comparably well and more reliably than performance-track careers. It is a less glamorous pitch than acting or directing, and the course doesn't try to disguise that; it sells itself on employability.

Students graduate having actually called cues and managed crews under production pressure, not simulated it, which is the main thing employers in this field say they can't get from a generalist arts degree.
curriculum:
Year 1: Stage Management Fundamentals, Introduction to Lighting and Sound Systems, Production Documentation and Scheduling, crewing on first-year productions
Year 2: Rigging and Automation, Production Electrics, Show Calling and Cueing, assistant stage manager role on a mainstage season
Year 3: Production Management, Touring and Event Logistics, Health and Safety in Live Production, capstone role as stage manager or production manager on a full NIDA season
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion (or equivalent) plus interview; no audition required
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Fine Arts (Design for Performance)
description:
The Master of Fine Arts (Design for Performance) takes designers who already have a foundation (often a BFA, an art or architecture degree, or professional design experience) and puts them through an intensive studio program spanning set, costume, lighting and increasingly video design, with an explicit push toward cross-disciplinary fluency rather than a single specialism. Past cohorts have travelled to Europe as part of the course, including a documented trip built around the Avignon Festival, reflecting NIDA's view that design training benefits from exposure to major international festival production at scale.

Students take on real design roles on NIDA's own season during the course, working alongside directing and technical production students under production conditions rather than in a design studio disconnected from staging. The emphasis throughout is on collaboration: a design that only works on paper but can't survive contact with a director, a budget and a get-in schedule isn't considered finished training.

Graduates leave positioned for design and associate design roles in theatre, opera and screen production, with a portfolio built from produced, reviewed work rather than speculative concepts.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Design Studio (set and costume integration), Spatial and Scenic Design, Collaborative Process with Directors and Actors
Semester 2: Lighting and Video Design, Design for Opera and Large-Scale Work, international studio intensive
Semester 3 (final): capstone design role on a NIDA mainstage production, professional portfolio and industry presentation
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus portfolio submission and interview
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Fine Arts (Directing)
description:
The Master of Fine Arts (Directing) is an 18-month, full-time studio course rather than a research degree: there is no thesis in the academic sense, only a body of directed work culminating in NIDA's Festival of Emerging Artists, where each graduating director stages a 40-minute production in front of the public and industry. Entry is by audition and interview, typically drawing on applicants who already have some directing or assistant-directing experience in theatre, screen or opera, and cohorts are small enough that supervisors can shape training around each director's existing voice rather than a fixed syllabus.

The course moves across classical text, contemporary and devised work, screen directing and opera, on the reasoning that a director who has only ever staged one mode of performance is under-prepared for the freelance reality of the profession. Alumni tracked by NIDA include Tony-nominated director Kip Williams, Emmy and DGA-recognised director Shannon Murphy, and Opera Queensland's Patrick Nolan, a spread that reflects the course's insistence on cross-form fluency rather than specialising early.

Because the degree culminates in a publicly reviewed festival rather than a closed assessment, graduating directors leave with a produced, witnessed piece of work and, often, the first professional relationships that come from being seen by working practitioners in the room.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Directing Studio I (text-based theatre), Dramaturgy and Script Analysis, Working with Actors, Directing for Screen introduction
Semester 2: Directing Studio II (contemporary and devised performance), Directing Opera and Music Theatre, Collaborative Design Process, assistant-directing placement on a NIDA or partner production
Semester 3 (final): capstone production for the Festival of Emerging Artists, professional practice and industry engagement seminars
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus audition/portfolio and interview (approximate, typical bar, not program-page-verified)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall (typical bar for postgrad at private AU providers, approximate)

name: Master of Fine Arts (Writing for Performance)
description:
The Master of Fine Arts (Writing for Performance) is NIDA's dramatic writing degree, run under the course title MFA (Dramatic Writing) and built as an 18-month intensive rather than a slow-paced workshop model. Writers work across theatre, film, television and interactive forms simultaneously, producing two full-length works over the course alongside multiple treatments, outlines and pitches. That output mirrors what a working screenwriter or playwright actually has to generate, rather than a single polished thesis script.

Work is developed in the room with actors and directors rather than in isolation: scripts get workshopped, read aloud and revised against what actually happens when performers pick them up, which NIDA treats as the central discipline of the course. Alongside the writing itself, students study contemporary philosophy, ethics, cultural studies and classical rhetoric, a somewhat unusual combination for a practical writing degree, justified by NIDA on the grounds that dramatic writing is argument and worldview as much as craft.

Graduates leave with a portfolio built for pitching: treatments and outlines as well as finished scripts, reflecting the reality that professional writers sell ideas as often as they sell finished work.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Dramatic Writing Studio I, Script Analysis and Structure, Writing for Theatre
Semester 2: Writing for Screen and Interactive Media, Workshopping with Actors and Directors, Contemporary Philosophy and Cultural Studies for Writers
Semester 3 (final): second full-length work, portfolio of treatments and pitches, industry engagement and professional practice seminar
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus submission of writing samples/portfolio and interview
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Behavioural Science (Psychology)
description:
QUT's Bachelor of Behavioural Science (Psychology) is the first three years of the standard path into registered practice, and it's accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council on that basis, meaning graduates who continue into the Honours year and beyond are working through a nationally recognised sequence rather than a QUT-only track. The degree spends its early semesters on the empirical spine of the discipline: research methods, statistics, biological bases of behaviour, cognition, developmental and social psychology, before students pick from areas like forensic psychology, health psychology and organisational behaviour in later years.

What distinguishes it from a generic psych degree is QUT's applied, Brisbane-industry-adjacent framing: the course sits inside the Faculty of Health and draws on QUT's connections to hospitals, schools and community health services for guest input and, in some units, observation opportunities, rather than treating psychology purely as a laboratory science. Students planning to become a psychologist should expect this degree to be step one of a longer sequence: an Honours year (also APAC-accredited at QUT) followed by supervised practice or further postgraduate study is still required before registration with the Psychology Board of Australia.

Graduates who don't continue into clinical training still leave with a solid quantitative and behavioural-science skill set that's found use in HR, market research, policy and community services roles across Queensland.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Psychology, Research Methods and Statistics I, Lifespan Development, university-wide elective units
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Social Psychology, Research Methods and Statistics II, Personality and Individual Differences, introductory units in an applied area (forensic, health or organisational psychology)
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology, Psychological Assessment, an applied psychology elective sequence (choice of forensic, health, organisational or community strands), a research project unit
Throughout: professional practice and ethics content embedded across units; APAC-accredited sequence continues into a separate Honours (4th) year for students pursuing registration
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12, ATAR approx. 75-80
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Business (Management)
description:
The management major inside QUT's Bachelor of Business is built around a fairly practical premise: most graduates will spend their first years managing people and projects rather than setting corporate strategy, so the course front-loads organisational behaviour, HR fundamentals and operations before getting into higher-level strategy content in the final year. QUT Business School's location in the Brisbane CBD (the Gardens Point campus sits a short walk from the city's professional services and government precinct) feeds into guest lectures, case studies drawn from Queensland employers, and internship placements that many students slot into their elective units.

The course structure is standard business-degree scaffolding: core units in accounting, economics, marketing and business law sit alongside the management major. But the major itself covers change management, leadership, and increasingly workplace-technology and people-analytics content that reflects how HR and line-management roles have shifted. Students can combine the major with a second major (a reasonably common QUT pattern for business students) or take it as a single-major degree with a broader elective spread.

It suits students aiming at generalist graduate programs, HR, operations or team-leadership roles rather than those set on investment banking or actuarial-style careers, where the finance or business analytics majors are the more direct fit.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting for Business, Economics for Business, Marketing Principles, Managing Organisations, Business Law
Year 2: Human Resource Management, Organisational Behaviour, Business Statistics, second major or elective units, work-integrated learning options
Year 3: Strategic Management, Leadership and Change, a capstone business project or internship unit, remaining major and elective units
Throughout: real-client consulting-style projects embedded in several core units via QUT's industry-connected teaching model
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12, ATAR approx. 70-75 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Data Science (Business Data Science)
description:
This is QUT's attempt to sit data science and commerce in the same degree rather than bolting a stats minor onto a business degree or vice versa. The Business Data Science specialisation keeps the core data science spine (programming, statistics, machine learning, databases) but routes the applied units and electives toward business analytics, decision science and the kind of reporting and forecasting work that sits inside marketing, finance and operations teams rather than pure research.

QUT built its data science offerings around the university's Centre for Data Science, and the teaching staff include people doing applied analytics work with government and industry partners, which shows up in the project-based later units where students work with real (or realistically messy) datasets rather than cleaned textbook examples. Python and R are the working languages, SQL and data visualisation tools get dedicated unit time, and there's a capstone industry project in the final year.

Graduates land in business intelligence, data analyst and junior data science roles, generally with employers who want someone who can talk to a marketing or finance team as comfortably as they can build a model. The degree's business framing is a genuine differentiator from a straight computer-science-flavoured data science degree.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Programming, Statistics for Data Science, Introduction to Business, Databases and Data Management
Year 2: Machine Learning Fundamentals, Data Visualisation, Business Analytics, Applied Regression Analysis
Year 3: Big Data Technologies, Decision Analytics, an industry capstone project, business data science electives (forecasting, marketing analytics or financial analytics strands)
Throughout: real-dataset projects in partnership with QUT's industry contacts; SQL, Python and R used across units rather than a single toolchain
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with Mathematical Methods, ATAR approx. 75-80
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Design
description:
Choose your major early and stick with a flexible shell around it. That's the practical shape of QUT's Bachelor of Design. Incoming students pick one of five majors (architectural studies, fashion, industrial design, interaction design or visual communication design, with a strategic design major due to launch for 2027 entry), then build out minors or specialisation units around it rather than sampling broadly before committing.

QUT's design programs run out of the Kelvin Grove creative industries precinct, and the course leans into studio-based, critique-driven teaching rather than a lecture-heavy model, so expect a lot of in-progress work pinned up and picked apart by staff and peers. The interaction design major in particular has been a strong QUT drawcard given Brisbane's growing tech and games sector, though QUT has flagged it's being phased into an Experience Design major from 2027, so students entering under the old name should confirm with QUT which version their course code maps to.

What makes the degree distinctive against other design schools is the ease of pairing it with a second QUT degree. Architectural studies students, for instance, commonly combine with engineering, since QUT explicitly markets several design/engineering and design/business double-degree pathways.
curriculum:
Year 1: Design Thinking and Studio Practice foundations, major-specific introductory studio units, Design History and Theory
Year 2: Major studio sequence (architectural studies, fashion, industrial, interaction or visual communication design), technical/software units specific to the major, an optional minor sequence begins
Year 3: Advanced major studio units, a design research or professional practice unit, a capstone folio or major project
Throughout: critique-based studio assessment rather than exam-heavy assessment; optional international exchange or industry-project units
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12, ATAR approx. 65-70; folio may be required for some majors
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
QUT's primary teaching degree runs across four years and is built to satisfy the professional experience hours the Queensland College of Teachers requires for full registration, meaning the practicum components aren't an add-on but a structural part of every year of the course, starting with observation-style placements in first year and building to a substantial supervised block in final year. Curriculum content covers the full spread of primary subject areas (literacy, numeracy, science, HASS, health and PE, the arts) alongside pedagogy, child development and increasingly inclusive-education content reflecting Queensland's push on differentiated classrooms.

QUT's education faculty has a long-standing relationship with Queensland state and Catholic school systems for placements, which matters practically since most graduates end up teaching in Queensland schools and the professional networks built during placement often lead directly to graduate teaching positions. Literacy and numeracy testing (the LANTITE requirement) sits outside the degree itself but QUT builds preparatory support into the course.

Students wanting a specific subject specialisation for upper-primary or middle-years teaching can pick relevant elective sequences, but the degree is fundamentally a generalist primary qualification rather than a subject-specialist pathway.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Teaching and Learning, Child and Adolescent Development, Literacy Education foundations, first professional experience placement (observation)
Year 2: Numeracy and Mathematics Pedagogy, Science and Technology Education, Inclusive Education, second placement block
Year 3: HASS and Arts Curriculum, Health and Physical Education Pedagogy, classroom management units, extended placement block
Year 4: Advanced pedagogy electives, Professional Practice capstone unit, final extended internship placement in a partner school
Throughout: LANTITE preparation embedded across coursework; placements arranged through QUT's partnerships with Queensland state and Catholic school systems
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with English and Mathematics, ATAR approx. 65-70
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 overall, no band below 7.0

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) (Civil)
description:
QUT structures its civil engineering degree around a genuinely substantial placement requirement: 60 days, or roughly 450 hours, of professional work placement that students complete across the degree rather than in one block, arranged through QUT's relationships with firms like CPB Contractors, John Holland, Lendlease, GHD, Stantec and BMD, plus government infrastructure agencies. That placement load is the thing that differentiates the QUT version of a civil degree from a more theory-heavy equivalent: students graduate having actually spent time on-site or in a design office, not just having done capstone coursework that simulates it.

The technical content covers the expected core: structures, geotechnical engineering, hydraulics and water resources, transport engineering. QUT's location gives students exposure to subtropical/Queensland-specific engineering problems like flood mitigation, cyclone-resilient design and bushfire-adjacent infrastructure, areas where QUT researchers have an active applied research presence.

The Honours designation is built into the four-year degree rather than a separate add-on year, in line with Engineers Australia's accreditation requirements, and the capstone project in final year typically tackles a real or realistic industry brief rather than a purely academic design exercise.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Mathematics, Mechanics of Solids, Introduction to Civil Engineering, Engineering Design fundamentals
Year 2: Structural Analysis, Geotechnical Engineering I, Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics, Surveying
Year 3: Reinforced Concrete Design, Transport Engineering, Water Resources Engineering, first extended industry placement block
Year 4: Capstone Engineering Project (industry-linked brief), Structural Design electives, Construction Management, final placement block
Throughout: 60 days/450 hours of professional work placement distributed across the degree via partner firms and government agencies
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with Mathematical Methods, ATAR approx. 80-85
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Laws (Honours)
description:
QUT's law degree is a Queensland-facing professional qualification first and a general humanities degree second. The course is built to satisfy the academic requirements for admission as a lawyer in Queensland, which means the compulsory Priestley 11 subjects (contracts, torts, property, criminal law, evidence, equity, and the rest) anchor the structure regardless of which electives students choose around them. The Honours component is built into the four-year degree rather than bolted on, reflecting a fairly common structure among Queensland law schools.

QUT Business School and Law sit close to Brisbane's legal and government precinct, and the faculty runs clinical legal education options: supervised work on real client matters through a legal practice clinic, which is a more hands-on alternative to purely theoretical electives for students wanting practice experience before graduate positions. Moot court and advocacy training are also a visible part of the elective offering.

Most QUT law graduates go on to complete Practical Legal Training (PLT) before admission, since the LLB itself covers the academic but not the practical-skills admission requirement, a distinction worth knowing going in, since the degree alone doesn't make you an admitted lawyer.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Law and Legal Reasoning, Contract Law A and B, Torts Law, foundational elective units
Year 2: Property Law, Criminal Law, Administrative Law, Equity and Trusts
Year 3: Evidence, Civil Procedure, Company Law, elective law units (commercial, criminal justice or public law strands)
Year 4: Legal Ethics and Professional Responsibility, an Honours research or clinical legal education unit, remaining electives, capstone units
Throughout: option to undertake clinical legal education working on real client matters; moot court and advocacy electives available
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12, ATAR approx. 85-90
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
The QUT nursing degree is built to the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia's registration standard, so a fixed number of clinical placement hours (roughly 800 to 840 depending on the placement mix in a given year) sit alongside the classroom and simulation content. This isn't optional or supplementary; it's what makes the degree a registration pathway rather than a health-science degree with a nursing flavour. QUT runs its own clinical simulation labs at Kelvin Grove that mimic hospital ward environments, which is where students first practise procedures before moving into real clinical placements across Brisbane's public and private hospital network.

The course structure moves from foundational anatomy, physiology and pharmacology in first year through medical-surgical nursing, mental health nursing and maternal/child health in the middle years, to more specialised and leadership-oriented content by final year, including a period of near-graduate-level practice placement intended to smooth the transition into a graduate nurse program.

Queensland's public hospital system is the main employer destination for most graduates, and QUT's placement partnerships with Metro North and Metro South health services give students a reasonably direct line into graduate program applications at those services.
curriculum:
Year 1: Anatomy and Physiology, Foundations of Nursing Practice, Pharmacology basics, first clinical placement block
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing I and II, Mental Health Nursing, Pathophysiology, ongoing clinical placements
Year 3: Maternal and Child Health Nursing, Complex Care Nursing, Leadership in Nursing Practice, extended clinical placement block including a transition-to-practice rotation
Throughout: approximately 800+ hours of NMBA-mandated clinical placement across Brisbane public and private health services; simulation lab training precedes most placement blocks
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12, ATAR approx. 70-75; open to domestic students only
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 6.5

name: Bachelor of Science (Environmental Science)
description:
Set against Queensland's own environmental pressure points (the Great Barrier Reef, coastal development, bushfire risk, water catchment management), QUT's environmental science major has a fairly local flavour compared to a generic environmental degree, with field trips and research projects that draw on southeast Queensland ecosystems and QUT researchers' active work in reef and catchment science. The degree sits inside the broader Bachelor of Science framework, so students get a solid grounding in chemistry, biology and earth systems before specialising.

Field work is a real component rather than an occasional add-on: students can expect sampling trips, ecological survey work and lab analysis built into core units, not just theoretical coverage of environmental monitoring techniques. The later years let students lean toward conservation biology, environmental management, or more policy-and-planning-adjacent content depending on career direction.

Career outcomes split fairly evenly between government environmental agencies (state Department of Environment roles, local council sustainability positions) and private environmental consulting firms doing impact assessments for development and infrastructure projects. QUT's Brisbane location puts it close to both sectors.
curriculum:
Year 1: Chemistry I, Biology of Organisms, Earth Systems Science, Introduction to Environmental Science
Year 2: Ecology, Environmental Chemistry, Geographic Information Systems, field-based sampling and survey units
Year 3: Conservation Biology, Environmental Management and Policy, Water and Catchment Science, a research project unit
Throughout: field trips and ecological survey work built into core units; research projects often connect to QUT's applied reef and catchment research groups
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12, ATAR approx. 70-75
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Business Administration (Digital MBA)
description:
QUT markets this specifically as a Digital MBA, and the distinguishing feature is real: the degree is delivered flexibly with a strong online component and folds digital transformation, data-driven decision making and technology strategy into what would otherwise be a fairly standard MBA core (strategy, finance, marketing, leadership). It's aimed squarely at working professionals rather than a full-time cohort straight out of undergrad. QUT's MBA intake skews toward people already in mid-career roles looking to move into more senior leadership or to pivot into a digitally-oriented function.

The core units cover the traditional MBA ground, but electives let students go deeper into areas like digital strategy, innovation management or data analytics for business, which is where the Digital branding earns its keep rather than being a marketing label over an unchanged program. Group-based case work and a capstone strategy project (often tied to a real organisation) are the assessment backbone in the later stages.

QUT Business School's connections to Brisbane's corporate and government sector feed guest speakers and capstone project partners, though as with most Australian MBAs the value is heavily networking-and-credential driven rather than purely content-driven.
curriculum:
Core units: Strategic Management, Managerial Finance, Marketing Strategy, Leading People and Organisations, Digital Business Strategy
Elective strands: Data Analytics for Managers, Innovation and Entrepreneurship, Digital Transformation, International Business
Capstone: an applied strategy project conducted with a real host organisation, presented to faculty and industry assessors
Delivery: flexible/blended format aimed at working professionals, with intensive block and online components
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree plus at least 3 years professional work experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Data Science
description:
Run out of QUT's Centre for Data Science, this master's leans on staff who do applied analytics work with government and industry partners rather than a purely theoretical statistics faculty, and that shows up most in the final capstone, where students take on an industry project or industry research placement working with a real dataset and stakeholder rather than a simulated one. The course covers computational data science, statistical modelling, machine learning and information systems analytics as named specialisation strands, letting students lean the degree toward whichever of those areas matches their prior background and career target.

It's designed as a conversion-friendly degree: QUT accepts students from a range of quantitative undergraduate backgrounds, not just computer science or statistics, provided they can pick up the programming and stats foundations in the early units. Python, R and SQL are the working tools throughout, with dedicated units on big data infrastructure and data visualisation alongside the modelling content.

Graduates go into data analyst, data scientist and data engineering roles across finance, government and increasingly health-sector employers in Brisbane and beyond, with QUT's teaching staff research connections in finance and public-sector data work feeding directly into the kinds of case studies used in class.
curriculum:
Foundational units: Programming for Data Science, Statistical Methods, Databases and Big Data Technologies
Core units: Machine Learning, Data Visualisation and Communication, Information Systems Analytics
Specialisation strands: Computational Data Science, Statistical Data Science, or Biomedical Data Science (choose one focus for advanced electives)
Capstone: an industry project or industry-based research placement, working with a real organisation's data and presenting findings to stakeholders
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree in a quantitative discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Education (Educational Leadership)
description:
Aimed at practising teachers and school staff already eyeing (or already in) leadership roles, such as deputy principal, head of department, or curriculum coordinator, rather than at people entering education from scratch, this QUT master's is built around real school-leadership problems: staff management, school improvement planning, change leadership, and the policy environment Queensland schools operate in. Most units assume some teaching or school-based experience, and assessment tasks frequently ask students to apply frameworks to their own school context rather than a hypothetical one.

QUT's education faculty has close relationships with Queensland state and Catholic education systems, and the degree's content reflects current Queensland Department of Education priorities (school improvement frameworks, workforce planning, wellbeing-focused leadership) more than a generic international leadership-theory course would. Students can typically study part-time alongside full-time school roles, which is how most of the cohort completes it.

It functions as much as a credentialing step for principal-track career progression as it does a theoretical qualification, a fairly explicit trade-off for anyone weighing it against a more research-focused education master's.
curriculum:
Core units: Leading School Improvement, Educational Policy and Governance, Managing Change in Schools, Leading Teaching and Learning
