At 100 credit points it's a single intensive year built around an accredited research thesis alongside advanced coursework, and because the year functions as the gateway into every specialist psychology career path (clinical, forensic, organisational, sport and exercise), Swinburne treats it less as a general capstone and more as a professional screening year.

Graduates who complete it are positioned for the 4+2 or 4+1+1 postgraduate/supervised practice pathways toward psychologist registration with AHPRA, or direct entry into competitive APAC-accredited master's and doctoral programs.
curriculum:
Advanced coursework units: advanced research methods and statistics, psychological assessment, advanced topics across clinical, organisational, developmental and cognitive psychology
Honours research thesis, supervised, conducted across the year
Entry requirement: Distinction average (70%) in third-year core psychology units; credit or higher in second- and third-year core/major units (maximum one exception)
APAC-accredited sequence, required for progression to postgraduate psychology training and eventual AHPRA registration
Total: 100 credit points, one year full-time
admission_requirements: ATAR ~70+ (or equivalent Year 12)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
The signature unit in Swinburne's MBA is the Organisational Growth and Innovation Capstone Project, which puts the final assessment squarely on solving a genuine organisational problem rather than sitting a comprehensive exam, a design choice consistent with Swinburne's broader house style of industry-linked capstones across its business, IT and engineering degrees. Students work through core units covering strategic management, finance, marketing and leadership before landing on that project, where prior coursework gets applied against a live business challenge rather than a hypothetical one.

Swinburne's MBA also draws on the university's identity as a technology-focused institution rather than a pure business school: expect more emphasis on digital transformation and data-driven decision making than at MBAs housed in universities without Swinburne's engineering and computing base.

The degree suits mid-career professionals looking to move into general management or executive roles, and the capstone project format gives students a tangible deliverable they can discuss directly in job interviews or promotion conversations, rather than an abstract description of "an MBA project."
curriculum:
Core units: Strategic Management, Managerial Finance and Accounting, Marketing Management, Leadership and Organisational Behaviour, Business Analytics for Decision Making, Economics for Managers, Digital Transformation and Innovation
Elective units in an area of specialisation (subject to availability)
Capstone: Organisational Growth and Innovation Capstone Project (BUS60017), applying prior coursework to a live organisational challenge
Delivered across trimesters/semesters depending on study mode; total credit points and duration vary with prior credit granted
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus at least 2 years professional work experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Data Science
description:
Swinburne's Master of Data Science makes the industry-based capstone mandatory rather than optional: every student works with an external client on a real business problem before graduating, not just those who opt into an industry track. High-performing students (Credit average or better) can go further and apply for the internship unit (ICT80004), which places them directly inside a company for the duration rather than working client problems from campus.

The course is structured with a graduate-certificate exit point after 8 core units, so students who need to stop partway (a job offer, a visa change, a change of plans) leave with a genuine, transcript-backed credential rather than nothing. That's a more forgiving structure than degrees where the only recognised outcome is the full masters.

Given Swinburne's engineering and computing strengths, the data science degree tends to lean toward applied, production-oriented data science, building and deploying models for real organisational use, over a purely theoretical statistics-heavy curriculum, which suits students aiming at industry data science and machine learning engineering roles rather than academic research.
curriculum:
8 core units (graduate certificate exit point): programming for data science, statistical modelling, machine learning, big data systems, data visualisation, data ethics and governance
Additional core and elective units toward the full masters (2 further core units plus 1 elective, subject to specific course version)
Optional: Internship Project (ICT80004) for students with a Credit average or higher
Capstone: mandatory Industry Capstone Project, delivered for an external client organisation
Total award requirements vary by entry pathway and credit granted; typical full-time load is 8 units/year
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a quantitative or IT-related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
Swinburne's Master of Information Technology closes with a capstone that puts students in front of an actual external client rather than a simulated case study. Teams spend their final semester delivering a working solution to a real organisation's problem, which is a heavier industry-facing finish than the research-essay capstone many IT master's degrees default to. Students who keep a Credit average across the degree can additionally apply for a 12-week professional internship that counts toward the qualification itself, rather than sitting outside it as an optional add-on.

At 200 credit points across roughly two years of full-time study, the degree gives students room to specialise (an Information Systems stream is one of the named pathways) while still anchoring everyone in a shared core. Swinburne's Hawthorn campus sits inside Melbourne's tech and startup corridor, and the capstone client pool tends to draw on that local industry base rather than generic case studies licensed from a textbook publisher.

For career changers without an IT background, the degree is commonly taken as a genuine retraining pathway into software, data or systems roles, with the capstone project doubling as the first real Australian industry reference a graduate can put on a resume.
curriculum:
Core units across data structures and algorithms, systems analysis and design, database systems, IT project management, cloud computing and enterprise architecture
Specialisation stream (e.g. Information Systems) or elective units depending on prior background
Optional: 12-week Professional Masters Internship (available to students maintaining a Credit average), credited toward the degree
Final semester: Capstone Project, delivered for an external industry client or business
14 units (200 credit points) total; typical full-time load is 8 units/100 credit points per year
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline) or higher, or Graduate Certificate/Diploma of Information Technology; Postgraduate Qualifying Program available for international applicants who don't meet direct entry.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (Swinburne standard for MIT and other general postgraduate degrees).

name: Bachelor of 3D Art and Animation
description:
TAFE NSW frames this degree explicitly around commercial production pipelines rather than pure fine-arts animation theory. Students work in deadline-driven environments meant to mimic actual studio conditions in feature film, games, television, advertising and visualisation work, and graduate with a bachelor's degree plus a showreel built for client and employer review rather than just an academic portfolio. That production-pipeline framing runs through the whole course: students don't just learn individual 3D and animation skills in isolation, they practice working with others across a production pipeline to deliver a finished result against a brief, the way an actual studio team would.

Run out of Design Centre Enmore, one of TAFE NSW's specialist creative campuses, the degree blends theoretical grounding in art and animation principles with the technical software skills the games and VFX industries actually use day to day.

Graduates aim at roles across feature filmmaking, game production, television and online content, and advertising and visualisation, a broader placement than a games-only or film-only animation degree, useful for students who aren't yet sure which specific corner of the visual effects and animation industry they want to land in.
curriculum:
Core subjects: animation principles, 3D modelling and texturing, rigging and character animation, visual effects and compositing, lighting and rendering, art and design theory
Production-pipeline studio projects simulating deadline-driven commercial briefs
21 core subjects, 3 elective subjects (24 total, 240 credit points)
Final-year capstone: client-brief production project, delivered as part of a team, contributing to a graduate showreel
Delivered at Design Centre Enmore; total three-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant Diploma pathway, portfolio may be requested
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Applied Commerce
description:
The Bachelor of Applied Commerce carries triple professional-body accreditation: CPA Australia, Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CAANZ), and the Financial Advice Association Australia (FAAA). That's a heavier accreditation load than most standalone accounting or financial planning degrees carry individually, since it's built to satisfy the education requirements of both the accounting and financial planning professions at once. Students choose a major in accounting or financial planning, or take a double major covering both, a genuinely unusual combination given how differently those two professions are regulated and how rarely degrees try to service both simultaneously.

A third-year industry placement is built into the structure, developed in consultation with industry so the practical component reflects what employers in accounting and financial services firms are actually looking for rather than a generic business internship.

Coursework runs beyond pure numbers into client psychology and communication, reflecting how much of financial planning practice in particular depends on advising real people through decisions rather than just producing correct calculations.
curriculum:
Core units: accounting principles, financial planning fundamentals, marketing, client psychology and communication, management, economics, business law, taxation
Major (choose one or both): Accounting / Financial Planning
Third-year industry placement, developed in consultation with accounting and financial services employers
Accreditation alignment: CPA Australia, CAANZ, and FAAA education requirements built into course design
Total: three-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant VET Diploma/Advanced Diploma pathway
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
TAFE NSW's Bachelor of Business builds toward three named specialisations: marketing, management, or hospitality and hotel management. The placement requirement is deliberately scaled to match: 60 hours minimum for marketing and management students, but a much heavier 300 hours for the hospitality and hotel management stream, reflecting how much that industry expects hands-on shift experience before graduation. Students commit to a specialisation from second year, choosing four relevant electives in year two and another four in year three that build toward it, rather than declaring a major on day one and locking it in.

Coursework spans management, economics, finance, marketing, communications technologies, business statistics, law and people management, a broad general-business foundation before the specialisation electives narrow things down. Being a TAFE NSW degree rather than a university one, the course leans into applied, workplace-facing content and built-in professional placement as differentiators, consistent with the sector's practical training reputation.

Graduates come out with both a bachelor's qualification and documented, assessed workplace hours in their chosen specialisation, which matters particularly for the hospitality stream where employers routinely want to see real service-floor or front-of-house experience.
curriculum:
Core units: business theory and practice, management principles, economics, finance, marketing fundamentals, communications technologies, business statistics, business law, people management
Year 2: 4 specialisation electives (marketing, management, or hospitality and hotel management)
Year 3: 4 further specialisation electives, building toward the chosen stream
Work placement: minimum 60 hours (marketing/management) or minimum 300 hours (hospitality and hotel management)
Total: three-year bachelor's degree, specialisation confirmed through elective selection rather than a separate application
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (ATAR not required; portfolio/mature-age and VET pathway entry accepted) or a relevant Diploma/Advanced Diploma
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Business (Hospitality and Hotel Management)
description:
This is the hospitality and hotel management specialisation of TAFE NSW's broader Bachelor of Business, and the placement load makes the distinction obvious: 300 hours minimum, five times the 60-hour minimum set for the marketing and management streams of the same base degree. That reflects how hospitality employers hire, since a degree without extensive documented shift and service-floor experience carries a lot less weight in that industry than one that does.

Students share the same core business foundation as other Bachelor of Business students (management, economics, finance, marketing, business law, communications technologies, statistics) before specialising into hospitality and hotel-specific electives from second year onward, so graduates leave with both general business competence and hotel/hospitality-specific operational knowledge rather than one at the expense of the other.

Given TAFE NSW's long history running vocational hospitality training (commercial cookery, hotel operations, tourism) alongside this degree, students in this stream often have access to industry connections and placement employers built up through the organisation's much larger hospitality training footprint, rather than a placement office that's improvising industry contacts from scratch.
curriculum:
Core business units: management principles, economics, finance, marketing fundamentals, business law, communications technologies, business statistics, people management
Year 2 hospitality and hotel management electives: front office and rooms division operations, food and beverage management, event and conference operations
Year 3 hospitality and hotel management electives: revenue management, hotel operations strategy, tourism and hospitality marketing
Work placement: minimum 300 hours in a hospitality or hotel setting
Total: three-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant VET Diploma/Advanced Diploma pathway
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Creative Practice (Music Production and Performance)
description:
This degree is the top tier of a deliberately staged three-year pathway: a one-year Diploma of Music first, in a student's choice of Sound Production, Performance, or Creation and Composition specialisation, followed by the two-year Bachelor of Creative Practice (Music Production and Performance) itself. That staged structure means students test their specialisation choice at diploma level before committing to the longer bachelor's stage, and it gives TAFE NSW a natural exit point for students who want a shorter, standalone qualification rather than the full degree.

Unlike a conservatorium-style performance degree that concentrates heavily on classical technique and repertoire, this program is built for working across performance, production and composition simultaneously, reflecting how contemporary music careers rarely stay confined to just one of those roles. The Sound Production diploma track, for instance, is explicitly aimed at assistant sound engineer and sound designer roles in the entertainment industry, while Creation and Composition leans toward electronic production, sound design and music distribution.

Students come out with both technical production skills and performance capability, positioned for careers as recording artists, producers, composers or session musicians rather than a single narrow professional track.
curriculum:
Year 1: Diploma of Music, one specialisation chosen — Sound Production, Performance, or Creation and Composition
Years 2-3: Bachelor of Creative Practice (Music Production and Performance) core units — music production techniques, live performance practice, composition and arrangement, music business and industry practice, studio recording and mixing
Elective units aligned to the student's diploma specialisation background
Final-year capstone: original creative project (performance, production, or composition portfolio)
Total: three-year packaged pathway (1-year diploma + 2-year bachelor's)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant Diploma pathway, audition/portfolio may be requested
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood Education and Care (Birth-5 years)
description:
This ACECQA-approved degree qualifies graduates as early childhood teachers, not just educators, which puts it in the same regulatory category as equivalent university early childhood teaching degrees despite being delivered by TAFE NSW. The four-year structure carries 805 hours (115 days) of work placement, a substantial practicum load that's woven through the degree rather than concentrated in a single final-year block, giving students repeated, staged exposure to real early learning settings as their coursework deepens.

Curriculum content runs across children's development, language and literacies, STEM, Indigenous education, leadership, inclusive and gifted education, health and wellbeing, and the arts in the early years: a broader spread than a narrower early childhood care qualification, reflecting the birth-to-five age range the degree is built to cover rather than splitting infant/toddler care from preschool teaching into separate credentials.

Because it's delivered through TAFE NSW's applied learning model, students combine contemporary early-childhood research with heavily practice-oriented coursework, which the university positions as a direct pathway into preschool and long day care teaching roles as well as broader children's and family services positions.
curriculum:
Core units across children's development and learning theory, language and literacies, STEM in the early years, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives, inclusive and gifted education, leadership and service management, health, safety and wellbeing, creative arts pedagogy
805 hours (115 days) of supervised work placement, staged progressively across the four years
ACECQA-approved sequence, required for recognition as a qualified early childhood teacher
Final-year capstone integrating leadership and service management with an extended placement block
Total: four-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care, plus a Working with Children Check
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Fashion Design
description:
Delivered through TAFE NSW's Fashion Design Studio, a name in Australian fashion education dating back to 1955, this three-year degree ends with the sort of milestone most fashion schools treat as the whole point: in third year, students design and present their own collection and graduate holding a portfolio of realised, physical garments rather than just a folio of sketches and coursework grades. Two separate work placements are built into the structure, positioned by the university as much for building professional networks in the industry as for skill development.

The course is taught through what TAFE NSW calls a global fashion business lens, meaning students aren't just learning pattern-making and construction but also studying the industry side: trend forecasting, international market awareness, and the commercial context a design has to survive in once it leaves the studio.

As a TAFE NSW degree rather than a standalone art school program, students get access to the technical machinery and production facilities the vocational fashion program uses, which tends to mean more hands-on garment construction time than programs run purely as academic design theory courses.
curriculum:
Core subjects: pattern making and garment construction, textile and fabric knowledge, design fundamentals, fashion illustration, fashion history and trend analysis, global fashion business and market awareness
21 core subjects and 3 elective subjects (24 total, 240 credit points)
Two industry work placements across the degree
Third-year capstone: design, construct and present an original fashion collection, submitted alongside a portfolio of realised work
Total: three-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant Diploma of Fashion Design, portfolio may be requested
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Information Technology (Cyber & Network Security)
description:
TAFE NSW's own bachelor's degree in cyber and network security is a genuinely different animal from its VET certificates in the same subject area. This is a 24-subject, 240-credit-point higher education award, assessed and structured as a degree rather than a training package. What sets it apart from an equivalent university IT degree is where it sits inside the organisation: TAFE NSW runs vocational cyber security qualifications right up to diploma level at the same campuses, so students move through Certificate/Diploma pathways into the bachelor's without changing institutions, and staff teaching the degree often come out of hands-on industry security roles rather than purely academic backgrounds.

The curriculum covers network design, administration and security, with a deliberate emphasis on critical analysis of security risk and applying real mitigation policies rather than treating security as a bolt-on topic within a general IT degree. Cybercrime protection and the use of emerging technologies to manage security threats sit at the centre of the coursework, not the periphery.

For students who want practical, industry-facing training with a straight line to network security and cyber operations roles, without the more theoretical computer science load a traditional university IT degree might carry, this is one of the more targeted options available in NSW.
curriculum:
21 core subjects covering network design and administration, security architecture, cybercrime prevention, data protection, risk analysis and threat management
3 elective subjects, chosen according to specialisation interest and campus availability
Progressive practical labs building toward applied network security projects rather than a single end-of-course assessment
Total: 24 subjects, 240 credit points, delivered as a stand-alone bachelor's degree or via Diploma-to-Bachelor packaged pathway
Not all elective subjects run at every TAFE NSW location each semester
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (TAFE NSW's own published bachelor-entry bar)

name: Bachelor of Information Technology (Data Engineering)
description:
This is TAFE NSW's data engineering bachelor's, delivered out of the Meadowbank campus, and it's built specifically around the infrastructure and pipeline side of data work: designing, implementing and managing big data systems, rather than the more analysis-and-modelling focus a typical data science degree takes. Students work across data security, cloud computing on both AWS and Microsoft Azure, and emerging database technologies, with the course explicitly designed around industry certification pathways from Cisco, AWS, Microsoft, Red Hat and CompTIA rather than treating certification as an optional extra.

At 24 subjects and 240 credit points over three years, the structure mirrors TAFE NSW's other IT bachelor's degrees, with 21 core subjects and 3 electives, and the practical partnerships with vendors like Palo Alto, Juniper and Oracle mean students are training on tools those companies actually use in production, not generic teaching environments.

Graduates go on to roles like data engineer, SQL developer, cloud data engineer, big data analyst and data warehouse engineer, a more infrastructure-and-pipeline-focused set of outcomes than the model-building and analytics roles a pure data science degree tends to produce.
curriculum:
21 core subjects: data analysis foundations, machine learning fundamentals, AI engineering, data security, networking and infrastructure, cloud computing (AWS and Microsoft Azure), database design and administration, emerging data technologies
3 elective subjects
Industry certification alignment built into coursework (Cisco CCNA, AWS, CompTIA and related vendor pathways)
Total: 24 subjects, 240 credit points, three-year degree, delivered at Meadowbank campus
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant VET Diploma/Advanced Diploma pathway in IT
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Interior Design
description:
TAFE NSW structures the practical component of this interior design degree in two distinct stages: 70 hours of mandatory work placement earlier in the course, then a compulsory final-year internship in a professional interior design practice that's assessed as its own subject rather than treated as a pass/fail add-on. Students already working in the industry, or those for whom a suitable internship placement can't be found, can substitute one of three alternative electives (sustainability design, total experience design, or lighting interior environments), which is a more flexible arrangement than degrees that make the internship a hard, non-negotiable gate.

Coursework builds from generating original design concepts through to the spatial, structural and material analysis of real interior environments, and the degree deliberately folds in project management and business development skills alongside the creative content, reflecting that most interior designers eventually run or work inside small practices where those business skills matter as much as design talent.

Run through TAFE NSW's Design Centre Enmore, the course emphasises future-focused digital design tools alongside the traditional colour, furniture and fixture specification skills the profession has always required.
curriculum:
Core subjects: design concept generation, spatial and structural analysis, materials and finishes, colour theory and application, furniture and fixture specification, digital design tools and visualisation, project management and business development for designers
70 hours mandatory work placement
Final-year professional internship (compulsory subject) in an interior design practice, or an alternative elective (sustainability design / total experience design / lighting interior environments) where an internship isn't available
Delivered at Design Centre Enmore; total three-year bachelor's degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant Diploma of Interior Design, portfolio may be requested
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Property Valuation
description:
TAFE NSW makes a specific, verifiable claim about this degree: it's the only specialist valuation degree in Australia, rather than valuation being taught as a subset within a broader property or business degree elsewhere. It's accredited by the Australian Property Institute (API) for Associate Membership, and graduates with two years of subsequent professional experience become eligible for Certified Practising Valuer (CPV), Certified Property Practitioner (CPP) or Certified Development Practitioner (CDP) status: the actual professional credentials the valuation industry requires for signing off on formal valuations.

At 24 subjects across residential, commercial and specialist valuation areas, the degree is narrower and more technically concentrated than a general property or real estate degree, training students specifically in the methodology, legal frameworks and market analysis techniques a working valuer applies rather than the broader property development, agency or funds-management content a property degree elsewhere might carry.

Given how tightly this program tracks to a single professional credential, it suits students who already know valuation is the specific career they want, rather than those looking for a general property qualification with several possible career exits.
curriculum:
Core subjects: valuation theory and methodology, residential valuation, commercial and industrial valuation, specialist valuation (rural, plant and machinery), property law, real estate economics, statutory valuation and compensation
21 core subjects, 3 elective subjects (24 total, 240 credit points)
Capstone valuation practice project, applying methodology across mixed property types
Graduates eligible for API Associate Membership; CPV/CPP/CDP eligibility after two years' professional experience
Total: three-year bachelor's degree, the only specialist valuation degree offered in Australia
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or a relevant VET Diploma/Advanced Diploma pathway
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 5.5

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
TAFE Queensland's Bachelor of Business runs through the same University of Canberra partnership arrangement that underpins its creative-industries degrees, giving students access to a metropolitan business curriculum without leaving Brisbane's South Bank, Mt Gravatt or Coomera campuses. Class sizes are smaller than at a standard university business school, and a lot of the assessment is built around applied projects with real local businesses rather than case studies written for a textbook.

The core is conventional business fundamentals: accounting, marketing, management, economics and business law, but students choose a major partway through, with options that track Queensland's actual employment mix: management, marketing, human resource management and event/tourism-adjacent majors show up more than a generic finance-only track would. Because the degree sits inside a TAFE campus rather than a university one, students doing a business major alongside, say, a hospitality or IT diploma at the same site can cross-enrol in electives from those areas, which isn't something a standalone university business degree typically allows.

Graduates go into generalist business, management-trainee, marketing coordinator and small-business roles across Queensland, and the degree also functions as a credentialing step for TAFE Queensland students moving up from a business-related diploma.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Principles, Introduction to Management, Marketing Fundamentals, Business Economics, Business Law, Business Communication
Year 2: Organisational Behaviour, Financial Management, major-specific units begin (Management, Marketing or Human Resource Management stream), Business Analytics, Business Ethics and Sustainability
Year 3: Strategic Management, major capstone units, Applied Business Project (client-based consulting project), electives from cross-campus TAFE Queensland offerings
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Creative Industries (Drama and Performance)
description:
Run out of TAFE Queensland's South Bank campus in partnership with the University of Canberra, this degree trains performers alongside the people who will end up producing, facilitating and managing the work around them. The course explicitly covers the role of arts facilitators, educators, producers and project managers in creating socially engaged performance work, not just acting technique.

It's built to take students at very different starting points: TAFE Queensland describes it as suited to complete beginners as much as emerging or already-working performers who want to formalise their practice, sit alongside performance theory and pick up professional and entrepreneurial skills they may not have needed for community or amateur work. South Bank's location gives the cohort proximity to Brisbane's professional theatre scene, and the course draws on that for industry contact and, per TAFE Queensland's own program materials, an active on-campus theatre community.

It's a three-year, Commonwealth Supported Place degree with entry based on an entrance rank and typical alternate pathway and admission scheme options. Graduates move into performance work, but the producer/facilitator strand of the curriculum also opens out into arts administration, community arts and theatre-in-education roles that a pure acting degree wouldn't prepare students for as directly.
curriculum:
Year 1: Performance Foundations, Voice and Movement, Introduction to Devising, Theatre History and Theory, Ensemble Practice
Year 2: Text-Based Performance, Physical Theatre, Performance for Social Change, Arts Facilitation and Community Practice, production placement
Year 3: Directing and Dramaturgy, Producing and Project Management for the Arts, Entrepreneurship for Performing Artists, capstone performance season (devised or directed public production)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); audition/interview may be requested
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Creative Industries (Visual Arts)
description:
Like the Visual Communication Design degree, this is a combined qualification: a TAFE Queensland Diploma of Visual Arts feeds into the University of Canberra's Bachelor of Creative Industries (Visual Arts) award. The structure suits students who aren't certain yet whether they want a strictly technical art practice or a broader creative-industries career, since the diploma phase is studio-heavy and the degree phase opens out into curating, arts administration and public art.

Studio practice spans drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking and increasingly digital and mixed media, with the later degree units pushing students toward professional contexts such as exhibition planning, artist statements, grant writing, and gallery relationships that a purely technical diploma wouldn't cover. Brisbane's South Bank campus sits a short walk from the Queensland Art Gallery and GOMA, and the course leans on that proximity for guest critiques and exhibition opportunities rather than treating it as incidental.

Career outcomes are deliberately broad: gallery and museum work, arts education, arts administration, curating, exhibition and display design and public art commissions all show up as destinations, which reflects the creative-industries framing more than a narrower "fine artist" pathway would.
curriculum:
Diploma phase: Drawing and Visual Language, Painting Studio, Printmaking, Sculpture and 3D Practice, Materials and Processes, diploma exhibition project
Degree phase (University of Canberra): Contemporary Art Theory, Curatorial Practice, Arts Administration and Grant Writing, Exhibition and Display Design, Professional Studio Practice, capstone body of work and public exhibition
Credit pathway: TAFE Queensland diploma credit transfers up to 24 credit points into the bachelor's
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); folio may be requested
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Dental Prosthetics
description:
This AQF Level 7 degree is accredited by the Australian Dental Council and approved by the Dental Board of Australia, and it trains one of the few allied dental professions that can treat patients directly rather than only supporting a dentist. Dental prosthetists issue, maintain and examine dentures, insert and try in prosthetics, take impressions and carry out the technical laboratory work themselves, a scope of practice that's genuinely unusual in dentistry, where most non-dentist roles are lab-only or chairside-assist-only.

Coursework covers not just full and partial dentures but more specialised appliances: sleep apnoea and anti-snoring devices, splints, and immediate dentures fitted the same day as extractions. Training happens in TAFE Queensland's working denture clinic, where students treat real patients under supervision using the same lab equipment they'll use professionally, rather than working exclusively on models.

The entry requirement that gets flagged repeatedly by TAFE Queensland itself is manual dexterity: it's assessed at admission and has to be maintained throughout enrolment, which says something about how hands-on the daily work actually is. Graduates are eligible to register as dental prosthetists with the Dental Board of Australia and can go into private practice, dental laboratories or continue into further postgraduate dental study.
curriculum:
Year 1: Oral Anatomy and Physiology, Dental Materials Science, Introduction to Denture Construction, Infection Control and Clinical Practice, Impression Taking and Casting
Year 2: Complete Denture Prosthetics, Partial Denture Design, Occlusion and Articulation, Clinical Practice I (working denture clinic, supervised patient treatment)
Year 3: Immediate Dentures and Same-Day Prosthetics, Sleep Apnoea and Splint Devices, Removable Prosthodontic Complications, Clinical Practice II, Professional and Regulatory Practice for Dental Prosthetists
Clinical training: supervised patient treatment throughout in TAFE Queensland's on-site working denture clinic and dental laboratory
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent) plus relevant work placement component; accredited by the Australian Dental Council
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Design (Visual Communication Design)
description:
Delivered by TAFE Queensland in partnership with the University of Canberra, this is a dual-award structure: students complete a TAFE Queensland Diploma of Graphic Design en route to the University of Canberra's Bachelor of Digital Design (Visual Communication Design) testamur, which is the actual degree name that appears on the parchment despite the program being commonly listed under the broader title. The arrangement means students get a vocational, portfolio-heavy first phase before the degree work broadens into strategy and theory.

Studio work covers typography, logotype and identity design, publication layout, packaging, environmental graphics and digital design, taught by working designers rather than exclusively by academic staff. Class sizes at the South Bank and Coomera studios are kept small enough that students get direct one-on-one critique, which matters in a discipline where the difference between a portfolio that gets a graduate an interview and one that doesn't often comes down to individual feedback rather than course content.

Graduates leave with an industry-ready portfolio and typically move into junior graphic design, brand identity, digital design or in-house studio roles; the credit-transfer arrangement (any one-year TAFE Queensland diploma articulates with 24 credit points, equivalent to a full year of the bachelor's) also makes this a common re-entry point for students who started a diploma elsewhere and want to upgrade to a degree.
curriculum:
Diploma phase: Design Fundamentals, Typography 1 & 2, Digital Imaging, Layout and Publication Design, Branding and Identity, Packaging Design, industry-based diploma project
Degree phase (University of Canberra): Design Theory and Criticism, Environmental and Wayfinding Design, Interactive and Motion Design, Design for Social Impact, Professional Practice, capstone design project and portfolio exhibition
Credit pathway: completed TAFE Queensland diplomas can transfer up to 24 credit points (one year) into the bachelor's component
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); delivered in partnership with the University of Canberra
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Information Technology (Cyber Security)
description:
This degree sits inside TAFE Queensland's broader IT offering at the Coomera campus, where students share lab space (the IT, Immersive Technology and Cyber Security Labs) with games design and network engineering cohorts rather than working in isolation. That cross-pollination matters more than it sounds: a lot of the practical cyber security work students end up doing (penetration testing a web app, hardening a small business network) touches the same infrastructure other students are building.

The course covers programming, networking and database management before narrowing into security-specific work: threat modelling, intrusion detection, digital forensics and governance frameworks. Queensland's cyber security workforce shortfall is cited constantly in TAFE Queensland's own marketing for this course, and it isn't exaggerated. Demand spans banking, healthcare, retail, defence contractors and state government simultaneously, which gives graduates more geographic flexibility within Queensland than a narrower specialisation would.

Graduates typically land entry-level security analyst, SOC analyst or junior penetration tester roles, and the degree articulates directly into TAFE Queensland's Graduate Diploma and Master of Cyber Security for anyone who wants to keep going.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming Fundamentals, Network Fundamentals, Database Design and Management, IT Systems and Infrastructure, Introduction to Cyber Security, Professional Practice in IT
Year 2: Network Security and Defence, Operating Systems Security, Web Application Development and Security, Ethical Hacking Fundamentals, Cloud Computing, Systems Analysis and Design
Year 3: Digital Forensics, Cyber Security Governance and Risk, Incident Response and Threat Intelligence, Secure Software Development, capstone industry project (client-based security assessment), electives in IoT security or cryptography
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
TAFE Queensland's Bachelor of Nursing is built around clinical hours rather than lecture hours. The course schedules 840 hours of Professional Experience Placement across the three years, which clears the 800-hour minimum the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia sets for registration eligibility, and placement blocks are threaded through every year of study instead of stacked at the end.

Before students set foot in a ward, they work through scenarios in TAFE Queensland's simulated hospital wards, which run mock handovers, deteriorating-patient drills and medication rounds under the same documentation standards used in Queensland Health facilities. The course markets itself as "designed by nurses for nurses," and the teaching staff are practising or recently practising RNs rather than career academics, which shows up in how much time is spent on the unglamorous procedural detail of real ward work.

Graduates are eligible to apply for registration as a Registered Nurse with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (subject to AHPRA requirements) and typically move into acute care, aged care, community health or mental health settings across the Queensland public and private hospital systems.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology A & B, Introduction to Health Assessment, Psychology for Health Professionals, Professional Communication in Health, first Professional Experience Placement block (aged care/sub-acute)
Year 2: Pathophysiology and Pharmacology, Acute Care Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Nursing Older Persons, Primary Health Care, Research and Evidence-Based Practice, second and third PEP blocks (medical/surgical wards)
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Perioperative and Critical Care Nursing, Child and Family Health, Leadership and Transition to Professional Practice, one elective unit, final PEP blocks including a graduate transition placement
Clinical placement: 840 hours total across acute, sub-acute, mental health, community and aged care settings, exceeding the 800-hour AHPRA/NMBA minimum
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, plus health/immunisation checks (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall (typical registration-body bar for nursing programs, approximate)

name: Bachelor of the Built Environment (Architecture)
description:
Delivered with the University of Canberra, this degree is part of an Architects Accreditation Council of Australia-accredited pathway that continues into the Master of Architecture, meaning it's structured from year one as the first half of a longer registration pathway rather than a terminal qualification, which matters for students weighing it against a straight university architecture degree.

Work-integrated learning is built into every stage rather than bolted on as a single placement unit: TAFE Queensland promotes a series of "live" projects run with practising architects and design firms, plus internship placements at local, national and international practices. Studio culture leans into critique from working professionals rather than purely academic staff, and coursework is framed around developing "informed critique" of architecture as both creative and professional practice. The ethical and environmental responsibilities of the profession get explicit attention alongside design skill.

Entry is based on entrance rank, and it's a Commonwealth Supported Place, which keeps the cost profile closer to a standard university architecture degree than to a private design school. Graduates continue to the Master of Architecture for registration eligibility, or move into design, drafting and project roles in the built environment sector without completing the full registration pathway.
curriculum:
Year 1: Architectural Design Studio 1 & 2, History and Theory of Architecture, Construction Technology 1, Digital Representation and CAD, Environmental Design Principles
Year 2: Architectural Design Studio 3 & 4, Structures and Materials, Construction Technology 2, Urban Design and Context, live industry project 1
Year 3: Architectural Design Studio 5 & 6, Professional Practice and Ethics, Sustainable Design, live industry project 2, internship placement, portfolio for progression to Master of Architecture
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); accredited by the Architects Accreditation Council of Australia
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Graduate Diploma in Cyber Security
description:
This is TAFE Queensland's bridging qualification for people who already have IT or related experience but need a formal, accredited cyber security credential fast, and its own marketing is explicit that the intended endpoint is the Master of Cyber Security (Advanced), with graduates able to fast-track straight in rather than starting a master's from scratch. As a standalone qualification it also stands on its own for anyone not planning to continue to postgraduate level.

Content splits fairly evenly between technical security work (system security, digital forensics, ethical hacking and defensive techniques) and governance: cyber policy, compliance and organisational risk. That combination is deliberate; TAFE Queensland is explicit that the course is meant to produce people who understand both the attack surface and the regulatory environment around it, rather than pure penetration testers.

Entry accepts a relevant AQF 5 qualification plus two years' relevant work experience, a relevant bachelor's degree completed within six years, or three years of directly relevant work experience with no formal qualification, which makes this a realistic option for experienced IT staff without a cyber-specific degree.
curriculum:
Core units: System Security and Hardening, Digital Forensics Fundamentals, Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing, Cyber Policy and Governance, Risk Management and Compliance, Network Defence Techniques
Capstone: applied security assessment project
Progression: graduates can fast-track into the Master of Cyber Security (Advanced) with credit for equivalent units
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in any discipline (or relevant industry experience considered)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Cyber Security
description:
TAFE Queensland pitches this degree specifically at people who don't want to choose between the technical and policy sides of cyber security. The course is built to produce graduates who can both run an incident response and sit across the table from a board explaining what happened and why the organisation's governance failed. That dual framing is unusual for a technical postgraduate degree in this space, where most competitors lean hard into one side or the other.

Entry is flexible by design: applicants can come in via a relevant AQF 5 qualification plus two years' work experience, a relevant bachelor's degree, or three years of straight industry experience with no formal cyber credential at all, which makes it a realistic upgrade path for IT professionals who moved into security informally. Students who complete the Graduate Diploma in Cyber Security first (offered at the same campus) can fast-track directly into this Master's, and TAFE Queensland also runs a "Master of Cyber Security (Advanced)" variant with an extended research or industry project component for those wanting a deeper technical specialisation.

The course leans on Queensland's acute cyber workforce shortage (the state's banking, health, legal, retail, defence and government sectors are all short-staffed at once), and graduates move into security architecture, GRC (governance, risk and compliance), and senior analyst roles rather than purely entry-level positions given the postgraduate entry bar.
curriculum:
Core: Advanced Network Security, Cyber Security Policy and Governance, Digital Forensics and Incident Response, Security Risk Management, Applied Cryptography, Cyber Law and Ethics
Advanced/capstone stream: Enterprise Security Architecture, Threat Intelligence and Analytics, industry-based capstone project (real client security assessment or research thesis for the Advanced stream)
Delivery: coursework plus an industry-linked capstone; fast-track entry available for Graduate Diploma in Cyber Security completers, who receive credit for foundational units
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in IT or a related discipline (or relevant industry experience considered)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The degree runs 15 core subjects against 9 electives, a heavier core-to-elective ratio than a lot of comparable business degrees, which front-loads shared fundamentals (business communication, understanding people and organisations, customer experience management, marketing fundamentals) before students branch into electives across marketing, public relations, event management, tourism and hospitality.

Two features do most of the work distinguishing this from a generic business degree: a mandatory 300 hours of industry-relevant experience built across the course rather than a single placement block, and a compulsory Industry Consulting Project subject where students work on an actual business problem for a real organisation rather than a simulated case study. That project is usually the first thing graduates put on a resume.

240 credit points, three years full-time standard, with part-time and accelerated study options and delivery across Torrens' Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Adelaide campuses as well as online.
curriculum:
Core subjects: Business Communications, Understanding People and Organisations, Marketing Fundamentals, Business Environment, Accounting Principles, Customer Experience Management, Industry Skills Projects, Business Law, Economics for Business
Electives (choose from): Marketing, Public Relations, Event Management, Tourism and Hospitality streams
Capstone: Industry Consulting Project (client-based applied business project)
Work experience: 300 hours of industry-relevant experience integrated across the degree
Total: 240 credit points across 24 subjects
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); no prerequisite subjects
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Design (Graphic and Communication Design)
description:
This runs under Torrens' Billy Blue design school brand, and the course content pushes well past traditional graphic design into service design and CX: alongside brand strategy, packaging and storytelling, students work through UI/UX design and design thinking methodologies aimed at digital product work, not just print and identity design.

The signature subject is Design Studio, which is run deliberately like a working creative agency: students respond to briefs in small teams and are expected to defend design decisions to a "client" rather than simply submit finished artwork for grading. Sustainability in design also gets explicit curriculum time, which is a newer addition reflecting where the industry itself has moved.

Delivered across Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane campuses plus online, full-time, part-time or accelerated. Graduates go into art direction, UX design, graphic design, web and exhibition design, and branding/advertising/marketing specialist roles, a wider spread than "graphic designer" alone, reflecting how much of the later curriculum is aimed at digital and strategic design work.
curriculum:
Foundational: Design Fundamentals, Typography, Visual Communication, Design History and Theory
Core studio sequence: Design Studio (agency-style collaborative briefs, run across multiple trimesters at increasing complexity), Brand Strategy, Packaging Design, Storytelling and Visual Narrative
Digital/UX stream: UI/UX Design, Design Thinking, Service Design and CX
Sustainability and professional practice: Design for Sustainability, Professional Practice and Portfolio
Capstone: industry-briefed final major project and portfolio presentation
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); portfolio may be requested
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Hospitality Management
description:
Structured as 8 common business core subjects, 10 specialised hospitality subjects and 6 electives across 240 credit points, this degree keeps a genuine business core rather than treating hospitality as a purely vocational add-on. Students graduate able to speak the language of a hotel group's finance and marketing teams, not just its floor operations.

The defining feature is two separate Industry Practicum placements rather than one, totalling a minimum of 800 hours of industry placement concentrated in second year. That's a substantial chunk of the degree spent working in the field partway through rather than only at the end, which means students get a second placement to apply what the first one taught them before they graduate.

Torrens also runs a related Bachelor of Business (Hospitality and Tourism Management) with a slightly different subject mix (20 core, 4 electives) for students wanting a broader tourism focus rather than a hospitality-management-specific one; the two are commonly confused because of overlapping subject names.
curriculum:
Business core (8 subjects): Business Communications, Accounting Principles, Marketing Fundamentals, Economics, Business Law, Understanding People and Organisations, Customer Experience Management, Business Analytics
Hospitality specialisation (10 subjects): Rooms Division Management, Food and Beverage Operations, Hospitality Financial Management, Revenue Management, Event and Conference Management, Hospitality Marketing, Hospitality Law, Sustainable Hospitality Operations, Human Resources in Hospitality, Hospitality Strategy
Industry placement: two Industry Practicum subjects totalling a minimum of 800 hours, concentrated in second year
Electives: 6 subjects from the broader business or hospitality/tourism elective pool
Total: 240 credit points across 24 subjects
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
22 subjects, 240 credit points, with one outsized final subject, ATW306 Advanced Tech: Work Integrated Learning, worth 30 credit points instead of the standard 10, effectively a triple-weighted capstone that anchors the whole degree around a substantial applied project rather than treating work-integrated learning as a token add-on.

Coverage spans programming, web development, data management and cybersecurity broadly enough that graduates aren't locked into one specialisation on paper, and Torrens frames the outcome explicitly around software engineering, cloud computing and cyber security demand, three areas where Australian employer demand has consistently outstripped supply. Delivery is online or on campus.

The single heavily-weighted capstone subject is the structural detail worth knowing if comparing this against other providers' IT degrees. Most spread work-integrated learning across two or three smaller subjects rather than concentrating it into one triple-credit unit near the end.
curriculum:
Core: Programming Fundamentals, Web Development, Database Systems, Network Fundamentals, Data Structures and Algorithms, Systems Analysis and Design, Cybersecurity Fundamentals, Cloud Computing
Electives: chosen across software engineering, cyber security or data-focused streams depending on trimester offering
Capstone: ATW306 Advanced Tech: Work Integrated Learning (30 credit points — triple the standard subject weight)
Total: 240 credit points across 22 subjects
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Torrens' Bachelor of Nursing carries the standard 800-hour clinical placement requirement across hospitals, aged care facilities, community health centres and other industry settings, but it's paired with an on-campus simulation hospital built to mirror real clinical environments before students ever go out on placement: assessment and clinical decision-making, person-centred care and professional communication get practised in a controlled setting first.

One thing Torrens does that's genuinely useful for students rather than just a marketing line: its Clinical Placement Program (CPP) provides paid clinical placements, addressing the unpaid-placement problem that's a live financial issue for nursing students nationally (most Australian nursing degrees still run placements unpaid). It's a relatively recent addition and worth noting because it changes the real cost of doing this degree compared to competitors that haven't moved on it.

Three years full-time, evidence-based curriculum, and graduates are eligible to apply for registration as a Registered Nurse with AHPRA on completion.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing, Anatomy and Physiology, Health Assessment, Professional Communication in Health, first simulation-hospital placements
Year 2: Pathophysiology and Pharmacology, Mental Health Nursing, Acute Care Nursing, Nursing the Older Person, clinical placements in hospital and aged care settings
Year 3: Complex and Critical Care Nursing, Primary Health Care, Research and Evidence-Based Practice, Transition to Professional Practice, final clinical placement block
Clinical placement: minimum 800 hours across hospital, aged care, community health and industry settings, with paid placement available through Torrens' Clinical Placement Program (CPP)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent), plus health/immunisation and police checks
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0 (nursing registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
This degree carries full APAC (Australian Psychology Accreditation Council) accreditation, backdated to Trimester 1 2024 so that every enrolled cohort is covered rather than only students who started after a given date. That detail matters because APAC accreditation is the non-negotiable first step toward registering as a psychologist in Australia, and a degree without it simply doesn't count toward that pathway regardless of course content quality.

Structurally this is Torrens' entry point into the standard Australian psychology registration pipeline: a three-year accredited undergraduate degree, followed by further accredited postgraduate study (typically an Honours year or Master's) and supervised practice before registration with the Psychology Board of Australia. Students who complete this degree without continuing to postgraduate psychology study still graduate with a solid grounding in research methods, statistics and behavioural science applicable to allied-health-adjacent and human-services roles.

Delivered across Torrens' health-focused campuses with the standard mix of research methods, biological and cognitive psychology, developmental and social psychology coursework that APAC's accreditation standard requires.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Psychology, Research Methods 1, Social Psychology, Developmental Psychology
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Research Methods 2 and Statistics, Abnormal Psychology, Psychological Assessment, Personality and Individual Differences
Year 3: Health Psychology, Research Methods 3 (empirical thesis/project), Professional Ethics in Psychology, electives, capstone research project
Accreditation: APAC-accredited (backdated to Trimester 1 2024), first stage of the Australian psychologist registration pathway
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Torrens' MBA is built around six core leadership subjects and then hands most of the customisation over to the student: elective streams run through Marketing Management, Business Analytics and Insight, Project Management, Engineering Management, Technology and Digital Innovation, Strategy and Entrepreneurship, Health Leadership, CX and Service Design, and Finance, and students aren't locked into picking just one: electives can be mixed across streams rather than treated as a fixed specialisation.

The exit-point structure is the more unusual design choice: a student who needs to stop partway through can leave with a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma of Business Administration rather than nothing, which matters for working professionals whose circumstances change mid-degree. Full-time completion runs 1.5 years standard or one year accelerated, with part-time and blended online/on-campus options across Torrens' city campuses.

Given the elective spread, this MBA tends to attract people already mid-career who want to redirect rather than restart, someone moving from operations into digital strategy, or a clinician moving into health leadership, more than fresh graduates.
curriculum:
Core (6 subjects): Leading and Managing People, Strategic Marketing, Financial Management for Decision Making, Business Analytics, Global Business Environment, Leadership and Ethics
Elective streams (choose one or combine): Marketing Management, Business Analytics and Insight, Project Management, Engineering Management, Technology and Digital Innovation, Strategy and Entrepreneurship, Health Leadership, CX and Service Design, Finance
Capstone: applied strategy project
Exit points: Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma of Business Administration available before full MBA completion
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline), professional experience considered favourably (typical MBA entry bar, approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Design
description:
Torrens' postgraduate design offering (delivered through the Billy Blue design school) is built for people who already have design experience or an undergraduate design qualification and want to move into strategic or leadership-level creative roles, such as creative direction, design strategy, or service design leadership, rather than a from-scratch design conversion degree.

The curriculum extends the same strategic and service-design emphasis that runs through Torrens' undergraduate design courses: brand strategy, CX and service design, and design thinking applied at a systems level rather than a single-artefact level, with a major independent research or industry project forming the spine of the degree.

Delivered on campus in Sydney, Melbourne or Brisbane, or online/blended, typically over 1.5 to 2 years full-time depending on advanced standing granted for prior design study.
curriculum:
Core: Design Strategy and Leadership, Advanced Design Research Methods, Service Design and CX at Scale, Design Management
Electives: brand strategy, UX/UI leadership, sustainable design practice (subject to trimester offering)
Capstone: major independent design research or industry-partnered project
Entry: undergraduate design qualification or significant industry design experience, with advanced standing assessed individually
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in design or a related field; portfolio may be requested
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
Torrens offers both a standard Master of Information Technology and an "Advanced" variant; the Advanced stream runs 160 credit points over 13 subjects, including a 20-credit-point capstone (ITW601) and a 30-credit-point advanced project (ITA602), which is a noticeably heavier project load than most coursework master's degrees carry.

Content mixes core software and systems units, including Principles of Programming, Secure by Design, and Software Engineering Principles, with electives in cloud computing, artificial intelligence and data modelling, letting students weight the degree toward development, security or data depending on where they're headed. Entry expects an existing IT-adjacent bachelor's degree covering programming, networks, databases and web development, so this isn't designed as a from-scratch career-change degree the way some competitor "IT conversion" master's programs are.

Delivered online or on campus, with the Advanced version taking around two years full-time for international students.
curriculum:
Core: Principles of Programming, Secure by Design, Software Engineering Principles, Cloud Computing, Data Modelling, Systems Analysis and Design
Advanced stream extras: extended capstone (ITW601, 20 credit points) and advanced industry project (ITA602, 30 credit points)
Electives: artificial intelligence, advanced cloud architecture, cybersecurity, data analytics (subject to trimester offering)
Entry: relevant IT-related bachelor's degree required (programming, networks, databases, web development)
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Public Health
description:
Torrens runs both a standard Master of Public Health (1.5 years full-time, one year accelerated) and a Master of Public Health (Advanced), a two-year version aimed at health professionals who want deeper grounding in the social determinants of health rather than a faster generalist qualification. The Advanced stream is explicitly framed as building on existing clinical or health-sector experience rather than being a from-scratch entry point.

Torrens also offers combined degrees pairing an MPH with a Master of Global Project Management or a Master of Business Administration, aimed at students who want public health content married to leadership or project-delivery credentials, a combination that's more common among students already working in health system management or NGO/government health roles than clinicians heading toward direct patient care.

Delivered on campus at Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and Adelaide as well as online, with core public health methods (epidemiology, biostatistics, health policy) underpinning both the standard and Advanced streams.
curriculum:
Core: Foundations of Public Health, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Health Policy and Systems, Health Promotion, Research Methods in Public Health
Advanced stream extras: Social Determinants of Health (extended), Health Systems Leadership, additional applied research project
Electives: global health, environmental health, health program evaluation (subject to trimester offering)
Capstone: applied public health project or research thesis
Combined degree options: available with Master of Global Project Management or Master of Business Administration
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in health science, nursing, or a related field
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
A three-year, 72 credit point arts degree built around a core major in Arts plus one specialist major chosen from about ten options, including Creative Writing, Digital Media, Film Production, Game Development, Journalism, Global Studies, Marketing Communication, Culture and Heritage, Literary Studies and Sports Media. The rest of the degree is open electives, so students can add a second major or spread across disciplines.

Teaching is project-based, and work integrated learning through internships, mentorships and placements is a required part of the structure rather than an add-on. Applicants can enter on academic results or through a portfolio that demonstrates creative potential. Graduates move into content and copywriting, production, curatorial and heritage work, communications and policy roles, with the exact path shaped by the major chosen. It suits students who want a flexible humanities and creative-industries degree with a clear practical and industry-facing emphasis.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Arts and Design (Honours)
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Building and Construction Management (Honours)
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 70-75 (or equivalent); Mathematics at a senior secondary level recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
UC's Bachelor of Business is built around five shared core units in accounting, economics, management, marketing and business law, on top of which students pick a major: Management, Marketing, International Business, Business Informatics or the university's well-known Sport Management stream, which trades on Canberra's cluster of national sporting bodies rather than generic case studies.

Work Integrated Learning is treated as a graduation requirement rather than an optional add-on. Depending on major, that can mean an industry project, a study tour, a placement with a local business, or, for Sport Management students, a 150-hour internship in the final year arranged through UC's ties to organisations such as the AIS, Cricket ACT and various NRL and Super Rugby franchises based in or visiting the capital.

Because the degree is offered both on campus and fully online, cohorts mix school-leavers with working professionals returning to formalise a business qualification, which shapes discussion in electives toward real workplace scenarios rather than textbook cases.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting for Managers; Economic Principles; Introduction to Management; Marketing Principles; Business Law; major foundation unit
Year 1-2: Statistics for Business; Business Communication; Human Resource Management; major core units
Year 2: Major specialisation units (choice of Management, Marketing, International Business, Business Informatics or Sport Management); breadth minor or elective units
Year 2-3: Strategic Management; Work Integrated Learning unit (industry project, placement or internship depending on major)
Year 3: Advanced major units; capstone business project or internship report; free electives
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Business Informatics
description:
A three-year degree (72 credit points) that sits deliberately between business and IT, built around systems analysis, database design, enterprise systems and workflow management, with a specialisation in cybersecurity and system administration, data science, or cloud computing and IoT.

It is accredited by the Australian Computer Society at professional level. The final year includes a group project that analyses a real IT problem and builds an IT strategy for it, and the program lists internships with PwC, Fujitsu Australia and government agencies. Entry is a selection rank of about 60 with basic ICT knowledge assumed. It suits students who prefer analysing requirements, managing data and designing systems over pure programming, and Canberra's government sector is a large employer of these graduates.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 70-75 (or equivalent); Mathematics at a senior secondary level recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Business, Government and Policy (Honours)
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Commerce (Business Economics)
description:
A three-year, 72 credit point commerce degree with a specialist major in business economics, combining core commerce units, the economics major and open electives. The major covers microeconomics, macroeconomics and econometrics, with an emphasis on working through ambiguous or incomplete information and communicating findings to non-specialists. A capstone project pulls the degree together, and authentic work integrated learning runs through internships, industry projects and case studies.

Graduates work as economists, economic and business analysts, forecasters and policy advisers across government, consulting and the private sector, which is a natural fit in Canberra given the concentration of federal departments and agencies. Delivery is flexible, with online and blended options and completion timeframes from three years part-time upward. It suits students who want quantitative economic training inside a broader business degree rather than a pure economics program.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Communication and Media
description:
A three-year degree (72 credit points) with a choice of six majors: journalism, sports media, media production, public relations and strategic communication, social media and content creation, or marketing communication, with a double-major option.

Up to 200 hours of professional experience is built in, including at least 100 hours of approved internship placement, with partners such as the ABC, Seven West Media, the Brumbies and the Australian Public Service. Students work with real facilities: the UCFM radio station, television studios and editing suites, and The Owl publishing platform. Entry is a selection rank of about 60 with no assumed knowledge. It suits students who want to build a portfolio and try several media disciplines before committing to one.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Creative Industries
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Design
description:
A three-year studio-based degree with five majors: interaction design, industrial design, visual communication design, game development, or a multidisciplinary design pathway. Learning is built around collaborative studio projects, with industry briefs from partners such as Breville, the National Film and Sound Archive and the National Gallery of Australia.

Work-integrated learning runs through all three years via internships, live briefs, field trips and international study tours, and students graduate with a reviewed portfolio. Entry is a selection rank of about 60, or a portfolio submission with no ATAR required. It suits people who want to solve problems through design across digital products, physical products, branding or games.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Digital Design (Digital Media)
description:
A three-year, 72 credit point digital media degree delivered jointly with TAFE Queensland at the South Bank campus in Brisbane, so students take University of Canberra units alongside TAFE Queensland electives and studio classes.
