Core study covers 3D media art production, animation, sound design, digital photography, interactive fiction and emerging virtual and augmented reality tools, together with professional practice and a work integrated learning placement.

Entry is by selection rank, with a portfolio pathway available, and strong students can progress to an honours year. Graduates work as digital media and motion designers, animators, videographers and VR or AR content specialists across games, screen, advertising and immersive media. It suits students who want a hands-on, technology-heavy creative production degree and are based in or willing to study in Brisbane rather than Canberra.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood and Primary Education
description:
A four-year degree (96 credit points) that qualifies graduates to teach across the whole birth-to-year-6 span, from preschools and early learning centres to primary schools, which is a broader qualification than a primary-only or early-childhood-only degree.

Students complete at least 132.5 days of placement across early childhood and primary settings, pass both parts of the LANTITE test and a Teaching Performance Assessment, and the program is approved by ACECQA for early childhood and registered with the ACT Teacher Quality Institute for primary. Entry is a selection rank of about 60 plus a suitability statement and, for teacher registration, IELTS 7.5 with 8.0 in speaking and listening. It suits people set on early-years and primary teaching who want both credentials.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate required prior to professional placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood Education (Birth to Five)
description:
A three-year, 72 credit point initial teacher education degree that qualifies graduates to teach children from birth to five years, accredited by the Australian Children's Education and Care Quality Authority. Holders of an ACECQA-approved diploma can complete it in two years. Delivery is blended, on-campus or online, at the Bruce campus in Canberra and the Sydney Hills campus in New South Wales.

Study covers child development, early literacy, STEM, play-based learning, behaviour guidance, Indigenous pedagogies and leadership, with a minimum of 95 days of supervised placement across a range of early childhood settings. Working with Vulnerable People registration is required before placement. Graduates work as early childhood teachers and centre directors, and move into education leadership, curriculum and policy roles. It suits students committed specifically to the early years rather than primary or secondary teaching.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate required prior to professional placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 70-75 (or equivalent); Mathematics at a senior secondary level recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Engineering Technology
description:
A three-year, 72 credit point degree that pairs a broad information and communication technology core with an engineering technology specialisation and open electives. Core units cover database design, systems analysis, software technology and professional IT practice, while the specialisation adds cloud computing, cybersecurity, mobile technologies and digital signal processing.

One point to be clear on: this degree is not accredited by the Australian Computer Society, and students who need ACS-accredited qualifications should look at UC's other IT degrees. Admission is generally through transfer from approved articulation partners rather than direct school-leaver entry. Graduates work in networking, system administration, software development and technical support roles that value applied ICT skills alongside communication and business awareness. It suits students articulating from a diploma who want a bachelor-level ICT qualification with an engineering-technology slant.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 70-75 (or equivalent); Mathematics at a senior secondary level recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Exercise Physiology and Rehabilitation
description:
A four-year degree accredited by Exercise and Sports Science Australia, so graduates are eligible to apply for accreditation as an exercise physiologist and, along the way, as an exercise scientist. Students complete at least 500 hours of placement across hospitals, clinical health services, sporting organisations, private practice and community health.

The program frames exercise as medicine, working with people across the lifespan on injury recovery, chronic disease, aged care and rehabilitation, with an emphasis on clinical reasoning and person-centred care. Entry is a selection rank of about 70 with assumed knowledge in biology and mathematical methods, and IELTS 7.0 with no band below 7.0. It suits students who want a clinical allied-health career rather than a fitness or coaching one.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 75-80 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate and immunisation compliance required prior to clinical placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Bachelor of Film Production
description:
A three-year production-focused degree that takes students through the full pipeline from concept to delivery, with specialisation possible in directing, cinematography, editing, sound design or producing, and dedicated units in screenwriting, documentary and creative producing.

Students use film cameras, lighting, green screen, and industry-standard editing and colour grading software, and complete a 100-hour work-integrated learning placement. Past placements include Wildbear, Channel 9, the National Film and Sound Archive and ABC TV productions. Entry is a selection rank of about 60, or a portfolio. It suits people who want hands-on, collaborative filmmaking training with a real production network rather than a purely theoretical screen-studies degree.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Government
description:
UC's Bachelor of Government sits within the Canberra School of Government and Policy and is built around the university's location in the middle of the federal public service: something the course leans on hard, given how many of its students already work in or alongside government departments based in the ACT.

Core units introduce politics, economics, law and management before students choose a major in Economics, Politics and International Relations, or Public Policy and Administration. The emphasis is consistently on how decisions actually get made and implemented at each level of government, rather than abstract political theory.

The course is offered flexibly, with some units delivered entirely online, which suits students who are already in public-sector roles and studying part time toward a formal qualification in government and policy work rather than starting a graduate career from zero.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Australian Politics; Principles of Economics; Law and Society; Introduction to Public Administration; Foundations of Policy Analysis
Year 2: Comparative Government; Public Sector Economics; major units (Economics, Politics and International Relations, or Public Policy and Administration stream)
Year 3: Policy Implementation and Evaluation; Government and the Media; Professional Placement or Applied Policy Project; advanced major electives
Capstone: Applied Government and Policy Project
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Health Science
description:
A three-year broad health degree rather than a clinical registration pathway, pairing a health science core with an applied health major and electives in areas such as health promotion, global health and ecological public health practice.

Students complete a 120-hour work-integrated learning placement in the final year plus professional practice units throughout. The degree is designed as a foundation for honours and then a professional master's such as public health, occupational therapy or speech pathology, or for non-clinical work in health policy, promotion and research. Entry is a selection rank of about 60. It suits students who want a flexible entry into the health sector while deciding on a specialisation.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Health Sciences (Honours)
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Human Nutrition
description:
A three-year science degree (72 credit points) on the role of nutrition in health across different societies, built on biochemistry, physiology and food science alongside the psychological, social and cultural drivers of what people eat.

It does not lead to dietitian registration. Graduates are eligible for registration as an Associate Nutritionist with the Nutrition Society of Australia, and those who want to practise as dietitians progress to a master's such as UC's Master of Nutrition and Dietetics, for which this degree is a direct pathway. A placement is required, with Working with Vulnerable People and sometimes police and vaccination checks. Entry is a selection rank of about 60 with assumed knowledge in chemistry and mathematics. It suits students interested in nutrition science, public health, the food industry, research or an allied-health graduate pathway.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
UC's Bachelor of Information Technology sits inside the Faculty of Science and Technology and lets students specialise in one of four areas: Cloud Computing and the Internet of Things, Cybersecurity and System Administration, Data Science, or Robotics and Artificial Intelligence. Only three majors total (core, specialist and breadth) can be completed across the degree, which keeps the structure from sprawling into an unfocused generalist qualification.

Students take at least 24 credit points as a breadth major, minor or set of individual units drawn from outside IT altogether, a deliberate design choice that pushes technical students into some contact with other disciplines rather than three years of pure computing units.

Graduates with a strong GPA can progress directly into a one-year Honours program in the ITS discipline, useful for anyone eyeing research or a PhD pathway in cybersecurity, data science or AI rather than heading straight into industry.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Programming; Computer Systems Fundamentals; Database Systems; Networking Fundamentals; Web Technologies; Discrete Mathematics for Computing
Year 2: Data Structures and Algorithms; Systems Analysis and Design; Operating Systems; specialist major units (Cloud/IoT, Cybersecurity, Data Science, or Robotics/AI stream); breadth units
Year 3: Advanced specialist major units; IT Project Management; Professional and Ethical Issues in IT; capstone IT project; breadth major or minor units
Optional: Honours year (research thesis) for eligible high-GPA graduates
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Justice Studies
description:
A three-year degree (72 credit points) that takes a broad view of the justice sector rather than specialising narrowly in criminology or policing. Units span criminal justice, social justice, environmental justice, Indigenous justice and family law, with electives in human rights and judicial administration.

A 75-hour internship in a justice workplace is required, with past placements at community legal centres, courts, the Commonwealth Ombudsman, government departments and Legal Aid ACT, and a capstone that includes practical dispute management. Entry is a selection rank of about 65 with alternative pathways available. It suits students who want to work across the justice system as policy officers, probation and parole officers, police, corrections officers or public servants, without doing a full law degree.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
A four-year professional LLB (three years for graduate entry) accredited by the ACT Legal Practitioners Admission Board and, through mutual recognition, accepted for admission in every Australian state and territory. Graduates still complete separate practical legal training before they can be admitted.

Work-integrated learning is substantial: students take at least one law elective with a practical placement component, and UC runs a legal advice clinic for small business where students assist under supervision. Past internships have included community legal centres, courts, government departments and overseas placements. High-achieving students can add an embedded honours unit in the final year without extending the degree. Entry is a selection rank of 85, with alternative pathways including work experience and paralegal experience. The Canberra location gives good access to courts, government legal teams and policy work.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 70-75 (or equivalent); Mathematics at a senior secondary level recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Medical Imaging
description:
A four-year, 96 credit point degree in diagnostic radiography, with first intake in Semester 1, 2027 at the Bruce campus. Study covers imaging anatomy, radiographic technique, the physical principles of imaging, CT, radiation dosimetry, image interpretation and research methods, taught in progressive levels.

Clinical work integrated learning is substantial, structured as four five-week blocks plus two 13-week residencies in metropolitan, regional and rural hospitals. Graduates are eligible to apply for registration as diagnostic radiographers with the Medical Radiation Practice Board of Australia; formal professional accreditation is expected to be assessed in 2028 after the first cohort begins. Entry assumes Year 12 biology, physics and mathematics, and requires police clearance, immunisation records and current first aid. Graduates work as radiographers and move into mammography, sonography, clinical education and research. It suits students set on a medical radiation career.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 85-90 (or equivalent); highly competitive limited-entry program with clinical placement compliance (National Police Certificate, immunisation).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Bachelor of Medical Radiation Science (Medical Imaging)
description:
An accelerated 3.5-year degree in diagnostic radiography, six months shorter than the standard four-year qualification elsewhere. It is accredited through the Medical Radiation Practice Board of Australia, so graduates can apply for registration as a diagnostic radiographer and for membership of the Australian Society of Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy.

Clinical training is four five-week placement blocks and two 13-week residencies across metropolitan, regional and rural hospitals and private practice, after simulation practice on campus. Entry is a selection rank of about 85 with assumed knowledge in biology, physics and mathematics, IELTS 7.0 in every band, and police, immunisation and first aid clearances. It suits school leavers who want the quickest accredited route into radiography.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 85-90 (or equivalent); highly competitive limited-entry program with clinical placement compliance (National Police Certificate, immunisation).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Bachelor of Medical Science
description:
A three-year science degree built around two majors, pathological basis of disease and genetic basis of disease, covering anatomy, physiology, disease mechanisms, genetics, genomics and bioinformatics, with laboratory-based professional practice units and the option of a supervised research project.

It is a common preparation for graduate-entry medicine via the GAMSAT, as well as for research careers and an honours year. Entry is a selection rank of about 60 with assumed knowledge in biology, chemistry and mathematical methods. It suits students aiming at medical research or postgraduate medicine, or who want a strong grounding in human health and disease before deciding.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Midwifery
description:
A three-year degree accredited by the Australian Nursing and Midwifery Accreditation Council, leading to eligibility for registration as a midwife with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. It is built on a continuity-of-care model: each student follows 22 women through pregnancy, birth and the postnatal period, attending their regular appointments and being on call for labour, which requires real flexibility.

Students complete 1,310 clinical practice hours over the three years, more than at many comparable programs. Entry is a selection rank of about 70 plus police, immunisation, tuberculosis and Working with Vulnerable People clearances, with IELTS 7.0 and at least 6.5 in writing. It suits people committed specifically to midwifery and woman-centred maternity care rather than general nursing.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 75-80 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate and immunisation compliance required prior to clinical placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
UC's Bachelor of Nursing opens with a ten-day clinical placement in first semester specifically so students can test, early, whether nursing as a career matches what they expected. It's a deliberate design choice rather than easing students in slowly. Across the rest of the degree, students complete a minimum of 800 hours of clinical practice spanning community care, mental health, aged care, medical and surgical wards, rehabilitation, palliative care, operating theatre, emergency department and ICU.

Placements run through Canberra Hospital, North Canberra Hospital, Goulburn Base Hospital and a number of private clinics across the ACT, southern NSW and as far as Bega, giving students exposure to both metropolitan and regional health settings within the one degree.

On-campus preparation makes heavy use of high-fidelity simulation (manikins, emerging AI and VR tools, and even trained actors standing in for patients), so students rehearse clinical and communication skills repeatedly in a controlled setting before they're let loose on the placement hours that make up the bulk of their professional preparation.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice; Human Anatomy and Physiology; Health Assessment; Introduction to Professional Nursing; ten-day orientation clinical placement
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing; Mental Health Nursing; Pharmacology for Nurses; Aged Care Nursing; clinical placements in community and acute settings
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing; Emergency and Critical Care Nursing; Palliative Care; Perioperative Nursing; further clinical placement blocks (ED, ICU, operating theatre)
Throughout: minimum 800 hours of supervised clinical placement across metropolitan and regional healthcare settings; transition-to-practice unit ahead of registration as a nurse with AHPRA
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate and immunisation compliance required prior to clinical placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements for nursing.

name: Bachelor of Occupational Therapy
description:
A four-year, 96 credit point degree that prepares graduates to assess and support people's participation in everyday activities across health, disability, education and aged care settings. Study covers occupational therapy theory and practice, anatomy, mental health and research methods, with competencies built through structured clinical blocks totalling around 1,000 hours of supervised fieldwork in hospitals, clinics, schools and community organisations.

The course is accredited by the Occupational Therapy Council of Australia and approved by the Occupational Therapy Board of Australia, so graduates are eligible to apply for registration as occupational therapists, and it meets World Federation of Occupational Therapists standards. High-achieving students can transfer into an honours stream. Graduates work in public, private and community services including rehabilitation, forensic and community health settings. It suits students committed to a registered allied health profession with strong hands-on placement content.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 85-90 (or equivalent); highly competitive limited-entry program with clinical placement compliance (National Police Certificate, immunisation).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Bachelor of Pharmacy
description:
A four-year degree fully accredited by the Australian Pharmacy Council, combining laboratory and clinical training. Students take repeated two-week placements in community and hospital pharmacies over the winter periods, plus shorter placements through the teaching semesters.

The degree makes graduates eligible for the supervised internship year that leads to registration as a pharmacist. Entry is a selection rank of about 75 with prerequisites in mathematical methods, chemistry or physics, and biology or human movement, and IELTS 7.0 with no band below 7.0. It suits students who want a clinical, patient-facing health career centred on medicines, clinical reasoning and medication management.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 85-90 (or equivalent); highly competitive limited-entry program with clinical placement compliance (National Police Certificate, immunisation).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Bachelor of Physiotherapy
description:
UC's four-year Bachelor of Physiotherapy is shaped by a Course Advisory Group drawn from Canberra Hospital, Calvary Hospital and the Australian Institute of Sport, which keeps the curriculum tied to what those services actually need from new graduates rather than a purely academic syllabus.

Clinical placements run in blocks, often outside normal teaching weeks, and students treat patients across all age groups and genders under full supervision, including through the UC Health Clinic on campus, which doubles as a low-cost physiotherapy service for the Canberra community. Before any placement, students must complete an immunisation schedule, hold current First Aid/CPR certification, and pass an AFP check for ACT placements, with additional state-based police checks for interstate rotations.

The course is accredited by the Australian Physiotherapy Council and approved by the Physiotherapy Board of Australia, so graduates can apply directly for registration to practise. High-performing students can also apply for the Honours pathway via academic record, interview and application.
curriculum:
Year 1: Human Anatomy; Human Physiology; Introduction to Physiotherapy Practice; Biomechanics; Foundations of Musculoskeletal Practice; Psychology for Health Sciences
Year 2: Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy; Neurological Physiotherapy; Cardiorespiratory Physiotherapy; Exercise Prescription; Clinical Placement Block 1
Year 3: Advanced Musculoskeletal Practice; Paediatric and Older Person Physiotherapy; Pain Science; Clinical Placement Blocks in hospital and community settings
Year 4: Complex Clinical Presentations; Professional Practice and Ethics; Clinical Placement Blocks (including UC Health Clinic rotation); Research Project
Optional: Bachelor of Physiotherapy Honours (additional research year) for eligible students
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 85-90 (or equivalent); highly competitive limited-entry program with clinical placement compliance (National Police Certificate, immunisation).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Bachelor of Politics and International Relations
description:
A three-year degree (72 credit points) pairing a core major in government and policy with a specialist major in politics and international relations, plus open electives, covering economics, political institutions, democracy, national security and Asia-Pacific geopolitics.

Work-integrated learning runs through internships and a capstone, with past placements at the Australian Border Force, the Centre for Defence and Strategic Studies and the Australian Institute of International Affairs, and exchange options are available with program approval. Being in Canberra puts students near Parliament, the public service and diplomatic missions. Entry is a selection rank of about 65 with no assumed knowledge. It suits students aiming at policy, diplomacy, intelligence, political journalism or international development work.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Primary Education
description:
The Bachelor of Primary Education is a four-year degree preparing graduates to teach Kindergarten through Year 6, and it treats professional placement as the spine of the course rather than an add-on: students complete a minimum of 80 days of practical placement across different school levels and settings, building to a 30-day teaching placement in the final year that functions as a genuine trial run at the job.

From second year onward, the course's Pedagogical Content Knowledge units are taught on-site in schools rather than in a lecture theatre, so students are regularly working with children of primary age well before their major placement blocks begin.

UC also offers several targeted variants of the same degree (with specialisations in Health and Physical Education, Creative Arts, or STEM), all following the same 80-day-plus-30-day placement structure but layering in subject-specific pedagogy for students who already know which curriculum area they want to teach into.
curriculum:
Year 1: Child Development; Introduction to Curriculum and Pedagogy; Literacy Education 1; Numeracy Education 1; Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Education
Year 2: Literacy Education 2; Numeracy Education 2; Pedagogical Content Knowledge units (taught on-site in schools); inclusive education units; practicum placement block
Year 3: Science and Technology Education; Humanities and Social Sciences Education; Assessment and Reporting; further on-site Pedagogical Content Knowledge units; practicum placement block
Year 4: Classroom Management; Professional Studies; capstone research or project unit; final 30-day teaching placement
Throughout: minimum 80 days of practical school placement, building to the final-year teaching placement
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate required prior to professional placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.5 (no band below 7.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 102, PTE 69), reflecting registration-body English requirements for teaching.

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
A three-year, 72 credit point science degree with a required core major in Science plus one specialist major chosen from Biomedical Science, Biological Science, Chemical Science, Environmental Science, Human Movement or Nutrition Studies, and eight open electives that can add a second major or broaden the degree.

The curriculum emphasises scientific reasoning, data analysis and communication, with laboratory and field work integrated throughout and professional practice units that place students in industry and research settings using current equipment. Entry is a selection rank of about 60, with Year 12 biology, chemistry and mathematical methods as assumed knowledge and IELTS 6.0 for international students. Graduates work as laboratory and research officers, environmental and sustainability officers and biomedical scientists, or move into STEM teaching with further study. It suits students who want a flexible science degree with a clear applied and work-integrated focus.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Science in Psychology
description:
A three-year APAC-accredited psychology sequence covering how and why people think, feel and behave, from research methods and statistics through the core areas of the discipline. The degree on its own does not qualify anyone to work as a psychologist.

Registration requires further study: an honours year followed by either a two-year clinical or professional master's and supervised practice. High-achieving students progress to that honours year at UC. Entry is a selection rank of about 60 with alternative pathways available. It suits students heading toward professional psychology, and it also works well as a second major alongside law, business or sport science for roles in HR, policy research, marketing, disability and community health.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Software Engineering
description:
The Bachelor of Software Engineering runs over six semesters full-time and carries accreditation from the Australian Computer Society at the Professional level, which matters for graduates aiming at roles requiring formal ACS recognition, including some skilled migration pathways.

Rather than a single fixed syllabus, students tailor later years toward robotics and AI, computer security, network computing, games development, digital forensics or intelligent systems, overlapping with the same specialist streams (Cloud Computing/IoT, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Robotics and AI) offered across UC's broader IT course family in the Faculty of Science and Technology.

Work Integrated Learning is compulsory, giving students real or close-to-real workplace experience before graduation, and the degree places heavy emphasis on communication and critical systems analysis alongside coding, on the reasoning that engineers who can't explain a design decision to a non-technical stakeholder are only doing half the job.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming Fundamentals; Object-Oriented Software Development; Computer Systems Architecture; Discrete Mathematics; Database Systems; Web Application Development
Year 2: Data Structures and Algorithms; Software Requirements and Design; Operating Systems; Software Testing and Quality; specialisation stream units (Security, Networks, AI/Robotics, Games, Digital Forensics)
Year 3: Software Architecture; Software Project Management; Work Integrated Learning industry placement/project; Professional Practice in Engineering; capstone Software Engineering Project
Accreditation: Australian Computer Society (Professional level)
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 70-75 (or equivalent); Mathematics at a senior secondary level recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science
description:
Canberra is the base of the Australian Institute of Sport, and UC's Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science leans on that geography directly: students complete 250 hours of Work Integrated Learning, with internship placements available through partners including the AIS itself, NRL and Super Rugby clubs, WNBL and W-League programs, and the ACT's community sport network via UC's on-campus Sporting Commons facility.

The course is accredited by Exercise and Sports Science Australia, so graduates can seek accreditation as an exercise scientist immediately on completion, rather than needing a further conversion year. Coursework covers biomechanics, exercise physiology, motor control and nutrition, building toward a research project students choose within their own area of interest in sport or exercise science.

UC reports that placement-to-employment conversion is unusually strong for this course, with some students securing ongoing roles with their placement organisation before they've even graduated, a reflection of how tightly the internship network is woven into the ACT's sporting institutions.
curriculum:
Year 1: Human Anatomy; Human Physiology; Foundations of Sport and Exercise Science; Biomechanics of Human Movement; Nutrition for Health and Performance; Psychology of Sport and Exercise
Year 2: Exercise Physiology; Motor Control and Learning; Strength and Conditioning; Research Methods in Sport Science; Functional Anatomy; elective units
Year 3: Clinical Exercise Physiology; Sport Injury Prevention and Management; Applied Sport Science Practicum (Work Integrated Learning internship); Sport and Exercise Science Research Project; electives
Throughout: 250 hours of supervised Work Integrated Learning placement with community, professional or institute-of-sport partner organisations
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Vision Science
description:
A three-year science degree in the biology, optics and health of the visual system. It is the required first half of UC's optometry pathway: the degree on its own is not a clinical qualification, and graduates go on to the two-year Master of Optometry to become registered optometrists.

The final year includes an integrated eye care and ocular therapeutics unit with clinical and non-clinical placement, using the University of Canberra Hospital. Entry is a selection rank of about 80 with assumed knowledge in mathematical methods, chemistry and physics, plus immunisation, first aid and Working with Vulnerable People checks. It suits students committed to the full optometry pathway, or to vision research and the optical industry.

name: Juris Doctor
description:
UC's Juris Doctor is a graduate-entry law degree for people who already hold a bachelor's degree in a non-law field, delivered fully online across 24 units, each run in a seven-week block rather than a traditional semester. With six intakes a year, students can start almost whenever life allows rather than waiting for a February or July opening.

To graduate, students must complete the foundation units, all Priestley 11 units (the national core required for admission to legal practice in Australia), the program's additional core units, and at least one of three Research and Internship Stream units, filling out the rest with electives.

Those electives lean toward technology, innovation and dispute resolution, which fits UC's broader positioning as a public-policy and government-adjacent university; several electives sit at the intersection of law and public administration, useful for JD students already working in or heading toward Commonwealth legal or policy roles based in Canberra.
curriculum:
Foundation units: Introduction to Law and Legal Reasoning; Legal Research and Writing
Priestley 11 core units: Contracts; Torts; Criminal Law; Property Law; Equity; Company Law; Administrative Law; Federal and State Constitutional Law; Civil and Criminal Procedure; Evidence; Professional Conduct (Ethics)
Additional core units: Public International Law; Legal Theory
Research and Internship Stream (complete at least 1): Legal Internship; Directed Research Project; Law Reform Project
Electives (remaining units to reach 24 total): drawn from technology and law, alternative dispute resolution, and public-sector/government law offerings
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (or equivalent); this is a graduate-entry law qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Architecture
description:
A two-year graduate-entry master's for people who hold a Bachelor of Architecture or an equivalent design degree with a credit average in studio work; a strong portfolio can support an application with lower grades. It is accredited by the Architects Accreditation Council of Australia, and completing it after an accredited bachelor's degree covers the qualifying steps toward registration as an architect.

Four major design studios sit at the core, several taught with practising architects and built around live projects, with electives in areas such as heritage, technology and research. Canberra itself, a planned capital, is used as a design case study. It suits architecture graduates who need the accredited master's to register and want a focus on contemporary urban architecture.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in architecture or a related built-environment field (typically following an accredited bachelor's degree) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Building and Construction Information Management
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in construction management, architecture, engineering or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
UC frames its MBA around the fact that Canberra is the seat of national government as much as a business centre, pitching the degree at professionals moving into executive roles across corporate, government and not-for-profit sectors alike. The core 12-unit structure covers strategy, finance, marketing, economics and people management, and finishes with a substantive research or consulting project rather than a conventional exam.

An MBA (Plus) variant is available for students who want to go deeper in one functional area (human resource management, marketing, or international business) by adding four specialised units on top of the core program.

Work Integrated Learning is built into the online delivery model too: rather than a single internship, students work through applied projects set by real organisations, which UC positions as giving graduates a portfolio of demonstrated outcomes for job interviews rather than just a transcript.
curriculum:
Core units: Managing People and Organisations; Accounting for Managers; Economics for Managers; Marketing Management; Strategic Management; Business Law and Ethics; Financial Management; Operations and Supply Chain Management; Managing in a Global Environment; Business Analytics
Applied component: Work Integrated Learning consulting project with an external organisation
Capstone: MBA Research Project or Strategic Management capstone
MBA (Plus) pathway: additional four specialisation units chosen from Human Resource Management, Marketing, or International Business streams
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree plus at least 2-3 years of relevant professional work experience (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Business Informatics
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in business, IT or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Clinical Psychology
description:
A highly selective two-year master's (48 credit points) covering the Level 3 and 4 graduate competencies set by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council, combining coursework, 1,000 hours of supervised placement across four rotations, and a three-part research project ending in a capstone.

Early placements run in UC's student-led health clinic, later ones across the lifespan in external services. Graduates are eligible for general registration as a psychologist and entry to the registrar program for clinical endorsement through AHPRA. Entry requires a four-year APAC-accredited psychology sequence, usually honours, completed within the last decade with at least 75 percent in the final year, plus eligibility for provisional registration. Shortlisted applicants are interviewed, and Commonwealth-supported places are limited and awarded on merit.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in psychology (typically an APAC-accredited honours degree), highly competitive limited-entry program (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Master of Communication
description:
A two-year master's (48 credit points) with seven core units on politics, communication trends and research methods, a restricted set of electives, and one specialisation of five units in strategic communication, marketing, journalism, or digital marketing.

It is open to graduates of any discipline, and applicants with a related degree can receive up to 12 credit points of advanced standing, shortening the program to about 18 months. A 180-hour internship is built into the curriculum, with placements in agencies, PR firms, government departments and non-profits, in Australia or overseas, which is a real advantage given Canberra's concentration of government communication and public affairs work. It suits people moving toward senior roles in strategic communication, brand and marketing, or journalism.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in communication, media or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Counselling
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in psychology, social science or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Creative Industries
description:
A deliberately flexible two-year master's (48 credit points) that students shape around their own goals, with core units, a specialisation in digital marketing, creative leadership, design, or heritage materials conservation, a wide elective pool spanning marketing, UX, entrepreneurship and creative business finance, and a work-integrated learning or research component.

The industry element can be an internship, a research project or a work-based project done with a partner or at the student's own workplace. Entry is a bachelor's degree in any field, with credit for relevant graduate certificates and a professional pathway for experienced applicants. It runs on campus, online or blended, and suits people moving into leadership and business roles across the creative and cultural sector.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a creative or related discipline (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Data Science
description:
The Master of Data Science is a two-year, full-time program built around a flexible 12-credit-point core rather than a rigid unit list: students can mix and match from units like Business Intelligence Systems, Database Systems, Artificial Intelligence Techniques, Soft Computing, Data Analytics and Business Intelligence, and Computer Vision and Image Analysis, unless they want a named specialisation printed on their testamur.

Three specialisation tracks are on offer: Sports Analytics, Business Intelligence, and Artificial Intelligence and Computational Modelling. Sports Analytics is a distinctly UC offering, drawing on the same AIS and elite-sport connections that shape the university's exercise science program, applied here to performance data rather than physiology.

Work Integrated Learning is again a required element rather than an optional extra, with students applying data science methods to a real industry problem before graduating. UC pitches this as the point of difference against more theory-heavy data science masters elsewhere.
curriculum:
Foundation units: Database Systems (PG); Statistics for Data Science; Programming for Data Science
Core/elective pool (12cp, mix per specialisation): Business Intelligence Systems; Artificial Intelligence Techniques; Soft Computing; Data Analytics and Business Intelligence; Computer Vision and Image Analysis; Data Science Technology and Systems; Econometrics
Specialisation tracks (optional, for testamur notation): Sports Analytics; Business Intelligence; Artificial Intelligence and Computational Modelling
Applied component: Work Integrated Learning industry data project
Capstone: Data Science Research Project or Industry Project
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a quantitative discipline (or equivalent); some programming or statistics background expected.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Engineering
description:
A two-year graduate-entry master's (48 credit points) with a network engineering focus, covering the design, development and operation of networking systems. Entry requires a four-year engineering degree, a three-year Engineers Australia accredited technologist degree, or a UC degree in IT, software engineering or a relevant science major, with assumed knowledge in ICT and basic programming.

The course includes 450 hours of work-integrated learning and a two-part capstone that delivers a real engineering solution for a business, government or community client. UC states it will pursue accreditation with Engineers Australia at professional engineer level and with the Australian Computer Society, so applicants should confirm the current accreditation status before enrolling. It suits engineering and computing graduates moving into network engineering, ICT security engineering, IoT or IT project roles.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in engineering or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Information Sciences (Research)
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree with honours (or equivalent) in a related field, and an approved research proposal with confirmed supervisor availability.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Information Technology and Systems
description:
A two-year master's (48 credit points) that takes graduates from any field into IT, so no prior computing study is assumed. Thirty credit points of core cover introductory IT, systems analysis and modelling, professional practice, research methods and a technology capstone research project; the remaining 18 form one specialisation from cybersecurity, AI and machine learning, cloud computing and IoT, data science, or a general track.

It is fully accredited at professional level by the Australian Computer Society, and work-integrated learning places students with organisations, which matters in Canberra given the size of the federal government technology workforce. Delivery is flexible across weekday, evening, blended and online options. It suits career changers moving into roles such as systems analyst, cybersecurity specialist, data analyst or IT manager.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (extended IT conversion program for non-cognate graduates) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of International Development
description:
A two-year master's (48 credit points: 30 required, 12 restricted-choice, 6 elective) covering sustainable development, gender and development, humanitarian intervention, global health, and the planning, monitoring and evaluation of development projects.

The nine-credit-point Development Research Project lets students investigate a real initiative, often tied to their current job, with past work examining programs in Papua New Guinea, Indonesia, Mexico and Pakistan. Entry is a bachelor's degree in any field, with a professional pathway for people with relevant experience, and holders of a graduate certificate or diploma in the field receive credit. Being in Canberra puts students near DFAT and the aid and NGO sector. It suits people heading into roles as program managers, monitoring and evaluation officers, gender advisers or development consultants.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Medical Imaging
description:
An accelerated graduate-entry master's that compresses a normal three-year radiography qualification into 2.5 years. Entry is a bachelor's degree in any field with a credit average plus at least two degree-level units of anatomy and physiology, with introductory physics, psychology and statistics assumed, and IELTS 7.0 in every band.

It is an approved program of study with the Medical Radiation Practice Board of Australia, so graduates can apply for registration as a diagnostic radiographer. Clinical training is substantial: four five-week placement blocks and two 13-week residencies across general radiography, CT, MRI, mammography and ultrasound, after practising on campus equipment first. It suits graduates changing career into diagnostic imaging who want the fastest registrable route.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in medical radiation science or a cognate clinical science field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Master of Nursing Practice (Graduate Entry)
description:
A two-year graduate-entry nursing degree for people who already hold a bachelor's degree in any discipline and want to become a registered nurse. It is taught in intensive theory blocks supported by online content and interspersed with clinical placements.

Students complete 800 hours of supervised clinical practice across settings including medical and surgical wards, emergency, intensive care, paediatrics and aged care, at Canberra Hospital and regional NSW facilities. The course is accredited by ANMAC and approved by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, so graduates are eligible to apply for registration as a nurse through AHPRA. Entry requires a completed degree with a credit average finished within the last ten years, IELTS 7.0, and the usual immunisation, police and first-aid clearances. It suits career changers committed to clinical nursing.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (graduate-entry pathway to nursing registration) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.5 (no band below 7.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 102, PTE 69), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Master of Nutrition and Dietetics
description:
A two-year master's (48 credit points) that qualifies graduates as an Accredited Practising Dietitian through Dietitians Australia, a credential recognised internationally. Year one is eight units of clinical, community and research content; year two is almost entirely placement.

Students complete up to 24 weeks of full-time workplace education across hospitals, community health services and food service settings, plus an additional four-week internship that UC builds in for networking and job-seeking. Entry is demanding: a bachelor's degree in human nutrition plus specific degree-level study in chemistry, human biology and physiology, biochemistry, and food and nutrition science, and IELTS 7.0 with no band below 7.0. It suits nutrition graduates set on clinical and community dietetics practice, with a stated emphasis on ageing populations.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in human nutrition, food science or a related field, highly competitive limited-entry program (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Master of Occupational Therapy
description:
A two-year graduate-entry master's, starting in Semester 2, open to graduates of any discipline with a credit average. Students complete 1,000 hours of practical education in hospitals, clinics, community organisations, schools and aged care, locally and interstate, with placements run full-time and travel and accommodation at the student's expense.

The degree is accredited by the Occupational Therapy Council of Australia and approved by the World Federation of Occupational Therapists, so graduates can apply for registration with the Occupational Therapy Board of Australia and have their qualification recognised in many other countries. Entry requires IELTS 7.0 with no band below 7.0, a police check, Working with Vulnerable People registration, immunisation records, and first aid and CPR. It suits graduates committed to enabling people with disability, injury or age-related limitation to take part in daily life.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in health science or a related field, highly competitive limited-entry program (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Master of Optometry
description:
A two-year graduate-entry master's open specifically to graduates of UC's Bachelor of Vision Science. It is accredited by the Optometry Council of Australia and New Zealand, and completing both degrees makes graduates eligible to apply for registration as an optometrist with the Optometry Board of Australia, including autonomous prescribing of ocular therapeutics.

Clinical placements are full-time and generally involve interstate travel at the student's own cost, and students buy a set of specialist equipment (around A$5,000) before placement. It suits Vision Science students continuing straight through to clinical qualification, with graduates working in private practice, hospitals, community eye care and research.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in vision science or a related field, highly competitive limited-entry program (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Master of Pharmacy
description:
A two-year graduate-entry pharmacy degree for people who already hold a bachelor's degree in any field with a credit average and have completed one unit in five of six sciences: chemistry, biochemistry, microbiology, anatomy, physiology and pharmacology.

It is fully accredited by the Australian Pharmacy Council, so graduates can go on to the supervised internship year that leads to registration as a pharmacist. Placements include two-week blocks in community and hospital pharmacies over the winter periods plus shorter placements through each teaching semester, with the usual police, immunisation and Working with Vulnerable People clearances. It suits career changers who want to become pharmacists without repeating a four-year undergraduate degree.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in pharmaceutical science or a related field, highly competitive limited-entry program (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Master of Physiotherapy
description:
A two-year graduate-entry master's (48 credit points) for people who hold a health science bachelor's degree with a credit average and prior study in musculoskeletal and functional anatomy, exercise physiology and biomechanics.

Clinical education is four five-week full-time placements spanning acute care, rehabilitation and aged care. Placements are full-time only and typically require interstate travel at the student's own cost. The course is accredited by the Australian Physiotherapy Council, and graduates are eligible to apply for registration as a physiotherapist through AHPRA. It suits health graduates, often from exercise or sport science, who want the fastest accredited route into physiotherapy practice rather than a four-year undergraduate degree.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in exercise science, health science or a related field, highly competitive limited-entry program (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Master of Primary Teaching
description:
A two-year graduate-entry teaching degree for people whose bachelor's degree includes at least one year of full-time study relevant to a primary curriculum learning area. It is registered by the ACT Teacher Quality Institute and recognised as a teaching qualification across Australia.

Students complete 60 days of supervised professional experience in Canberra partner schools and must pass a moderated Teaching Performance Assessment to graduate, as well as both parts of the LANTITE literacy and numeracy test. All applicants attend a suitability interview (CASPI). The English requirement for entry and for later registration is high: IELTS 7.5 overall with 8.0 in speaking and listening. It suits graduates moving into primary teaching who can evidence relevant prior study.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (graduate-entry pathway to primary teaching registration) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description:
A two-year conversion master's (48 credit points) taught on the Bruce campus, accredited by both CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, so graduates meet the academic entry requirement for the CPA and CA ANZ professional programs.

Thirteen core units cover accounting systems, corporate and management accounting, business finance and auditing, with electives in areas such as risk management, entrepreneurship and revenue law, plus a capstone that can be a research project, an industry project or an internship. It is built for career changers with a non-accounting degree and for internationally trained accountants seeking Australian recognition; applicants who already hold an accounting major from an Australian university are not eligible. No prior accounting study or work experience is required to enter.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Public Health
description:
An 18-month master's (36 credit points), with 27 points of required study covering epidemiology, biostatistics, health economics, health promotion, ecological public health, policy, and a research project, and 9 points of electives in areas such as communicable disease control, global health, Indigenous health and program evaluation.

Work placements and applied research projects are available through the elective units, with students working alongside UC Health Research Institute staff and partners in government, NGOs and community organisations. Being based in Canberra puts students close to the federal health department and national agencies. Entry is a completed bachelor's degree, with admission on academic merit and some basic biostatistics knowledge assumed. It suits clinical and non-clinical health workers moving into public health officer, policy, health promotion or community health roles.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in health science, medicine, nursing or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Public Policy
description:
UC's Master of Public Policy is delivered fully online and built from 12 core units, each running on a compressed seven-week cycle rather than a standard semester; the university advises 15-20 hours of study per week, which lets motivated students finish in as little as two years while working full time.

The content is explicitly applied rather than theoretical: policy analysis, economic modelling, data analytics and program evaluation sit alongside more traditional units on the machinery of government. Being based in the national capital gives UC's politics and public policy staff direct lines into Commonwealth departments and agencies, which shows up in guest contributions and case material drawn from actual ACT and federal policy processes rather than generic international examples.

The degree sits within a nested suite (Graduate Certificate, Graduate Diploma and Master), so students can exit early with a lower award or step up into the full Master of Public Policy depending on how their circumstances change during study.
curriculum:
Core units (12 x 7-week blocks): Foundations of Public Policy; The Policy Process; Public Sector Economics; Policy Analysis and Evaluation; Government and Governance; Data Analytics for Policy; Program Evaluation; Public Finance and Budgeting; Regulation and Policy Instruments; Comparative Public Policy; Strategic Policy Leadership; Applied Policy Project
Exit points: Graduate Certificate in Public Policy (4 units); Graduate Diploma in Public Policy (8 units); Master of Public Policy (12 units)
Capstone: Applied Policy Project addressing a real government or public-sector problem
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (or equivalent); relevant government/public-sector experience well regarded.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Research
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree with honours (or equivalent), and an approved research proposal with confirmed supervisor availability.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Secondary Teaching
description:
A two-year graduate-entry secondary teaching degree. Entry requires a bachelor's degree with a major in a school teaching area such as English, mathematics, science, a language, humanities and social sciences, health and physical education, technologies, or creative and performing arts, with a second teaching area preferred.

Students complete 60 days of supervised placement in Canberra region secondary schools, pass a Teaching Performance Assessment, and pass both components of the LANTITE test. All applicants sit a suitability interview (CASPI), and the English requirement is IELTS 7.5 with 8.0 in speaking and listening. The course is registered by the ACT Teacher Quality Institute and recognised nationally. It suits graduates with a strong discipline background who want to teach years 7 to 12.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a discipline relevant to a secondary teaching specialisation (graduate-entry pathway to secondary teaching registration) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Social Work (Qualifying)
description:
A three-year qualifying master's (16 study blocks) for graduates who hold a bachelor's degree in a related field such as psychology, allied health, counselling, education or sociology, with prior study in social science and human behaviour. It is delivered online, with in-person attendance required only for placement.

Students complete 1,000 hours of field education across two supervised placements. The program is undergoing provisional accreditation with the Australian Association of Social Workers rather than holding full accreditation, which applicants should weigh, since AASW eligibility is what allows practice as an accredited social worker. Recognition of prior learning of up to 25 percent is available to social welfare and community services graduates. It suits career changers moving into aged care, disability, child and family, mental health, justice or policy work.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (qualifying pathway to social work registration) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Master of Speech Pathology
description:
A two-year graduate-entry master's for people who already hold a bachelor's or postgraduate degree in any field with a credit average. It has full accreditation from Speech Pathology Australia, so graduates are eligible for practising membership and can work as speech pathologists across Australia.

Clinical placements run four days a week at health and education sites including the UC Health Precinct and regional and remote locations. The course is framed around producing researcher-practitioners and builds in substantial research training alongside clinical work in speech, language, swallowing and communication disorders across all age groups. The English requirement is unusually high at IELTS 8.0 with no band below 8.0, alongside police, immunisation and Working with Vulnerable People checks.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline, highly competitive limited-entry program (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Master of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL) & Foreign Language Teaching (FLT)
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a related field (relevant for practising or aspiring language educators) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Professional Doctorate in Business Administration (Research)
admission_requirements: A relevant master's degree (e.g. MBA) plus substantial senior management/professional experience and an approved research proposal.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: UC Connect
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 11 (or equivalent secondary schooling); designed as an alternative entry pathway into UC bachelor's degrees for students who do not yet meet direct-entry ATAR requirements.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.0-5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 35-46, PTE 30-42), depending on the specific stream.
intake_dates: February, July (rolling entry also available for some streams)

name: UC Preparation Scheme
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 11 (or equivalent secondary schooling); designed as an alternative entry pathway into UC bachelor's degrees for students who do not yet meet direct-entry ATAR requirements.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.0-5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 35-46, PTE 30-42), depending on the specific stream.
intake_dates: February, July (rolling entry also available for some streams)

name: Undergraduate Certificate in Education
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate required prior to professional placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: University of Canberra International Foundation Studies
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 11 (or equivalent secondary schooling) for international students seeking an alternative pathway into a UC bachelor's degree.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.0-5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 35-46, PTE 30-42), depending on the specific stream.
intake_dates: February, July (multiple intakes for some streams)

name: Bachelor of Counselling
description:
The Bachelor of Counselling sits a little apart from the rest of the University of Divinity's catalogue, which is otherwise almost entirely theology and ministry. This is a professional counselling degree, though it's taught within a university whose identity and college network are explicitly Christian, and several of its member colleges (Whitley College, Eastern College Australia among them) fold a pastoral or values-based counselling orientation into the training rather than treating it as incidental.

Students complete core counselling theory, ethics and practice units alongside supervised placement hours, working toward eligibility for professional counselling registration in Australia (typically ACA or PACFA-aligned pathways depending on the specific college and cohort). The counselling degree exists partly because chaplaincy, pastoral care and church-based welfare work are common destinations for University of Divinity graduates broadly, and a dedicated counselling qualification lets students formalise that pastoral instinct into a registrable clinical skill set.

Graduates go into private practice, community and church-based counselling services, and pastoral care roles in hospitals, schools and aged care, often building on a values framework that's more explicit here than in a secular counselling degree elsewhere.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Counselling Theory, Human Development, Communication Skills, Ethics in Counselling
Year 2: Counselling Practice and Techniques, Family and Relationship Counselling, Trauma-Informed Practice, supervised placement I
Year 3: Group Work and Facilitation, Counselling in Faith and Community Contexts, advanced supervised placement, capstone case study portfolio
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Ministry
description:
The Bachelor of Ministry is the more vocationally focused sibling of the Bachelor of Theology: same three-year, four-field structure (Humanities, Biblical Studies, Christian Thought and History, and Theology: Mission and Ministry), but weighted harder toward the Mission and Ministry strand and toward practical placement, aimed squarely at students heading into lay ministry, youth or community ministry, or pastoral leadership roles that don't require the extended academic and language training built into a Master of Divinity.

Students complete it through one of the University of Divinity's member colleges, and many are already working in a church or parachurch role while studying part-time, which the degree structure accommodates: it can stretch to nine years part-time, the same maximum as the Bachelor of Theology.

It functions as a practical entry point into vocational ministry for people who know their calling is hands-on pastoral and community work rather than academic theology, without foreclosing the option of moving on to a Master of Divinity or Master of Theology later.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Old Testament, Introduction to New Testament, Foundations of Christian Ministry, Humanities elective
Year 2: Pastoral Care and Ministry Practice, Christian Thought and History unit, supervised ministry placement I
Year 3: Leadership in Ministry Contexts, advanced Mission and Ministry electives, capstone ministry placement and reflective portfolio
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); typically undertaken alongside a church/ministry placement
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Theology
description:
The Bachelor of Theology is the University of Divinity's foundational undergraduate degree, but "the university" here is a loose word for what's actually a federation: students enrol through one of the constituent colleges (Catholic Theological College, Pilgrim Theological College, Ridley College, Whitley College and others spanning Anglican, Baptist, Catholic, Lutheran, Uniting Church and Salvation Army traditions) rather than a single central campus, and take classes structured around four fields: Humanities, Biblical Studies, Christian Thought and History, and Theology: Mission and Ministry.

That federated structure is the actual selling point, not a bureaucratic quirk. A Bachelor of Theology student can end up studying alongside seminarians from a different denomination entirely, taught by faculty formed in a different tradition, in a way that a single-denomination bible college simply can't replicate. The university has described itself as one of the more sustained ecumenical experiments in Australian higher education, going back over a century to its 1910 founding as the Melbourne College of Divinity.

The three-year, full-time degree suits people heading toward ministry, chaplaincy, religious education or further postgraduate theological study, and it can be completed over as long as nine years part-time, which matters given how many students are already working in parish or pastoral roles while they study.
curriculum:
Field of study across the degree: Biblical Studies (Old and New Testament units), Christian Thought and History (patristics through to modern theology), Theology: Mission and Ministry, Humanities electives
Year 1: Introduction to Old Testament, Introduction to New Testament, Introduction to Christian Thought, foundational Humanities unit
Year 2: further Biblical Studies units, Church History, Ethics, a Mission and Ministry practicum unit
Year 3: advanced electives across the four fields, capstone unit chosen in consultation with the student's college
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Diploma in Theology
description:
The Diploma in Theology is the University of Divinity's entry-level credential, shorter than the three-year bachelor degrees and pitched at students testing whether formal theological study suits them, those wanting a foundational qualification for a church or parachurch role without a full degree commitment, or students planning to build credit toward a Bachelor of Theology or Bachelor of Ministry later; completed units typically count toward the bachelor's degree if a student decides to continue.

It draws on the same four-field structure as the university's bachelor degrees (Humanities, Biblical Studies, Christian Thought and History, and Mission and Ministry), just compressed into a shorter, more introductory sequence, and like the rest of the university's offerings it's delivered through one of the constituent colleges rather than a single central faculty.

Graduates commonly move into entry-level church ministry support roles, or use the diploma as a stepping stone into a full bachelor's program once they've confirmed the direction suits them.
curriculum: Introduction to Old Testament, Introduction to New Testament, Introduction to Christian Thought, Foundations of Christian Ministry, one Humanities elective, one further elective chosen from Biblical Studies or Mission and Ministry
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); no prior theological study required
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Doctor of Philosophy (Theology)
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy (Theology) is the University of Divinity's highest research degree and, unlike the coursework-heavy Master of Divinity, it's almost entirely independent research: a substantial thesis supervised by a scholar drawn from one of the constituent colleges, examined externally in the standard Australian PhD model. Candidates work across the university's full theological range: biblical studies, systematic and historical theology, ethics, liturgical studies and practical theology, and supervision is matched to a candidate's specific research question rather than assigned by a single central department, since expertise is distributed across the college network.

What makes doctoral study here distinctive is the ecumenical breadth of supervisory expertise available under one doctoral framework: a candidate researching, say, Catholic sacramental theology and one researching Uniting Church ecclesiology can both be supervised and examined within the same PhD program, drawing on faculty across traditions the university has spent over a century bringing together.

Graduates go into academic theology, senior denominational leadership, and specialist research and teaching roles at seminaries and universities, both in Australia and internationally.
