english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Engineering Honours (Civil Engineering)
description:
Sydney's civil engineering program benefits from the university's location in a city undergoing genuinely large infrastructure expansion. Sydney Metro, WestConnex, and other major transport projects have provided a steady stream of real capstone and thesis project material, and the school's structural and geotechnical research groups have direct industry ties into the firms delivering that infrastructure. The four-year Bachelor of Engineering Honours (Civil) is Engineers Australia accredited and follows the newer flexible-first-year structure the university introduced, where students choose their engineering specialisation from a common engineering foundation rather than committing to civil from day one of enrolment.

A mandatory professional practice component, around 60 days of industry experience, is built into the degree, and Sydney's placement office draws on the university's large alumni base in Sydney's construction, consulting engineering, and transport infrastructure sectors to help students find relevant placements, though students are still expected to do a fair amount of the searching themselves rather than being handed a placement.

The capstone thesis project in the final year is individually supervised and, for students in structural or geotechnical specialisations, frequently connects to genuine ongoing research in areas like resilient infrastructure design, a research strength that's grown given increasing attention to climate-related infrastructure risk in Australian engineering practice.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering foundation units common across specialisations — Mathematics for Engineers, Engineering Mechanics, Introduction to Engineering Design, Materials Science
Year 2: Civil engineering core begins — Structural Analysis, Fluid Mechanics, Geotechnical Engineering, Surveying
Year 3: Structural Design (steel and concrete), Water and Environmental Engineering, Transportation Engineering, Professional Practice (industry placement, approx. 60 days)
Year 4 (Honours): Advanced Structural or Geotechnical Design, Engineering Thesis (individual research project), technical electives
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent) with ATAR of approximately 90-95; strong background in mathematics and physics recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Engineering Honours (Software Engineering)
description:
Sydney's software engineering degree sits within the same faculty as the university's strong computer science research base, and students get exposure to genuine research areas: the Australian Institute for Machine Learning and the university's cybersecurity research groups feed into elective offerings in a way that a purely vocational software degree wouldn't provide. The Bachelor of Engineering Honours (Software) is four years, Engineers Australia accredited, and shares a common first year with the rest of the engineering cohort before specialising, which suits students who aren't entirely sure between software and another engineering discipline early on.

Sydney's central location and reputation give students unusually direct access to the city's large finance, consulting, and tech-sector employers for the mandatory professional practice placement (around 60 days), and it's common for students to convert their placement into part-time work through their final year of study, sometimes leading to a graduate offer well before finishing the degree.

The final-year thesis project is individually supervised and can be research-based (attached to a faculty research group) or industry-based, and students interested in machine learning or cybersecurity specialisations tend to gravitate toward the research-based option given the faculty's active work in those areas.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering foundation units common across specialisations — Mathematics for Engineers, Introduction to Programming, Engineering Mechanics, Discrete Mathematics
Year 2: Software engineering core begins — Data Structures and Algorithms, Software Construction, Computer Systems, Database Systems
Year 3: Software Architecture, Software Testing and Quality, Professional Practice (industry placement, approx. 60 days), electives (options in AI, cybersecurity, distributed systems)
Year 4 (Honours): Advanced software electives, Engineering Thesis (research-group or industry-based project)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent) with ATAR of approximately 92-96; strong background in mathematics recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
Sydney's Bachelor of Science covers an unusually wide major list, and several of its life sciences majors benefit directly from the university's genuine research depth. The Charles Perkins Centre brings together researchers working on metabolic health, nutrition, and chronic disease, and undergraduates in relevant majors get exposure to that interdisciplinary research culture earlier than a purely departmental science degree would allow. Marine science and environmental biology students also have access to genuine field research infrastructure through the university's field stations, giving hands-on fieldwork experience rather than lab-only coursework for those majors.

Students choose one or two majors from options spanning the physical, life, and mathematical sciences, and the degree structure is designed around combinability: pairing, say, data science with biology, or chemistry with a second science major, is a normal and expected path rather than an edge case the timetabling struggles to accommodate. A capstone research or project unit in third year is common across most majors, giving students a genuine taste of independent research before deciding on honours.

Because Sydney's science faculty is large and covers so many disciplines, the actual day-to-day experience differs substantially by major. A physics student and a marine biology student are living quite different versions of "the science degree," which is worth knowing going in rather than assuming a single unified experience across all majors.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundational units across chosen majors (Chemistry, Biology, Physics, Mathematics typically among first-year choices), Introduction to Scientific Thinking
Year 2: Major-specific core units (one or two majors selected from options including Marine Science, Data Science, Chemistry, Biology, Physics, Environmental Studies), Research Methods
Year 3: Advanced major units, Capstone Science Project, electives
Optional Year 4: Honours year with individual research thesis (competitive entry based on GPA)
Distinctive majors: life sciences majors with Charles Perkins Centre research connections, Marine Science with field station access
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent) with ATAR of approximately 85-92; background in mathematics and a science subject recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Doctor of Medicine
description:
Sydney Medical School runs one of the older and more clinically distributed graduate-entry MD programs in the country. Students need a completed bachelor's degree plus the GAMSAT before applying, and the four-year MD moves quickly into clinical placements compared to some competitor programs, with clinical schools spread across Sydney's major teaching hospitals (Royal Prince Alfred, Westmead, Concord, Royal North Shore, Nepean) as well as a dedicated rural clinical school network based out of Dubbo and Orange that places a meaningful share of each cohort in regional NSW for extended blocks.

The MD structure blends case-based and problem-based learning in the early years with a strong emphasis on early clinical contact: students are in hospitals and general practices from year one rather than confined to lecture theatres. The later years are essentially a series of rotating clinical placements across the affiliated hospital network, meaning the actual clinical experience differs quite a bit depending on which teaching hospital or rural site a student is assigned to in a given term.

Sydney's rural clinical school placements run for extended periods (a full year in some cases) rather than short rotations, which the university markets as building genuine competence in rural and generalist medicine, a deliberate response to the persistent shortage of doctors willing to work outside major cities in Australia.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Foundations of clinical practice (case-based and problem-based learning), Human Structure and Function, Population Health, early clinical placements in hospitals and general practice
Years 3-4: Core clinical rotations — medicine, surgery, psychiatry, obstetrics and gynaecology, paediatrics, general practice, emergency medicine — across metropolitan teaching hospitals (RPA, Westmead, Concord, Royal North Shore, Nepean) and the rural clinical school (Dubbo/Orange, extended placements)
Selective and elective terms in later clinical years, including options for overseas or research-based electives
Entry: completed bachelor's degree, GAMSAT, interview
admission_requirements: Completed bachelor degree (any discipline) with a minimum credit average, competitive GAMSAT score, and satisfactory performance in a multi-mini interview (MMI).
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0 (or equivalent).

name: Juris Doctor
description:
Sydney Law School's JD is the graduate-entry law degree for students without an undergraduate law background, and the law school's reputation (regularly ranked the top or near-top law school in Australia) means the JD cohort is genuinely competitive to get into and draws heavily from students with strong results in other disciplines (commerce, science, arts) looking to pivot into law rather than students who simply didn't get into an undergrad law program.

The degree covers the full Priestley 11 subjects required for legal practice admission in NSW, and Sydney's elective offerings in the later JD years reflect the law school's genuine research depth in areas like international law, competition law, and intellectual property, taught by academics who are frequently cited in Australian case law commentary. The law school also runs an active clinical legal education program, placing students in supervised casework with community legal centres and the Public Interest Advocacy Centre, giving some JD students real client-facing experience before graduating.

Because Sydney's JD cohort is large and draws from such varied undergraduate backgrounds, the study groups and class discussion tend to be more interdisciplinary in flavour than at law schools with a smaller, more law-focused JD intake, something graduates often cite as a genuine strength of the program rather than a side effect.
curriculum:
Year 1: Legal Reasoning and the Common Law Tradition, Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Public Law
Year 2: Property, Equity, Corporations Law, Evidence, Administrative Law, electives
Year 3: Civil and Criminal Procedure, Professional Responsibility, Clinical Legal Education placement option, advanced electives (options include International Law, Competition Law, Intellectual Property)
Covers Priestley 11 subjects required for admission to legal practice in NSW; Practical Legal Training required post-graduation
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor degree in any discipline with a strong academic record; competitive LSAT score recommended for domestic applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 overall, no band below 7.0 (or equivalent).

name: Master of Commerce
description:
Sydney's Master of Commerce is a flexible graduate business degree that lets students without a business undergraduate background convert into a commerce specialisation, with majors spanning finance, accounting, marketing, and business analytics among others, a genuinely popular option for international graduates from engineering, science, or arts backgrounds looking for a business-focused postgraduate qualification without committing to a full MBA's cost and work-experience expectations.

The degree can be tailored quite differently depending on major choice (a finance-focused MCom looks and feels quite different from a marketing or business analytics-focused one), and Sydney Business School's genuine research depth in financial markets (given the university's proximity to the ASX and Sydney's financial sector) shows up directly in the finance major's elective offerings and guest teaching.

Most students complete the degree in 1.5 to 2 years depending on their undergraduate background, and a capstone project or internship-style unit in the final semester gives students a chance to apply coursework to a real business problem before graduating, something Sydney's careers service actively supports given the large number of Sydney-based employers the university has relationships with.
curriculum:
Core units: Managerial Economics, Accounting for Managers, Quantitative Methods for Business, Business Ethics and Sustainability
Major coursework (choose one): Finance, Accounting, Marketing, Business Analytics, International Business, Human Resource Management
Electives within chosen major, plus cross-disciplinary electives
Capstone: Business Project or Internship unit (final semester)
Duration: 1.5 to 2 years full-time depending on prior qualifications
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor degree in a related discipline with a minimum credit average; relevant work experience viewed favourably.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Master of Computer Science
description:
Sydney's computer science school sits close to some genuinely strong applied research groups. The Australian Institute for Machine Learning has a formal AI-focused offshoot, and the university's robotics and computer vision work (the field robotics group has real runs on the board in agricultural and mining automation) feeds into elective and project options that go beyond a standard coursework degree. The Master of Computer Science is built for students converting from other disciplines as much as for CS graduates, with an extended two-year stream for those without prior computing background and a 1.5-year stream for people who already hold a related degree.

Specialisation strands include artificial intelligence, data science, and software development, and students in the AI stream in particular get access to units taught by researchers active in the field rather than only generalist lecturers. Sydney's central location gives students a genuine edge on internships and part-time work with the city's large finance, consulting, and tech-sector employers. A lot of coursework master's students in this program are juggling paid industry work alongside study by their final semester, and the university's careers service leans into that with dedicated tech-sector recruitment events.

The capstone project unit can be taken as an industry project, a research project attached to a supervisor, or a coursework-based project depending on the student's stream, giving genuine choice in how the degree culminates rather than one fixed thesis format for everyone.
curriculum:
Foundation units (extended pathway only): Introduction to Programming, Data Structures and Algorithms, Discrete Mathematics for Computing
Core coursework: Software Construction and Design, Computer Networks, Database Systems, Machine Learning Fundamentals
Specialisation streams: Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Software Development
Capstone: choose between Industry Project, Research Project (with academic supervisor), or Coursework Capstone Project
Standard pathway (relevant bachelor's): approximately 1.5 years; extended pathway: approximately 2 years
admission_requirements: Australian bachelor's degree in any discipline with a credit average (65%), or equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (University's standard postgraduate coursework requirement).

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The Bachelor of Business at the University of Tasmania is a standard broad-based business degree (accounting, finance, marketing, management and economics majors are all available), but it's taught through the Tasmanian School of Business and Economics, which carries AACSB accreditation, the same international quality benchmark held by a relatively small number of Australian business schools. For a business degree at a university of Tasmania's size, that's a genuine point of comparison against much larger metropolitan business schools that hold the same accreditation.

The degree is flexible by design, letting students combine a major with a minor or a second major rather than locking into a single specialisation from day one, and Hobart's compact business community means placement and internship opportunities with local firms, Tasmanian government agencies and the state's growing tourism and agribusiness sectors are more directly accessible than the same search would be in a crowded mainland capital.

Graduates go into accounting, banking and finance, marketing and general management roles, both within Tasmania's own business sector and, for those who want it, into mainland or international graduate programs where the degree's AACSB accreditation carries recognised weight.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Principles, Economics for Business, Introduction to Management, Business Statistics
Year 2: major and minor units begin (Accounting, Finance, Marketing, Management or Economics streams), Business Law, Organisational Behaviour
Year 3: advanced major units, capstone business strategy unit, optional industry placement or work-integrated learning unit
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 65 recommended
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

name: Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
The Bachelor of Education (Primary) qualifies graduates to teach in Tasmanian primary schools and, with mutual recognition, in other Australian states, and it's shaped in part by Tasmania's specific education challenges: the state has historically had lower rates of Year 12 completion and adult literacy than the national average, and the university's teacher education faculty has built a reputation around place-based and community-engaged approaches to literacy and numeracy teaching as a direct response to that local context, rather than importing a generic national curriculum framework unchanged.

The degree includes substantial supervised professional experience placements in schools across the state, satisfying the practicum requirements set by the Teachers Registration Board of Tasmania and the national Australian Institute for Teaching and School Leadership standards, and students move through progressively more independent teaching placements from first observation-based rounds to a final extended internship.

Graduates are registered to teach in Tasmanian government and independent primary schools, with the state's own persistent teacher shortages in regional and rural areas meaning local graduates are often recruited directly out of their final placement school.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Teaching and Learning, Child Development, Literacy Education I, first classroom observation placement
Year 2: Numeracy Education, Curriculum and Pedagogy, Inclusive Education, expanded classroom placement
Year 3: Assessment and Reporting, Science and Technology Education, Health and Physical Education, extended professional placement
Year 4: Professional Practice and Ethics, capstone internship placement, portfolio for teacher registration
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent) with satisfactory results in English; ATAR of approximately 65 recommended
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.5, no band below 7.0 (Australian teacher registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
The Bachelor of Laws at the University of Tasmania is one of the older law schools in the country, and it trades on a genuine structural advantage over larger mainland schools: a small, tight-knit cohort in Hobart means students get more direct contact with judges, practitioners and the Tasmanian legal profession than is realistic in a Sydney or Melbourne law school with several hundred students per year group. The Tasmanian Supreme Court and legal profession are compact enough that moot courts, clerkships and work placements tend to be genuinely accessible rather than intensely competitive scarce slots.

The degree covers the standard Priestley 11 core subjects required for admission to legal practice anywhere in Australia, and the law school has historically had a particular strength in constitutional and public law given Tasmania's role in several significant High Court cases (the Tasmanian Dam Case being the best known), which shows up in how constitutional law is taught here.

Graduates go on to practical legal training and admission, with a notable number staying in Tasmania to article with the state's law firms, courts and government legal service, a smaller but less saturated market than the graduate glut common in the eastern mainland capitals.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Law, Contracts, Torts, Legal Research and Writing
Year 2: Criminal Law, Property Law, Administrative Law, Constitutional Law
Year 3: Equity and Trusts, Evidence, Company Law, elective units
Year 4: Civil Procedure, Professional Responsibility, further electives (public international law, environmental law, and similar), capstone or clinical legal education placement
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 80 recommended
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

name: Bachelor of Marine and Antarctic Science
description:
The Bachelor of Marine and Antarctic Science is the only degree of its kind in Australia, and geography does most of the selling: Hobart sits closer to Antarctica than any other Australian capital, is home port to the CSIRO and Australian Antarctic Division research fleet, and hosts the university's own Institute for Marine and Antarctic Studies (IMAS) on the Taroona waterfront, where undergraduates take classes alongside researchers actively publishing on Southern Ocean ecosystems rather than in a department that merely teaches about them secondhand.

The standard course is three years full-time, with a four-year embedded honours pathway for students who want a research year before going further. IMAS deliberately blends natural science with policy, management and law content, on the reasoning that marine and Antarctic science graduates increasingly need to operate in fisheries management, conservation policy and international Antarctic governance as much as in a lab, so the degree doesn't confine students to a single-discipline science track.

Graduates go into fisheries and marine park management, Antarctic and Southern Ocean research support roles, environmental consultancy and government science agencies. It's a smaller, more specialised job market than most science degrees feed into, but one where a Tasmanian marine science credential carries specific recognition given the concentration of relevant employers within a short drive of the university itself.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Marine and Antarctic Science, Chemistry and Biology foundations, Earth Systems Science, Mathematics for science
Year 2: Oceanography, Marine Ecology, Antarctic Environments, Marine and Antarctic Policy and Law
Year 3: specialisation units (fisheries, marine biology, glaciology or policy stream), field trip and vessel-based practical units, capstone research project
(optional Year 4: embedded Honours research thesis)
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent) with satisfactory results in English and a science subject; ATAR of approximately 70 recommended
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

name: Bachelor of Medical Science and Doctor of Medicine
description:
The Bachelor of Medical Science and Doctor of Medicine is Tasmania's combined medical pathway: three years of medical science foundations followed by the four-year MD, rather than a separate graduate-entry MD alone. Its defining feature is where students end up training: the university runs rural clinical schools across Tasmania (including Launceston and rural placement sites), reflecting a deliberate policy push, shared with several Australian medical schools, to train doctors in the kind of regional and rural settings they're most needed in rather than concentrating clinical training entirely in one metropolitan teaching hospital.

The medical science years build the standard preclinical foundation (anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, pathology) before students move into the MD's clinical years, which are built around extended rural and rotational placements across Tasmania's hospital network rather than a single fixed hospital site, giving graduates broader exposure to generalist practice than a purely metropolitan clinical school typically offers.

Graduates emerge with provisional registration and move into internship and residency, with Tasmania's own health system, persistently short of doctors in regional areas, a common and immediate destination, alongside interstate and, for some graduates, international training pathways.
curriculum:
Years 1–3 (Bachelor of Medical Science): Human Anatomy and Physiology, Biochemistry and Cell Biology, Pathology and Pharmacology, Population Health and Epidemiology, clinical skills foundation units
Years 4–7 (Doctor of Medicine): core clinical rotations (medicine, surgery, paediatrics, obstetrics and gynaecology, psychiatry, general practice), extended rural clinical placement year, elective specialty rotation, final-year internship-preparation clinical placement
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with high ATAR (approximately 90+), UCAT score, and interview; competitive selection
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0, no band below 7.0 (or equivalent)

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
The Bachelor of Nursing trains students for clinical placement across a state where rural and remote healthcare delivery isn't a special elective topic but the default context most graduates will actually work in. Tasmania's population is spread across small regional centres as much as Hobart and Launceston, and the degree's placement structure reflects that, sending students into rural hospitals and community health settings as a matter of course rather than as an optional rural health unit bolted onto a metropolitan-focused course.

Clinical placement hours meet the national accreditation standard required for registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, and the course combines campus-based simulation and skills labs with hospital and community placements building progressively across the degree, from observation-heavy first-year placements to near-independent practice in the final year.

Graduates register as nurses and typically go into acute care, aged care, community and rural health roles, with Tasmania's own public health system, spread thin across a small population, a common and immediate employer for local graduates.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Health Assessment, introductory clinical placement
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology, expanded clinical placement including rural rotation
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Aged Care and Chronic Disease Management, Leadership in Nursing Practice, final capstone clinical placement
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent) with satisfactory results in English; ATAR of approximately 65 recommended
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0, no band below 7.0 (registration requirement for nursing)

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
The Bachelor of Psychological Science is the accredited undergraduate entry point into psychology in Australia, built to the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council standard that any student aiming for provisional registration and eventual practice needs. At Tasmania it's taught through a psychology department with a long research profile in areas like cognitive neuroscience and mental health, and undergraduates get exposure to active research labs earlier than at some larger universities simply because cohort sizes are smaller and staff-to-student contact is closer.

The degree covers the core content areas APAC mandates (biological bases of behaviour, cognition, developmental and social psychology, statistics and research methods), building toward fourth-year Honours as the next required step for anyone pursuing registration as a psychologist, which the bachelor's degree alone doesn't confer.

Graduates who don't continue into Honours and postgraduate training still leave with a strong quantitative research skill set that transfers into human resources, market research, policy and community services work, which is where a meaningful share of psychology bachelor graduates nationally actually end up.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Research Methods and Statistics I, Biological Bases of Behaviour
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Research Methods and Statistics II
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology, Personality, Advanced Research Methods, capstone research project (required for APAC-accredited sequence, pathway to Honours)
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 70 recommended
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

name: Master of Information Technology and Systems
description:
The Master of Information Technology and Systems is a conversion-friendly postgraduate IT degree, aimed as much at graduates moving into tech from an unrelated undergraduate background as at computer science graduates deepening their qualification, with core units in programming, systems analysis, databases and networking alongside specialisation options in areas like cybersecurity, data analytics or enterprise systems depending on current course structure and student interest.

Being based in Hobart rather than a larger tech hub means the degree leans on Tasmania's smaller but genuinely growing digital economy: state government IT, agtech and data-driven agriculture given Tasmania's agricultural base, and a modest but real local software and services sector, rather than assuming graduates will inevitably relocate to Sydney or Melbourne, though many do.

Graduates move into systems analysis, software development, IT project management and business analysis roles, with the degree commonly chosen by international students and career-changers specifically because it doesn't assume an undergraduate computing background, unlike a straight Master of Computer Science.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Programming Fundamentals, Systems Analysis and Design, Database Systems
Semester 2: Networking and Security, Enterprise Systems, IT Project Management
Semester 3: specialisation electives (cybersecurity, data analytics, or software engineering stream), Research Methods in IT
Semester 4: capstone IT project or industry-based project, professional practice unit
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant or any discipline (typical Australian postgrad IT/CS entry bar used as approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
UTS's Bachelor of Business is a generalist business degree that leans on a major rather than forcing students to declare a specific professional identity from day one. Accounting, finance, management, marketing, international business and a handful of other majors sit under the one course code, and the first year is largely shared foundation subjects across all of them.

The business school occupies the Dr Chau Chak Wing Building, the Frank Gehry-designed building near Central Station that's become something of a Sydney landmark, and the course markets its connections to the CBD's finance and consulting employers heavily, including a work-integrated learning subject most students take in their final year with a real organisation.

Because majors can be combined (a second major, or paired with a business minor), the degree gives students more flexibility to pivot mid-course than a narrowly-titled Bachelor of Commerce or Bachelor of Accounting would, at the cost of being somewhat less immediately legible to employers who are looking for a specific accreditation pathway (accounting students, for instance, need to check their major satisfies CPA Australia or CAANZ requirements specifically).
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: Accounting for Decision Making, Economics for Business, Marketing Foundations, Management, Business Statistics
Year 2: Major subjects begin (Accounting / Finance / Marketing / Management / International Business), Business Law, Business Analytics
Year 3: Advanced major electives, Work-Integrated Learning subject (industry placement or consulting project), capstone strategy subject
Majors (choose one or combine two): Accounting, Finance, Marketing, Management, International Business, Human Resource Management, and others
CPA/CAANZ accreditation available depending on major and subject selection
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR approximately 82; sound understanding of Mathematics recommended
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

name: Bachelor of Communication (Honours)
description:
Communication (Honours) at UTS folds the honours research component into the standard degree rather than tacking it on afterward, similar to the law degree's model: students complete an honours thesis or major project in their final year rather than needing a separate fourth year. The course covers a broad communication and media studies base before students specialise into streams like journalism, public communication, social and political sciences, or creative writing.

UTS's journalism-adjacent teaching has a reputation for being hands-on rather than purely theoretical: students in the journalism stream produce actual published work through student-run outlets and industry placements rather than only writing essays about media theory. The Sydney location gives the course easy access to major mastheads and broadcasters for placements, something the faculty leans on in its industry-engagement subjects.

The honours thesis or project in the final year is individually supervised and can take the form of a traditional research thesis, a long-form journalism piece, or a creative/professional communication project depending on the student's stream and interests.
curriculum:
Duration: 4 years full-time
Year 1–2: Communication and Media foundations, Writing and Editing, Media Law and Ethics, stream selection (Journalism / Public Communication / Social and Political Change / Creative Writing)
Year 3: Stream-specific subjects, Industry Placement or Professional Practice subject
Year 4 (Honours): Research Methods, Honours Thesis or Major Project (research thesis, long-form journalism piece, or creative/professional project)
Electives available across streams and cross-faculty options
Final thesis/project individually supervised and presented to faculty panel
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR approximately 85-90, competitive entry across communication majors
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

name: Bachelor of Design in Architecture
description:
The Bachelor of Design in Architecture is the first half of UTS's five-year path to a professional architecture qualification (it's typically paired with the Master of Architecture afterward). What sets the course structure apart is the density of studio time: six dedicated Architectural Studio subjects run across the degree, one nearly every session, each built around a different design problem, and students are in studio roughly six contact hours a week on top of the compulsory theory and technical subjects.

Year 1 and 2 pair one 12-credit-point studio with two 6-credit-point subjects each session; year 3 shifts to one studio, one compulsory subject and one elective, giving students more room to specialise toward computational design, sustainability or heritage depending on interest. The faculty's building has laser cutters, 3D printers and dedicated studio floors that stay open outside class hours, which matters for a discipline where a lot of the real learning happens building physical models at 11pm before a crit.

Graduates who go on to the Master of Architecture emerge eligible to register as architects in NSW; those who stop at the bachelor's typically move into architectural assistant or design roles while completing further study part-time.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: Architectural Studio 1 & 2, Architectural History and Theory, Construction and Structures fundamentals
Year 2: Architectural Studio 3 & 4, Environmental Design, Digital Design Tools, Building Technology
Year 3: Architectural Studio 5 & 6, elective (computational design / sustainability / heritage), Professional Practice introduction
Structure: 6 Architectural Studio subjects (12cp each) plus compulsory and elective subjects each session
Pathway: typically followed by Master of Architecture for professional accreditation
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR approximately 80, portfolio not typically required
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

name: Bachelor of Design in Visual Communication
description:
Visual Communication at UTS runs as a studio-first degree: 144 credit points made up mostly of core studio subjects (108 credit points), plus dedicated design studies and a smaller elective allowance. The teaching model is brief-based: students get a mock client and a design problem most sessions and have to interpret, develop and present a resolved outcome, which mirrors agency workflow more than it mirrors a lecture-and-exam degree.

First year is deliberately narrow, hammering the fundamentals (image, typography, composition, hierarchy) before second year opens things up into content and the relationship between form and message. By the time students reach the third year, the electives and design studies component let them lean toward branding, motion, editorial or interaction design depending on where their portfolio is heading.

UTS's Faculty of Design, Architecture and Building has a track record of producing folio-heavy graduates who go straight into small-to-mid Sydney studios, and the program's connections into that local design scene (via guest critics, competition briefs and studio visits) are part of what distinguishes it from a more theory-heavy communication design degree elsewhere.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time, 144 credit points
Year 1: Introduction to Visual Communication, Typography 1, Image, Composition and Hierarchy studios
Year 2: Content and Form studios, Design Studies (theory/history), Typography 2, Interaction Design fundamentals
Year 3: Advanced studios (student-directed toward branding, editorial, motion or interaction), Design Studies electives, capstone folio project
Structure: 108cp core studio subjects + 24cp Design Studies + 12cp electives
Final capstone: portfolio-based major project presented to industry critics
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR approximately 80-85; folio/interview may be considered for some entry pathways
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) in Software Engineering
description:
Software Engineering at UTS sits inside the Bachelor of Engineering (Honours), which means students get the full four-year accredited engineering treatment rather than a computer-science-adjacent degree with "engineering" in the name for marketing purposes. It's accredited by Engineers Australia and recognised under the Washington Accord, so the qualification travels internationally.

What distinguishes it from a straight CS degree is the amount of systems-level and professional-practice content: subjects on requirements engineering, software architecture and formal engineering practice sit alongside the expected programming, algorithms and databases sequence. Many students take the course through UTS's Diploma in Professional Engineering Practice pathway, which embeds paid industry placements into the degree. UTS has one of the larger cooperative-education programs among Australian engineering schools, with placement partners across Sydney's finance, defence and telecommunications sectors.

Fourth year centres on a substantial capstone engineering project, usually with an external client or research supervisor, which functions as the honours thesis component. Engineers Australia accreditation also means the degree satisfies a chartered engineer pathway later on, something worth knowing if a student's ambitions run past their first graduate job.
curriculum:
Duration: 4 years full-time (or 5 years with Diploma in Professional Engineering Practice / industry placement)
Year 1: Engineering Study and Professional Practice, Programming Fundamentals, Mathematical Modelling for Engineers, Introduction to Electrical Engineering
Year 2: Data Structures and Algorithms, Object-Oriented Software Development, Software Architecture, Discrete Mathematics, Systems Analysis
Year 3: Requirements Engineering, Database Systems, Software Construction and Testing, Engineering Elective, Industry-focused Professional Practice subjects
Year 4: Capstone Engineering Project (thesis-equivalent, 2 sessions), Software Engineering electives, Professional Engineering Practice
Optional: paid industry placement (Diploma in Professional Engineering Practice) adds roughly 12 months across the degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 with strong Mathematics background; ATAR approximately 85-90
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
The Bachelor of IT at UTS is the shorter, more direct sibling of the engineering-accredited Software Engineering degree: three years rather than four, and structured around a major rather than a full engineering practice sequence. It suits students who know they want to work in tech but aren't chasing an Engineers Australia-accredited qualification specifically.

Majors have included enterprise systems development, games development, information systems and technology, and networking, and because the course sits within the same faculty (FEIT) as the Master of IT and the software engineering degree, subjects and even some teaching staff overlap across levels, a strength when it comes to breadth of games or systems electives, since the faculty has invested in that infrastructure across several award levels rather than one.

UTS's inner-city Ultimo campus gives students easy access to internships with nearby tech employers, and the course includes an explicit professional practice subject aimed at getting students placement- and job-ready rather than leaving that entirely to careers services.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: Programming Fundamentals, Introduction to Information Systems, Web Systems, Mathematics for IT
Year 2: Data Structures and Algorithms, Database Fundamentals, Systems Analysis and Design, major subjects begin
Year 3: Major electives (Enterprise Systems / Games Development / Networking / Information Systems), IT Professional Practice, Industry Project subject
Majors (choose one): Enterprise Systems Development, Games Development, Networking, Information Systems and Technology
Capstone: industry-based project subject in final year, often with an external client
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR approximately 80 (guaranteed entry lower with adjustment factors)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

name: Bachelor of Laws (Honours)
description:
The Bachelor of Laws (Honours) at UTS is notable for not requiring a separate honours year. Honours is built into the standard degree through a research methodology subject and a research thesis, so a student who wants first or second class honours doesn't have to add time to their course. Two thesis pathways exist: a set honours stream in Legal Futures and Technology, aimed at students interested in how automation, data and platform regulation are reshaping legal practice, or an open-topic thesis supervised individually, drawing on options like criminology, media law, privacy or jurisprudence.

UTS Law has leaned publicly into a "law in context" identity rather than a black-letter one, and the technology-and-law angle shows up across the degree, not just in the honours stream: the faculty runs its own legal tech incubator space and has partnerships with several commercial firms building AI tools for legal practice.

The degree satisfies academic admission requirements for the NSW Supreme Court, and students can complete their Practical Legal Training either within the course or afterward via a separate Graduate Certificate in Professional Legal Practice (C11232). Graduates who complete PLT are eligible for admission as a lawyer in NSW without further study.
curriculum:
Duration: 4 years full-time (LLB Honours)
Core law subjects across the degree: Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Property Law, Constitutional Law, Administrative Law, Equity, Evidence, Civil and Criminal Procedure
Honours component: 76090 Research Methodology, 76040 Research Thesis (or Legal Futures and Technology honours stream)
Options subjects (choose from): Criminology, Privacy Law, Media Law, Jurisprudence, International Law, and other electives
Optional: Practical Legal Training (PLT) embedded in-course, or via postgraduate Graduate Certificate in Professional Legal Practice after graduation
Final year typically combines options subjects with the thesis or Legal Futures stream
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR approximately 92-95, highly competitive entry
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
UTS's nursing program is built around clinical placement volume: up to 840 hours across the standard three-year degree, spread over seven placement-embedded subjects, in settings that include more than 100 partner hospitals and clinics across Sydney and regional NSW. Placements start in first session of first year, which is earlier than a lot of comparable programs, and they run in blocks of two to six weeks during non-teaching periods, including over summer.

The university's health faculty sits close to Royal Prince Alfred and other major Sydney teaching hospitals, and clinical rotations cover acute care, aged care, mental health, community and paediatric settings by the time students graduate. Because the degree leads to registration eligibility with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, the course is necessarily prescriptive about sequencing. Students can't just pick subjects in whatever order suits them, since clinical subjects have theory prerequisites that must be passed first.

Students entering with a health-related diploma or relevant work experience sometimes move through an accelerated 640-hour placement pathway rather than the full 840, though eligibility depends on prior recognised learning.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Health Assessment, first clinical placement block (Session 1)
Year 2: Nursing Care of the Adult, Mental Health Nursing, Child and Family Health, Pharmacology, ongoing clinical placements each session
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Aged Care, Community and Primary Health Care, Transition to Professional Practice, final 4–6 week placement block
Total clinical placement: 840 hours embedded across 7 subjects (640 hours on the accelerated pathway for eligible students)
No separate thesis; final session includes a transition-to-practice subject preparing students for graduate nurse programs
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR approximately 78; National Police Check and immunisation compliance required for clinical placements
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 6.5 (or equivalent, per NMBA registration standard)

name: Master of Architecture
description:
The Master of Architecture is the professional, accredited half of UTS's architecture pathway, undertaken after the Bachelor of Design in Architecture or an equivalent qualification, and required for anyone who actually wants to register as a practising architect in Australia. It's accredited jointly by the Architects Accreditation Council of Australia, the NSW Architects Registration Board, the Australian Institute of Architects and the Commonwealth Association of Architects, which matters if a graduate ever wants to practice outside NSW or overseas.

The two-year full-time structure (four years part-time) shifts the emphasis from the bachelor's broad studio exploration toward professional competency. Students take Professional Practice core subjects covering project management, contracts and financing alongside continued design studios, with the studios becoming more technically demanding and project-scaled as students approach graduation.

Because the degree functions as a practice-readiness qualification rather than a purely academic one, a meaningful share of students are already working part-time in architecture firms while completing it, and the program structure (flexible subject selection, part-time option) reflects that reality rather than assuming a purely full-time cohort.
curriculum:
Duration: 2 years full-time (4 years part-time)
Year 1: Advanced Design Studios, Advanced Building Technology, Architectural Theory and Research Methods
Year 2: Design Studios (project-scaled, technically advanced), Professional Practice (project management, contracts, financing), capstone design thesis project
Accreditation: Architects Accreditation Council of Australia, NSW Architects Registration Board, Australian Institute of Architects, Commonwealth Association of Architects
Entry pathway: typically follows Bachelor of Design in Architecture (C10004) or equivalent
Capstone: final design thesis project, often exhibited publicly at year's end
admission_requirements: Bachelor of Design in Architecture or equivalent recognised undergraduate qualification in architecture
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
UTS's MBA is run out of the university's business school in the middle of Sydney's CBD, and the program leans on that geography deliberately: a lot of the case work and guest teaching draws on ASX-listed companies and government agencies headquartered within walking distance of the campus. It's aimed less at fresh graduates and more at people with several years of work experience already, and admission typically expects that.

The course structure covers the standard MBA spine (strategy, finance, leadership, marketing) but UTS markets its point of difference as a stronger focus on digital transformation and data-driven decision making than some of the more traditional Group of Eight MBA offerings, reflecting the university's broader identity as a "university of technology." Students can typically choose specialisation electives or a capstone consulting project with a real organisation as the final component, rather than a purely theoretical thesis.

Class sizes tend to be smaller than the big-name MBA cohorts, and much of the teaching happens in the evening or in intensive block mode to accommodate students still working full-time.
curriculum:
Duration: 1.5–2 years part-time (most students), full-time options available
Core subjects: Strategic Management, Managerial Finance, Marketing Management, Leading People and Organisations, Business Analytics and Decision Making, Digital Business Transformation
Elective/specialisation block: choose from Finance, Marketing, Entrepreneurship, or Business Analytics streams
Capstone: industry-partnered consulting project or strategy capstone in final session
Delivery: evening and intensive block modes common for part-time cohort
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree plus at least 3 years professional work experience (or equivalent), or approved postgraduate qualification
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

name: Master of Data Science and Innovation
description:
The Master of Data Science and Innovation is UTS's transdisciplinary flagship in this space: 96 credit points split across a core (44cp), specified data-science optional subjects (32cp) and genuinely open electives (20cp) that can be drawn from almost anywhere in the university. The pitch is less "learn to code models" and more "learn to run data science as an organisational capability," with subjects like Data Science for Innovation and Innovation Labs sitting alongside the expected statistics and machine learning content.

First year covers the technical spine (statistical thinking, machine learning algorithms, data science foundations), while second year shifts toward visualisation, narrative and an Innovation Labs subject where students work on real problems brought in by industry or government partners, often in small interdisciplinary teams rather than solo.

Because a third of the credit points are genuinely free electives, students frequently use the degree to pair data science technical skills with a domain they already know (health, law, design, business), which UTS positions as the actual differentiator versus a narrower straight machine-learning master's.
curriculum:
Duration: 2 years full-time, 96 credit points
Year 1: Data Science for Innovation, Statistical Thinking for Data Science, Machine Learning Algorithms and Applications, 3 electives
Year 2: Data Visualisation and Narratives, Innovation Labs (industry-partnered team project), 4 electives
Structure: 44cp core, 32cp specified data science optional subjects, 20cp open electives (any faculty)
Capstone: Innovation Labs project with external industry or government partner
No separate thesis requirement; project-based capstone instead
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree; duration (1-2 years) depends on prior qualifications and relevant work experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
UTS built its Master of Information Technology around the idea that most people arriving in the program are switching lanes: economics grads, biomedical scientists, business analysts, people who did a humanities degree and then discovered they actually like writing code. The course leans into that with a foundation block before students pick a major, rather than assuming everyone already knows what internetworking or machine learning even mean.

The faculty (FEIT) has strong ties to the local tech and finance sector through Sydney's CBD-adjacent campus, and a good chunk of the major electives get taught by people still working part-time in industry: expect guest lectures from Atlassian or one of the big four consultancies rather than purely academic case studies. Majors on offer have included software architecture, business intelligence, information systems, games development, and internetworking, though not every major runs every session (internetworking wasn't offered in the Spring 2026 intake, for instance).

Graduates go on to roles like business intelligence analyst, IT security analyst, e-business developer, and software architect. The 96-credit-point structure means students without a technical background typically move through it slower initially, taking foundation-level programming and systems subjects before the major electives kick in, but it's designed to get a non-IT graduate to employable competence in under two years full-time.
curriculum:
Total: 96 credit points, full-time approx. 1.5–2 years
Foundation subjects (for students without an IT background): Programming Fundamentals, Systems Analysis and Modelling, Database Fundamentals
Core subjects (7): includes Applications Programming, Software Development Studio, IT Project Management, Professional Programs in IT
Major (6 subjects, choose one): Software Architecture / Business Intelligence / Information Systems Management / Games Development / Enterprise Systems Development / Internetworking (availability varies by session)
Project and elective block (3 subjects): capstone research or industry project (6cp or 12cp) plus remaining electives from data science, cybersecurity or cross-faculty subjects
No formal thesis requirement; capstone project can be industry-partnered through the Master's Data Science and Innovation-style project unit
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, writing 6.0 minimum.

name: Bachelor of Behavioural Science (Psychology)
description:
The Bachelor of Behavioural Science (Psychology) is UniSC's standard three-year accredited pathway into professional psychology, structured so graduates who want to keep going can move directly into the one-year Honours program, which is separately APAC-accredited and required for anyone continuing toward registration as a psychologist. The Honours year is genuinely research-heavy: students complete a dissertation (PSY408A/B) alongside advanced coursework in statistics, ethics, and the legislative framework governing psychological practice in Australia, rather than honours being a token add-on year.

UniSC also runs a combined Behavioural Science (Psychology) / Counselling degree for students who want dual accreditation pathways (APAC alongside the Australian Counselling Association and PACFA), which is a slightly unusual offering. Most universities keep counselling and psychology as fully separate degrees rather than building a combined pathway.

The standard bachelor's on its own doesn't lead to registration; it's the first stage of a longer pathway (Honours, then postgraduate training or supervised practice) that mirrors the national psychology registration requirements everywhere in Australia, so students need to plan the full sequence rather than assuming the bachelor's alone gets them into practice.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time (Bachelor), plus 1 year Honours (APAC-accredited)
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Research Methods, Biological Bases of Behaviour, Social Psychology
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Psychological Assessment, Statistics for Psychology
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology, Personality Theory, advanced electives, research preparation
Honours (optional 4th year): PSY400 Research Methods and Analysis, PSY401 Advanced Theoretical Issues, PSY402 Professional Practice of Psychology, PSY403 Ethical and Professional Issues, PSY408A/B Research Dissertation
Combined pathway available: Bachelor of Behavioural Science (Psychology) / Bachelor of Counselling (dual APAC/ACA/PACFA accreditation)
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The Bachelor of Business at UniSC is a fairly standard generalist business degree in structure (foundation year, then a major, then advanced electives and a work-integrated learning component), but it's worth knowing in context of where UniSC sits: a regional Queensland university whose graduate outcomes lean heavily on Sunshine Coast and Brisbane employers rather than the big multinational graduate programs that Group of Eight business schools feed into more directly.

Majors typically include accounting, marketing, management, tourism and event management (reflecting the region's genuine tourism economy), and human resource management. The tourism and event management option in particular draws on UniSC's location. The Sunshine Coast is a real tourism and hospitality economy, not just a marketing backdrop, and placement partners for that major include local tourism boards and event companies rather than purely hypothetical case studies.

Accounting students need to check their specific subject selection against CPA Australia or Chartered Accountants ANZ requirements if they want the degree to satisfy those professional accreditation pathways directly, since not every accounting-adjacent subject in the course automatically counts.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: Accounting Principles, Economics for Business, Marketing Fundamentals, Management, Business Statistics
Year 2: Major subjects begin (Accounting / Marketing / Management / Tourism and Event Management / Human Resource Management), Business Law
Year 3: Advanced major electives, Work-Integrated Learning placement or industry project, capstone strategy course
Majors (choose one): Accounting, Marketing, Management, Tourism and Event Management, Human Resource Management
CPA/CAANZ accreditation pathway available depending on major and subject selection
admission_requirements: ATAR 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Communication
description:
UniSC's Bachelor of Communication runs students through the standard media, journalism, and public relations foundations before letting them specialise, and the degree leans on the university's growing profile in regional and digital media rather than pretending to compete head-on with the big-masthead placement networks that Sydney or Melbourne journalism schools can offer. Students get exposure to regional broadcasters, local papers, and the Sunshine Coast's expanding digital content and marketing sector, which is a genuinely different professional network than what a capital-city program would provide.

The course covers writing, media law and ethics, and digital content production, with students able to lean toward journalism, public relations, or social media and digital communication depending on their career direction. A work-integrated learning placement in the final year is standard, and UniSC has been building out its digital media production facilities on campus in recent years as student demand shifts away from traditional broadcast toward content creation and social platforms.

Graduates typically move into roles in regional media, corporate communications, digital marketing agencies, or government and not-for-profit communications teams.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: Introduction to Communication and Media, Writing for Media, Media Law and Ethics, Digital Media Production
Year 2: stream selection (Journalism / Public Relations / Digital and Social Media), Media Research Methods, Content Strategy
Year 3: Advanced stream subjects, Work-Integrated Learning placement, capstone communication project or portfolio
Streams: Journalism, Public Relations, Digital and Social Media
Capstone: industry placement-linked portfolio or campaign project
admission_requirements: ATAR 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Criminology and Justice
description:
Criminology and Justice at UniSC covers the expected sociological and legal foundations of the field (theories of crime, criminal justice systems, victimology), but the program has a practical bent toward the actual justice sector employers in Queensland: police, corrections, youth justice, and community services organisations. Students typically complete a work-integrated learning placement in their final year with one of these agencies rather than finishing the degree on coursework alone.

The Sunshine Coast region's demographic mix (a growing population, a significant retiree community, and pockets of real socioeconomic disadvantage inland from the coast) gives the program's community and justice case studies a genuinely local texture rather than pulling every example from interstate or overseas.

Graduates commonly move into policy or operational roles in corrections, youth justice, victim support services, or further study toward psychology, social work or law, and the degree is often taken as one half of a combined degree (paired with criminology and psychology, or with justice and legal studies) for students who know early they want a specific combination of skills.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: Introduction to Criminology, Australian Legal System, Sociology of Crime, Research Methods
Year 2: Criminal Justice Systems, Victimology, Youth Justice, Policing and Society
Year 3: Corrections and Community Justice, Work-Integrated Learning placement (justice sector agency), capstone research project, electives
Elective areas: Family Violence, Cybercrime, Restorative Justice
No separate thesis; capstone is placement-linked applied project
admission_requirements: ATAR 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
UniSC's Bachelor of Education (Primary) requires 80 days of supervised professional experience delivered as four full-time placement blocks, plus 40 hours of separate wider field experience, a structure that front-loads real classroom time earlier and more heavily than some equivalent degrees. Students need a Blue Card before their first placement, with applications needing to go in a full twelve weeks ahead of the block start, which is a scheduling constraint that shapes first-year enrolment planning more than students often expect going in.

From second year, students choose between an English or STEM specialisation, a fork that reflects the two national curriculum priority areas primary schools have been under the most pressure to strengthen over the past several years, particularly STEM given well-documented national concerns about numeracy outcomes.

The degree leads to provisional registration with the Queensland College of Teachers on graduation (subject to standard requirements), and UniSC's placement network draws heavily on Sunshine Coast and wider regional Queensland schools, giving graduates a practical head start on employment in regional and rural postings that some metropolitan-based teaching degrees don't emphasise as strongly.
curriculum:
Duration: 4 years full-time
Year 1: Foundations of Teaching, Child Development, Literacy Foundations, Numeracy Foundations, first professional experience block
Year 2: specialisation choice (English or STEM), Curriculum and Pedagogy, Inclusive Education, ongoing professional experience blocks
Year 3: Advanced specialisation subjects, Classroom Management, Assessment and Reporting, professional experience block
Year 4: Capstone professional experience block (extended), Professional Practice seminar, graduate readiness subjects
Total: 80 days Supervised Professional Experience (4 full-time blocks) + 40 hours Wider Field Experience
Requirement: Blue Card required before first placement, application 12 weeks in advance
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent, Working with Children Check required
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 (no band below 7.0)

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) - Civil Engineering
description:
UniSC's Civil Engineering (Honours) degree is accredited at Professional Engineer level by Engineers Australia and structured around 384 total units across four years, with the honours classification calculated from the mean mark across the 96 units of AQF8-level (400-coded) courses in the final stage of the degree, a fairly transparent way of determining honours class compared to some universities' more opaque weighting systems.

Core subjects run through the full range of civil engineering practice: structural design, road and traffic engineering, concrete design and technology, water and wastewater systems, and environmental engineering, with two dedicated engineering project courses providing the capstone research and design component. Students must also complete a minimum of 60 days of approved industry work experience, which UniSC treats as a hard requirement rather than an optional add-on.

The Sunshine Coast's rapid regional growth (new housing estates, transport corridors, and coastal infrastructure under constant development) gives students a genuinely active local pipeline of real projects and employer placements, rather than relying purely on textbook case studies from elsewhere in the country.
curriculum:
Duration: 4 years full-time, 384 total units
Year 1: Engineering Fundamentals, Mathematics for Engineers, Physics for Engineers, Introduction to Civil Engineering
Year 2: Structural Design, Water and Wastewater Engineering, Engineering Mechanics, Surveying
Year 3: Road and Traffic Engineering, Concrete Design and Technology, Structural Modelling, Environmental Engineering
Year 4 (AQF8, 400-coded, 96 units): Advanced Structural Analysis and Design, Sustainable Transport Systems, Engineering Management, two Engineering Project courses (capstone)
Requirement: minimum 60 days approved industry work experience
Accreditation: Engineers Australia (Professional Engineer level)
admission_requirements: ATAR 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
UniSC's law degree covers the standard Priestley 11 academic requirements for legal practice admission in Australia, including Contracts, Torts, Property, Constitutional Law, Equity and Trusts, Corporations Law, Evidence, Administrative Law and the rest, but distinguishes itself with two courses that put students in front of real legal problems before graduation. LAW423 Community Legal Practice has students shadowing practising lawyers and assisting with actual client work, and LAW400 Negotiation and Dispute Resolution runs as a simulated clinic where students work in fictional firms resolving hypothetical client disputes.

Because UniSC is a regional university without the long institutional pedigree of the sandstone law schools, the program leans on this practical-exposure angle as its point of difference, along with combined degree options (Bachelor of Laws / Bachelor of Business, /Bachelor of Arts, /Bachelor of Environmental Management) that let students pair legal training with another discipline rather than studying law in isolation.

Graduates still need to complete a separate period of practical legal training after finishing the degree before admission as a legal practitioner. The degree itself satisfies the academic component only, consistent with how legal admission works across Australia.
curriculum:
Duration: 4 years full-time (or as a combined degree, e.g. with Business, Arts, or Environmental Management)
Core courses: Foundations of Australian Law, Criminal Law and Procedure, Torts, Contracts, Property, Constitutional Law, Equity and Trusts, Corporations Law, Civil Procedure, Evidence, Administrative Law, Professional Conduct
Practical courses: LAW423 Community Legal Practice (WIL placement shadowing practitioners), LAW400 Negotiation and Dispute Resolution (simulated clinic)
Electives: Commercial Law, Children and the Law, Intellectual Property, Employment Law, Family Law
Post-graduation requirement: separate practical legal training period before admission as a legal practitioner
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Nursing Science
description:
UniSC's nursing degree requires a minimum of 800 clinical placement hours for NMBA registration eligibility, delivered in consecutive-week blocks that students find out about roughly ten weeks ahead of time, a scheduling rhythm that shapes how students plan work and life around the degree more than most other bachelor programs would. Placements begin in first year and run across hospital, aged care, community and primary health settings, with a Clinical Placement Office handling allocation separately from the academic teaching team.

The teaching model blends clinical simulation labs and virtual reality environments with the placement hours themselves, and electronic medical records training is built in from early in the course rather than left for graduates to pick up on the job. UniSC's health teaching facilities on the Sunshine Coast campus are relatively new, built with simulation wards designed to mimic hospital layouts rather than generic classroom space.

A graduate-entry pathway exists for students who already hold a related degree, compressing the timeline, and the standard degree can also lead into an honours year for students interested in nursing research rather than moving straight into clinical practice after graduation.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time (graduate-entry pathway available for eligible students)
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Health Assessment, first clinical simulation and placement block
Year 2: Adult Health Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology, Child and Family Health, ongoing block placements
Year 3: Complex and Critical Care Nursing, Aged Care Nursing, Community and Primary Health, Transition to Practice, final placement block
Total clinical placement: minimum 800 hours across hospital, aged care, community and primary health settings
Optional: Honours year (research-focused) available after completion of the standard degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent) with an ATAR of approximately 65 or QTAC selection rank; competitive selection with National Police Check and vaccination/immunisation requirements for clinical placements
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with no band below 7.0, or equivalent (required for AHPRA registration as a nurse)

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
UniSC's Bachelor of Science is a flexible, major-based science degree rather than a narrowly specified single-discipline qualification, letting students choose from majors spanning environmental science, biology, chemistry, marine science, and similar fields depending on the year's offering. Given the campus's location, the environmental and marine science options draw genuine advantage from proximity: the Sunshine Coast sits between coastal reef and estuary systems and the Great Sandy biosphere region, and UniSC's own research strengths (the university has notable output in coastal ecology and marine science) filter down into undergraduate field trips and lab work in a way a landlocked science faculty couldn't replicate.

First year is common core across majors (general biology, chemistry, and quantitative methods) before students specialise from second year, with an increasing share of major electives and a capstone research or field project in the final year.

Graduates typically move into environmental consultancy, laboratory and research assistant roles, government environmental agencies, or further postgraduate study, with the university's regional environmental science reputation being a genuine drawcard for that particular major relative to some metropolitan competitors.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: General Biology, Chemistry Fundamentals, Quantitative Methods for Science, Earth and Environmental Systems
Year 2: Major selection (Environmental Science / Biology / Chemistry / Marine Science), major core subjects, Research Methods in Science
Year 3: Advanced major electives, field-based subjects (marine or environmental fieldwork depending on major), capstone research project
Majors (choose one): Environmental Science, Biology, Chemistry, Marine Science
Capstone: independent research or field project supervised by faculty
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science
description:
The Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science at UniSC is accredited at Exercise Science level with Exercise and Sports Science Australia, meaning graduates can call themselves accredited exercise scientists on completion rather than needing further study to use that title. It sits on the Sunshine Coast campus, which gives the program unusually direct access to elite outdoor training environments. The region's surf, running and triathlon culture feeds into applied placements that a landlocked campus couldn't replicate as easily.

The degree requires a minimum of 270 supervised professional practice hours, with 140 of those specifically counting toward ESSA membership requirements, so the practical component isn't an afterthought tacked onto lecture-heavy science subjects. Students are out doing supervised assessment and program design work well before final year.

Course subjects like Exercise Prescription and Programming and Introduction to Coaching Science sit alongside the expected anatomy and physiology base, and UniSC also offers pathway degrees (Clinical Exercise Physiology, Clinical Exercise Science) for students who decide partway through that they want the higher clinical accreditation rather than stopping at exercise science.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: HLT140 Think Health, LFS112 Human Physiology, LFS122 Human Anatomy, SCI110 Science Research Methods, SPX100 Physical Activity and Health, SPX101 Introduction to Sport and Exercise Science
Year 2: SPX102 Introduction to Coaching Science, SPX121 Exercise Prescription and Programming I, Biomechanics, Nutrition for Performance
Year 3: Exercise Prescription and Programming II, Sport Psychology, supervised professional practice placements (minimum 270 hours total, 140 hours toward ESSA)
Accreditation: Exercise and Sports Science Australia (Exercise Science level)
No separate thesis; assessment via essays, reports, seminar presentations and supervised practice
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent) with an ATAR of approximately 60 or QTAC selection rank; Mathematics and a science subject recommended but not required
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0, or equivalent

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
UniSC's MBA is a smaller, regionally-rooted program compared to the metropolitan MBA heavyweights, and it markets that directly: smaller cohorts, closer contact with teaching staff, and case material drawn from Queensland regional business as much as from ASX-listed multinationals. It suits students already working, often in management roles in regional businesses, government, health, or education sectors along the Sunshine Coast and wider South East Queensland corridor, rather than assuming a purely career-break, full-time cohort.
