The course covers the expected core spine of strategy, finance, marketing and leadership, with a capstone project that's typically applied to the student's own organisation or a local industry partner rather than a purely theoretical case competition, reflecting the practical, work-integrated bent that runs through most of UniSC's postgraduate business offerings.

Delivery is flexible, with online and block-intensive options available for the substantial share of students studying part-time while working, and the program doesn't assume a finance or consulting background walking in the door the way some more competitive-entry MBAs do.
curriculum:
Duration: 1.5–2 years part-time (or accelerated full-time option)
Core subjects: Strategic Management, Financial Management, Marketing Management, Leading and Managing People, Business Analytics
Elective block: choose from Innovation and Entrepreneurship, Project Management, Health Management, or Public Sector Management streams
Capstone: applied strategy or consulting project, often based in student's own organisation or a regional industry partner
Delivery: online and block-intensive options for part-time students
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus relevant work experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Master of Information and Communications Technology
description:
UniSC's Master of ICT is built for people entering tech from somewhere else, and the program is upfront about it: 14 courses covering cybersecurity, data analytics, programming, and AI, deliverable in 14 months if a student pushes through fast or closer to two years at a normal pace. It runs across the Sunshine Coast, Adelaide, and online campuses simultaneously, which is a bit unusual for a postgrad ICT degree and reflects UniSC's broader push into flexible, multi-campus delivery over the last several years as it's grown from a regional university into a larger multi-state one.

The course is professionally accredited by the Australian Computer Society, and UniSC embeds vendor certifications directly into coursework rather than treating them as optional add-ons: Microsoft Security, Compliance and Identity Fundamentals shows up as a named credential students pick up along the way, which matters to employers scanning a resume for something concrete.

Students without an IT background start with foundational programming and systems courses before moving into the data-and-security-heavy back half of the degree, and the specialisation option lets students lean further into data management and analysis if that's the direction they're aiming for.
curriculum:
Duration: 14 months–2 years, 14 courses total
Foundation courses (non-IT background entrants): Programming Fundamentals, IT Systems and Infrastructure
Core courses: Data Analytics, Cybersecurity Fundamentals, Software Development, Research Methods for ICT
Specialisation option: Information and Communications Technology Specialisation (data management and analysis focus)
Embedded certifications: Microsoft Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals and other vendor credentials
Capstone: applied ICT project or research course in final term
ACS professional accreditation
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant or any discipline (typical Australian postgrad IT/CS entry bar used as approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
UWA's Bachelor of Arts is a broad-based humanities and social sciences degree with majors spanning history, literature, politics, anthropology, linguistics, Asian studies and more, built on UWA's New Courses curriculum structure that lets students combine a major with a genuinely broad set of electives rather than locking into a narrow single-discipline pathway from first year, the way older-style Australian arts degrees used to.

Being based in Perth, the degree has some specific regional strengths worth naming directly. Asian studies and Indian Ocean-focused international relations content benefit from Perth's geographic position closer to Southeast Asia than any other Australian capital, and Indigenous studies units draw on UWA's location on Noongar country and long-running partnerships with WA Aboriginal communities.

Graduates go into a wide range of fields, including media, public policy, government, education pathways via further study, and the arts and cultural sector, with the degree's broad structure making it a common double-degree partner alongside commerce, law or science at UWA rather than a purely stand-alone qualification.
curriculum:
Year 1: broad elective units across humanities and social sciences, introductory major unit(s), academic writing and research skills unit
Year 2: major units (chosen from history, politics, literature, anthropology, Asian studies, linguistics and others), second major or broadening units
Year 3: advanced major units, capstone research or thesis unit, further electives
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (WACE or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 80+.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
The Bachelor of Commerce is UWA's core business degree, run through the UWA Business School, which holds the AACSB and EQUIS dual accreditation that puts it among a small number of Australian business schools recognised at that level internationally. Majors span accounting, finance, economics, marketing, management and human resources, and students combine a major with a broad-based commerce core before specialising.

Perth's economy gives the degree a distinct regional flavour compared with a Sydney or Melbourne commerce degree: resources sector finance, mining company accounting and corporate roles tied to WA's energy and minerals sector feature more prominently in local graduate outcomes and industry connections than they would at an eastern-states business school, alongside the standard banking, consulting and professional services pathways common to any commerce degree.

Graduates pursue chartered accounting, finance and banking, corporate roles in the resources sector, and general management pathways, with UWA Business School's international accreditation carrying weight for graduates who look toward global rather than purely domestic careers.
curriculum:
Year 1: Economic Principles, Accounting Principles, Business Statistics, Introduction to Management
Year 2: major units begin (Accounting, Finance, Economics, Marketing or Management stream), Business Law, Organisational Behaviour
Year 3: advanced major units, capstone business strategy or applied project unit, optional industry placement
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (WACE or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 85+.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Design
description:
The Bachelor of Design at UWA is the university's studio-based creative degree, covering streams that typically include architecture-adjacent design, interior architecture, urban and landscape design, and product or visual design depending on current stream offerings, taught through project-based studio work rather than conventional lecture-and-exam assessment for most of its core content.

It functions as UWA's foundation pathway into the Master of Architecture and related postgraduate design qualifications, which is the standard structure in Australia now that architecture is a postgraduate accredited qualification rather than a single undergraduate degree, so most Bachelor of Design students intending to become registered architects treat this as stage one of a longer combined pathway rather than a terminal qualification.

Graduates who don't continue into a design-specific master's move into design-adjacent roles in urban planning, construction and design consultancy, while those continuing typically progress into UWA's Master of Architecture or a related postgraduate design degree to complete their accreditation pathway.
curriculum:
Year 1: Design Studio I, Visual Communication, Design History and Theory, Digital Design Tools
Year 2: Design Studio II (stream specialisation begins), Structures and Materials, Design Studio III
Year 3: advanced Design Studio units, capstone design project, portfolio development for postgraduate progression
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (WACE or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 85+; portfolio not typically required.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
UWA's Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) is a four-year accredited degree: engineers here graduate with honours built in as standard, in line with the Washington Accord structure most Australian engineering schools now use rather than treating honours as an optional extra year. Perth's economy leans heavily on resources and energy, and UWA's engineering school reflects that: mining, mechanical, chemical and civil engineering all have direct pipelines into the state's mining and oil and gas sector, alongside newer strength in areas like renewable energy engineering as the WA economy diversifies.

Students choose a specialisation stream after common first-year engineering foundations, and the degree includes mandatory industry-relevant project work and, depending on the stream, placement or work-integrated learning components that connect directly to WA's resources employers, a genuine local advantage given how concentrated mining and energy company headquarters and operations are in Perth compared with the eastern states.

Graduates move into mining, oil and gas, civil infrastructure and increasingly renewable energy roles, with strong graduate starting salaries in the resources-linked specialisations reflecting sustained WA industry demand for locally trained engineers.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Mathematics, Engineering Mechanics, Introduction to Engineering Design, Chemistry or Physics foundation
Year 2: specialisation stream begins (Civil, Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Mining or Software Engineering), Thermodynamics or equivalent core unit, Engineering Computation
Year 3: advanced specialisation units, industry-based project or internship, Professional Engineering Practice
Year 4: capstone engineering design project, further advanced electives, honours thesis or major design project
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (WACE or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 90+ with prerequisite Mathematics Methods and Physics or Chemistry.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Philosophy (Honours)
description:
The Bachelor of Philosophy (Honours) is UWA's flagship program for its highest-achieving school leavers, and it isn't a philosophy degree despite the name. "Bachelor of Philosophy" here is used in the older, broader sense (as in Oxford's PPE-adjacent BPhil tradition) rather than referring to the discipline. Students design an individualised, interdisciplinary program across UWA's schools, take small specialist seminars capped well below normal first-year lecture sizes, and complete an honours-level research project earlier than students in a standard single-discipline degree would.

Entry is competitive and typically requires an ATAR near the top of the state's distribution, and the program functions as UWA's answer to the flagship honours colleges that several other Group of Eight universities run: a way of keeping high-achieving students who might otherwise look interstate or overseas, by offering genuine academic flexibility and research exposure from first year rather than making them wait until an honours year bolted onto the end of a conventional degree.

Graduates typically go on to competitive postgraduate study, research careers, or professional pathways in law, medicine or policy, carrying an honours-level research thesis completed years earlier than most of their undergraduate peers.
curriculum:
Year 1: foundation seminars across chosen disciplines, research skills and academic writing intensive, individualised program design in consultation with academic mentors
Year 2: advanced disciplinary units, interdisciplinary seminar series, preliminary research proposal
Year 3: specialised units in the student's chosen area(s), continued interdisciplinary coursework, honours thesis research and writing, final oral presentation
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (WACE or equivalent); ATAR of 98+ typically required, plus a supplementary application and interview.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Science (Agriculture)
description:
The Bachelor of Science (Agriculture) sits inside a state where agriculture is a genuinely dominant export sector (Western Australia produces roughly half the nation's wheat), and UWA's agriculture program leans directly into that regional weight, covering plant and animal production, soil science, agricultural economics and increasingly agtech and precision agriculture content, with field-based practical components that draw on WA's actual grain, livestock and horticultural industries rather than generic textbook agriculture.

The degree is taught with strong links to WA's Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development and to grower groups and agribusiness employers across the Wheatbelt and southwest, giving students industry contact that a purely metropolitan science degree elsewhere in the country typically can't offer at the same scale.

Graduates move into agronomy, agribusiness management, agricultural research and government agricultural policy roles, with strong local graduate demand given the size and continued growth of WA's grains, livestock and horticultural export sectors.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Agricultural Science, Soil Science, Plant Biology, Chemistry foundation
Year 2: Crop and Pasture Production, Animal Production Systems, Agricultural Economics, Field Practicum
Year 3: Precision Agriculture and Agtech, Agribusiness Management, capstone research or industry placement project
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (WACE or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 75-80.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Science (Marine Science)
description:
The Bachelor of Science (Marine Science) at UWA benefits from an unusually good stretch of coastline right on its doorstep: Perth sits between the temperate Indian Ocean reefs of Rottnest and the Ningaloo Reef further north, one of the largest fringing coral reefs in the world and considerably less studied and less crowded than the Great Barrier Reef, which gives UWA marine science students field research opportunities in relatively pristine reef systems that eastern-states marine science programs simply don't have local access to.

The course combines core marine biology and oceanography with UWA's own strengths in areas like fish ecology and coral reef research, and field components take advantage of WA's marine research stations and the university's own vessel-based and reef-based fieldwork rather than relying purely on aquarium or lab-based teaching.

Graduates move into marine research, fisheries and conservation management roles, often with WA state agencies managing the Ningaloo and Rottnest marine parks, as well as into further postgraduate marine science research both in Australia and internationally.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Marine Science, Biology foundation units, Chemistry, Earth and Ocean Systems
Year 2: Marine Ecology, Oceanography, Marine Invertebrate and Vertebrate Biology, field-based practical units
Year 3: Coral Reef Ecology, Fisheries Science, Marine Conservation and Policy, capstone field research project
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (WACE or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 85+ with prerequisite Mathematics Methods and a science subject.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
The Master of Information Technology is UWA's conversion-friendly postgraduate IT degree, designed for graduates moving into computing from an unrelated undergraduate discipline as much as for computer science graduates deepening their qualification, covering programming fundamentals, systems analysis, databases and networking before moving into specialisation options that typically include areas like cybersecurity, data science or software engineering.

Perth's tech sector is smaller than Sydney or Melbourne's but has real specific strength tied to the resources sector: mining technology, automation and remote operations software, since WA's major mining companies run some of the most automated mine sites in the world and need software and IT talent to support that, giving the degree a regional industry angle that a generic east-coast IT master's doesn't share.

Graduates move into software development, systems analysis, IT project management and, for a meaningful share of WA-based graduates, mining technology and automation roles specific to the state's resources sector.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Programming Fundamentals, Systems Analysis and Design, Database Systems
Semester 2: Networking and Security, Software Engineering Principles, Data Structures and Algorithms
Semester 3: specialisation electives (cybersecurity, data science or software engineering stream), Research Methods in Computing
Semester 4: capstone IT project, professional practice and industry engagement unit
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant or any discipline (typical Australian postgrad IT/CS entry bar used as approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
A fairly standard humanities generalist degree, whose distinguishing feature is breadth. UOW's BA covers majors from history and English literatures through creative writing, politics, sociology, and Asian studies, and it's genuinely flexible about double majors and combining with education, law, or science. It runs through the Faculty of the Arts, Social Sciences and Humanities.

Because Wollongong's cohort is smaller than the capital-city sandstones, tutorials tend to run at a size where students get to know staff by name. The creative writing major in particular has built a local reputation through a student anthology the program publishes each year.
curriculum:
Year 1: two introductory subjects in each of two chosen majors, plus electives
Years 2-3: minimum 8 subjects per major, increasing specialisation, research methods subject in at least one major
Typical majors: English Literatures, History, Creative Writing, Politics and International Relations, Sociology, Asian Studies, Philosophy
Capstone: independent research project or internship subject in final year, depending on major
admission_requirements: ATAR 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
UOW's business generalist degree, run out of the Faculty of Business and Law. Majors span accounting, finance, marketing, management, and international business, with the accounting major accredited by CPA Australia and CAANZ, which is relevant for anyone planning to go into public practice.

The degree leans on UOW's industry links in the Illawarra (BlueScope, Port Kembla logistics firms, regional financial services) for internship placements, and there's a business analytics elective stream that's grown in enrolment as demand for data-literate commerce graduates has increased.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Fundamentals, Economics for Business, Business Statistics, Marketing Principles
Year 2: Corporate Finance, Management and Organisational Behaviour, first major subjects
Year 3: second major or elective deepening, Business Law, Strategic Management
Major options: Accounting, Finance, Marketing, Management, International Business, Human Resource Management
Capstone: work-integrated learning subject or business strategy capstone, final year
admission_requirements: ATAR 75 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Communication and Media
description:
Run through the School of the Arts, English and Media, this degree covers journalism, digital media production, public relations, and media studies as combinable strands rather than forcing an early major choice. UOW has invested in student-run media output, a digital publication and campus radio-adjacent projects, that functions as informal work experience alongside the formal internship subject.

It's a smaller program than the media schools at bigger metro universities, which in practice means more hands-on time per student on the video and podcast equipment rather than queueing for bookings.
curriculum:
Year 1: Media and Communication, Introduction to Journalism, Digital Media Production, Communication Theory
Year 2: Public Relations Principles, Media Law and Ethics, Video and Audio Production, Social Media Strategy
Year 3: specialisation electives (journalism, PR, digital production), Media Industries and Policy, Internship (WIL)
Capstone: portfolio or major media production project, final year
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Computer Science
description:
The undergraduate sibling of UOW's Master of Computer Science, this degree covers programming fundamentals through software engineering practice, security, and a choice of specialisation streams: the school offers strands touching games and interactive media, data-adjacent electives, and networks and cybersecurity. UOW's CS undergrad has an established internship option that a meaningful slice of students take up, usually with regional employers or Sydney firms willing to take on Illawarra-based interns.

First year is common across CS, IT and related degrees, so switching majors early is low-friction. The degree is accredited with the Australian Computer Society, which matters for anyone aiming at visa-sponsored roles later.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Programming, Data Structures and Algorithms, Discrete Mathematics, Computer Systems
Year 2: Object-Oriented Design, Database Systems, Operating Systems, Software Engineering
Year 3: Networking, specialisation electives (security, AI/ML, interactive media), Professional Practice
Optional: Professional and Community Engagement (WIL/internship) subject in place of an elective
Capstone: team-based major project, Year 3
admission_requirements: ATAR 75 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Data Science and Decisions
description:
A newer-generation undergraduate degree pairing statistics and computing with decision science and business analytics, pitched at the gap between a pure CS degree and a pure statistics degree, aimed at students who want to work as analysts or data scientists rather than software engineers or statisticians specifically. Taught jointly by the business faculty and computing school, which shows up in units combining optimisation and decision theory with programming and machine learning.

Because it's a relatively new offering, cohort sizes are still modest, and the school has used that to keep project work genuinely individualised rather than templated group assignments.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Programming, Statistics for Data Science, Business Decision Making, Mathematics for Data Science
Year 2: Databases, Machine Learning Fundamentals, Optimisation and Decision Analysis, Data Visualisation
Year 3: Big Data Analytics, Applied Business Analytics, Capstone Data Science Project, electives
Capstone: applied project with an industry or research dataset, final year
admission_requirements: ATAR 80 or equivalent, Mathematics recommended
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) - Civil Engineering
description:
A four-year Engineers Australia-accredited degree run through the School of Civil, Mining and Environmental Engineering. Students get access to the SMART Infrastructure Facility's transport and infrastructure modelling research, and the degree includes a mandatory minimum 12 weeks of industrial experience, which the school helps place, often with Illawarra-region firms doing heavy industry, port, or rail infrastructure work given the area's industrial history around the steelworks and Port Kembla.

Structural, geotechnical, water, and transport engineering are the core specialisation threads, and the thesis project in the final year is usually tied to a live industry or research problem rather than a hypothetical brief.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Mechanics, Mathematics for Engineers 1 & 2, Materials Science, Engineering Design
Year 2: Structural Analysis, Fluid Mechanics, Geotechnical Engineering 1, Surveying
Year 3: Structural Design (steel and concrete), Water Engineering, Transport Engineering, Construction Management
Year 4: Capstone Engineering Design Project (thesis), advanced electives, Professional Practice
Mandatory: minimum 12 weeks industrial experience
admission_requirements: ATAR 80 or equivalent, completion of Year 12 with Mathematics
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Environmental Science
description:
Sits within the Faculty of Science, Medicine and Health and makes practical use of Wollongong's geography: the Illawarra escarpment, coastal wetlands, and nearby national parks are used as actual field sites rather than being theoretical case studies. Fieldwork is a genuine differentiator here; students spend blocks of time out of the classroom on ecological surveys, water quality monitoring, and soil sampling from early in the degree.

Graduates go into environmental consulting and local or state government environmental roles. The degree includes a professional practice subject aimed specifically at that job market, and there's crossover with the university's earth and environmental sciences research groups for students wanting an honours pathway.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Environmental Science, Ecology, Earth Systems, Chemistry for Environmental Science
Year 2: Environmental Monitoring and Assessment, Soil Science, Hydrology, GIS and Remote Sensing
Year 3: Environmental Management and Policy, Conservation Biology, field research project, Professional Practice
Fieldwork: recurring field-based subjects using Illawarra escarpment, coastal and wetland sites
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
UOW's LLB is taught out of the School of Law on the main campus and is accredited for admission purposes in NSW. It can be taken standalone but most students do a combined degree: Laws/Arts, Laws/Commerce, Laws/Science are the common pairings. The law school runs a clinical legal education program through the Illawarra Legal Centre, giving students real client contact under supervision before they graduate, a differentiator from programs that stay purely classroom-based until Practical Legal Training.

Wollongong isn't a huge legal market compared to Sydney, so a lot of graduates end up doing PLT and early career work there, but the local legal aid and community legal centre placements give students exposure most city-campus students don't get until much later in their careers.
curriculum:
Core (Priestley 11 subjects): Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Property, Equity, Constitutional Law, Administrative Law, Evidence, Civil Procedure, Company Law, Professional Conduct
Electives: minimum 8 subjects from areas including IP law, family law, international law, employment law
Clinical option: supervised placement at Illawarra Legal Centre (credit-bearing)
Capstone: research subject or moot competition, final year
admission_requirements: ATAR 90 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Medical and Health Sciences
description:
This one is UOW's on-ramp into its own Graduate School of Medicine. Most students taking it are aiming at the Doctor of Medicine, and the course is built around that transition: a defined number of places carry a guaranteed pathway into the MD for students who hit the GPA and interview bar, rather than everyone having to sit GAMSAT cold. It sits in the Faculty of Science, Medicine and Health and shares anatomy and physiology teaching space with the medical school next door.

First year is standard biomedical science: anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, cell biology, shared with other health science cohorts. From second year it narrows into pathophysiology, pharmacology, and population health, with an honours research year in fourth year that pairs students with active medical research groups, several connected to the Illawarra Health and Medical Research Institute on campus. Not everyone ends up in medicine; it's a legitimate finishing degree for people heading into health policy, medical research, or postgraduate allied health study, but the MD pathway is the reason most people enrol.
curriculum:
Year 1: Human Biology, Chemistry for Health Sciences, Foundations of Anatomy and Physiology, Introduction to Health and Medical Sciences
Year 2: Systems Physiology, Biochemistry, Microbiology and Immunology, Pathophysiology
Year 3: Pharmacology, Population and Global Health, Research Methods, discipline electives
Year 4 (Honours): independent research thesis with a medical/health research supervisor, advanced seminar subjects
MD pathway: GPA threshold assessed progressively, guaranteed interview and provisional entry confirmed by end of Year 3
admission_requirements: ATAR 85 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
UOW's nursing degree leads to registration eligibility with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. It carries a heavy clinical placement load: well over 800 hours spread across acute, aged care, community, and mental health settings, mostly within Illawarra Shoalhaven Local Health District facilities given the university's location next to Wollongong Hospital.

Simulation labs on campus get heavy use in first and second year before students move to live placements, and the school runs a specific rural and remote placement stream for students willing to travel, which some take up for the different clinical exposure it offers.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Health Assessment, first clinical placement block
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology, Aged Care placement
Year 3: Acute and Critical Care Nursing, Community and Primary Health Care, Paediatric and Maternal Nursing, final capstone placement
Placement hours: 800+ across the degree, mix of acute, community, aged care and mental health settings
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 or equivalent, National Police Check and Working with Children Check required
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0)

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
An APAC-accredited undergraduate psychology degree, the standard first step toward provisional and eventual general registration in Australia. Taught within the School of Psychology, which has research groups in areas such as early childhood development and clinical neuropsychology that feed into elective options and honours placements.

The degree is explicitly the first three years of the accreditation sequence: students who want to practise go on to a competitive, GPA-gated Honours year and then postgraduate clinical training. UOW's cohort size means the practicals (running small real research studies as coursework) happen in genuinely small groups rather than being simulated at scale.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Psychology, Research Methods 1
Year 2: Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Cognition, Research Methods 2 (statistics)
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology, Personality, Psychological Assessment, Research Methods 3 (independent project)
Honours (separate, competitive entry): thesis plus advanced coursework, required for the provisional registration pathway
admission_requirements: ATAR 75 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
UOW's MBA runs through the Faculty of Business and Law and is AACSB-accredited. It targets working professionals: most units are offered in intensive or evening/weekend formats so people can study alongside full-time jobs, and the cohort skews toward students with several years' work experience rather than fresh graduates.

Core coverage is standard MBA territory (strategy, finance, marketing, leadership), but the elective structure lets students build a concentration: options have included international business and innovation/technology management, reflecting the region's manufacturing and steel industry links. A consulting-style capstone project replaces a traditional thesis for most students, usually done with a real host organisation.
curriculum:
Core: Managerial Economics, Financial Management, Strategic Management, Marketing Management, Organisational Leadership, Business Analytics for Decision Making
Electives: choose 4, options include International Business, Innovation Management, Human Resource Strategy, Entrepreneurship
Capstone: applied strategy/consulting project with a partner organisation, final session
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus 2 years relevant work experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Master of Computer Science
description:
UOW's Master of Computer Science runs out of the School of Computing and Information Technology, based across the main Wollongong campus and the SMART Infrastructure Facility building on the eastern side of campus. It's built for people switching into computing from another background as much as CS graduates topping up their qualification: there's a foundation stream covering programming and data structures for anyone without a CS undergrad, then the degree proper moves into data management systems, network design, and software architecture. Wollongong's CS group has a long-standing research strength in wireless networking, and that shows up in elective options around network and system security.

Class sizes are smaller than at the Group of Eight campuses in Sydney, and a fair chunk of the cohort is international, drawn partly by post-study work rights and partly by regional-campus fee settings that undercut the big Sydney universities. The degree finishes with an individual capstone project, supervised one-on-one, which functions as a portfolio piece students bring to interviews with Illawarra-region and Sydney tech employers.
curriculum:
Foundation session (waived with a relevant CS background): Programming and Data Structures, Data Management Systems
Core: Software Construction and Design, Advanced Database Systems, Strategic Network Design, Security, Ethics and Professionalism
Electives: choose from cloud computing, machine learning, mobile application development, distributed systems
Capstone: individual major project, supervised by CSIT faculty, final session
Optional: internship/WIL subject in place of one elective for eligible students
Duration: 24 months full-time or 48 months part-time
admission_requirements: A recognised bachelor's degree in any field with a weighted average mark (WAM) of 60% or above; applicants with other qualifications plus relevant professional experience may also be considered.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, minimum 6.0 in each band.

name: Master of Data Science
description:
Housed in the School of Computing and Information Technology, this is a conversion-friendly degree: people with a quantitative but non-CS background (maths, engineering, science, even some commerce graduates) can enter through the foundation stream. Coursework runs through statistics, machine learning, big data systems, and data visualisation, with more weight put on applied projects using real or realistic datasets than on pure theory.

UOW markets this partly on Wollongong's growing data-analytics employer base and partly on affordability relative to Sydney's data science masters programs, a genuine consideration for the international cohort making up a large share of enrolments.
curriculum:
Foundation session (background-dependent): Programming for Data Science, Statistics for Data Science
Core: Machine Learning, Big Data Management, Data Visualisation, Data Mining
Electives: deep learning, natural language processing, business analytics (varies by session offering)
Capstone: applied data science project, industry or research-based, final session
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Architectural Studies
description:
The first stage of UNSW's architecture pathway, leading toward the Master of Architecture for accreditation as a registered architect, taught through the Built Environment faculty with design studio as the backbone of every year rather than a single subject among many. Studio culture at UNSW leans toward digital fabrication and computational design, and the faculty's fabrication workshops give students hands-on model-making and prototyping access that shapes how design projects get assessed.

Sydney's architecture and construction industry provides the backdrop for a lot of studio briefs, and the degree includes history, theory, and technology subjects alongside the studio sequence so graduates aren't purely design-focused going into the Masters.
curriculum:
Year 1: Design Studio 1 & 2, Architectural History and Theory, Architectural Technology, Digital Representation
Year 2: Design Studio 3 & 4, Structures, Environmental Design, history/theory electives
Year 3: Design Studio 5 & 6, Construction and Materials, Professional Practice, portfolio development
Progression: leads into the Master of Architecture (separate, required for accreditation)
admission_requirements: ATAR 85 or equivalent, portfolio may be required
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
UNSW Business School's flagship undergraduate degree offers around 15 majors, from accounting and finance through to business analytics, cyber security management, FinTech, and international business: broader major choice than most competitor commerce degrees. A for-credit Work Integrated Learning course is compulsory, not optional, meaning every graduate has at least one internship, case competition, or applied project on their transcript by the time they finish.

The school's scale in Sydney gives it deep employer relationships with the big four banks, consulting firms, and the accounting majors' professional bodies (CPA Australia, CAANZ), and double-degree combinations with Law, Computer Science, or Science are common for students building a more technical or legal commercial profile.
curriculum:
Year 1: Financial Accounting, Microeconomics, Business Statistics, Marketing Fundamentals
Year 2: Corporate Finance, first major courses begin, Business Law, Organisational Behaviour
Year 3: major specialisation deepens (8 courses per major), Work Integrated Learning course (compulsory)
Majors: 15 available, including Accounting, Finance, Business Analytics, Cyber Security Management, FinTech, Marketing, International Business
Capstone: WIL course (internship, consulting project, or case competition), final year
admission_requirements: ATAR 92 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Computer Science
description:
Run through the School of Computer Science and Engineering, this is one of the most selective computing degrees in the country by ATAR cutoff, reflecting demand from Sydney's tech and finance sectors. Students can specialise from second year into streams like artificial intelligence, computer graphics and games, security, or programming languages and compilers, with a well-worn path into UNSW's CSE research groups for honours.

The degree carries a mandatory industrial training requirement (typically a placement over a summer break), and the school has a well-known extracurricular hackathon and competitive programming culture that a meaningful chunk of students plug into outside timetabled hours.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming Fundamentals, Data Structures and Algorithms, Mathematics for CS, Computer Systems Fundamentals
Year 2: Software Engineering, Databases, Operating Systems, Theory of Computation
Year 3: specialisation electives (AI, security, graphics, systems), Professional Issues and Ethics
Mandatory: minimum 60 days industrial training
Capstone: research or industry-linked project course, final year
admission_requirements: ATAR 96 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Economics
description:
UNSW's standalone economics degree, distinct from the Commerce degree's economics-adjacent majors, is more mathematically rigorous, aimed at students wanting genuine technical depth in econometrics and economic theory rather than a business-generalist qualification. The School of Economics has research strength in econometrics and behavioural and experimental economics, both of which show up as elective options by third year.

Graduates go into policy roles (Treasury, RBA, state government), banking and finance, and increasingly quantitative and data roles, and the degree's honours pathway (a genuine research year, competitive entry) is a well-worn route into economics PhD programs both in Australia and overseas.
curriculum:
Year 1: Microeconomics, Macroeconomics, Quantitative Methods, Statistics for Economics
Year 2: Intermediate Micro and Macro, Econometrics 1, Economic History or Policy elective
Year 3: Advanced Econometrics, specialisation electives (behavioural, labour, international, development economics)
Honours (separate, competitive): research thesis plus advanced coursework
admission_requirements: ATAR 90 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) - Software Engineering
description:
A four-year, 168-unit accredited engineering degree combining engineering design fundamentals with computing depth. It starts with the same common engineering core as UNSW's other engineering majors (Engineering Design and Innovation, first-year maths and computing) before specialising into software architecture, systems design, and software project management from second year. Distinct from the standalone CS degree in its engineering accreditation and heavier emphasis on large-scale system design and formal engineering process.

The degree requires a minimum of 60 days of industrial training, which the faculty helps place, often with Sydney's large tech, finance, and telecommunications employers given UNSW's location and industry relationships.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Design and Innovation, Programming Fundamentals, Mathematics 1A/1B, engineering foundations
Year 2: Data Structures and Algorithms, Software Engineering Design and Construction, Database Systems, Computer Architecture
Year 3: Software Architecture, Requirements Engineering, Systems Design Project, electives
Year 4: Capstone Engineering Design Project (thesis-equivalent), advanced electives
Mandatory: minimum 60 days industrial training, plus 168 units of credit overall
admission_requirements: ATAR 90 or equivalent, Mathematics Extension 1 recommended
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of International Studies
description:
Taught through UNSW Arts, Design and Architecture, this degree requires a study-abroad component (typically a semester or year at a partner university) as a core, not optional, part of the structure, which is its defining feature. Students combine a regional or language specialisation (options have included Chinese, Spanish, French, Japanese, Korean) with a disciplinary stream in international relations, politics, or global development.

It draws a mix of students aiming at diplomacy and foreign affairs careers, NGO and development work, and international business, and the language proficiency requirement means graduates come out with genuine working fluency, not just classroom exposure, assuming they complete the exchange component seriously.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to International Studies, chosen language track, Global Politics
Year 2: Regional Studies electives, continued language study, International Relations Theory
Year 3: Study abroad (semester or year at partner institution)
Final year: capstone research project, advanced language subjects
admission_requirements: ATAR 80 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
UNSW Law is one of Australia's higher-ranked law schools, and the LLB (usually taken combined with Arts, Commerce, Science, or Engineering) leans on the faculty's reputation for public interest and social justice law alongside commercial law strength. UNSW runs one of the country's larger law clinic programs, and the Kingsford Legal Centre gives students supervised real-client experience through community legal service placements, a genuine differentiator versus programs where clinical work is optional or minimal.

The faculty also has a strong human rights and international law research base, and students aiming at that side of practice rather than corporate law have real elective depth to draw on, not just one or two token subjects.
curriculum:
Core (Priestley 11): Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law and Procedure, Property, Equity, Constitutional Law, Administrative Law, Evidence, Civil Procedure, Corporations Law, Ethics and Professional Responsibility
Electives: minimum 8 subjects across commercial law, international law, human rights, IP, criminology
Clinical option: Kingsford Legal Centre supervised clinic placement (credit-bearing)
Capstone: research thesis or moot competition track, final year
admission_requirements: ATAR 98 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0)

name: Bachelor of Media (Media, Culture and Technology)
description:
A newer-style media degree from UNSW's Arts, Design and Architecture faculty that deliberately sits at the intersection of media production, cultural studies, and technology. Rather than a straight journalism or PR degree, it treats platforms and algorithms as objects of study alongside teaching production skills. Students work across content creation, media analytics, and critical media theory.

Because it's positioned against the backdrop of Sydney's media and tech industry, work-integrated learning options often connect to digital media, advertising, and platform companies rather than traditional broadcast newsrooms, a different emphasis from older-style journalism degrees elsewhere.
curriculum:
Year 1: Media, Culture and Technology foundations, Introduction to Media Industries, Digital Storytelling
Year 2: Media Data and Analytics, Platform Studies, Production (video/audio/digital), Media Theory
Year 3: specialisation electives, Media Industries Placement (WIL), capstone media project
Capstone: portfolio project or major research essay, final year
admission_requirements: ATAR 85 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Medical Science
description:
Positioned within UNSW Medicine & Health, this is a research-oriented biomedical science degree rather than a direct medical pathway. It doesn't guarantee entry to the MD, but it's a common and well-regarded lead-in for students applying via GAMSAT later, and its lab-based teaching draws on UNSW's medical research strength (the Kirby Institute, Lowy Cancer Research Centre, and similar are genuinely accessible for honours placements).

The degree is heavy on laboratory practical work from first year, with class sizes shrinking and specialisation increasing sharply by third year, when students choose a discipline stream such as pharmacology, pathology, neuroscience, or immunology.
curriculum:
Year 1: Human Biology, Chemistry, Foundations of Biomedical Science, Statistics
Year 2: Physiology, Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, Pharmacology, Anatomy
Year 3: discipline specialisation (pathology, neuroscience, immunology, pharmacology), Research Methods
Year 4 (Honours pathway, competitive): independent research thesis with a UNSW Medicine research group
admission_requirements: ATAR 95 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Psychology (Honours)
description:
This is a 4-year integrated Honours degree at UNSW rather than a 3+1 structure: honours-level research training is built in from the start rather than being a separate competitive add-on, relevant given Honours is generally required for clinical or organisational postgraduate training. The School of Psychology has research strength in areas including addiction, cognitive neuroscience, and clinical psychology, and undergraduate research placements draw directly on those active labs.

APAC accreditation covers the degree for provisional psychologist registration purposes, and the thesis in the final year is an actual independent empirical study, individually supervised, not a literature review dressed up as research.
curriculum:
Year 1: Psychology 1A/1B, Introductory Statistics, Biological Bases of Behaviour
Year 2: Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Cognitive Psychology, Research Methods
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology, Psychological Assessment, Advanced Statistics, Personality
Year 4 (Honours): independent empirical thesis, advanced seminars, supervised by an active research group
admission_requirements: ATAR 90 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
UNSW's general science degree covers an unusually wide span of majors (more than 20, from physics and chemistry through marine science, genetics, and data science) and lets students combine two majors or pair a major with a minor rather than committing early to a narrow discipline. First year is broad and shared, so switching majors after starting is genuinely low-cost.

UNSW's science faculty has strengths that show up in specific majors: quantum and astrophysics research feeds the physics major, and marine biology students get access to field stations rather than purely lab-based teaching. Honours, a separate competitive fourth year, is the normal route into a research career or PhD from here.
curriculum:
Year 1: common science core (mathematics, plus two of chemistry/physics/biology depending on major), Scientific Communication
Years 2-3: major-specific course sequence (minimum 8 courses per major), choice of a second major or minor
Typical majors: Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Marine Science, Genetics, Data Science, Mathematics, Psychology
Honours (separate, competitive entry): one-year research thesis with a UNSW research group
admission_requirements: ATAR 80 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Master of Business Administration (MBA)
description:
Delivered through UNSW Business School's Australian Graduate School of Management (AGSM), this MBA has a genuine executive-education pedigree. AGSM has run MBA programs since the 1970s, and the degree draws heavily on case-method teaching and cohort-based learning rather than a lecture-heavy format. Full-time and part-time/executive study modes are both offered, with the executive stream aimed at people staying in full-time work.

The capstone is a strategy consulting project with a real client organisation, and AGSM's alumni network in Sydney's corporate and finance sector is a genuine part of the pitch: a lot of the program's value proposition is built around access to that network as much as the coursework itself.
curriculum:
Core: Financial Management, Marketing Strategy, Organisational Behaviour and Leadership, Managerial Economics, Strategic Management, Data-Driven Decision Making
Electives: choose from finance, marketing, entrepreneurship, technology management, international business streams
Capstone: strategy consulting project with a partner organisation
Delivery: full-time or part-time/executive study modes
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus at least 2 years professional work experience
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Master of Data Science and Decisions
description:
A relatively new postgraduate program pairing UNSW's strengths in computer science and AI with the business school's decision science and operations research base. It's built to produce people who can do technical data science work but also translate it into business decisions, rather than training pure ML engineers. Courses cross-list between the Business School and the AI Institute.

Applicants come from varied first degrees (engineering, science, commerce, even social science with quantitative subjects), and the foundation stream adjusts for that. The capstone is typically an applied project with an industry partner, reflecting UNSW's broader push to place graduate projects with real organisations rather than purely academic problems.
curriculum:
Foundation (background-dependent): Programming for Data Science, Statistical Foundations
Core: Machine Learning, Data Management and Big Data Systems, Business Analytics and Decision Science, Optimisation
Electives: deep learning, natural language processing, applied econometrics
Capstone: industry-partnered applied data science project, final term
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a quantitative discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
UNSW's MIT is a conversion masters aimed squarely at people without a computing background wanting to move into tech: it's one of the larger postgraduate cohorts in the School of Computer Science and Engineering, and a big share of students come from commerce, engineering, or science degrees rather than CS. Foundation-level courses cover programming and systems from close to zero, then the degree moves into database systems, software engineering practice, and networking before students pick a specialisation.

Specialisation streams have included artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and enterprise systems, and which one attracts enrolment tends to track the Sydney tech job market at any given time. UNSW's CSE school has close ties to Sydney's tech and finance sectors, and MIT students get some access to that same careers pipeline, though the school is upfront that industry placement isn't guaranteed and depends on individual hustle.
curriculum:
Foundation (waived with prior CS study): Programming Fundamentals, Data Structures and Algorithms
Core: Database Systems, Software Engineering, Networks, Systems and Security
Specialisation (choose one): Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Enterprise Systems Development
Capstone: industry or research-based project course, final term
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (AQF Level 7 equivalent) in a cognate discipline (e.g. Computer Science, Software Engineering, IT) with a minimum WAM of 65%. Non-cognate applicants: 3-year bachelor's degree in any discipline (65% average) via the Graduate Certificate pathway.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
VU's general business degree lets students pick a major (accounting, marketing, human resource management, management or international business among them) after a common first-year foundation, and like the rest of VU's undergraduate offering it's delivered block-mode, one unit over four weeks rather than a full timetable of subjects running in parallel.

The course is aimed squarely at Melbourne's west: a large share of VU's business students are first-in-family university attendees or came through pathway diplomas, and the degree includes built-in study support and a Professional Year option that matters to the substantial number of international students in the cohort chasing skilled migration points after graduation. There's also a work-integrated learning unit in most majors, connecting students with local employers rather than leaving placement entirely up to students to arrange.

It's not a prestige-brand business degree in the way a Melbourne or Monash commerce degree might be, and VU doesn't pretend otherwise: its pitch is accessibility and a direct line into local industry rather than an elite cohort experience.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting for Business, Economic Principles, Marketing Fundamentals, Business Communication
Year 2: Business Law, Quantitative Methods, Major units begin (Accounting, Marketing, HRM, Management, or International Business), Work-Integrated Learning unit
Year 3: Advanced major units, Strategic Management, Business Capstone Project
admission_requirements: ATAR 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood and Primary)
description:
This is a dual-qualification degree: graduates come out eligible for registration to teach both early childhood settings and primary school classrooms, which broadens job options in a way a single-sector teaching degree doesn't. VU runs the course through its College of Sport, Health, Engineering (education sits within VU's broader teaching college structure) with mandatory professional experience placements spread across multiple year levels rather than backloaded into the final year.

Students complete placements in both long day care/kindergarten settings and primary classrooms, which means the practical component runs longer in total than a primary-only degree, offset by the broader employment scope it opens up afterward. VU has increasingly focused its teaching pathways on the acute teacher shortages in Melbourne's growth corridors to the west, and a fair number of placement partnerships sit in those newer school communities rather than established inner-city schools.

Coursework covers child development, literacy and numeracy pedagogy, curriculum planning, and inclusive education, with a research or capstone project in the final year addressing a self-chosen classroom practice question.
curriculum:
Year 1: Child Development, Introduction to Early Childhood Education, Literacy Foundations, Numeracy Foundations
Year 2: Curriculum and Pedagogy (Early Childhood), Curriculum and Pedagogy (Primary), Professional Experience Placement 1
Year 3: Inclusive Education, Assessment and Reporting, Professional Experience Placement 2
Year 4: Professional Experience Placement 3 (extended), Research Project in Teaching Practice, Professional Studies Capstone
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent, Working with Children Check required
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 (no band below 7.0)

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Engineering at VU runs on problem-based learning rather than the standard lecture-then-lab format: students in the College of Engineering and Science are handed open-ended engineering problems from early in the course and work through them in teams, with staff acting more as facilitators than lecturers delivering content. It's accredited by Engineers Australia across its specialisations (civil, mechanical, electrical and electronic, and architectural engineering are the usual streams), so graduates come out eligible for graduate membership straight away.

The four-year honours degree includes a substantial industry placement component, and VU's location in Melbourne's west, close to manufacturing, construction and infrastructure projects rather than the CBD, shapes a lot of the applied project work students get assigned. It's a smaller, less internationally ranked engineering school than the sandstone universities, but the trade-off VU offers is smaller class sizes in the specialist years and a teaching style built around solving real problems rather than sitting exams on theory alone.

Students choose their specialisation after a shared first year of core mathematics, physics and engineering fundamentals, then move into discipline-specific design and project units.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Mathematics, Engineering Physics, Introduction to Engineering Design, Engineering Mechanics
Year 2: Specialisation core units begin (Civil, Mechanical, Electrical and Electronic, or Architectural Engineering), Materials Science, Thermodynamics or Structures
Year 3: Advanced specialisation units, Industry Placement, Engineering Project Management
Year 4: Capstone Engineering Design Project (Honours thesis-equivalent), Professional Practice, Advanced electives
admission_requirements: ATAR 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
A three-year degree taught entirely in VU's block format, so students take one IT subject at a time for four weeks before moving to the next, rather than the usual four-subjects-at-once semester grind. VU has published its own research on this model and reports pass rates climbing from 77% to nearly 87% after it was introduced, which the university leans on heavily in how it markets the course to first-in-family students who might otherwise struggle with a traditional course load.

Students choose a major partway through (options typically include software development, cybersecurity, networking or data analytics), and the degree includes an industry-based learning placement in the final year, giving graduates workplace experience before they finish. VU's IT program has a large international cohort, and the block structure was partly designed with exactly that group in mind: intensive, single-subject study is easier to follow for students still building English academic fluency than four simultaneous subjects.

Graduates commonly go into junior developer, systems administrator or support analyst roles across Melbourne's west, an area VU has deliberately positioned itself to serve given its Footscray and Sunshine campus locations sit closer to industrial and logistics employers than the CBD-focused universities.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming Fundamentals, Web Development, Database Design, Networking Essentials
Year 2: Data Structures and Algorithms, Systems Analysis, Cybersecurity Principles, Major elective units begin
Year 3: Advanced major units (Software Development, Networking, or Data Analytics stream), Industry-Based Learning placement, IT Capstone Project
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent, VU Block Model entry
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
VU's law degree requires 384 credit points across four years: 96 points of first-year core study, 132 points of professional core law units (the ones needed for admission), 108 points of law electives and 48 points of non-law electives, and is taught out of VU's City campus, which the university markets as sitting inside Melbourne's legal precinct near the courts and major firms.

Students who perform strongly early (a distinction average across the first 192 credit points) can apply to transfer into the honours version of the degree, assessed against their top 12 law units, so the honours distinction isn't set from day one the way it is at some universities. It's earned partway through. Core areas covered are the ones required for admission to legal practice everywhere in Australia: contracts, torts, property, constitutional, criminal and corporate law.

Because VU draws heavily from Melbourne's west, a lot of the clinical and community legal placement options connect students with legal aid and community legal centres in that catchment rather than corporate firm internships, which shapes the kind of practical legal experience students tend to graduate with.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Law, Contracts, Torts, Legal Research and Writing
Year 2: Criminal Law, Property Law, Constitutional Law, Law elective
Year 3: Corporate Law, Administrative Law, Evidence, Law electives
Year 4: Professional Responsibility, Advanced law electives, Non-law electives, Clinical Legal Practice option
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
VU's nursing degree runs out of the St Albans campus and requires 288 credit points of core study plus roughly 800 hours of clinical placement and around 140 hours of simulation training at the Sunshine Clinical School, which sits alongside a working hospital precinct in Melbourne's west. The clinical simulation load is concentrated in third year, after students have built up foundational anatomy, physiology and nursing practice units in years one and two.

The course leads to registration eligibility with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, and VU's placement partnerships lean on the public hospitals across Melbourne's western and northern suburbs, with Western Health and its network featuring heavily, rather than a spread across the whole city, which means graduates often end up working close to where they trained.

A combined Bachelor of Midwifery/Bachelor of Nursing pathway also exists at VU for students who know from the outset they want registration in both areas, though the standalone nursing degree is the more common entry point.
curriculum:
Year 1: Anatomy and Physiology, Foundations of Nursing Practice, Health Assessment, Pharmacology Basics
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Clinical Placement Block 1
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Simulation-based clinical training (Sunshine Clinical School), Clinical Placement Blocks 2 and 3
Year 4: Specialty placements (paediatrics, aged care, community health), Transition to Professional Practice, Capstone
admission_requirements: ATAR 65 or equivalent, National Police Check and Working with Children Check required
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0)

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
An APAC-accredited undergraduate psychology sequence, which matters because it's the accreditation students need if they want to progress to honours and eventually provisional registration as a psychologist. A non-accredited psych degree closes that path off entirely. VU delivers the core sequence (research methods, cognition, developmental, social and biological psychology, and statistics) in its block format, meaning students spend four weeks immersed in, say, statistics before moving to the next unit rather than splitting attention across a semester.

Students needing the accredited sequence typically go on to VU's honours year or transfer into postgraduate psychology elsewhere, since the three-year bachelor alone isn't sufficient for registration. The course also serves students who don't intend to become psychologists at all: human resources, market research and community services graduates make up a meaningful share of the cohort, using the degree as a behavioural-science foundation rather than a clinical pathway.

VU's psych program is smaller than the large metropolitan universities' offerings, which in practice means smaller tutorial groups in the statistics and research methods units that trip a lot of students up elsewhere.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Psychology, Statistics for Psychology, Research Methods 1
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Research Methods 2
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology, Psychological Assessment, Research Methods 3, Applied Psychology electives
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Social Work
description:
A four-year professionally accredited degree (Australian Association of Social Workers accreditation applies) that trains students for statutory and community-sector practice across Melbourne's west, a region with some of the highest need for social services in the state. VU built the course around two substantial field placements (typically around 1,000 hours combined across the degree), placing students in child protection, community health, mental health and family services settings rather than leaving fieldwork to a single capstone block.

Like the rest of VU's course offering, theory units run block-mode, one subject over four weeks, though placement blocks necessarily run on the employer's schedule rather than the university's. The curriculum spends real time on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander social work perspectives and on Melbourne's west specifically as a case study in structural disadvantage, which reflects VU's own catchment: a large share of its students come from the same low-SES postcodes the degree is training them to work in.

Graduates go on to registration-eligible roles in child and family services, community mental health and case management, with VU's local reputation among Melbourne's west community organisations doing a lot of the placement-to-job pipeline work.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Social Work, Human Development, Sociology for Practice, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Perspectives
Year 2: Social Work Theory and Methods, Field Placement 1, Mental Health and Wellbeing
Year 3: Social Policy, Community Development, Field Placement 2
Year 4: Advanced Practice Methods, Research Project, Professional Ethics and Law
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent, National Police Check required
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0)

name: Bachelor of Sport Science
description:
This is where VU's biggest research reputation actually lives: the university's Institute for Health and Sport was ranked #6 in the world for sport science by ShanghaiRanking in 2025, and undergraduates in this course get taught out of the same $68 million exercise physiology, biomechanics and motor-learning facility at Footscray Park that the institute's 100-plus researchers and postgrad cohort use.

Students work through core units in exercise physiology, biomechanics, motor learning and skill acquisition before specialising toward strength and conditioning, clinical exercise or high-performance sport pathways, and the degree includes practical placement hours with sporting organisations. VU has longstanding research partnerships with elite clubs that occasionally translate into student placement opportunities, though those aren't guaranteed for everyone.

Compared to sport science programs that lean heavily on classroom theory, VU's course puts students in the lab early: first-year students are running basic physiological testing protocols rather than only reading about them, which is a deliberate consequence of the block model letting each subject go deep on one topic without competing for lab time against three other units.
curriculum:
Year 1: Human Anatomy, Exercise Physiology Fundamentals, Functional Anatomy, Introduction to Biomechanics
Year 2: Motor Learning and Skill Acquisition, Strength and Conditioning Principles, Research Methods, Nutrition for Performance
Year 3: Specialisation units (Clinical Exercise, High Performance Sport, or Strength and Conditioning), Practicum Placement, Sport Science Capstone Project
admission_requirements: ATAR 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Master of Applied Information Technology
description:
VU built this course for people who already have a degree in something else and want to pivot into IT without starting from zero. It runs on the university's block model, which means you study one unit at a time over four weeks rather than juggling four subjects across a semester, a format VU has been refining since 2018 after seeing first-year fail rates drop by roughly 40% under it, and the same intensive structure now applies right through postgraduate coursework.

The course covers programming, database design, systems analysis and network fundamentals before moving into electives in areas like cybersecurity or data analytics, aimed at getting career-changers to a point where they can sit entry-level developer or analyst interviews. Because it's pitched at non-IT graduates, the first few units spend more time than a typical postgrad program would on foundational coding literacy before the pace picks up.

Classes run out of VU's Footscray Park and City campuses, both a short train ride from Melbourne's CBD tech employers, and the course carries professional-year options that matter to international graduates chasing post-study work rights.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Programming Principles, Database Systems, IT Project Management, Networking Fundamentals
Trimester 2: Systems Analysis and Design, Web and Mobile Application Development, Cloud Computing Foundations, Elective (Cybersecurity or Data Analytics stream)
Trimester 3: Enterprise Architecture, Advanced Elective, IT Capstone Project
Optional: Professional Year pathway units for eligible international graduates
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant or any discipline (typical Australian postgrad IT/CS entry bar used as approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
VU's MBA is aimed at working professionals rather than fresh graduates (most cohorts expect several years of prior work experience) and runs core units in strategy, finance, marketing and leadership before students pick electives to angle the degree toward their own industry. Delivery follows VU's block model even at MBA level, so units run intensively rather than stretching across a full trimester, which suits people fitting study around a job better than a semester-long weekly-lecture format would.

The program doesn't carry the brand weight of a Melbourne Business School or AGSM MBA, and VU doesn't try to compete on that ground. Its pitch is a more affordable, flexible MBA aimed at Melbourne's west and at international students wanting an Australian postgraduate business qualification with a manageable course load and strong migration-relevant skills assessment outcomes.

A capstone consulting project in the final trimester has students working on a real business problem, often for a small-to-medium enterprise rather than a large corporate client, which keeps the project grounded in the kind of business VU's own graduate network tends to run.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Strategic Management, Managerial Finance, Marketing Management, Leading People and Organisations
Trimester 2: Business Analytics, Operations Management, Elective units (industry-specific)
Trimester 3: Global Business Environment, Elective units, MBA Capstone Consulting Project
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus relevant work experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Agricultural Science
description:
The Bachelor of Agricultural Science is taught at WSU's historic Hawkesbury campus, home to the university's working farm, biodiverse bushland, and facilities for plant breeding, greenhouse technology, biotechnology and soil research, genuinely hands-on infrastructure that traces back to the site's history as Hawkesbury Agricultural College, one of the oldest agricultural education institutions in Australia. The course takes a multidisciplinary approach that integrates the social, economic and environmental dimensions of agriculture rather than treating it as a purely production-focused science degree.

Students get direct exposure to modern precision-agriculture tools (satellite and drone-derived data, decision-support software) alongside the traditional soil science, plant and animal production fundamentals, reflecting how much the discipline has shifted toward data-driven farm management over the past decade. A work internship for science professionals, providing around 100 hours of placement depending on the student's major, connects coursework to real industry experience.

Graduates typically move into agronomy, farm and land management, agribusiness, biosecurity, or further postgraduate research, with the Hawkesbury campus's genuine working-farm environment being a meaningful point of difference from agricultural science programs taught mostly in a classroom setting.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: Introduction to Agricultural Science, Soil Science, Plant Biology, Animal Science Fundamentals
Year 2: Plant Production Systems, Animal Production Systems, Agricultural Biotechnology, Farm Business Management
Year 3: Precision Agriculture (satellite/drone decision-support tools), Biosecurity, advanced electives, Work Internship for Science Professionals (approx. 100 hours placement)
Facilities: University Farm, greenhouse and biotechnology labs, biodiverse bushland field sites
Capstone: applied agricultural project or research subject in final year
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The Bachelor of Business at Western Sydney University is built around a broad first year of shared foundation subjects before students commit to a major. Accounting, finance, marketing, management, international business, and a few others are typically on offer, with the option to combine two majors within the same degree rather than being locked into one professional identity from day one.

WSU's School of Business runs primarily out of Parramatta City campus, in the heart of what's increasingly called Sydney's "second CBD," and the course leans on that location for placement and internship partnerships with the growing corporate and government presence that's moved into Parramatta over the last decade (several state government departments have relocated headquarters there, along with a number of corporate regional offices).

A work-integrated learning subject is standard in the final year, and accounting-track students need to check their specific subject combination against CPA Australia or CAANZ requirements to ensure it satisfies those professional body pathways, since the degree's flexible major system means not every combination automatically ticks every accreditation box.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: Accounting Principles, Economics for Business, Marketing Principles, Management, Business Statistics
Year 2: Major subjects begin (Accounting / Finance / Marketing / Management / International Business), Business Law
Year 3: Advanced major electives, Work-Integrated Learning subject, capstone strategy subject
Majors (choose one or combine two): Accounting, Finance, Marketing, Management, International Business, Human Resource Management
CPA/CAANZ accreditation pathway available depending on major selection
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Communication
description:
